      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program offers salary subsidies to employers who hire youth who have completed a post-secondary program for positions relating to clean technology. Up to $30,000 is available for a maximum of 11 months of full-time employment in STEM*  fields. To support the ‘green economy,’ provide graduates with meaningful experience and reduce the financial risk for employers, the federal government is offering a wage subsidy to facilitate this type of hire.Grant Value:80% up to $20,000 in wages for  job ready youth + $5,000 training subsidy;80% of wages up to $25,000 in wages for youth facing barriers + $5,000 training subsidy.Note: youth facing barriers includes women, racialized youth, youth living with a disability, indigenous youth, youth from a rural, remote, northern or fly-in community, and 2SLGBTQI+ youth.Turnaround Time: Notified within 2 -3weeks of submission.Eligible Employers:Be a Canadian organization/company;Be one of the following organization types:Small- and medium-sized enterprises (<500 employees);Large corporation (500+ employees);Non-profit organization;Non-government organization (NGO);Post-secondary institution;Indigenous organization; andGovernments of any level or Crown corporation.Be able to supervise and mentor interns;The employer must have an established payroll account; andEmployers can apply with or without a participant.Eligible Participants:Post-secondary graduates;Aged between 15-30 at the start of the internship;Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents or refugees (work permits not eligible);Legally entitled to work in Canada and in province relevant to the position;Cannot be receiving Employment Insurance during the internship;Not previous participants of a Science Horizon internship program; andNot an employee of the employer prior to this internship (co-op and interns are still eligible).Internship Details:Clean technology is defined by the program as technology that includes any process, good, or service that reduces environmental impacts through:Environmental protection activities that prevent, reduce, or eliminate pollution or any other degradation of the environment;Resource management activities that result in the more efficient use of natural resources, thus safeguarding against their depletion; orThe use of goods that have been adapted to be significantly less energy or resource-intensive than the industry standard.Must be in a *STEM field and be related to climate change or environmental protection through the development of clean tech, such as:Green manufacturing;Green services and retail;Health - Technologies and practices related to health and the environment;Resources conservation/management and sustainable development;Sustainable energy systems;Wildlife conservation;Carbon and climate change mitigation;Sustainable planning/urban design; andEco-tourism,Must be full-time (min. 30 hours per week);Placements must be between 26 to 48 weeks;Placement must be complete by February 28, 2026;Must include a supervision and training plan for the intern;The funding cannot be used:For a position receiving a Science Horizon Youth Internship grant from another delivery organization;For a currently filled position;To replace an employee who is on leave; andFor a current employee moving to a new position.Priority will be given to employers that hire youth facing barriers to employment including but not limited to:Women;Indigenous youth;Youth with disabilities; and Youth from Northern, rural, remote, or fly-in communities.*STEM: Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program cannot be stacked with other Provincial or Federal grants.Process Best Practices:Employers should have a business number, budget, and contact information of the supervisor ready at the time of applying;Employers can apply for positions prior to having an intern;Please ensure job roles are highly technical STEM positions;Reimbursement occurs at mid-point (50%) and upon internship completion (50%); Midterm and final report requirements; andAll applications are submitted on Career Launcher's online portal. There is no option to save an application once you have started, therefore you must keep the webpage open until you are ready to submit.Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers up to $120,000 in salary subsidies to help high-growth Alberta SMEs attract and retain business talent to promote the commercialization of new products/services.  Companies developing innovative technological or knowledge-based solutions are eligible to apply. Funding is provided for a one year term, with a possible extension to a second year. The program aims to help Alberta companies scale new technologies, create high skill jobs, and de-risk the commercialization process. Grant Value: 75% of the candidates salary to a maximum of $120,000. Turnaround Time: 6-8 weeks.Eligible Employers: For-profit SME incorporated in Alberta with less than 500 full-time employees;Must have annual revenues less than $50,000,000;Must be developing innovative technologies or knowledge-based solutions;Not have more than 2 active Alberta Innovates-funded associates simultaneously;Applicants are required to have a significant portion of their physical and operational presence in Alberta;Discernible intent for operational benefits to flow primarily within Alberta; andHave up-to-date corporate filings (Alberta Innovates may perform a corporate search including bankruptcy and litigations). Eligible Associates:Cannot be a shareholder of the applicant company with over 15% of total shares;Has no more than 12 months of previous employment with the applicant company; andMust be legally entitled to work in Canada and prepared to live in Alberta for the duration of the internship.Note: Preference will be given to Associates who have formal business education (e.g. BBA, BCom, MBA, etc.).Program Details:Applicant companies should be developing mid-to-late stage technologies*; Early developmental stages will be considered on a case-by-case basis;The application must identify a phase of product development that can be completed and evaluated in 1 year;Successful applicants can reapply for an extension at the end of the first year;The funded position must focus on the commercialization of technology and include activities relating to: business development, product validation, manufacturing analysis, production planning, exploration of new markets, sales, and marketing, financial strategy, etc.;Position must be full-time (min. 30 hours per week);The applicant company must be able to pay 25% of the candidate's salary; andFunding will be disbursed upon the completion of milestones outlined in the funding agreement. **See here for more details on  Technology  Readiness  Levels  (TRLs)

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:The candidate's salary cannot be funded by any other provincial and federal programs;This program does not offer retroactive funding. Only costs incurred after the signing of the funding agreement will be eligible for reimbursement;Process Best Practices:Applicants are encouraged to seek a Technology Development Advisor (TDA) before submission of application to discuss project details. Please refer to this portal to contact a TDA.If you have already identified a candidate, you can submit part 1 and part 2 of the application at the same time. Once you have submitted your application package, you should aim to start your project activities within 60 days of submission (not approval). This number is flexible as long as it is AT LEAST 60 days from submission (ex. project dates may start 90 days from submission);If you have not identified a candidate, you can submit part 1 of the application, wait for an approval, and then submit part 2 of the application. The applicant has 6 months from approval of part 1 to hire a candidate. Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This sought-after program provides a 100% wage subsidy (capped at $24,000) for digital tech internships (maximum 6 months in duration) for graduates aged 15-30. Placements must be full-time and related to the digitization of the company and/or its products or processes. Employers may also opt for up to $4,000 in training costs to further develop the skills of the intern. Grant Value: Maximum 100% of wages up to $24,000 including an optional $4,000 training subsidyTurnaround time: Funding decisions will be announced 1 week after closing the application periodEligible Employers:Canadian for-profit and non-profit organizations or their subsidiaries;500 employees or less; The employer must have an active payroll account; andEmployer can submit the initial application without a participant.Eligible Participants:Post-secondary graduates (diploma or degree required);Residents of Yukon, Northwest Territories, and Nunavut are exempt from this requirement;Aged 15-30 at the start of placement;Unemployed or underemployed;Underemployed: working part-time or below one's level of education or not in their field of study.Must have basic digital skills knowledge (self-study credentials permitted); Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents or refugees (work permits not eligible); Legally allowed to work in Canada as per federal and provincial requirements;Cannot be previously employed by the employer (co-op and student internships do not count as employment); and Cannot be receiving Employment Insurance benefits during the internship. Internship Details:Must be in a digital field and/or support the digitization of the company and/or its products or processes;3D printing, AI, Big data, Cybersecurity, Film, video or game editing, Graphic design and Robotics;Placements must have a start date between April 1 and August 31, 2022;Placements must have an end date of January 31, 2023, or earlier;Must be full-time (min. 30 hours per week);Maximum 6 months in duration;Maximum 2 internship applications per employer across all Career Launcher programs;All approved employers will be required to register for an employer orientation session;The grant covers 100% of wage for 6 months or until the maximum is reached;Eligible training costs include the following:Online learning and professional development workshops;Training with a Colleges and Institutes Canada Member;In-house training (to a maximum of $2,000); Must be fully developed training with specific learning objectives; andCannot cover any standard onboarding and training offered as part of the new hiring process.Note: Training must be pre-approved by Colleges and Institutes Canada;The employer must have a nepotism policy with respect to the intern;The employer must provide on-the-job mentorship and support;Employer and intern must complete midterm and final reports;Reimbursement at mid-point (50%) and upon internship completion (50%); The subsidy covers employer charges including the Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Employment Insurance (EI) and vacation pay;Employers may choose to pay out the 4% in lieu of vacation or to offer vacation within the contract.The subsidy must not be for currently filled positions, current employees moving to new positions or to replace an employee on leave.

      Best Practices & Forms

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program helps employers in the digital economy hire Canadian post-secondary students by subsidizing up to 70% of the student's salary to a maximum of $7000. The goals of the program are to increase the job-readiness of students looking to build careers in a digital field and to offset the cost of hiring for employers.Grant Value:70% of wages to a maximum of $7,000 for underrepresented participants50% of wages to a maximum of $5,000 for regular participantsTurnaround Time: 10-15 business daysEligible Employers:Companies in one of the following information and communications technology sectors are prioritized:Advanced Manufacturing;Biotechnology;Cybersecurity & Big Data;Clean Tech;Connected Transportation;E-commerce;Entertainment & Gaming; andFinancial tech.Have general liability insurance in the workplace;Be a registered business in Canada with the HR and financial capacity to hire, onboard, and pay the student; andEnsure new hires are on payroll.Eligible Candidates:Current full- or part-time student (Masters and Ph.D. students included) in publicly funded post-secondary institutions;Degree, Certificate, and Diploma programs are all eligible, as long as they are at an accredited Canadian institution;Students must provide proof of enrolment for the duration of the placement.Students who finish classes in April/May and are returning to school in September are eligible for the Summer 2025 semester intake.Canadian citizen, Permanent Resident, or refugee status;Legally entitled to work in Canada;Not an immediate family member of anyone in the organization; andNot replacing a displaced worker or filling a role left vacant due to a labour dispute.Underrepresented participants must self-identify as being in one of the following groups:Women in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics);Indigenous students;Newcomers to Canada (immigrants who immigrated within the last 5 years);Students with disabilities;Visible minorities; andFirst-year students.Program Details:Applications are being accepted for:Winter 2025(December 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026): OPENSummer 2025 (April 1, 2025 to August 31, 2025): CLOSEDFall 2025 (September 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025): WAITLISTINGPlacement length 4-16 weeks;NOTE: may allow for shorter than 4 weeks if they are applying for consecutive terms and the second term is only for example 2 weeks. Applications must be created in the application portal prior to the student’s start date (previously must be submitted prior to the start date);The position must provide a student with a meaningful work placement that includes a Digital or Technology component and uses technology in some capacity;Full- and part-time positions are eligible (no minimum or maximum hours);The placement must be no more than 16 weeks in duration (maximum duration for funds to be provided);The intern may be kept at the company beyond the length of the placement;Funding is only provided for the time that the student is enrolled in a post-secondary program. Students undertaking an internship in their final semester of study will only be eligible for funding until they graduate (ie: a student who graduates in June will not be funded for July and August);Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Should your net new forecast be inaccurate, the application will be sent back for correction in order to have the application approved.The employer must have a nepotism policy with respect to the intern;This program has increased flexibility with consecutive placements as well as the duration of the placement(s);There is no limit to the number of WIL Digital internships an employer can apply for, but they can only apply for 10 BC Innovator Skills Initiative placements;The employer must provide on-the-job mentorship and support;Interns can take online courses to add to their on-the-job learning;Course topics: Advanced Manufacturing, Artificial Intelligence,
Cybersecurity, FinTech, and Intelligent Retail and Commerce.If the participant is a returning student, this needs to be mentioned in their PIF form and the job description must indicate how their job skills will change and increase in the subsequent placement;A learning plan should be submitted to ICTC within 2 weeks of the start of placement;Remote work option for students available;A mid-term check-in form will be required; andFinal evaluation and proof of payroll should be submitted in the last 2 weeks of the placement.

      Eligible Best PracticesThis program can be combined with Provincial wage subsidies as long as the funding does not exceed 100% of the participant's salary;This program does not provide retroactive funding;Placements could have started earlier than the application submission, but the start date in the application must be after the submission date.Process Best Practices:The program requires employers to login from time to time and update/re-submit the application form;Employers must have the following information ready as they will be required in the application form:The Company Profile form;The EFT form (Electronic Funds Transfer authorization);The Void Cheque upload;The Placement Information form; andInvite their student to provide a Recommendation (i.e., the student application form).If the position has been reviewed by ICTC prior to applying, employers must upload a Position Pre-Approval letter in the application;Employers can apply using the online application system. They will be able to save changes and return to the application if a user account is created;Claims can be submitted at the mid-point of placement to apply for 50% of paid wages and at the end of the placement term. Employers must have the ability afford wages for this intern until claims are processed and paid out (4 week turnaround time); andIf employers have trouble finding candidates, they can check out our partners at Hatchways who have a pool of candidates of developers & designers and can assist with the hiring process here; andExtensions on placements are allowed as long as the employer provides a rationale for why they want to continue with the participant and how they will continue to provide the participant with on-the-job, work-integrated learning. If a placement is successfully extended beyond 16 weeks, and they are a BC employer, funding will be provided at the regular 75% to a maximum of $7,500.Forms: Program website: click hereApplication Portal: click here

The position must be at least 30 hours/week, and therefore the employees must not be enrolled in full-time studies and cannot be returning to full-time studies after the subsidy term is complete.Grant value: $3,600 wage subsidy + an additional training subsidy of up to $1,000 for external training per personTurnaround time:  5 business daysEligible Employers:BC employers in all industries;Have been in operation for at least one year;Have a WorkSafe BC account; andMust ensure new hires are on payroll.Eligible Participants:Between the ages of 17 and 29 (inclusive);Unemployed or precariously employed (ie. irregular hours, unreliable wages or below living wages);Canadian Citizens, Permanent Residents or Protected Persons;A resident of BC and legally entitled to work in Canada; andPart-time students are eligible.Ineligible Participants:Full-time students or returning to school full-time after placement is completed;Previous employee of the applicant company; andParticipating in other provincially or federally funded labour market program.Placement Details:Must be a long-term position;Minimum placement duration: 3 months;Minimum 30 hours per week;Maximum number of applications per employer: 2;Employers will be able to submit more applications when the ongoing placements are completed or about to be completed. No partial payments will be made.Training Subsidy:External training is optional;Must be recognized training provider;Recognized online courses (e.g. Udemy) are eligible;Multiple courses are allowed;Covers tuition and the cost of textbooks. Other costs will be considered on a case-by-case basis; andTuition over $1000 must be covered by the employer.Note: Training subsidy may not be used to cover mentor/supervisor hours spent on on-the-job training.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best PracticesThis grant cannot be combined with other federal and provincial wage subsidy programs;The only exception is if the other program is a hiring incentive (ie. programs that do not require pay stubs and/or reimbursements).The program does not accept retroactive applications;Process Best Practices:Applicants applying on the last few days of the month are advised to be prepared to act quickly. Eligible services include:Market Entry Strategy or Export plan;Legal Advice (patent protection advice);Accountancy Advice (taxes, receivables etc.);Tariff, Certification Requirements or Regulations Advice;Export Pricing strategy;Distribution and Logistic;International Marketing plan; andTranslation support (to translate user manuals, product guides etc.).Ineligible Activities:Overhead costs charged to employee labor rates;Sales and marketing collateral;Software critical to the project;Acquisition of land, building, or capital assets;The under-appreciated value of eligible capital costs;Capital improvements;Capital Equipments;Costs relating to travel (including mileage and accommodation), meals, entertainment, hospitality and gifts;Passport or immigration fees;Reimbursements for airfare purchased with personal frequent flyer program;Commuting costs between place of residence and place of employment;Costs associated with applying for government grants and programs;Provisions for contingencies;Technical or professional journals;Routine testing and maintenance;Advertising Costs;Collection charges, allowance for interest on debt, fines, and penalties;Federal and provincial income taxes, goods, and service taxes;Expenses for projects or activities outside the approved project; andOther costs Alberta Innovates deems ineligible.Documents Required:Financial statements of the past 3 years (if available);Business plan for the next 3-5 years;Financial projections for the investments leading up to revenue generation and 3 years post-revenue; andQuotes from Service Provider(s) or sub-contractor(s); andOptional: a letter of interest.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program is a matching fund and requires 1:1 matched investment and therefore is open to combining with other government funds (Federal or Provincial) as long as it is not combined with another Alberta Innovates fund program; A business plan is required (3-5 years financials); It is advised that clients do not launch patent-related activities prior to applying if they are grant reliant; While the program does not offer retroactive funding, it may be able to cover some patent lawyer's costs if the activities carried out occur in line with timing; 25% of the investment must come from SME. This can be based on current market value rates; andCompanies should log in to the online app portal to obtain full and detailed evaluation criteria. Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program assists Canadian businesses in the print and digital publishing industries. Employers are given the opportunity to adapt to dynamic market trends, diversify their content and encourage innovation. The program provides up to $75,000 over two fiscal years (max.) in direct financial support to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Canada.Grant value: 75% of eligible costs to a maximum of $75,000 per project (maximum contribution per fiscal year is $50,000).Note: Only one application may be submitted per fiscal year.Timelines: Applications for projects beginning in the 2022-23  fiscal year are due September 15, 2022; Projects must be completed within two fiscal years (interim report required); andAdjudication time: 20 weeks.Eligible Applicants:Canadian publishing firms producing either digital or print periodicals;Entities may be incorporated for-profit or not-for-profit;Note: Sole proprietors are eligible (refer to best practices below).Must have a business number; andFor additional requirements specific to publication type, see table below.Ineligible Applicants:Newspapers;Newsletters;Blogs that are branded to an individual;Loose leaf magazines;Free print magazines;Academic journals;Promotional pamphlets;Publications that report on the activities of a specific organization or association;Government publications;Publications that contain over 50% reprinted/repurposed material;Publications in which over 50% of content is in any of the following categories:Listings, catalogues, directories;Guides;Financial reports;Schedules, calendars, timetables;Comic books, cartoons, puzzles, games;Horoscopes and/or almanacs.Eligible Projects:Projects should increase the viability and competitiveness of the applicant periodical by:Adapting new technologies;Increasing market access;Developing the next generation of publishing professionals; and/orEnhancing the diversity of  editorial content;Examples of eligible projects include:Conducting market research;Developing a new business model, method, or process;Improving products, services, or systems;Digitizing back issues;Rebranding or Redesign;A special issue (outside of regular publishing schedule);Adoption or use of new media;Creation of mobile app;Web design/development;Expansion into new markets; andAdvertising/promotional campaigns.Eligible Expenses (must be directly related to the project):Promotion costs (design, production, printing, & testing);Venue and equipment rental;Software licensing;Professional fees (e.g. contractors, etc.);Training and professional development;Paid internships;Travel expenses;Salaries (max. 25% of total eligible expenses);Paid internships; andOverhead Expenses (max. 10% of total eligible expenses).Ineligible Expenses:Activities completed prior to application approval;On-going core/operational activities (must be new, strategic endeavor);Capital expenditures;Hospitality costs;Cots related to awards, incentives, and prizes;Incidentals, meals and per diems; andProject contingency funds.Additional Eligibility Criteria for Print PublishersPublication must be printed and appear in consecutively numbered issues under a common title;Must release 2 - 56 issues per year (includes special issues);Have at least 50% paid or 50% request circulation;Does not apply to: Aboriginal, ethnocultural, official-language minority and LGBT publications;Paid circulation magazines must be sold at one of the following prices:Minimum average subscription price of $12 per year;Minimum average subscription price of $1 per copy;Minimum  average single-copy price of $1 per copy.Subscription or single-copy prices appear on the cover or in the masthead of the magazine; andAverage circulation of 250-100,000 copies per issue.Note: The primary goal of the content must not be to promote or enhance the goods/sales/activities of any organization.

Only costs incurred after the signing of the funding agreement are eligible for reimbursement;This program can be combined with other provincial and federal sources of funding.       The CanExport SME program provides a subsidy to businesses of 50% up to $50,000 per project in matching contributions to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Canada seeking to develop new export opportunities and markets. This program requires a minimum annual revenue of $100,000 as shown on a business' corporate tax return. Eligible activities include marketing and promotional materials, legal fees, and consultant expenses. The intent of the program is to help Canadian companies prepare for and establish a presence in the international markets.Grant Value: 50% of eligible costs for $10,000 to $50,000 in funding per projectTurnaround Time: Committed to providing a decision within 60 business days.Timelines: Projects can stretch over multiple fiscal years; andA new project cannot be applied for until a previous project is completed.Eligible Applicants:Incorporated for-profit organizations in Canada;Up to a maximum of 500 FTE employees; Have an active Canada Revenue Agency business number; andNo less than $100,000 and no more than $100 million in annual revenue declared in Canada in the previous tax year (as declared on Line 101 of the applicant's prior year GST return).For cannabis products:Eligible only for medical purposes:Includes: Cultivators, processors, and sellers;Companies must be official Licensed Producers with Health Canada.Eligible Target Markets:Up to 5 markets can be targeted within the same project; andMust be a non-sanctioned country and account for the following during the company's last complete GST tax reporting year (or last 12 months for quarterly or monthly filers):Less than $100,000 in sales;  ORLess than 10% of total sales; ANDIf your project includes multiple markets, total sales across all target markets/regions are less than 10% of your company’s total sales (aggregate).Projects that target the US may not include any other target market country;Projects that target any country other than the U.S. may not include the U.S. as a target market.Eligible Activities:Category A: International travel for meetings or events with key contacts;Per diems to a maximum of 90 days per project;Maximum 2 travellers per trip;Electronic travel authority fees;Quotes agreements;Certification application fees;Fees related to product testing, inspection, and/or development are NOT eligible.Fees to register the product (not the company) in the target market;Supplier diversity certification (to displace women, Indigenous, LGBTQ2+, etc. ownership).Category F: Consulting - business, tax, and legal adviceExpert advise on legal, tax, business matters, regulatory Please ensure all the criteria are met.Eligible Activities:Activities in pursuit of key strategic partnerships with foreign organizations and individuals, with the overarching aim of commercializing technology:Partnerships should have the following objectives:Securing investments from foreign partners for R&D work;Licensing or purchasing the Intellectual Property of foreign partner's technology;Negotiating R&D collaborations that will lead to development, adaptation or validation of applicant's technology.Technology development or enhancement work with foreign partner, including:Working with the foreign partner to conduct a pilot of the applicant's technology:Working with the foreign partner to conduct clinical trials using the applicant's technology;Leveraging the technical expertise and/or technology of the foreign partner to test the applicant's technology.Technology validation:Pilot application and clinical trials.Virtual meetings;Pre-identified in-person meetings;Seeking expert legal business advice from consultants;For the purposes of:New certification requirements (only for countries where there is a pre-identified partner);Navigating foreign market legal framework;Pursuing IP protection;Due diligence on foreign partner and its technology;Drafting/ reviewing legal agreements;Identifying potential foreign partners;Market research; andInternational expansion roadmap.Development of professional promotion plans or materials for meetings with potential partners;Applying for intellectual property (IP) protection in the country of the foreign partners;Shipping applicant's technology for assessmentIneligible Activities:All activities after partnership formalization;Any services requiring payments to/from foreign partners;R&D activities;Customizing the technology to client's needs;Activities for sales and distribution purposes;Manufacturing;Client acquisition; andLobbying.Eligible Expenses:Consultant and legal fees (previously capped at $4,000); Foreign regulation certification fees;Only eligible in countries where the applicant has a pre-identified partner.Intellectual property protection fees;Development and printing of promotional materials;Translation or interpretation services (maximum cost: $2,000); Shipping costs (maximum cost: $4,000); Eligible travel expenses;Approval will be assessed based on:Duration - maximum of 5 days per travel destination;Number of participants - maximum of 2 travelers per trip;Costs (high costs may impact approval).Per diem (ie. accommodation & meals);Capped at $400 per approved travelerSingle entry visas; andRegistration fees for virtual/in-person events; andCost of video conferencing platform (only covered during the months in which meetings with the project partners are scheduled to take place).  Note: The program only supports travel activities that comply with the Government of Canada's travel advisories.Ineligible Expenses:Expenses incurred prior to application submission;Any travel expenses that are inconsistent with Canada's official travel advisories;Airfare costs paid with bonus points from programs such as Air Miles/Aeroplan/World Points or any other barter systems;Capital costs and office supplies;Cell phone charges;Passport costs;Costs of hospitality, entertainment, and gifts;Core activities and overhead expenses;Salaries and commissions;Goods and Services Tax; Event registration that includes booth fees; Events where meetings and pre-identified foreign partners have not been confirmed; andRental and/or installation of a booth for a conference or exhibition.Note: Please see guidelines for a full list of eligible and ineligible expenses. The list above is a selection of most common expenses.Program Details:If a project is approved, the start date of the funding agreement (the date that expenses are eligible) will be the application submission date;The program does not reimburse expenses incurred prior to a project’s start date.A project must focus on only 1 technology per project application;A project can target multiple partners to achieve multiple R&D objectives;Assessment criteria:Applicant eligibility;Technology readiness (TRL 4 and above - beyond ideation stage and into initial prototype creation) and ownership;The methodology used for pursuing partnership;Selection of foreign partners.Must demonstrate:Appropriate skillsExpertiseTechnology compatibility;Ability to make technical contributions.Successful applicants will receive a funding agreement by email, and must sign the agreement within 20 business days. Failure to do so may result in the forfeiture of the funds; Funding recipients must submit a final report no later than 7 days after the completion of the project; andThough all decisions made by CanExport are final and non-negotiable, however, revised applications may be resubmitted.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Applicants must clearly indicate all sources of government funding (federal, provincial/territorial, and municipal) they have received in the form of grants and non-repayable contributions, Canadian government assistance must not exceed 75%;This program is not to cover R&D expenses, those will be incurred after the agreement is signed, so don’t include those expenses in your application;Your product should be IP protected and ownership of the IP should be the applicant of this program; This program is not meant to fund sales, distribution, or manufacturing agreements. Any of these types of activities will be rejected.Process Best Practices:CanEx Innovate is a competitive program with limited funding, so the quality of the application is extremely important. Applications should tell the full story of the organization's plans for pursuing foreign R&D partnerships/investments. Forms and Links:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program pays for up to 100% of training to a maximum of $15,000 per participant per year. It is an ideal program to upgrade the skills within your organization or to provide training to a new hire within your company. The CAJG provides employers with the flexibility of choosing a training provider that meets their needs in terms of location, pricing, and curriculum, provided that the course meets the preliminary eligibility requirements.   Grant value: Employed trainee: 66.67% of eligible training costs to a maximum of $10,000 per traineeUnemployed trainee: 100% of training costs covered to a max. $15,000 per traineeNote: There is an individual employer cap of $300,000 of approved funding per fiscal year (April 1 to March 31).Turnaround Time: 15 business daysEligible Applicants:Be one of the following organization types:Incorporated under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta);A partnership registered under the Partnership Act (Alberta);A sole proprietor with a trading name registered under the Partnership Act (Alberta);Registered under an act of the legislature of a province or the Parliament of Canada;A non-profit registered under a special act or a private act of the Alberta legislature;A non-profit registered under part 9 of the Companies Act (Alberta);Crown Corporations: Agriculture Financial Services Corporation and ATB Financial (Alberta Treasury Branches) in communities with a population of less than 100,000;First Nations; andMetis Settlements. Located and operating in Alberta for a minimum of 1 year before the application is received; andProvide safe working conditions, be in good standing and comply with the Employment Standards Code, Occupational Health and Safety Act, Workers’ Compensation Act.Note: Unincorporated businesses registered for less than one year prior to the date the application is received may be considered as eligible employers if they can demonstrate they have been operating for more than one year.Eligible Trainees:Be Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents, or Protected Persons;Be living in Alberta;Employed trainees:Currently employed by the employer; ORHave been unemployed for 30 days or less prior to being hired.Unemployed trainees:Have been unemployed for more than 30 consecutive days; ORHave worked for the employer for 4 weeks or less and were previously unemployed for more than 30 consecutive days.Note: Unemployed trainees need to submit a conditional offer of employment letter - The letterhead of the letter must match the legal entity name of the applicant's business.Contractor if they are the employer applicant;Seasonal employees - but only under the Employed Trainees stream.Seasonal employees can start and complete their training during their off-season.Currently employed family members:Family members must be currently employed with the employer for a minimum of 90 days before the application received date; andApplicants may be required to verify the employment start dates of their employed eligible family members using T4s or paystubs.Business owners (incorporated, unincorporated/sole-proprietor and partnerships) with 4 or fewer employees;Business owners are ineligible under the unemployed stream.Note: Verification of employment status may be required. Verification may be in the form of a previous year’s T4, a paystub, or other suitable documentation.Ineligible Trainees:Any member of the employer's board or council with 5 or more employees (including all owners);Unemployed family members;Contractors who are not the employer applicant;Temporary foreign workers or anyone temporarily working in Canada; andIndividuals who will not be employed by the employer upon completion of training. Eligible Training:Be relevant to current business operational needs;Be provided by an Alberta-based trainer or take place in Alberta;Online training is considered to take place in Alberta.Must be at least 21 instructional hours in length (for one or multiple courses per application);Only hours spent on instructional content are counted;Course assignments, homework, exams, quizzes, coaching, consulting, mentoring, research, implementation, projects, and pre-course work are not considered instructional hoursHours are not calculated on a per-participant basis;Ie. a 4.5-hour course is a total of 4.5 hours, no matter the number of trainees in the application.Start within 6 months from the approval date;Be completed within 52 weeks from the start date on the application;Training must be delivered by a third-party training provider;Training must be the main business activity of the training provider and must be in business for a minimum of 2 years.Training must result in a form of credentials:Record of completion, certification, diploma, degree, mark, or industry-recognized credential;Post-secondary courses that lead to a degree or diploma are eligible if the course(s) is/are relevant to the current needs of the business and the available job.Be delivered online, onsite, or in a classroom;Self-directed online learning must include instructor interaction. The training provider’s course outline must state that students will have access to an instructor.Training may be customized;Part-time and full-time are eligible;The training provider may be public or private;Note: all training providers must be separate and distinct from the employer.Note: Training can be purchased before the application is submitted. However, an application must be received before training can begin.Ineligible Training:Pre-recorded video content with no instructor interaction;Software providers/IT consultants - those that sell software or are involved in customizing, installing, or implementing software;Training must be billed separately from the other services rendered by these providers.Apprenticeship training;Practicums;Research Papers;Coaching;Conferences;Business Consultingservices;Consulting;Self-study for an exam;Self-study without instructor interaction;On-demand / pre-record video content;Instructional DVDs; andAudiobooks.Eligible Expenses:Tuition fees or fees charged by a third-party training provider;Mandatory student fees and exam fees;Fees for textbooks, software, and other supplies required for the delivery of the training;Travel costs:May qualify if training is highly specialized and not offered in Alberta;Are limited to:Small and medium-sized businesses;Trainees working/training in a community outside Edmonton or Calgary;Travel 100km or greater one way from workplace to a training centre in Alberta; and1-5 days training maximum.Ineligible Expenses:Child care costs;Living allowances;Trainee wages;Physical or digital assets (e.g. laptops, software, hardware) that are retained after training is complete;Apprenticeship training;Note: pre-apprenticeship training is eligible.Health care premiums; andTraining for personal interest.Program Details:Calculating the number of employees of an applicant company:Add the number of employees working for the company at the time of application and all owners of the company (even if owners are not active in the day-to-day operation).Applications are assessed on a first-come, first-served basis, with the exception of applications for unemployed trainees, which are assessed on a priority basis;Employee count may be validated at the discretion of the program.Verification may be in the form of a previous year’s T4 or paystub.All trainees in the application should take all courses in the application at the same time;Employers will be required to demonstrate that training aligns with the needs of the business and the employee's job;All trainee(s) must sign and submit their consent form before the application will be considered received;Prior to submitting the Trainee’s personal information, the Trainee must authorize the CAJG Program to collect the Trainee’s personal information from the Employer. The information entered regarding the Trainee must be reviewed by the Trainee.Training may commence once the application is received;Applications are not considered received by the program until ALL trainees have actioned the generated email by clicking "I confirm".Unemployed trainees are not permitted to fund their training costs upfront and get reimbursed. The employer must pay the training provider directly; andAt the end of the training, the trainees must not bear any of the employer training costs incurred.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:The program does not allow funding to be used in conjunction with other provincial or federal funding;This program will now allow for retroactive funding (training can only start after the application is received by the program);Applicants are advised to submit the application a minimum of 30 days in advance of the training start date to apply for application processing clarification;Federally incorporated or extra-provincial employers must register extra-provincially to obtain an Alberta Corporate Access Number (ACAN) and Certificate of Registration. This can be completed through Alberta Corporate Registries;To obtain the required WCB-Alberta clearance letter, sign into your myWCB account or call WCB-Alberta at 1-866-922-9221;To obtain the required WCB-Alberta exempt industry letter, call WCB-Alberta at 1-866-922-9221;Trainees can still start the training, however, the employer will run the risk of not having the training funded should the application gets rejected;By paying for the training before the application is approved, the applicant bears all financial risks if their application is unsuccessful;Applicants are also advised to check the refund policy of the training provider in case there are delays in the CAJG turnaround times.Groups of staff taking the exact same training can all be put into one application, but non-employed and employed trainees need to be on separate application forms;The employer must notify the Government of Alberta of any changes so a recalculation can be completed for the final reimbursement amount;If the eligible training provider issues a refund, the employer must refund the Government of Alberta within 30 days of the refund date; andHandwritten trainee name(s), course title(s), etc., on a receipt will invalidate the receipt, and a new receipt from the training provider will be required.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click hereGranted Starter Application Process

      Grant Criteria 
      The AgriAssurance Program provides up to $50,000 for agriculture, agri-food, and seafood businesses to implement assurance certification for export to international markets. Applicants must be for-profit organizations incorporated in Canada with annual revenues not exceeding $100 million. The intent of the program is to help increase and diversify exports to markets where Canada has Free Trade Agreements are in place.Grant Value: 50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $50,000 (total contribution towards multiple projects cannot exceed $100,000)Turnaround Time: 75 business daysEligible Applicants:Must be operating in the agriculture, agri-food, and seafood sectors;For-profit organizations incorporated in Canada, including but not limited to:Businesses and corporations;PartnershipsCo-operatives;Communes;Indigenous groups (First Nations, Métis, Inuit).Note: Preference may be given to organizations that are not subsidiaries or members of a larger group of companies.Be directly involved in growing harvesting, processing or otherwise transforming or consolidating their products;Project is aimed at meeting actual market-specific certification requirements (support under this component is only provided for initial certifications, not subsequent renewals);Have up to 500 full-time equivalent employees;Have annual revenues up to $100 million; andBe legal entities capable of entering into legally binding agreements.Eligible Activities:Activities that help employers obtain a third-party certification to meet international market requirements for export opportunities:Contracting professional services (consultants, translators, technical and equipment rental services) to obtain third-party certification to access specific markets;Hiring employees dedicated to making arrangements for such certification; and Salaries and benefits cannot exceed 10% of the total project budget.Traveling to enable the certification (transportation, accommodation, and per-diems).Eligible Expenses:Salaries and benefits:Includes Mandatory Employment Related Costs (MERCs), Employment Insurance (EI), Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Quebec Pension Plan, vacation pay, and benefits;Must be directly related to the project;Salaries and benefits must be incremental to existing costs; andBenefit costs must not exceed 25% of the eligible salary costs for each employee.Contracted Services:Includes inspection, consultant/expert services, financial auditing (required for the project), environmental assessment, research, interpretation and translation services and project management.Travel:Includes per diems, transportation, hospitality, and the purchase of carbon offset credits;Travel costs must be directly related to the project;Other direct project costs:Includes shipping, conference fees, registration fees, construction material costs, translations, and marketing costs related to the production of materials/documents/marketing plans.Note: Only costs as of April 1, 2023, and after application approval are eligible. Costs incurred before this date will not be considered part of the cost-share.Program Details:The program ends on March 31, 2028;Project priorities:Help Canadian agricultural and agri-food sector (including fish and seafood) SMEs adopt the assurance systems and supporting tools required to meet a specific export opportunity or domestic market opportunity for Indigenous Peoples (e.g. with a defined grocery retailer).Assessment criteria:the application is complete and the proposed project is eligible;the proposed activities, including outcomes, support program objectives:Increase and diversify exports to markets where Canada has Free Trade Agreements in placeSupport industry to develop, verify and integrate assurance systems to address market and regulatory requirements (e.g. food safety, plant and animal health surveillance, animal welfare, environmental sustainability, traceability, market attributes, and quality standards);Enable the industry to make credible, meaningful, and verifiable claims about the health, safety, and quality of Canadian agriculture products.All sources of funding for the proposed project to be funded under this program are identifiedReports applicants must submit:Progress reports — reports describing the activities completed and progress made towards the completion of activities described in the project work plan;Performance Reports — annual and end-of-year reports that track progress against mutually agreed to performance measures outlined in the contribution agreement;Financial Reports — reporting is required with each request for reimbursement of expenditures, in addition to year-end accounting and other financial reports.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:The program can be combined with other provincial and federal sources of funding, but total government funding cannot exceed 85% or project costs;This program is not retroactive. Costs must be incurred after application approval AND April 1, 2023;The applicant's contribution to the project must be in cash (not in-kind);Process Best Practices:Applicants are advised to contact a program officer to discuss project details before applying; andThe program will prioritize projects that focus on international export markets as opposed to domestic ones. Forms: Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

        Recently Changed 
        June 19, 2024:The intake is now open until July 12, 2024;The maximum funding has now increased to $500,000 or 75% of total eligible costs - whichever is less; andThe program now also has a start-up stream to develop businesses that have not started or been in operation for less than 12 months.The program will provide funding of up to 50% to a maximum of $10,000.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The Canada Periodical Fund - Business Innovation Component provides funding of up to $500,000 or 75% of total eligible costs to assist Canadian businesses in the print and digital media industries. This program also provides funding of 50% to a maximum of $10,000 for digital-only start-up projects. Applicants must be a Canadian-owned/controlled publishing firm producing printed or digital periodicals. The intent of the program is to enable print and digital periodicals to overcome market disadvantages.Grant value: Regular applicants:Up to $500,000 or 75% of total eligible costs - whichever is lessStart-up applicants:Up to 50% to a maximum of $10,000Eligible Applicants:Canadian publishing firms producing either digital or print periodicals;Be one of the following organization types:For-profit organizations;Non-profit organizations;Partnerships; andSole proprietorship.Be majority-owned and controlled by Canadians;Have the principal place of business in Canada;Must have a business number; andHave periodicals that are edited, designed, assembled, and published in Canada;Have completed at least 1 uninterrupted 12-month publishing cycle before the application;Have periodicals containing at least 80% Canadian editorial content in the issues published during the reporting period;Contain an average of no more than 70% advertising in all issues published during the reporting period;Advertising content is calculated as a percentage of total content published. Note that advertorial and sponsored content are included in this calculation; andContain at least 50% original content in the issues published during the reporting period.Print magazines must also:Be printed and appear in consecutively numbered or dated issues published under a common title;Be published at a frequency of between two and 56 issues per year, including special issues;Have an average circulation of no less than 250 and of no more than 100,000 copies per issue;Have subscriptions sold at a minimum average subscription price of $12 per year or at a minimum average subscription price of $1 per copy;Have a total average circulation of the magazine during the 12-month reporting period that does not exceed 100,000 copies per issue.Digital-only magazines must also:Be available through a valid URL, an app for download, email format, or a third party publishing platform;Maintain a regular publishing schedule in which the majority of editorial content changes at least twice during a 12-month period;Have articles date-stamped with identified authors;Be one of the following types of verifiable circulation:Paid subscription service;Email-based service;Open access-service.Regularly represent written content from more than 1 person;Have generated revenue between $2,500 and $500,000 in the fiscal year (e.g., subscription revenues, advertising sales, etc.).Start-up projectsmust also:Be a developing business that has not yet started, or that has been in operation less than 12 months.Ineligible Applicants:Newspapers (daily and non-daily);Website, blogs, and digital periodicals that are branded to an individual;Loose leaf magazines;Free print magazines;Academic journals;Promotional pamphlets;Publications that report on the activities of a specific organization or association;Professional association publications;Publications that contain over 50% reprinted/repurposed material;Publications in which over 50% of content is in any of the following categories:Listings, catalogues, directories;Guides;Financial reports;Schedules, calendars, timetables;Comic books, cartoons, puzzles, games;Horoscopes and/or almanacs.Eligible Projects:Project activity must be incremental and not be repeated from previous Business Innovation projects designed to achieve specific goals with measurable results over a fixed time period;Be outside of and in addition to regular, recurring or ongoing operations, including editorial, production and distribution activities; andExamples of eligible projects include:Conducting market research;Developing a new business model, method, or process;Improving products, services, or systems;Digitizing back issues;Rebranding or Redesign;A special issue (outside of regular publishing schedule);Adoption or use of new media;Creation of mobile app;Web design/development;Expansion into new markets; andAdvertising/promotional campaigns.Eligible Expenses (must be directly related to the project):Promotional and marketing costs (design, production, printing, & testing);Venue and equipment rental;Software licensing;Professional fees (e.g. contractors, etc.);Training and professional development;Paid internships;Travel expenses;Salaries (max. 25% of total eligible expenses);Paid internships;Cost of audited financial reports for the project;Project-related overhead Expenses (max. 10% of total eligible expenses).Project Details:Applicants are limited to 1 application per periodical per government fiscal year;Successful applicants receiving $250,000 or more will be required to submit audited financial reports for the project;Required documents for application submission:Proof of legal status (for a first-time applicant or incorporated in the year if applicable);Quotes from consultants, if applicable;Written confirmation of in-kind contributions to the project and other sources of funding, if applicable; andNot-for-profit organizations: a copy of the resolution of the Board of Directors in support of the project and identifying the authorized signatory.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program does not provide retroactive funding. Only costs incurred after the signing of the funding agreement are eligible for reimbursement;This program can be combined with other provincial and federal sources of funding. However, total government funding cannot exceed 75% of eligible costs;Applications should focus on one primary activity. Supporting activities may be included, but should be related to the primary activity;If you have applied to the program previously, make sure your new application focuses on a new activity. The program is unlikely to fund the same applicant more than once for the same activity. For example, if you previously received funding from the Canada Periodical Fund to record promotional videos, you should not apply a second time to record new videos;Applicants should ensure that there is no news/current events coverage displayed on their websites, as news publications are not eligible for this grant.Forms: Program website: click hereApplication guidelines: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program provides up to $75,000 per year to increase sales, reduce market risk, and enhance long-term sustainability for B.C.’s agriculture, food and beverage exporters by providing cost-shared funding to undertake market development activities outside of B.C. that enable sector businesses and associations to maintain, expand and/or diversify export markets.Grant Value: Food producers, processors and cooperatives, 50% of eligible expenses from a minimum of $5,000 up to a maximum of $50,000 per year or 30% of last year's annual revenue, whichever is lessIndustry associations, boards and councils, 70% of eligible expenses from a minmum of $5,000 up to a maximum of  $75,000.Note: Producers, processors, and cooperatives that have previously received 50% Ministry / 50% Recipient funding from the Program can expect to receive 35% Ministry / 65% Recipient for projects that are offering to take on the same activities in the same locations in the previous year that they received funding.Turnaround Time: Notified October-November 2025Eligible Applicants:Organizations will be required to apply for one of two funding streams based on their organization type:1. Producers and Processors which include:Primary agriculture producers;Agriculture food and beverage, and/or
seafood processors; andAgriculture, food and beverage
cooperatives.2. Industry Associations which include:Agriculture, food and beverage, and/or seafood industry associations, boards, and councils representing B.C.
agrifood and seafood sector businesses/
organizations.Have a head office in B.C. or be entitled to do business in B.C.;Be selling or marketing a product grown or processed in B.C.;Processed in BC (i.e.  Processing food, beverage, or agricultural and seafood products which are processed and packaged in BC with more than 85% of the product’s main ingredients produced in BC  (Note:  in cases where the main ingredients are not available in  BC  in sufficient quantities,  the food must be processed and packaged entirely in BC);If the organization is a cooperative be producing fresh food, beverage,or agricultural products that are 100% grown or raised in B.C.;The project budget must contribute a minimum of:50% for B.C.-based primary agriculture, food and beverage, and/or seafood processors;30% for industry associations, boards, or councils.Have a minimum annual gross revenue of $100,000 annually for the 2 most recent consecutive years.Note: Seafood producers/processors cooperatives/industry associations are not eligible.Eligible Activities and Expenses: NOTE: For a project to be funded through the program, an application must include 1 or more of the 3 activities listed below:Export Market Tradeshows, Food Fairs, and Sales Exhibitions (Commercial Buyers Only)Participating in interprovincial/international tradeshows, food fairs, and sales exhibitions to connect with commercial buyers, including associated costs related to:Booth rentals, booth accessories, and services, translators, meeting buyers on the margins of the event, or shipping produce samples to and from the event.Consumer-Focused Promotional Activities in Export Markets;Conducting consumer-focused retail or food service promotions in export markets, including associated costs such as:hiring brand ambassadors, renting pop-up booths, purchasing serving utensils, or shipping samples to
and from the retail or food service establishment.Marketing Collateral and Advertising or Social Media Campaigns;Developing export-focused marketing materials, including: Videos, brochures, rack cards, posters, banners, recipe
cards or point-of-sale signage for retail or food service promotions (e.g., shelf talkers, menu inserts, etc.);Delivering paid advertising campaigns (print, radio, TV, digital) to promote specific products;Hiring a third-party social media contractor in a specific export market for community management, social
outreach, content curation and analytics to promote specific products in export markets; andTranslating online or print communications to a foreign language to promote a specific product(s) in export
markets.Note: A full list of Eligible Activity types and outputs can be found in Appendix 1: here.Ineligible Activities/Expenses: Consumer-focused tradeshows or events;Meals and per diems;Buyers’ meetings as a standalone activity (i.e., not directly related to tradeshow attendance);Accommodation and travel expenses exceeding basic room rates and taxes. Room service, mini-bar,
movies, spa treatments, business & first-class flights, hotels exceeding 3-star rates are not eligible
expenses;Activities that take place before the approved project start date or after the project completion date.
Deposits paid for tradeshows prior to receiving funding approval may be considered eligible. Having
made a deposit does not mean that the project or activity will receive funding. Deposits paid shall be
made at the Applicant’s own risk;Any costs associated with obtaining product certifications, licenses or related fees required to be
deemed as ‘market ready’;Cost of producing/packaging product samples;General administrative and operational costs such as: Salaries (including project management,
coordination, or project delivery, including social media, by salaried staff), Packaging materials,
equipment, office expenses, business cards, rent and other ongoing costs related to day-to-day business
incurred by the applicant, or firms represented by the applicant (hiring staff, holding a conference or
annual meeting, etc.);Costs associated with giveaways or promotional products, including those planned for re-sale such as
branded glasses, coasters, buttons, bags, clothing, aprons, etc;Expenses for attending consumer-focused tradeshows or events;General industry events that are not focused on market development such as annual general meetings;Costs associated with developing and submitting applications;Any activities that may be considered to denigrate other products, commodities or regions (e.g. farmed
vs. wild salmon; organic vs. conventional agriculture);Costs where the payee is a government (i.e. government of BC, Canada, etc.);All product-related expenses and brand development such as labels and coupons;Costs incurred if the Project or element of the Project is abandoned;Legal Fees;Normal operating costs associated with out or expanding a business’ current operations (including
planning and delivery of annual events, tours, purchasing of office supplies);Building and implementing an e-commerce tool or website; Funds to sponsor a third-party activity; andCannabis-related activities. Note:  This is not an exhaustive list.Program Details:Anticipated Project start date November 17, 2025;Project completion date March 1, 2026;Quotes are required for costs over $5,000;Funding reimbursements are made following the submission of paid invoices and a Financial Report at the deadlines set out in the agreement; andApplicants must have the ability to commit to providing, a minimum percentage of the total Project budget in cash, towards eligible project costs as follows:50% for producers, processors, and cooperatives; and30% for industry associations, boards, or councils.

Agreement has been fully executed; andApplicants are encouraged to include only activities that they are confident will be completed on time and within budget.Forms:Program website: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program supports BC producers and processors in the agri-food sector to obtain up to 75% funding to support research and commercialization of a product with a project start date between April 1, 2022, and December 31, 2022. The purpose of this program is to help organizations implement innovative projects that will benefit BC’s agricultural sector.Grant Value: Up to 75% of cash costs for eligible expensesTypically, non-repayable contribution varies from 30%-75%, depending on:The scope of the project;The level of innovation proposed by the project;The amount of risk that the innovation would yield to the applicant organization during the repayment period; andHow wide and significant the benefits of the project will be in terms of the organization, the sector and the BC economy.Turnaround time: 5 monthsEligible Applicants:Must be registered, licensed, and certified to do business in BC; BC agri-food sector producers and processors;Industry associations/organizations;Food retailers and wholesalers who are involved in the agri-food value chain including importers and distributors;Input, technology, and support services providers;Primarily Sector - other (e.g. auction yards, fairs, warehouse storage, transporters, importer);Processing Sector - other (e.g. distributors, warehouse storage, transporters, importers); andValue Chains (e.g. producer-processor-distributor).Academic institutions and research organizations;Regional districts and local governments;Non-timber forest resource harvesters and wildcrafters;Eligible Activities:Approved activities with a start date from April 1, 2022, to December 31, 2022;The activities in the project must facilitate innovation in BC's agriculture and/or agri-food sector. Examples include but are not limited to:Advancements in plant, animal, and food science;Energy and waste management;New product development and commercialization;Improvements in soil, water, and air quality; andClimate change adaptation.Ineligible Activities:Activities that do not provide a direct benefit to agriculture and the agri-food industry;Business Risk Management and related activities;Operational expenses;Purchase of common items that can be used for multiple purposes (e.g., digital cameras, GPS, smartphones, measuring tapes);Capital expenditures unless expressly approved for the project;NOTE: No land or building costs.Activities related to aquaponic food production, and to aquaculture, seaweed, fish and seafood production and processing;Tax credits or rebates;Development and enforcement of regulations;Projects or proposals that are considered long-standing practices in the Province of British Columbia;Activities that are unlikely to result in an improvement of product attributes; and/or reduce the production cost, increase productivity or advance the sustainability of a commodity group or region;Activities that cannot demonstrate a benefit to the regional economy or commodity group;Activities considered direct income support to a producer or processor;Costs incurred for the delivery of services/activities to ineligible individuals and/or organizations;Activities that do not comply with laws/regulations;Buying, starting, or expanding a farm or business;Basic research is defined as experimental or theoretical work that is undertaken primarily to acquire new knowledge without a commercial or specific application;Lobbying or influencing any level of government; andActivities related to medical marijuana. Eligible Expenses:Direct expenditures required to implement the
projects are eligible for cost-sharing. Examples include but are not limited to:Costs of goods and services and all related shipping costs;Salaries and benefits of personnel working directing on the project;Costs of rental or lease of facilities, equipment, or machinery;Accommodations;Telecommunications;Hospitality;Travel;Intellectual property registration and licensing fees;Non-reimbursable portion of GST; andTranslation of information to the public.

        February 25, 2025Application deadline has been extended until March 3, 2025.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program offers salary subsidies to employers who hire youth to manage projects that are beneficial to the Agri-Foods sector. It covers up to 50% of wages to a maximum of $14,000 to hire youth to help build career-relevant experience and up to 80% of costs to a maximum of $14,000 for youth facing barriers. If required, placements are also eligible for $5,000 to relocate for the position or expenses to help overcome barriers. The intent of the program is to help youth and those facing barriers build meaningful work experience in the agricultural sector and for agri-employers to build their talent pipeline.Turnaround time: 50 business daysGrant Value:50% of wages to a maximum of $14,000 + 50% of relocation costs up to $5,000 for regular participants80% of wages to a maximum of $14,000 + 80% of barrier-related expenses up to $5,000 for youth facing barriers (see Participant Eligibility section down below)Eligible Applicants:Be one of the following organization types:For-profit organizations;Not-for-profit organizations;Associations, sector councils, community/charity organizations, and corporations.Individuals or sole proprietorships;Provincial, territorial, and municipal governments;Academia.Be an agricultural-related organization, including but not limited to:Farmers;Agricultural businesses (greenhouses, orchards, vineyards, vegetable producers, etc.);Businesses that supply agricultural services;Food processors;Agricultural related non-government organizationsEmployers do not need to identify a candidate before submitting an application. Note: Agri-food distributors, wholesalers, and Agri e-commerce employers are not eligible unless they also produce food.Eligible Candidates:Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents, or refugees (work permits are not permitted);Aged 15-30 at the start of the internship;Unemployed or underemployed;Unemployed refers to those are new to the organization, a new hire can also include someone hired up to 3 months before the date the application was submitted; andEmployees already employed by the employer may be eligible if they will be moving to a new position that be can considered a career advancement or a promotion.Cannot be receiving Employment Insurance (EI) during the project period;Youth facing barriers:Living with disabilities (mental health-related, physical or learning disability);Indigenous;Visible minorities;Recent immigrant (have been granted status within 5 years);2SLGBTQI+Persons living in an Official Languages Minority Community;e.g. A Francophone residing outside of Quebec or an Anglophone residing in Quebec.Living in a low-income household;Please see the low-income household definitions here.Single parent;Early school leaver; andResiding in a remote, northern and/or fly-in-community.NOTE: Employees who have been previously hired under the YESP program are not eligible.Eligible Expenses:Salary;Social benefits that the employer already pays to all employees:health benefits;Vacation pay;Employer contributions to benefits programs (CPP, EI, Health service fund etc.).Reasonable relocation costs;Costs to remove barriers for youth:Assistance with dependents;Accommodation needs; andAccessibility equipment/technology.Note: All expenses claimed must involve a cash payment. Taxes paid for barrier-related expenses are not eligible for reimbursement.Program DetailsEligible positions:If the company is firmly in the agri-food sector: any position is eligible;If the company is not entirely in the agri-food sector: the position must support the agriculture industry AND the job must be agriculture and agri-food related;i.e. anything related to changing the physical nature of the product such as a food canning technician.Ineligible positions:The program does not provide support for a delivery driver or marketing agent for meal delivery types of businesses.Full-time, part-time, seasonal, or casual work are all eligible;Minimum duration: 2 months;Maximum placements per employer: 1;Earliest internship start date: April 1, 2025;The internship must be completed by March 31, 2026;Salary is limited to a maximum of $60,000 per annum;The employer must provide on-the-job mentorship and support;The employer must offer meaningful and career-related agricultural work experience;Positions not directly related to agriculture (ie. marketing or accounting in an agricultural company) may be eligible;The program has funded such positions in the past. Will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.Projects should include those that benefit the Agri-Food industry;Reimbursement issued at the end of the internship (for projects under 8 months in duration) or split between 50% at mid-point and 50% upon completion (for projects between 8-12 months in duration);Successful applicants are responsible for completing and submitting evaluation and participant information forms at the mid-point and/or at the end of the project.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This funding can be used in conjunction with other government sources of funding up to 100% of eligible costs;Interns receiving Employment Insurance (EI) are eligible, but must be off EI before the placement start date;Process Best Practices:The candidate does not need to be identified at the employer application stage; andEmployers who do not use all the approved placements should let the program officer know so the funding is available for others.Forms:Program webpage: click hereApplication guide: click here
