      Grant Criteria 
      The B.C. Employer Training Grant subsidizes between 80% of eligible training costs to a maximum of $10,000 per participant per year. It is an ideal program to upgrade the skills within your organization, or to provide training for a new hire for your company. Training can be taken at a public post-secondary institution or through a private training provider (additional course syllabus requirements apply).There is a maximum claim amount of $300,000 per company per fiscal year. Funding StreamEligible Training TypesGrant coverage (Limit per fiscal year)TechnicalTraining for software, equipment or machineryIn-house training is eligible under this stream (must be delivered by a certified instructor).Technical skills may now include new manufacturing, production and construction methods.Training is allowed outside of BC if it’s specialized and no similar training is available from an eligible third-party training provider in BC.80%(Max. $10,000 per participant)An application must be submitted before training can begin.Turnaround time:  Approx. 6-8 weeksEligible Applicants*Business and non-profits in BC that have been:Registered with BC Registry Services for at least one yearIn possession of a municipal business license for at least one year or alternative proof of business existenceMust have a Business BCeID accountTrainees must be Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents or Protected PersonsTrainees cannot be family members of business owners*Applications are no longer reviewed on a first come first serve basis. First time applicants, small business applicants (under 50 employees), businesses in diverse regions in BC, and applicants who align with labour market priorities will be prioritized.Eligible ExpensesTuition fees and mandatory student fees (including GST) for training course programFees for textbooks, software and other supplies required for the trainingExam fees when attached to a training programCosts for an indigenous elder may, with prior approval, be considered an eligible fee charged by a third party training provider.Travel costs (incl. accommodation, only for business based outside of Metro Vancouver, Greater Victoria and in a community of pop. under 25,000)Ineligible Expenses Conferences, trade shows, seminars, membership fees, coaching, consulting or mentoring, work experience and paid practicum. Training for personal (versus professional) developmentMealsMaintenance training Task Summary Choose course with staffVerify eligibility: applicant, training and employer eligibilityApply for BCeIDSubmit applicationFor non-grant reliant courses*: start and pay for trainingApprovedSubmit "Participant Information Form" five days prior to trainingFor grant-reliant courses: pay and start trainingComplete reporting and reimbursement requirementsVerify payments has been received *Non-grant reliant courses: Employers may start training employees after grant application has been submitted if the payment of the training is not reliant on the grant. Best PracticesVerify 3rd party private training providers and ensure they are a fit for the program before you prepare your application Choose the right funding stream, applications will be rejected if they are put under the wrong stream Follow through with your training, it is important that you don't exceed the number of courses only to back out of them laterAdjudication time is long, make sure you are flexible with start dates for courses that you rely on for grant funding All tuition must be settled within 30 days of course start date. You may switch your participants or training provider if necessary. In group study, if a few participants drop, you will only obtain reimbursements for people who attended the trainingCopies of last year and this year's business licenses should be uploaded at the application stage

The intent of the program is to provide cross-disciplinary networking and peer-learning opportunities for research fellows who might not have otherwise in their careers.Grant Value: Program funds 50% up to $30,000 (minimum stipend for the participant must be $55,000)Turnaround Time: 6-8 weeks.Eligible Employer:For-profit or non-for-profit organization of any size;Canadian company or a foreign-owned organization located in Canada;Has an office or site located in the same province as the candidate’s university; Provides on-the-job mentorship and support to participants; andThey are end users of the research. Ineligible Employers:Government departments, agencies or ministries;Academic institutions;Indigenous governments; andForeign companies. Eligible Candidates:Ph.D. graduate (all degree requirements, such as signoff of the dissertation, must be completed prior to project start);Canadian citizen or permanent resident;International applicants are also eligible;The date of graduation from a Ph.D. program must not be more than 5 years prior to the proposed start date of the research project;Based in a university located in the same province as the employer; andNo more than 6 months of post-graduation work experience; Elevate alumni that have completed a 1 or 2 year Elevate project will be able to apply for another Elevate project; and Postdocs can only be funded for a maximum of 3 years.Program Details:Duration: 1 to 2-year fellowship;All research projects must demonstrate a viable economic or productivity orientation. Examples of research projects include (but not exclusive to):Creation of video games and apps for the purposes of being used in a festival;Development of a program to help stroke victims return to work; andResearch to better understand the impacts of blindness towards employment and working environments.Any potential conflict of interest must be declared and mitigated.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best PracticesParticipants may hold NSERC/CIHR/SSHRC or Mitacs Accelerate postdoctoral scholarship, but may not hold Mitacs Elevate award at the same time as any other federal, provincial or Mitacs grant or scholarship;Strongly suggest sending a draft proposal to elevate@mitacs.ca for a one-time pre-review before submission;Looking for clear methodology (not just what will be done but how) and a clear personal development section that explains how the post-doc will benefit from Elevate training AND personalized letters of support to why they should support that post-doc rather than another post-doc.Forms: Program website: click hereApplication form: click hereProposal writing guide: click here

Up to $20,000 is provided over five years (2018 to 2023).Grant value: Funding for up to 70% of eligible project costs upTurnaround time: 30 business daysEligible Applicants for General Program:Be based and operating in BC;File business or farm income taxes in BC;Be provincially or federally licensed;Maintains an active 9-digital business number with Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) or have an active GST number;Be a legal entity (association, corporation, partnership, proprietorship, trust or individual that has legal standing;Be  registered with the BC Premises Identification Program if the business raises livestock and/or poultry;A Premises ID is a unique 9-character code assigned to a single legal land description or land use permit.Be an agribusiness that handles food for human consumption in the following North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS):Manufacturing:3112 Grain and Oilseed Milling;3113 Sugar and Confectionery Product Manufacturing;3114 Fruit and Vegetable Preserving and Specialty Food Manufacturing;3115 Dairy Product Manufacturing;3116 Meat Product Manufacturing;3118 Bakeries and Tortilla Manufacturing;3119 Other Food Manufacturing.Beverage & tobacco product manufacturing:3121 Beverage Manufacturing;3123 Cannabis product manufacturing.Transportation and warehousing:481 Air transportation;482 Rail Transportation;483 Water transportation;484 Truck Transportation;4931 Warehousing and Storage.Ineligible Applicants:Operations that grow, process, or handle health or nutrition supplements;Health and/or nutrition supplement processing/handling operations;Operations producing pet food or food not intended for human consumption;Businesses only involved in primary production;Retail operations;Restaurants or other food service operations;Aquaculture and seafood production businesses;Unlicensed, unregistered, and/or uninspected facilities; andAny other business deemed ineligible by the Ministry.Eligible Activities:Gap-assessment or pre-audits, including:Costs for a gap-assessment or pre-audit by third party accredited auditors to identify;Opportunities for food safety improvements (including traceability);Development of a Food Safety work plan outlining the actions needed to implement a HACCP-based food safety program, including traceability planning.Food safety improvement activities, including:Developing traceability plans and implementing written food safety programs;Purchasing equipment that is directly and strongly related to food safety;Making facility upgrades for regulatory compliance;Conducting laboratory testing specifically required to reduce food safety risk including validation and/or verification of Critical Control Points (CCP)/ Preventative Control Plans (PCP).Third-party audited HACCP Certifications.Applicants will have to achieve the HACCP certifications in order to be reimbursed;Unsuccessful audits will not be reimbursed.Ineligible Expenses:Activities that are peripheral or not directly connected to food safety, including, but not limited to:Dead-stock disposal and removal or other waste disposals;Activities that support food quality rather than food safety; andAny other business deemed ineligible by the ministry.Eligible Activities:Food Safety PRoject categoryActivitiespercent cost-sharemaximum funding amounts1.       Grant Criteria 
      This federal program offers a wage subsidy of 80% to a maximum of $32,000 to employers in the natural resources who hire youth aged 15-30 for full-time placements of at least 3 months. The position must produce an environmental benefit. This program allows businesses to increase staff talent variety, meet company demands, and grow their business while giving youth with limited experience a chance to work in their field of interest.Grant Value: 80% up to $25,000 for regular participants80% up to $32,000 for youth facing barriers to employment (see Eligible Participant section)Turnaround time: 5 business daysEligible Employers:Companies and non-profits within the natural resources sector;Natural resource sectors include but are not limited to:Energy sector;Forestry sector;Mining, minerals and metal sector;Earth sciences and support sector;Clean technology; andClimate change adaptation.Be willing to add the participant to the employer’s payroll which includes Federal/Provincial tax deductions (CPP, EI, etc.);Offering a position job related to the green economy, classified as:  A position that requires environmental skills, knowledge, and experience to produce products or services with an environmental benefit;E.g. Architects and land-use planners who incorporate sustainability into designs, air quality engineers and conservation officers;A position that produces an environmental benefit but may not require specialized environmental skills;E.g. construction or trades workers that apply knowledge of standard construction techniques while completing green projects, manufacturing production workers, and companies that produce environmental goods.Eligible Participants:                   Between 15-30 years of age at the start of the placement;Not currently in school;Be a recent graduate;Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents or persons with refugee protection (work permits are not permitted);Legally entitled to work in Canada and in province relevant to the position;Participants on EI must provide proof of cancellation when they start the placement; Must not be a friend or family member of the employer; andMust be new to the organization (not current or previous employee);Youth facing barriers to employment:Indigenous youth, youth with disabilities, youth taking placements in the North (Yukon, Northwest Territories, and Nunavut), rural communities, and remote communities; andEmployers cannot hire a candidate before getting approval.Internship Details:Must be a full-time (min. 30 hours per week) position;Must be at least 3 months in duration (priority to those 6+ months) to a maximum of 12 months;Must be related to a natural resource sector in any of the sub-sectors listed here;Does not need to be a STEM-related role but employer must explain how the role supports the natural resource sector;Salary must be above minimum wage;The work experience must:Be related to the interests and pursuits of youth, andOffer skills development and training, and opportunities for advancement.The employer must provide on-the-job mentorship and support;Placements must start by Dec 31, 2021, and end by March 31, 2022, during which period they are eligible for funding;Positions can and are encouraged to continue after the program placement.For 6-month long placements, interns must start by September 30, 2021;Monthly financial claims and a post-intervention survey must be submitted to the program; andEmployers can apply for multiple placements;The employer must develop a Formal Learning Plan by the first week of placement.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This placement funding cannot be combined with any federal grants but can be combined with provincial grants;Employers must not hire before receiving approval—the contract must be signed before the participant starts (no retroactive funding, candidate must start work only after approval);Upon signing the contract following a successful application, employers will be asked for a Learning Plan: Must clearly demonstrate what types of knowledge, competencies, or skills that the participant will acquire over the course of their employment, and how these skills will support future employment in the sector or mobility to other sectors/regions;Employers currently seeking participants may post jobs on PetriDish™, the BioTalent job board; Consecutive placements with the same employer-intern match are not eligible; andFunding is disbursed monthly after each financial claim is submitted.Forms:Program website: click hereProgram details & application package: download here

for data collection, benchmarking, monitoring and analysis servicespurchase of instrumentation software and metering equipmentfees associated with training on the EMISsalariesprofessional, scientific, technical and contracting servicesdata collection, benchmarking, monitoring and analysis servicestrainingtechnical audits, assessments and evaluationsIneligible Activities:Fees for tasks started before NRCan’s approval and execution of a Contribution AgreementISO 50001 Energy Energy Management Systems Standard projectsEMIS projectsPI and CFD studiesenergy retrofitspurchase and installation of equipment and systems outside of instrumentation software and metering equipmentcapital projectsISO 50001 re-certification or fees associated with re-certificationenergy retrofitspurchase and installation of equipment and systems outside of instrumentation software and metering equipment for EMIScapital projectsequipment purchasescapital projects

      Grant Criteria 
      This offers Employment Counselling, Job Entry Skills, Certificate Training, Paid Work Experience, Mentoring and Post Job Placement Support to eligible workers aged 55 and older. Employers that hire and train eligible workers 55+ and provide full-time sustainable employment are eligible for a negotiated wage subsidy incentive up to $2,800 plus an additional $1,000 training subsidy.Grant Value: Up to $2800 wage subsidy + $1000 for an optional training subsidyTurnaround time: 5 business daysEligible Employers:BC employers in all industries;Have been in operation for at least one year;Have a WorkSafe BC account; andMust ensure new hires are on payroll.Eligible Participants: Aged 55 or older;Unemployed or precariously employed (ie. irregular hours, unreliable wages or below living wages);Canadian Citizens, Permanent Residents or Protected Persons;Resident of BC and legally entitled to work in Canada;Part-time students are eligible.Ineligible Participants:Full-time students or returning to school full-time after placement is completed;Previous employee of applicant company; andParticipating in other provincially or federally funded labour market program.Placement Details:Must be a long term position with support for initial 3 months;Minimum hours: 30/week;Employers must conduct their own recruiting and hiring;Participants must be identified prior to application submission;There are no caps on maximum placements per company at this point in time;Candidate(s) cannot be hired prior to approval from the program;On-the-job training is mandatory;Program will call candidate and employer on a monthly basis to ensure the position’s responsibilities match those in the application;Upon completion of the 3-month work experience, the $2,800 wage subsidy is reimbursed via cheque; andPaystubs will be required for reimbursement.Note: Placements that end prematurely before the completion of the 3 month duration are ineligible for funding. No partial payments will be made.Training Subsidy:Training is optional;Must be recognized third party training provider;Recognized online courses (e.g. Udemy) are eligible;Multiple courses are allowed; andTuition over $1000 must be covered by the employer.Note: Training subsidy may not be used to cover mentor/supervisor hours spent on on-the-job training.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best PracticesThis program can be combined with the Federal Government COVID and other Provincial wage subsidies as long as the Funding does not exceed 100% of the participant's salary;Applicants must ensure they have a plan in place to strive to keep the applicant on for the long term;The program may consider placements with less than 30 hours on a case-by-case basis if negotiated with program directly upfront;If the placements are less than 30hours/week, the subsidy would be reduced and prorated.It is suggested that you contact the Program Coordinator and discuss the placement during the application process.Forms: Program website: click hereEmployer application: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The objectives of the DS4Y program are to assist young people in gaining the skills and experience needed to successfully transition into and remain in the labour force; and to encourage not-for-profit organizations, as well as businesses with up to 100 employees across Canada to develop and apply Information and Communications Technology (ICT) related skills, knowledge and opportunities.  Grant Value: 50% of wages up to $8,450Turnaround Time: 2 weeksEligible Employers: Not-for-profit OR for-profit businesses with up to 100 employees across Canada;Media production companies or companies with media production in-house;Must be members of the CMPA in good standing - can join prior to application;Demonstrated commitment to the film, television and digital media production industry;Have the appropriate administrative support and capacity to train and mentor the participants to enhance and maximize the participants' experience; andSupport the participants in the development and implementation of work activities to provide participants with a meaningful internship described in the key performance.Eligible Participants:  Ages 15-30 inclusive;Must have recently (within two years prior to the start of their internship) completed post-secondary studies;Cannot be enrolled in a full-time educational program; andMust be Canadian Citizen, Permanent Resident, or persons who has been granted refugee status. Internship details: Companies are required to externally advertise Digital Skills For Youth positions prior to submitting an application to the CMPA;Digital media production/soft skills (creation of websites/digital campaigns, etc);Internship placement of 26 weeks of full-time work (40 hours per week);Intern must be on payroll; andMust be members in good standing of CMPA.Process: Please consult website and guidelines for full instructionsEmployer & candidate must be active CMPA members to be eligible;Candidate is a new hire who meets eligibility;Ensure you submit all pre-and post-hiring documents required before starting the candidate, including PIF’s to prevent ineligibility;Maintain payroll information etc. & observe course progress;Program Coordinator may have random/infrequent checks in person; andGather reimbursement documents IE invoices, receipts, paystubs, progress reports.Best Practices: The program is referred to as a mentorship, not an internship, as the purpose is to mentor and provide skills to the Participant;Both parties must be current members of the CMPA and apply together with one application package;Roles could be digital media content relevant but employers do not need to be in media production;Reimbursement occurs monthly and upon proof of final report and with paystubs;Documents required include: resume, letter of intent, two (2) letters of reference (download template from CMPA, and  Completed Youth Employment Strategy Participating Information Form (download from CMPA).

      Grant Criteria 
      DS4Y as delivered by the University of Calgary provides employers with the ability to hire interns that have the desire to increase their digital skills through work experience and also further education online. It is intended to provide Canadian youth (aged 15-30) with work experience and ICT skills to make them more productive and competitive in the knowledge economy and to encourage not-for-profit groups and businesses with up to 500 employees across Canada to develop and use ICT in their organizations.Grant Value:50% wage subsidy up to $10,500Turnaround time: 1-5 business daysEligible Applicants:Must have a physical space;Non-profit OR for-profit organizers with up to 500 employees.;Employers must have the appropriate administrative support and capacity to train and mentor the participants to enhance and maximize the participants' experience; Must  support the participants in the development and implementation of work activities to provide participants with a meaningful internship described in the key performance indicators.Eligible Participant:15-30 years old;Recent Post-secondary graduates (Min. 2 year diploma or 4 year degree); andMust be Canadian Citizen, Permanent Resident or person who has been granted refugee status. Internship details: Internship is capped at 35 hours per week (900 hours).;All internships are to be completed one month prior to the project end date of March 31, 2020;Position relating to digital / technical skills; andParticipant needs to be on payroll.Process: Please consult website and guidelines for full instructionsCandidate is a new hire who meets eligibility;University can assist you find a candidate if you require;Maintain payroll information etc. & observe course progress;Ensure you submit all post-hiring documents required before starting the candidate, including PIF’s;Program Coordinator may have random/infrequent checks in person;Ensure you submit all pre-and post-hiring documents required before starting the candidate, including PIF’s to prevent ineligibility; andGather reimbursement documents IE invoices, receipts, paystubs, progress reports.Best Practices:Funding ends March 31 2020, so ensure hiring makes adequate planning to take this short time frame into account;There is no limit to the number of new hires as long as the capacity to host/train them is available; Participants must take courses online during the placement, which are free and offered by University of Calgary. Course can be completed online and must be relevant to digital skills and completed in hours outside of placement;  In light of the short time frame, the required training course component will be significantly shorter, with a one-day course provided by the University of Calgary;training courses will be available in the following areas, but not limited to:Soft Skills: Communications;Entrepreneurship;Strategic thinking;Technical skills:Coding - Computer Programming;Web Development - Front End Web Development; Digital Media workshops - Integrated Digital Media;Marketing.

      Grant Criteria 
      Digital Skills for Youth provides employers with a $30,000 wage subsidy to hire a digital intern and offer digital skills training. It is intended to provide Canadian youth (aged 15-30 years old) with work experience and technological skills to make them more productive and competitive in the economy.Grant Value: 100% of wages subsidy for a maximum value of $30,000 (which may include a $4,000 bursary). Turnaround Time: up to 21 business daysEligible Employers:Non-profit or small business of up to 500 employees; Must pay for vacation pay, EI, CPP and WCP); Must post the job description on public job sites; andEmployers apply with or without a candidate.Note:  The employer will need to provide $1,000 worth of training for the participant at a third-party training provider.  Pre-approval is required prior to enrolling in course of study. This $1,000 contribution is matched up to $4,000 from the program and is geared towards digital and/or technical skills.   The $4000 contribution is part of the maximum $30,000 available. Eligible Participants:Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected persons;Age 15-30 (inclusive) at the start of the internship;Post-secondary graduates; andSelf-assessed as underemployed.Individuals who are employed below their level of education, outside their field of study or, hold part-time employment.Note: Family members of VCN or employer are ineligible. Internship Details:The position must be focused on ICT and other marketable skills including:Social Media and/or Analyst (New)Cloud applications and platforms;Programming;Web Design;Service-based Architecture;Chatbots and AI;Analysis;Data Design;Project Management (creation of software, SaaS, or Apps and not general project management);Note: Tasks cannot be clerical/unrelated activities (legal/accounting/manual labour etc)Minimum payment of $18 per hour and mandatory employment-related costs (CPP, EI, Worker's Compensation and vacation pay;Mandatory employment-related costs will need to include 2 days off work worth $1,000;Minimum 30 hours per week;Minimum placement of 6 months with an end date no later than March 31, 2023; The employer will need to guide and encourage the intern to select training during the work term that adds to their overall development and skills-set and long term growth;Participants must be on payroll; andReimbursement occurs upon proof of paystubs monthly.*Training-related activities eligible for the bursary (eg. workshops) are ineligible.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:The hiring process should start within 5 days of approval of the position, if the candidate has not yet been identified at the point of application - approved positions cannot be held for longer than 2 weeks;The process for approval is quite involved for both employer and intern. There may be follow-up requirements to ensure the program fit prior to approval. Job descriptions should be posted and visible to the public in order to be transparent and inclusive in the hiring process;Applicants on EI are able to apply as long as they remove themselves from EI at the start of the placement;The potential to keep interns after the end of the internship increases the priority for funding;Exposing intern(s) to work that enhances marketable skills is encouraged, especially with deliverable results that can be added to a portfolio or resume; andIf you have trouble finding candidates, you can check out our partners at Hatchways who have a pool of candidates of developers & designers and can assist with the hiring process here.Forms:Program guidelines: click hereApplication form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Ignite program provides up to $300,000 in funding to advance research and commercialization activities for collaborative, industry-driven, projects that will have significant benefits in the natural resources and applied sciences in BC. The program is focused on commercialization to support a clearly articulated solution to an existing industry problem, is beyond proof of concept but pre-commercial, and demonstrates the capacity to move the proposed innovation to market within 3 years.Grant Value: 33% of eligible expenses up to  $300,000NOTE: Only project activities beginning after application approval are eligible for funding. Turnaround Time: The final funding decision will be made in December 2024Eligible Applicants:Applicants must be a BC-based partnership made up of 2 or moreorganizationsAt a minimum, the partnership must contain 1 BC-based academic member (institution researcher) and 1 industry partner (company/non-profit, etc.).Have an innovation that is at a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 3 or higher;The partnership must have the right academic, business planning, financial, and technological expertise to successfully bring their innovations from the research and development phase to market;The partnership may be formal or informal, but there must be a clearly defined collaboration between partners; andHave a project that has strong market potential.Have at least 1 letter of support to demonstrate potential market impact and/or benefit to B.C.Company Partner Eligibility:Be an established company, start-up, or industry association;Must have a credible plan for exploiting research results for business and for the benefit of BC;Has the expertise and resources to accelerate the commercialization of the innovation;Preference is given to partners that are either end users or capable of market validation.May be from outside BC if:The majority of the team is from BC;An eligible BC organization maintains a leading role throughout the project; andProject results will be exploited in BC.Note: A researcher's own consulting company or sole proprietorship is not eligible as an industrial partner to collaborate on a project in which the researcher is the primary applicant or a co-applicant.Institution Researcher Partner Eligibility:Must hold or have a firm offer of a permanent academic appointment at an eligible BC institution at the time of application;Appointment can be a full-time faculty position or a lifetime professor emeritus, adjunct faculty, or other permanent part-time position.The researcher cannot have been barred from applying to NSERC, SSHRC, CIHR, MSFHR, or any other research funding organization; andProjects require active involvement from the researcher.Eligible Activities:Activities that demonstrate a strong need for relevance to the BC market; Research and development in natural resources, applied sciences, or engineering;Salaries/stipends for research and development technical personnel;Materials, supplies, and equipment directly related to the scientific or technical research and development work necessary for advancing the innovation towards commercialization(e.g., prototyping, scale-up, product refinement, validation studies, etc.);Necessary activities specifically related to technology transfer and commercialization (e.g., sharing of patenting and licensing fees with the university, consulting fees for IP strategy, etc.);Travel and accommodation for collaborative purposes; andUp to 10% of the Ignite funding request for indirect administrative costs (e.g., university overhead).  Ineligible Activities: Salary costs for the primary academic partner are not eligible for funding;Any project or activities that:Involve a researcher's own consulting company;Do not engage in research in natural resources, applied sciences or engineering;Do not relate to the research, commercialization of the research, and the problem outlined in the relevant industries;Are not at arm’s length from the owner and researcher;Represents a conflict of interest in the relationship between the partners; andResult in the research partner interfering with the company partner’s business operations.Documentation Required:Letter of Intent Form and the following documents:Clear and focused research objectives and achievable milestones;Outline of roles and demonstrated alignment of goals across partners;Market Analysis / Customer Needs;Commercialization Potential Outline;Research and Development Plan/ Business Model; andBudget/List of Investment secured.A clearly defined partnership between the institution researcher and industry partners in advance of applying;Any IP agreements in relation to the project; andThird-party match funding agreements if available.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Projects that have already begun can still apply but funding cannot be used retroactively;Partners are responsible for ensuring IP arrangements are in order and agreed to by all members in advance of applying;Projects must secure matching funds from industry or government sources at a ratio of 2:1 matching dollars to Ignite dollars;The Letter of Intent Form will require the applicant's top 3 areas of research; andAny claim for funding must go through the research institution.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program offers wage subsidies to employers in the electricity sector who hire students for work-integrated learning experiences. Employers can receive up to $7000 to offset the cost of hiring a co-op student. The goal of the program is to create opportunities in the electricity and renewable energy industry, and to prepare students for the workforce.Grant Value:50% of the student’s salary to a maximum of $5,000;70% of the student’s salary to a maximum of $7,000 for students in the following underrepresented groups:Women in STEM;Indigenous students;Visible minorities;Students with disabilities;Newcomers to Canada; andFirst year students.Turnaround Time: 5 business daysEligible Employer:Canadian-owned companies or subsidiaries;Companies primarily involved in the generation, transmission and distribution of electricity;Firms manufacturing equipment and providing services necessary to the generation of green energy;Firms that provide sector support in R & D, business development, or energy efficiency; Must have a nepotism policy in place; and Employers can apply without a candidate. Eligible Candidates:Be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person with refugee protection in CanadaThose on work or student visas are ineligible;Must be enrolled in a science, technology, engineering, mathematics, arts, or business program;Must be legally able to work in Canada according to the laws and regulations of the province or territory;Studying part-time or full-time at an accredited Canadian post-secondary institution;Must provide proof of co-op placement employment;Cannot have received Digital WIL funding with the same employer previously; andNot receiving Employment Insurance (EI) benefits.Ineligible Candidates:Students registered in trade or apprenticeship programs;Students in Canada on work visas or student visas; andReturning students who have been funded by the program previously.The same student will not be eligible for multiple rounds of funding for the same type of employment with the same employer.Program Details: Placements can be part-time or full-time;Maximum 30 hours per week;Maximum duration: 1 year;The program operates on a rolling intake basis;It does not offer funding based on the semester system like the other SWPPs.Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Participants must be on payroll;The placement must be with an employer in the electricity sector or placement must fulfill electricity job function; A Learning Plan outlining the position must be developed by the intern and the employer before the placement starts; andOnce approved, reimbursements occur monthly.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides funding to help social purpose organizations offering a direct benefit to communities on their pursuit to becoming investment-ready and thrive.Grant value: varies depending on project scope and vary from $10,000 to $75,000.Explore stream ($10,000 to $25,000)Stabilize and Build stream ($30,000 to $75,000)Application Timing:Applications open: September 29th, 2022Application deadline: November 22nd, 2022 at 5:00 PM ETTurnaround Time: Decisions communicated in February 2023.Eligible Applicants: Organizations must be for a social purpose;Must be one of the following:Registered charities or other qualified donees such as Indigenous governments; Incorporated non-profit organizations;Charitable co-operatives;Other co-operatives;Private social enterprise businesses advancing a social, cultural, or environmental mission (for-profit social enterprise);Hybrid entities such as Community Contribution Companies;Have a charitable number or have a business registration number registered prior to September 2021;Have or plan to have a business model that permits the organization to generate revenue for expanding to achieve its social, environment, and/or cultural mission;Have, or plan to operate, a mechanism that generates revenue from the sales of goods or services; Demonstrate they have a plan, capacity, and expertise to carry out the proposed project for which they are applying; Must use the majority of profits to achieve positive social, cultural or environmental objectives and expand the impact of its mission; andSoftware or web design product.Ineligible ExpensesCore operating costs; andHiring new permanent staff members.Program DetailsExplore stream ($10,000 to $25,000)This stream is for social purpose organizations that are:At the early stages of exploring, developing and testing their social enterprise idea. This may include items such as accessing legal advice, market expertise, etc.Stabilize and Build stream ($30,000 to $75,000)This stream is for social purpose organizations that are already have a well-developed enterprising model and are farther along in their understanding and preparation for taking an investment.Your organization is ready to take on a big project to increase your organization’s impact and get one step closer to your social finance goals.

        December 24, 2025The Career Starter Program is at capacity and no longer accepting new applications for Winter 2026;A new funding announcement is expected in April 2026.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The program provides 60% of the youth’s salary to a maximum of $20,000 in wage subsidies. This will help the employer adopt a diverse and inclusive work culture while satisfying their need for skilled labor, and will also help the employee get into the labor market and increase their knowledge of the sector’s needs. The intent of the program is to facilitate the transition of youth facing barriers into the labour market.Grant Value: 60% of wages up to $20,000;Program may provide wrap around support of up to $2,500 for the following:Relocation costs;Transportation supports;Housing Assistance;  Accessibility accommodations; Additional training for job success; Counselling and mental health supports; Personal protective equipment;  Childcare; Legal supports;  Cultural competency training; Networking events; Mentoring; Virtual networking sessions for participants; and Onboarding tools for employers, including a diversity and inclusion HR policy template and ongoing monitoring to ensure program success. Turnaround Time: 10 business daysEligible Employers: Be in one of the following industries:Bio-health;Bio-energy;Bio-industrial; andAgri-biotech.Have the ability to train and provide meaningful career;Maintain an internal process for supervising and mentoring for the participant; Have the participants on payroll which includes Federal/Provincial tax deductions (CPP, EI, etc.); andEmployers must identify a candidate before applying but they must not have started working.Eligible Candidates:Be Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or persons who have been granted refugee status in Canada;Legally entitled to work in Canada according to the relevant provincial and Canadian legislation and regulation;Be aged 15-30;Be a new hire;Identifying as a youth facing barriers including the following but not limited to: Involuntary not in education, employment, training for at least 6 months;With disability;Indigenous;A recent immigrant and/or refugee;A visible minority;LGBTQ2+;Homeless or at risk of becoming homeless;Living in a low-income household;Residing in a rural or remote location;Living with family care responsibilities;Affected by substance use;Currently in, coming out of, or who have been involved in the justice system;In or aging out of care; andLiving with low levels of literacy and numeracy.Ineligible Candidates:Candidates that have started employment at the organization prior to application submission; andCandidates must not have an existing relationship with the employer (must be arm's length).Program Details: Minimum hours/week: 30 (full-time only);Minimum of 3 months placement duration;Have an internal supervisor for a project;The work environment  must be safe, respectful, inclusive, free of harassment, abuse, and discrimination, and is in compliance with all applicable laws;The job placement must meet one of the following requirements:The work experience offers skills development and training opportunities;The work experience is related to the interests and pursuits of youth;The work experience offers a salary that is above the minimum wage; and/orThe work experience offers opportunities for advancement.The program now also provides additional support such as:Internal job coaching;Relocation support, if required;Online training courses for essential skills and technical skills;Access to BioSkills Recognition Program upon completion of the Career Starter program.The Job Coach and the participant will develop a Formal Coaching Plan before the start of the placement; The Job Coach will provide quarterly reports tracking the progress of the participant; andReimbursement claims are made monthly along with progress reports.

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program offers wage subsidies to hire current post-secondary students part-time or full-time. Undergraduate students and graduate students are eligible to apply. Employers must be willing to provide a quality learning experience to a student and have the financial capacity to pay the student for the duration of the placement in full. Students from under-represented groups are eligible for a 70% subsidy up to a maximum of $7000, while others will be eligible for 50% subsidy up to a maximum of $5000. Grant Value:50% of wages up to a maximum of $5000; or 70% of wages up to a maximum of $7000 for students from any of the following under-represented groups:Women in STEM;Indigenous persons;Newcomers to Canada;Persons with disabilities;Visible minorities; andFirst-year students.Turnaround time: 20-25 business daysEligible Employer:Registered for-profit businesses;Not-for-profit organizations;Must have the capacity (financially and otherwise) to hire and supervise a student.Ineligible Employer:Post-secondary institutions, hospitals, and long-term care facilities;Non-secular institutions; Federal, provincial, territorial and municipal governments; andFinancial institutions: click here to see the list of ineligible financial sector employers.Eligible Candidates:Must be a current student enrolled (full-time or part-time) in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Graduate students (ie. Master's and  Doctoral students) are also eligible.Undertaking the work opportunity as a work-integrated learning experience in connection with a course, degree, certificate, or diploma;Mentorships, co-ops, internships, practicums, and applied research projects are all considered eligible work-integrated learning experiences;The WIL component may be optional or required by the student's program. It may be for credit or not for credit;Magnet will send a letter template to pre-approved applicants. The student can use the template to request the required letter from a representative of their post-secondary institution, such as the Office of the Registrar, Career and Co-op Office, or Dean's office;For non co-op placements the letter must be signed by the Associate Dean of the relevant faculty or Program Director if applicable.Must be Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents, or persons with refugee protection legally entitled to work in their placement province; andInternational students are not eligible for the subsidy. Note: Only when the placement is considered "articling" would this be deemed ineligible (ie. student working towards their CPA, OBA, realtor license, etc)Program Details: Full-time or part-time positions;No maximum or minimum duration;Any industry and focus are accepted;Wage subsidy will apply to gross wages between;Winter Semester 2025 (January 1 - March 31, 2024) - CLOSED.Summer Semester 2025 (May 1 to August 31, 2025) - CLOSEDFall Semester 2025 (September 1 - December 31, 2025) - Opening August 1, 2025.Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Back-to-back placements are eligible only if the participant has 2 separate co-op requirements from their post-secondary institution;The employer must provide on-the-job supervision; The employer must ensure student hires are placed on payroll and are not contractors;Work-integrated learning must be in the participant's study plan and span over the duration of the placement;Employers will have the flexibility to postpone placement start dates to avoid rescinding placements; Employers will be able to apply for funding before they finalize their selection of students to hire; andThe program provides 1 reimbursement payment at the end of the placement.Note: Placements can begin earlier and end later than the funded semester, however only the placement between the semester start dates and end dates are eligible for funding.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: This grant cannot be combined with other federal wage subsidies. However, it can be combined with provincial tax credits, and with provincial, municipal, and/or territorial sources of funding, so long as total funding received does not exceed 100% of the gross wages paid to the student;If the student was funded by another federally funded program for a part of a semester, then the entire semester will be ineligible for the Magnet wage subsidy;The program will fund wages retroactively as far as as the start of the semester to which the subsidy applies;Process Best Practices:Applications are assessed on a first-come, first-served basis;Must provide students email address associated with their post-secondary institution as the program will send the student consent form directly to them, students must return the Student Consent Form from their student email;Proof of WIL eligibility letter must now be sent directly from the post secondary institution to the program to magnet@mail.outcomecampusconnect.ca with the application ID on the subject line; andIf you have trouble finding candidates relating to tech, you can check out our partners at Hatchways who have a pool of candidates and can assist with the hiring process here.Forms: Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This subsidy was introduced to help eligible Canadian businesses, charities, and non-profits offset up to 75% of salary on the first $58,700 (Maximum $847 per week per staff) up to July 4, 2020 (Details for CEWS Extension can be found here). It can be applied retroactively to March 15th, 2020.1  Eligible Employers:Must have experienced a reduction in revenues either by comparing revenues year over year (i.e. March 2019 revenues vs March 2020 revenues) OR March/April/May/June revenues compared to average revenues in January and February 2020, 15% reduction of their gross revenue in March; and/or 30% reduction of their gross revenue in April or May or June.AND taxable organizations paying salaries, wages, bonuses to employees on payroll (Note: contractors excluded) including:Canadian Private  Corporations;Non-profit organizations;Individuals; Partnerships consisting of eligible employers, non‑profit organizations and registered charities; andRegistered charities.Ineligible Employers:Public bodies (municipalities and local governments)Eligible Employees (How do you count # of employees):Full Time, Part Time, Casual Employees  where wages,  salaries, commissions, or taxable benefits are paid during qualifying periodsIneligible Employees:Staff who did not receive 14 consecutive days within claim period1Subsidy Detail: 100% refund for employer-paid contributions to EI and the Canada Pension Plan for the benefit period for staff on leave with pay;The subsidy is calculated on 4-week terms, for those who qualify for Period 1 (Mar 15 – Apr 11), they will also automatically qualify for Period 2 (Apr 12 to May 9), for employers qualifying for Period 2, they will automatically qualify for Period 3 (May 10 to Jun 6), for employers qualifying for Period 3, they will automatically qualify for Period 4 (Jun 7 to Jul 4);Applications can be made through the Canada Revenue Agency's My Business Account portal;Increased flexibility for revenue loss calculation may be adjusted for accrual (earned) or cash accounting (paid); andNon Profits/Charities: Flexibility on including/excluding government funding in revenues for revenue loss calculation purposes.Period 1(Mar 15 toApr 11)Period 2(Apr 12 toMay 9)Period 3(May 10 toJun 6)Period 4(Jun 7 toJul 4)Eligibility DeterminationRevenues Mar 2019 vs Mar 2020orJan/Feb 2020 Average Revenues vs. March 2020Revenues Apr 2019 vs Apr 2020orJan/Feb 2020 Average Revenues vs. Apr 2020Revenues May 2019 vs  May 2020orJan/Feb 2020 Average Revenues vs. May 2020Revenues June 2019 vs  June 2020orJan/Feb 2020 Average Revenues vs. June 2020Decrease in RevenuesMinimum 15%Minimum 30%Minimum 30%Minimum 30%Calculation Steps:Use the CRA calculator input obtain gross wages of eligible staff for the relevant claim period;Calculate and input the pre-COVID Average Weekly Baseline Income for eligible staff in Periods 1 to 4 (wages paid from Jan 1 to Mar 15 2020); Baseline Income calculation exclusive to Period 4 (wages paid from March 1, 2019 to May 31, 2019,  or March 1, 2019 to June 30, 2019) is permitted.The CRA Calculation will provide you with  Amount A which is the eligible claim amount based on gross payroll for the term.;If applicable, determine the EI benefit of any staff under the Work Sharing program, or Amount B; andCalculate the 10% wage subsidy amount, Amount C that your company qualifies for within the claim period, note that the periods overlap in odd ways so adjustments will need to be made to reflect relevant claim term, it may NOT simply be 10% of payroll of Amount A. See chart below.Remittance PeriodRelevant 10% TEWSCEWS Claim Period 1CEWS Claim Period 2CEWS Claim Period 3CEWS Claim Period  4March 2020Mar 18 to 31Mar 15 to 31April 2020Apr 1 to 30Apr 1 to 11Apr 12 to 30May 2020May 1 to 31May 1 to 9May 10 to 31June 2020Jun 1 to Jun 19Jun 1 to 6Jun 7 to 196. If you have any eligible staff who were receiving pay without actually working, your company would qualify for the employer portion of CPP and EI for the relevant weeks. Calculate this benefit based on the relevant claim period, or Amount D.Eligible Claim Amount Calculation: Amounts A - B - C + DBest Practices:You could apply for this funding on your own, but we do recommend you speak to an accountant about the calculations to ensure compliance prior to submitting the application;Business can apply through CRA  My Business Account, business representatives may apply on your behalf using "Represent a Client" account. If neither option is suitable, use the Web Forms application with your web access code;This program can be combined with certain provincial wage subsidies on a case by case basis;Those organizations that do not qualify for the Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy may continue to qualify for the previously announced wage subsidy of 10% of remuneration paid from March 18 to before June 20, up to a maximum subsidy of $1,375 per employee and $25,000 per employer;There is no overall limit on the subsidy amount that an eligible employer may claim;This wage subsidy can be used for workers who are also applying for the CERB program so long as their payroll is less than $1,000.       (Z-COVID) COVID - Work Sharing Program (EI)
    
  

  

  
    
      Grant Type
      Hiring, Market Expansion, Systems & Processes, Research & Development, Training
    
    
      Grant Amount
      $0
    
    
      Regions
      All of Canada
    
    
      Industries
      All Industries
    
    
      Program provided by
      
     

    
      Deadline
      
        

          Open until filled
      
    
    
  





    
      




  
      
        Recently Changed 
        Eligibility criteria have changed to include recovery-related roles such as sales, business development, and staff related to product/service output (i.e. web developer for a web development firm); these roles were previously ineligible.On March 18, 2020, the Prime Minister announced an extension of the maximum duration of the Work-Sharing program  76 weeks (previously 38 weeks) for employers affected by COVID-19.Staff in leadership (senior management) or sales roles may now qualify provided they have <40% of company shares.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      Work-Sharing is ideal for businesses that have experienced a decrease in business but do not want to layoff staff. It allows businesses to identify shared work hours among a team of staff to keep them employed at reduced hours while still qualifying for EI benefits.Turnaround time: 10 daysEligible Employers:Minimum 1-year business existence;Have the capacity and work to sustain employees; have experienced a decrease in business can share work between staff with a minimum of 10% work-sharing and a maximum of 60%.Eligible Employees:Must be eligible for EI;Must be current staff and normally employed by the companyMust opt-in to the program and agree to participate based on work-sharing termsNote: Staff in leadership (senior management) or sales roles may now qualify provided they have <40% of company shares.Ineligible Employees (May be flexible during COVID crisis):Temporary/seasonal workersCo-Op StudentsShareholders (>40%) Staff who don’t qualify for EIDetails:The maximum duration of the Work-Sharing program is 76 weeks for employers affected by COVID-19.Best Practices:Must provide equal sharing of work between each shared work unitEmployers must continue to pay participants benefits during work-sharing term.Completed application forms and questions should be directed to EDSC.WT.WS-TP.ESDC@servicecanada.gc.ca

      Best Practices & Forms
      Program website available here.Application guide available here.Application form available here.

      Grant Criteria 
      Companies seeking additional working capital can apply through the BDC for support to ensure that financially viable impacted companies have access to the credit and support they require during the coronavirus pandemic. Working capital loans of up to $2 million with flexible repayment terms for employers that need to access funds to boost inventory to meet demand, take advantage of suppliers discounts, or complement a line of credit.Interest rate floating at 3.3%Repayable over 3 yearsInterest only for first 12 monthsEligible Businesses:For Profit Companies in Canada;Minimum 2 years full in operations (financials for 2 years required);Good business and personal credit rating;Business is financially viable under normal circumstances (i.e. prior to COVID)Ineligible Businesses:Real estate (commercial/residential) deposits;Interest fees for other loans;See 'Declarations as to Eligibility' section via this link for more details.Best Practices:There is an application fee for this loan;Please know that a BDC representative will contact you to discuss your application;Please ensure all information on your application form are accurate;Prepare your financial statements (and any mini business plans if available);Ensure you have understood all terms, repayment dates and agreement must be agreed upon between yourself and the BDC.  Granted Consulting is unable to translate or interpret any loan terms and conditions, and it is suggested you seek legal or third party advice in the event you need help deciphering any of the agreement language.

      (Z-COVID) COVID - Farm Credit Canada (Loan) 
    
  

  

  
    
      Grant Type
      Hiring, Market Expansion, Systems & Processes, Research & Development, Training
    
    
      Grant Amount
      $750,000
    
    
      Regions
      All of Canada
    
    
      Industries
      Food Processing, Agriculture - Crop, Agriculture - Dairy, Agriculture - Livestock, Agriculture - Tree Fruit, Agriculture - Vineyard/Wine
    
    
      Program provided by
      Farm Credit Canada
     

    
      Deadline
      
        

          Open until filled
      
    
    
  





    
      




  
      
        Recently Changed 
        FCC has received an enhancement to its capital base that will allow for an additional $5 billion in lending capacity.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      Farm Credit Canada lends money to primary producers, food operations and agribusinesses that provide inputs or add value to agriculture.Turnaround time: Applicants will discuss their needs immediately with a program officer on the initial phone call, and their case can be approved after review within potentially two business days if all answers are completed and supporting documents are submitted accordingly.Application process: Applicants should call the number below or look up the best contact centre by region (see link below). They will then be asked to provide a summary net-worth, provide current income and go through a thorough review of operations with a relationship manager.  The loan will have a different process and a more thorough review if it is over $750,000. Both categories (under and over $750,000) have an application fee of $250. Eligible Companies:For those applying for under $750,000 and over $750,000 you should meet the following criteria:Be owner of a fully operational Canadian farm or Canadian based food processing plant; - Note: Food processing plants must  have a connection to Agriculture. Must be incorporated or a registered sole proprietor for one (1) year;Must have an income for 2 years;Be a Canadian Company;Have at least one Canadian citizen/Permanent resident shareholder;Have a stable income & good credit score.Best Practices:Ensure you have 2-3 years of corporate bank statements (2-3 years) and be prepared to answer operational questions if you are applying for over $750,000.Last income return.Notice of Assessment.Picture ID/ Passport available (photo email to program officer is OK during COVID)Statement of assets and liabilities.  Business Plan showing where the company is going, and financial projections (1 year min. but 3 is best). All loan terms, payment dates, and an agreement must be reviewed by yourself and the FCC. Please seek third party assistance or legal advice if you need help deciphering terms as Granted Consulting is unable to provide advice or guidance.Should generally plan to finance 20% of any purchases of new equipment (FCC will finance 80%)If you are applying for <$750,000, there may be leniency on income eligibility but you must be incorporated when you apply.If you are applying for >$750,000, additional documents may be required during the review process on a case-by-case basis.Note that you must permit your credit history to be checked in order to apply for this loan & be aware of any and all implications. All loan agreements, payment dates, interest rates etc. must be agreed in advance with the FCC as Granted Consulting is not a financial advisor.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Application Guide available hereMust call 1 306 780 8900 to apply or find regional office and call by phone here.

      (Z-COVID) COVID - EDC Business Credit Availability Program (Guarantee)
    
  

  

  
    
      Grant Type
      Hiring, Market Expansion, Systems & Processes, Research & Development, Training
    
    
      Grant Amount
      $6,250,000
    
    
      Regions
      All of Canada
    
    
      Industries
      All Industries
    
    
      Program provided by
      EDC
     

    
      Deadline
      
        

          Open until filled
      
    
    
  





    
      




  
      
        Recently Changed 
        Canadian exporters who can prove they will be exporting in the next 12 months may now be eligible. Also, if exporters are shipping components of end products, so long as they control over 50% of the finished product (i.e. including materials, labour, IP, etc.), such companies may also qualify.The funding available has increased from $10-billion to $65-billion under this program. Maximum loans have now also increased from $5M to $6.25M.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The EDC will guarantee 80% of new operating credit and cash flow term loans for financial institutions to extend to SMEs, up to $6.25 million. The program cap for this new loan program will be a total of $20 billion for export sector and domestic companies.Credit-worthy exporters whose activities fall within the mandate of either BDC and/or EDC are eligible to receive up to 80% finance guaranteed by the EDC.Application procedure: Businesses interested in accessing the BCAP should first contact their financial institution.Eligible Companies: Incorporated Canadian Companies; that are alsoExporters of Canadian goods and services OR control more than 50% of an exporters supply chain of activities (including materials, labour, IP, etc.); and In good credit; with A total loan need of under $6.25M.Businesses that were profitable pre-COVID, 12 months financials requiredCompanies with revenues < $1MM, loans of up to $312,500Companies with revenues <$1 MM to $50MM, loans up to $3.125 MMCompanies with $50 MM+, loans up to $6.25 MMEligible Expenses: Short term working capital;Liquidity during COVID-19;Coverage for losses incurred as a result of goods shipped.Best Practices:EDC or BDC work as sister crown corporations and are partnering on reviewing applications however no direct lending will occur from EDC it will always go through another financial institution.Ensure all loan terms, payment dates and any other key information is understood before signing an agreement as Granted Consulting is unable to provide any financial advice.Interest rates, terms, and conditions vary on a case by case basis. It is imperative speaking to your banker is your first step for any loan questions as Granted Consulting is unable to advice on any details.When preparing:Do not contact your financial institution or the BDC  without being prepared. It is imperative that in these times when the banks are so busy that each applicant has their documents in order, and has prepared themselves for the interview accordingly (review financial figures, goals, and know how much funding you need).Companies should prepare a mini business plan proving a plan for sustainability and description of how much revenue COVID has cost them in the short term.Cash flow: 2 years projections for the future should be prepared and ready to be emailed.Have your operational costs/corporate bank statements: 2-3 years ready to be emailed.When applying:Ensure you make it clear you are an "exporter" in your application form. If you are providing international services that you export, ensure your contracts are ready to evidence what you are doing. EG. Film/digital/other service contracts should be drafted and comprehensively showing the export relationships and partners. Ensure all information provided is as full, complete, and accurate as possible.The EDC may request for more information during the due diligence phase.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Information available here.Approach your financial institution bank to apply.

      (Z-COVID) COVID - Canada Emergency Response Benefit (CERB) - Individual
    
  

  

  
    
      Grant Type
      Hiring, Market Expansion, Systems & Processes, Research & Development, Training
    
    
      Grant Amount
      $12,000
    
    
      Regions
      All of Canada
    
    
      Industries
      All Industries
    
    
      Program provided by
      Government of Canada
     

    
      Deadline
      
        2020/12/02

          open until filled
      
    
    
  





    
      




  
      
        Recently Changed 
        'Earned income' is defined as gross income minus expenses (previously if unclear if expenses could be deducted).
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This  benefit will cover people who have lost their job, people who are sick or quarantined, and parents who must stay home without pay to care for children,  or have less than $1,000 in earned income per month. This program was designed to assist workers who do not qualify for EI benefits to have access to funding during the COVID crisis. Turnaround time: Funds are projected to be received approx. 10 days after the application has been submitted.Eligible Applicants:Must meet all of the criteria below: Be a Canadian resident (includes temporary foreign workers and foreign students if they meet the criteria below);Have earned less than $1,000 in employment and/or self-employment earned income for 14 or more consecutive days within the four-week benefit period of your claim;Have had $5,000 in employment income, self-employment income, or maternity or parental leave benefits for 2019 or in the 12-month period preceding the day the application is made;Those earning dividends are eligible;Did not leave their job voluntarily or request to be laid off;Are not receiving nor have you applied for the CERB from the Canada Revenue Agency nor are you receiving Employment Insurance benefits for the same benefit period;Expansion of program to include individuals who earn up to $1,000 a month of income (may include payroll or contract work);Inclusion of seasonal workers as those who qualify for this program; andIndividuals running out of EI benefits may apply and qualify for this benefit.Note: 'Earned income' is now calculated as gross income minus expensesBe one of the following: Employed workers who are not receiving income due to COVID work disruptions and/or lost their job;Self Employed and/or contractors;Caretaker of someone who is sick;Individuals in quarantine or self-isolation (involuntary); orWorkers caring for children at home due to school/daycare closures.Application:Applications must be submitted on the day of the week according to your birth month. See table below.Best Practices:CERB calculation of 'commissions income' is based on when earned, not when received;Applicants should ensure their "My Account" with CRA is live and they have registered for direct deposit (a mail cheque with payment will extend timing to receive benefit);Income and self-employed income refers to wages or salary;Contractors do qualify for this program if they meet all eligibility and income reporting criteria;CERB applications can cover periods of unemployment between March 15th, 2020 until October 3rd, 2020 and can be retroactive up until March 15th, 2020;If you’ve already applied for EI you do not need to reapply for the CERB. Your claim will be automatically moved over to the CERB, and benefits paid from this program first.;Workers who are applying for CERB benefits do not qualify for the wage subsidy program; andApplications need to be remitted every 4 weeks to confirm eligibility for next benefit term.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Application guidelines available here Application form available here FAQ available here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program allows employers to reduce payroll deductions required to the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). You can start reducing payroll remittances of federal, provincial, or territorial income tax in the first remittance period that includes remuneration paid from March 18, 2020 to June 19, 2020 up to a maximum subsidy of $1,375 per employee and $25,000 per employer.Employer Eligibility:Have an existing business number and payroll program account with the CRA on March 18, 2020;Pay salary, wages, bonuses, or other remuneration to an eligible employee;Can be one of the following: Individuals aka Sole Proprietorships (excluding trusts);Partnerships;Note: Partnerships are only eligible for the subsidy if their members consist exclusively of individuals (excluding trusts)Non-profit organizations;Registered charities;  andCanadian-controlled private corporations (including a cooperative corporation) eligible for the small business deduction.Employee Eligibility:An eligible employee is an individual who is employed in Canada; andFull-time, part-time, co-op students, casual employees, and other employees where wages, salaries and bonuses are reported to CRA (contractors ineligible).Documents Required:Total remuneration paid from March 18, 2020 to June 19, 2020;Federal, provincial, or territorial income tax amounts deducted from that remuneration; andNumber of eligible employees paid in that period.Note: The subsidy is manually calculated based on your payroll remittances each month. Calculate 10% of total payroll and reduce remittances each month.  See calculation examples below:Example:You have 10 employees earning total salaries $30,000;Maximum wage subsidy is 10% = $3,000;Total income tax based on these salaries equals $5,000;Total CPP/EI amounts = $4,000; andTotal Remittance before subsidy of 10% ($3000) is $9,000 ($5,000 in taxes + $4,000 in CPP/EI remittance).Total claim amount for all employees is $3,000, which can be reduced from the $5,000 income tax remittance for the month. With CPP/EI amounts, the total remittance to CRA is $6,000 ($2,000 in taxes + $4,000 in CPP/EI remittance).Note: Granted Consulting is not a tax/payroll advisor and should you have any queries pertaining to this government initiative contact your accountant or the Liaison Officer Service.

Ensure you submit this form (available here) ASAP  - do not wait until annual filing. March is a partial month calculation, remember to adjust remittance for eligible dates only;While the two wage subsidies cannot be used in conjunction, any 10% wage subsidy amount claimed will reduce the 75% Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy amount for the same claim period;Those organizations that do not qualify for the 75% Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy may continue to qualify for this 10% wage subsidy;If you receive this subsidy, it is taxable, and you have to report the total amount as income in the year in which the subsidy is received;If the income taxes you deduct are not sufficient to offset the value of the subsidy in a specific period, you can reduce future payroll remittances of income tax amounts to benefit from the subsidy. This includes reducing remittances that may fall outside of the application period for the wage subsidy (after June 19, 2020); andNote: You cannot reduce your remittance of CPP contributions or EI premiums. You must continue remitting the CPP contributions and EI premiums that you deducted from your employees, as well as your share of CPP contributions and EI premiums, to the CRA.Forms: More information available hereApplication procedure per above.
