        Recently Changed 
        To qualify, you must opt-in by October 30, 2020 here (FINAL DEADLINE, no more extensions expected);New applicants can apply for up to 5 months of rent assistance (from April through August) all at once; andIn the event of default, you (the property owner), will be obligated to repay the loan in full.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      Eligible commercial property owners can receive government support in the form of a forgivable loan for their property if they agree to reduce the gross rent of eligible small business tenants by 75% for April to September 2020.  The CECRA benefit will cover 50% of gross rent and at least 25% will be absorbed by the property owner. The outcome is 75% (25% + 50%) reduction of rent benefit for the tenant. Calculation of support is based on Gross Rent and includes 'Triple Net' or 'NNN' expenses including real estate taxes, building insurance, and maintenance.Note: Applicants (eligible landlords) must agree to reduce small business tenant's rent by at least 75% for the months of  April to September 2020.  The loans of 50% from the government will be forgiven if the property owner complies with applicable program terms and conditions.Interest-Free loan will be forgiven on December 31, 2020 assuming that terms and conditions of the loan are fulfilled.In the event of default, you (the property owner), will be obligated to repay the loan in full.Eligible Applicant (Landlord):Property owners of a commercial property where small business tenant are impacted by COVID (+70% drop in revenues or closed temporarily) - Tenants CANNOT apply for this funding directly;Eligible landlords must agree to include a moratorium on eviction for the period of  April to September 2020.;Rental income declared on tax return (personal or corporate) for tax years of 2018 and/or 2019;Landlord agrees to not recover rent abatement amounts after the program ends;Properties owned by eligible small business may qualify if they have a valid and enforceable lease agreement and the rent under the lease is at market rates;Properties with or without a mortgage both qualify;Properties owned by eligible small business may qualify if they have a valid and enforceable lease agreement and the rent under the lease is at market rates;Property owners of newly constructed or recently purchased properties may also qualify for the CECRA for small businesses, as well as property owners with short term, month-to-month leases, provided the other program requirements are met and there was a legally binding lease with an eligible tenant in place on or before April 1, 2020; andCommercial properties with a residential component and multi-unit residential mixed-use properties would equally be eligible with respect to their small business tenants.Note: Property owners must use funds from CECRA to refund amounts in excess of 25% paid by the eligible tenant for the period, or if the tenant prefers, be apply excess rent paid to a future rent payment (applied within 3 months timeframe).Ineligible Landlords:Properties own by the federal, provincial, or municipal governments;There are exceptions to this that include long term commercial leases with third parties operating the property such as:Airports;Post-Secondary Institutions;Hospitals;A Pension Fund;First Nation and any indigenous organizations/governments; andCrown Corporations with limited appropriations (determined eligible for CECRA by CMHC).Eligible Small Businesses (Tenant): Businesses, non-profit and charitable organizations;April to June 2020 rent assistance: Businesses (tenants) of commercial space who experienced a 70% drop or more in revenues or ceased operations as a result of COVID;July to September 2020 rent assistance: Businesses (tenants) who qualified for April to June 2020's rent assistance despite drop in revenues for term;Must be paying less than $50,000 per month to qualify1;Generate no more than $20 million in gross annual revenues on a consolidated basis (i.e. if a company owns 4 eligible businesses, revenue calculation is based on gross annual revenues at the ultimate parent level);Must have opened before March 1, 2020, and lease signed before April 1, 2020;Eligible to both Small Businesses that are tenants and subtenants. This includes impacted Canadian small businesses that occupy co-working spaces; andCommercial properties with a residential component and multi-unit residential mixed-use properties would equally be eligible with respect to their small business tenants.1 Gross annual revenues is calculated with whatever 12-month term a tenant uses to calculate 2019's financial revenues.Ineligible Small Businesses (Tenant): Those that opened on, or after, March 1, 2020 or signed leases before April 1, 2020Benefits to Eligible Tenant:Of the 75% rent reduction, 50% will be provided by government support, and 25% will be absorbed by the property owner;Rent during the period of  April to September 2020; andProtection of eviction under the terms of the program.Documentation Requirements:Tenant or Sub-tenant's Attestation (Sample);Property Owner's Attestation (Sample);Rent Reduction Agreement (Sample); andForgivable Loan Agreement (Sample).Note:  Applicants should prepare documents and register as per the day of the week below: Calculating Revenues:There are 2 scenarios by which to calculate your 70% reduction in revenues:If your small business was operating during April – July 2019, then compare your gross revenues from April, May, and June  2020 to your revenues of April, May, June 2019 (only tenants who qualified for April to June subsidy would qualify for the July extension); orIf your small business was not operating during April – July 2019, then compare your average gross revenues from April, May, and June of 2020 to your average gross revenues for January and February 2020 (only tenants who qualified for April to June subsidy would qualify for the July extension).Best Practices:The application process is staggered by day, check your eligibility on this page under 'How Do I Apply for the CECRA for Small Businesses Program?;Applicants must have requested July and August before opting-in for September extension;MCAP is working with First Canadian Title (FCT) to help deliver CECRA for small businesses. MCAP or FCT may contact the applicant throughout the application validation and funding processes;Some provinces (i.e. BC) ban commercial landlords who forgo federal rent relief from evicting tenants, check with provincial regulations relevant to your business;For specific questions pertaining to co-working spaces, please inquire directly with the program on; The application must be submitted by the property owner/landlord and therefore administrative work is required;Landlords apply to CECRA through the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC). CMHC will administer and deliver the CECRA. CMHC will advance funds to the mortgage lender on a case by case portfolio basis, every month, based on a report/claim provided by the mortgage lender;Franchise owners are considered the parent company for the purpose of income eligibility and thus their revenue is relevant (not the brand owner's);Applications can be submitted retroactively or in the future so long as proof can be provided to show compliance with program requirements - property owners must refund amounts paid by the small business for the period as agreed upon both parties and this refund could be applied for future rent;Good negotiation skills may be required as the landlord must agree to a 25% reduction of rent costs and the terms of this program in order for the tenant to receive the 75% rental reduction benefit;Calculation for drop-in revenues compares revenues from the same month in 2019 (i.e. April 2019 vs April 2020) OR average revenues from January and February 2020 with month in question;If applicant files for bankruptcy, restructure, reorganize, or dissolve their business, the loan must be paid back;In the event of default, CMHC has full recourse to recover the CECRA funding from you (the property owner);Gross annual revenues is calculated with whatever 12-month term a tenant uses to calculate 2019's financial revenues;Where there are long-term commercial leases with third parties to operate the property (for example, airports), the third party is eligible as the property owner;Application removes the need for landlord to provide financial details from tenant to prove drop in revenues;BC bans commercial landlords who forgo federal rent relief from evicting tenants; andProperty owners of newly constructed or recently purchased properties may also qualify for the CECRA for small businesses, as well as property owners with short term, month-to-month leases, provided the other program requirements are met and there was a legally binding lease with an eligible tenant in place on or before April 1, 2020.

The program's intent is to increase the job readiness of post-secondary students in Canada.Grant Value:50% of wages up to $5000 per participant (regularly represented groups).70% of wages up to $7,000 per participant in any of the following under-represented groups:Women in STEM;Indigenous students;Visible minorities;Recent immigrants (immigrated to Canada within the last 5 years);Persons with disabilities;First-year students;Students on their first work term. Turnaround Time: 10 business daysEligible Employers:Biotech or healthcare employers;Employers who do not meet the above criteria must have positions with biotech or healthcare focus.Have the capacity to hire and train a student in meaningful employment placement; Must have participants on payroll (includes, Federal/Provincial tax deductions such as CPP, EI, etc.); andEmployers must apply with a candidate. Eligible Candidates:Full-time or part-time post-secondary students (within the last three years) in STEM (science, technology, engineering or mathematics) and Business at a Canadian University (students from other majors/disciplines may qualify);Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents or refugees (work permits are not permitted); andLegally entitled to work in Canada and in the province relevant to the position.Note: Family members of the employer are not eligible.Program Details:Full- or part-time positions;Minimum hours: 10 per week;Placement duration: 4-16 weeks;Intakes available:Spring/Summer 2025 - April 1, 2025 to August 31, 2025: CLOSEDFall 2025 - August 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025: Closing September 10 2025;Winter 2025 - December 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026: Opening December 1, 2025Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Applications must be submitted at least 6 weeks in advance of the participants placement end date;Be with a bio-economy or healthcare employer and/or fulfilling a bio-economy or healthcare job function;Remote work is acceptable;Employers will have the flexibility to postpone placement start dates to avoid rescinding placements; andThe employer must develop a Formal Learning Plan with the participant, by the first week of placement.

      Eligible Best Practices:This program cannot be used in conjunction with other federally funded programs;The program does not allowed for retroactive placements.Process Best Practices:If the employer is applying for multiple students, or for the same student and multiple terms, the program will require a separate application for each student or term;Signatures must be digitally dated and time-stamped (using the Adobe signature feature) or handwritten. A typed signature in cursive font is not accepted; andIf the internship is longer than 16 weeks, please contact BioTalent as you could be eligible to apply for another funding term. Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click

      Grant Criteria 
      This program supports fish and seafood processors who have incurred COVID-19 related costs from March 15, 2020, to March 31, 2020. The non-repayable stream will cover 100% of eligible projects up to $100,000. Applications will close July 13, 2020, at 16:30 PDT or when funding is fully subscribed.Eligible Companies:Be located in British Columbia;Be a federally or provincially licensed fish processing facility or a registered processor of wild-capture or aquaculture products;Were a viable business before the COVID-19 pandemic and plan to continue to operate their business or resume operations; andCan demonstrate that their business currently meets health and safety requirements.ORBe a not-for-profit organization not engaged in fish and seafood processing, but whose activities support the fish and seafood processing industry in British Columbia.Note:  Eligible costs/activities can be retroactive up to and including March 15, 2020. All projects must be completed by March 31, 2021.Eligible Activities: Priority 1: Work health and safety activities related to COVID 19 including adjustments to current processes and manufacturing lines to accommodate physical distancing such as:Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) modifications or upgrades;Equipment such as safety barriers (plexiglass dividers) and handwashing stations;Non-disposable personal protective equipment (PPE) such as body temperature screening/fever detection systems, washing stations, workstation dividers, full and half facepiece respirators, impact goggles, face shields;N95 masks or similarly effective disposable surgical/medical face masks;Thermal scanners;Purchase and rental of portable buildings and installations/site modifications to meet worker health and safety requirements;Professional technical services (i.e. plant reorganization); andTraining for workers on additional health security measures.Eligible Costs:Capital assets (with the exception of land and buildings) specifically required for the completion of the project. Capital Assets are tangible assets that are purchased, constructed, developed or otherwise acquired;Contracted Services are professional or specialized services for which a contract is entered into;Salaries and benefits directly related to completing the activities of the project;Administration costs necessary to complete the project;Travel costs that are directly related to the project for essential services required for plant retrofits or adjustments; andOther direct costs for project-related deliverables.Ineligible Costs:Administration costs such as office supplies, materials, space, telecommunications, audiovisual, postage and freight;Costs associated with the Quarantine Act for isolation of Temporary Foreign Workers;Capital items not specifically required for the execution of the project;Costs for activities that are deemed to be part of normal business practice for any Recipient;Land and building acquisition;Refinancing of existing debt;Working capital;Hospitality (for example, alcohol, meals, entertainment, gifts, etc.);Travel not directly related to the project’s execution;Legal fees;The refundable portion of the Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST), value-added taxes, or other items for which a refund or rebate is received;Costs to prepare the Contribution Agreement or related schedules;Any portion of any cost that, in WD’s opinion, exceeds the fair market value for that cost item;Any cost, such as amortization that would not result in a direct, out-of-pocket expense for the recipient; andCosts being reimbursed under an existing federal, provincial or territorial program.Best Practices: This grant can be combined with other grants as long as total costs do not exceed 100%.For applicants hoping to obtain more than $1,000,000, they should apply to the repayable stream and may combine it with this application form. Documentation Required:A completed project budget (the application portal will prompt applicants to download a budget template);Audited or Review Engaged Financial Statements for the past two (2) years); and,A letter of support from your organization’s Health and Safety Committee (if one exists).IAF has the right to request more documentation.To be considered complete, an application form, project budget and supporting documents must be submitted to IAF before the application window closes.Applicants are encouraged to include only activities that they are confident will be completed on time and within budget. There is a cap of up to $100,000 per facility for the non-repayable stream but a cap of $1.1 million in total for a parent company. For example, a business with three facilities can receive $300,000 of nonrepayable financial assistance for priority 1 but will then be restricted to $800,000 of repayable financial assistance for priority 2. Applications will be assessed using the following criteria:Project alignment with CSSF program priorities and objectives;Applicant declaration that they are adhering to all applicable requirements of the Quarantine Act;The applicant’s attestation that they are a federally/provincially registered or licensed processor;Operational viability before COVID-19 and intent to continue operations in British Columbia for the foreseeable future;For repayable contributions, the applicant should demonstrate that it is in good standing with Western Economic Diversification Canada, the Investment Agriculture Foundation of BC and other outstanding financial obligations;The support should be in addition to other measures put in place by federal, provincial and municipal partners or other financial institutions specific to the fish and seafood industry. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      More info available here. BC specific info available here. Application form available here.

An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation.       Regions
      Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, Saskatchewan
    
    
      Industries
      All Industries
    
    
      Program provided by
      Government of Canada - Western Economic Diversification Canada (WD)
     

    
      Deadline
      
        

          Open until filled
      
    
    
  





    
      




  

      Grant Criteria 
      Eligible companies are western Canadian SMEs that do NOT qualify for the Canadian Emergency Business Account (CEBA) program or the RRRF – Community Futures Scheme.  Companies may receive a conditionally repayable loan up to $40,000 or a 100% repayable loan of up to $1,000,000. For those companies applying for up to $40,000, if they meet all required payment schedules, they are be eligible for a loan forgiveness of 25 percent of the contribution (up to $10,000). The RRRF supports businesses under two streams:The $40,000 partially repayable contributions. Those businesses that repay 75 percent of the contribution (up to $30,000) on or before December 31, 2022 will result in forgiveness of 25 percent of the contribution (up to $10,000); andThe $1,000,000 in repayable contributions to businesses that can demonstrate a meaningful contribution to the western Canadian economy, and are experiencing liquidity issues. These companies may not have accessed other Government of Canada relief programs, or may have accessed them, but require additional funding to mitigate cash flow pressures. This contribution is fully repayable.Turnaround time: approx. 10 business days if you are requesting up to $40,000. Timing would be longer for requests for $40,000 or more.Eligible Businesses:Have fewer than 500 full-time employees (FTEs);Are located in Western Canada (defined as British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan or Manitoba);Are not located in an area serviced by a Community Futures (CF) office:Find and contact your local CF office in British Columbia;Find and contact your local CF office in Alberta;Find and contact your local CF office in Saskatchewan; andFind and contact your local CF office in Manitoba;Are not eligible for the RRRF – Community Futures Stream;Have applied and were declined for funding from the Canada Emergency Business Account (CEBA) or were not eligible for CEBA funding;Were operational as of March 1, 2020;Have suffered financially because of the COVID-19 pandemic;Intend to continue operations in Western Canada; andMust be prepared to clarify their financial track record and operational costs and company details during COVID 19 (and prior), and will be adjudicated based on their financial need and impact of COVID 19.Ineligible Organizations:A government organization or body, or an entity owned by a government organization or body;A union, charitable, religious or fraternal organization or entity owned by such an organization or if you are, you are a registered organization that has filed your T2 return or T3010 return and that generates a portion of your revenue from the sales of goods or services;An entity owned by any Federal Member of Parliament or Senator; andAn entity that promotes violence, incites hatred or discriminates on the basis of sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, colour, race, ethnic or national origin, religion, age or mental or physical disability, contrary to applicable laws.Eligible Activities:The loan should enable businesses to overcome the following impacts as a result of COVID 19:Retain diverse and valuable talent;Maintain sector knowledge and skills;Maintain capital flow;Maintain critical supply chains and increase capacity to withstand supply chain disruptions; Protect technologies and processes that improve resilience, productivity, and/or competitiveness; and/or,Protect vital intellectual property.Best Practices:Only applicants projecting a loss will be eligible. Applicants estimating a surplus will be ineligible.This program is also delivered via Women's Enterprise Centre for female led organizations, click HERE. Applicants can vet their eligibility by clicking the eligibility assistant (see link below);Supplementary materials other than those identified in the application will not be assessed and should not be submitted;While completing the application form, always use the information and data as current as possible. Applications that do not have the mandatory information will be deemed incomplete and ineligible for funding;If your company is pre-revenue, please indicate if your business has received angel or venture capital funding in 2019 or 2020; andThe estimated % revenue deduction should be as a direct result of COVID 19.

      Grant Criteria 
      The LEEFF program will be open to large for-profit businesses as well as certain not-for-profit businesses such as airports, with annual revenues generally in the order of $300 million or higher. Note that those in the financial sector need not apply. To qualify, eligible businesses must be seeking financing of about $60 million or more, have significant operations or workforce in Canada, and not be involved in active insolvency proceedings.Turnaround time: on a case by case basis.Loan Value: Unsecured facility equal to 80% of aggregate loan and secured facility to 20% of aggregate loan amount, loan advanced in tranches over 12 monthsInterest rate: Cumulative at 5% per annum payable quarterly in arrears, increases to 8% at 1 year anniversary of loanTerm: 5 yearsEligible Companies Large for-profit enterprises in all sectors, except for those in the financial sector; Companies who either:  have a significant impact on Canada’s economy, as demonstrated by (i) having significant operations in Canada or (ii) supporting a significant workforce in Canada; OR Can generally demonstrate approximately $300 million or more in annual revenues; andRequire a minimum loan size of $60 million for the next 12 months. Certain not-for-profit enterprises, such as airports, could also be eligible. Companies that have been found guilty of tax evasion are not eligible under the program.Note: Loan sizes for each applicant is assessed on a case-by-case basis based on demonstrated need.Best Practices:Applicants should register their interest at LEEFF-CUGE@cdev.gc.ca. A CEEFC representative will promptly send applicants a non-disclosure agreement, application form, and instructions. The application form will request important information relating to the applicant and its financial condition.Applicants will be contacted by both representatives of CEEFC and ISED Canada to begin the process.Applicants can also fill out the application form below.In addition to the security interest on the secured facility and the interest rate charged for the loans, if the borrower is a Canadian public company (or the private subsidiary of a Canadian public company), the borrower must issue warrants with the option to purchase the borrower’s (or parent public company’s) common shares totaling 15% of the principal amount or receive cash consideration equivalent to the value of the warrants. The warrants will enable CEEFC to share in the upside of the borrower’s recovery.Restrictions: The borrower will be subject to certain operating requirements while the loan is outstanding including (i) prohibitions on dividends, capital distributions and share repurchases, and (ii) certain executive compensation restrictions.Covenants. The borrower will be subject to certain affirmative covenants while the loan is outstanding including (i) performance of obligations under existing pension plans; (ii) performance of material obligations under applicable collective bargaining agreements; and (iii) publishing an annual climate‑related financial disclosure report, highlighting how corporate governance, strategies, policies and practices will help manage climate-related risks and opportunities; and contribute to achieving Canada’s commitments under the Paris Agreement and goal of net zero by 2050.Governance. CEEFC will reserve the right to appoint an observer to the board of the borrower.If the borrower is a Canadian public company (or the private subsidiary of a Canadian public company), the borrower must issue warrants with the option to purchase the borrower’s (or parent public company’s) common shares totaling 15% of the principal amount or receive cash consideration equivalent to the value of the warrants. Granted Consulting is not a financial advisor and it is recommended decision-makers speak with financial/legal representatives and ensure they understand all loan terms. Please refer to the links below for any loan interest details and dates.

      Grant Criteria 
      The B.C. Employer Training Grant subsidizes  100% of training costs to a maximum of $20,000 per participant per year. It is an ideal program to upgrade the skills within your organization, or to provide training for a new hire for your company in BC impacted communities. Training can be taken at a public post-secondary institution or through a private training provider (additional course syllabus requirements apply). Training must not be more than 52 weeks in duration. The program was developed to support businesses that were directly and indirectly impacted by mill closures. COVID is not considered a natural disaster under this stream.There is a maximum claim amount of $300,000 per company per fiscal year.Funding StreamEligible Training TypesGrant coverage (Limit per fiscal year)Employment Transition Training StreamEssential skills: numeracy, reading, language skillsTrades trainingOccupational certification EG Residential Care Worker Certificate and Early Childhood Education CertificateIndustry-recognized training with transferable credentials recognized by employers across an industry. EG health and safety training (WHMIS, first aid), hospitality training (eg FoodSafe Level 1, Serving it Right) and computer or software training (EG Microsoft, Cisco)Technical training to develop new skills required to operate machinery, equipment or use software, an application or program, Technical training needed for the successful adoption of new technological systems including new manufacturing, production and construction methods.Business Skills/Management skills such as strategic planning, leadership recruiting and hiring.Business Improvement skills (EG marketing, performance management, communications, and sales)Other soft skills such as project management, professional communication, and cross-cultural competency.100%(Max. $20,000 per participant)An application must be submitted before training can begin.Turnaround time:  Approx. 4 weeksEligible Applicants: Unemployed persons, employees at risk of losing their jobs, or employees who need training to obtain a better or different job who were impacted by mill closures in BCSelf-employed people, including small business owners and independent contractors (e.g. owner/operators). These applicants must apply under their own business name;At least 16 years old; ANDUnemployed; OR Employees that will obtain a better or different job as a result of training; ORSelf-employed individuals including contractors;Live in an impacted community;Must have a Business BCeID account or an individual BCeID account;Employers must be in good standing with the province;Trainees must be Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents or Protected Persons;Trainees cannot be family members of business owners; andTrainee must be aged 16+ ( previously 15+).Eligible Expenses: Note: Training must be no more than 52 weeks in durationIn-house training (courses designed for the employer in-house)Tuition fees (including GST) for training course programOnline courses Expenses & financial assistance support for those with disabilitiesTravel costs are eligible when all of the following conditions are met:The participant lives and works in a community with a population of 25,000 or less, located outside the geographic boundaries of Metro Vancouver; The distance from the community where the participant lives and works to the location of the training is greater than 100 km one-way.Childcare—For a participant’s child while the participant is attending training or other services.Fees for textbooks, software, and other supplies required for the trainingAccommodation. Transportation—For the participants’ transportation to training, employment services or on-the-job training. Bus passes and mileage are eligible. The Maximum reimbursement that will be paid on flights is $800 (return) per participant. No part of the cost of first class or business class tickets will be reimbursed.Mileage.Refreshments—Food or light meals provided during training.Ineligible Expenses: ConsultingCoachingMentorshipsTrade showsAnnual meetingsNetworkingSeminarsConferencesPaid practicumsBest PracticesThis program is currently only accepting applications that support British Columbians impacted by mill closures or curtailments in B.C.Participants must live in an impacted community: “Impacted community” is defined as a community that has experienced or will experience a significant shift in labour needs due to events such as a natural disaster or the closure or curtailment of operations of a major employer.Training must align with business needs. Providing training must be the training provider's main focus.Active claimants in receipt of Employment Insurance (EI) Part I benefits or B.C. Employment Assistance clients in receipt of Income Assistance (IA) must obtain approval from the Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction prior to training.The program may ask for additional information, including value for money. Be prepared to provide additional information supporting your case.BCeID can take up to 15 days in some cases.Priority may be given to participants that are not eligible for Employment InsuranceSelf employed owners will need to demonstrate that the training aligns with a current or future business opportunity.Essential skills training must be delivered by a B.C public post-secondary institution or private training institution.Applications submitted to the wrong stream will be denied. There should be no conflict of interest, and family run businesses may find difficulty in applying for this program.Training cannot have started prior to an application being submitted.

          open until filled
      
    
    
  





    
      




  
      
        Recently Changed 
        'Notice to reader' financial statements for the last two (2) years are acceptable to satisfy the financial statement requirement. The application guidelines state review engagement or audited financial statements are required.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program provides up to $5M to eligible agriculture businesses, to aid them to improve, automate and modernize facilities needed to increase Canada’s food supply capacity and to assist companies to implement changes required by COVID-19 to safeguard the health and safety of workers and their families.  The program will provide a cash injection of $5M in funding to qualifying companies involved with food processing, manufacturing or greenhouse operations that are implementing changes in response to COVID-19. Eligible activities include improvements to operations, added public health protocols, and any other qualifying activities that help prevent Canadian food supply disruptions. Activities must be completed prior to September 30, 2020.Note:  Applications will be accepted on a continuous basis from program launch until  4:30 PM PT on July 3 2020 for BC, Alberta, and Saskatchewan. Applications are open until 12:00 p.m. (midnight) EDT Friday, July 31, 2020 for companies in Manitoba.Turnaround time:  1-10 days.Eligible Applicants:An incorporated company since June 2018;Is focused on food production in Canada, in one of the following areas:agricultural food processing – cleaning, sorting, cutting, packaging of food for consumption or as an ingredient. This applies, as well, to agricultural producers growing or rearing product which have a processing line which processes products grown or reared at the facility. For example, greenhouses that also clean, sort and package their or other greenhouses production; ORagricultural food manufacturing – comprised of establishments primarily engaged in producing food; ORagricultural producers that are converting or adapting existing greenhouses to increase year-round horticultural production.Eligible Costs: Eligible costs must pertain to one of the following activities that will be completed by September 30th 2020:Activities associated with adjustments made as a result of COVID-19 to existing plants to implement added public health protocols and requirements and adapt production processes for the health and safety of workers and their families, such as:Non-disposable or reusable Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including:body temperature screening/fever detection systems;washing stations;workstation dividers/protective barriers;full and half face-piece respirators; andimpact goggles and face shields.Installation of sanitation stations, protective barriers;Adjustments to current processes and manufacturing lines to accommodate social distancing;Rental or purchase of portable buildings and installations/site modifications and/or transportation for social distancing and wellness checks;Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning (HVAC) modifications or upgrades;Training for workers on additional health security measures;Disinfection and cleaning in the event of a plant closure;Labor costs only as are needed for the installation of the protective measures; andOther activities that a company can demonstrate are resulting from COVID-19 public health adjustment requirements.Activities associated with humane slaughter of surplus animals as a result of COVID-19 at processing facilities, such as:Extraordinary adjustments to slaughter line/facility necessary to change slaughter capacity;Retrofitting or adding temporary new slaughter lines;Disposal on site or transportation to disposal facilities;Labour costs only as are needed for the installation of the measures; andOther activities that can be demonstrated are resulting from COVID-19 food supply disruptions.Activities considered to have a strategic benefit to the company or are permanent increases in production beyond the COVID-19 situation and will remain in place after COVID-19Activities associated with improvements or modernization of food processing or manufacturing facilities to manage surplus stock; increase production; or that are operating at less than full capacity or closed, including conversion or adaptation of existing greenhouses to increase horticultural production, such as:Rental or purchase, shipping and installation of automation equipment new to the plant;Rental or purchase and installation of additional production or packaging equipment;Rental or purchase and installation of increased warehousing and/or cold storage capacity;Equipment technicians fees, travel and accommodation to make installation;Plant or line retrofits to accommodate the new equipment;Training of employees on the new equipment;Other activities, other than labour, that can be demonstrated as needed as a result of the installation of the automation. Ineligible Costs:Labour costs, other than as part of installation costs, including wage subsidies;Administration costs such as office supplies, materials, space, telecommunications, audiovisual, postage and freightSingle use Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) equipment that is required for normal operations, and all disposable or non-reusable equipment, including:Face masks and coverings, including N95 masks;Sanitizers and cleaning products;Particulate filters and gas/vapor cartridges;Safety glasses;Disposable and non-disposable gloves, for example kevlar or wire mesh cutting gloves;Disposable and non-disposable gowns and laboratory coats;Disposable and non-disposable ear plugs; andHair nets and foot coverings.Costs associated with the Quarantine Act for isolation of temporary foreign workers;Costs for activities that are deemed to be part of normal business practice for any recipient;Costs related to marketing activities and business promotion;Land purchases;Hospitality,  travel; and in-kind contributions;Legal fees;Refundable portion of the Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST), value-added taxes, or other items for which a refund or rebate is received;Costs related to the preparation of this application, the Contribution Agreement or related schedules;Any portion of any cost that is deemed to exceed a fair market value for that cost item; andAny cost, such as amortization that would not result in a direct, out-of-pocket expense for the recipient.Best Practices:This program can be combined with other Canadian government Provincial/Federal sources up to 75%. In the event that an exceptional need is proposed, the program may make an exception and consider up to 100% of costs covered by other government sources. The program focuses on meat processing facilities are the highest priority, followed by all other food processing, manufacturing and greenhouse operations.Audited or review engagement financial statements for the past two years  required attachments/supporting documents. 'Notice to reader financial' statements (processed with a third party) will be sufficient. Be prepared to demonstrate how you will meet any costs related to the budget beyond the grant contribution. The program may request additional documentation.The program will fund activities retroactive to March 15, 2020.A Letter of support from the applicant’s union or health and safety committee may be requested upon application review.In addition to for-profit companies, the program also deems cooperatives, and/or indigenous groups eligible.First come first served: funding may be depleted prior to the deadline.Note: The program also offers a separate repayable option for relevant applicants that have not been affected by COVID-19.How to Apply: For companies in British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan:If applying for under $100,000, apply to IAF directly (see application form below).If applying for over $100,000 apply to Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada directly (see application form below).For companies applying in Manitoba contact:If applying for under $100,000, apply to Agricultural Adaptation Council:Pre-screening form and application form available here. Telephone: 519-822-7554 Email: epf@adaptcouncil.orgIf applying for over $100,000, apply to Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada directly (see application form below).

      Best Practices & Forms
      Guideline available here.Under $100,000 funding application form available here (BC/Alberta/Sask).Over $100,000 application form available here (Canada-wide).

      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers training subsidies to ensure Saskatchewan based employers can maintain regular business activities while continuing to promote workplace safety and stimulate competitiveness amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. The program will cover 100% of training costs up to $10,000 per business.Turnaround Time: 5 business daysEligible Applicants:Must have a Saskatchewan Corporation Registry Number;Must be on the Government of Saskatchewan's list of critical public services and allowable businesses during the emergency period OR eligible to resume operations in a confirmed phase of the Re-Open Saskatchewan Plan;Must be on the list of critical public services and allowable businesses when the application is received or during the eligibility assessment period; andPublicly funded organizations are NOT eligible for this program (ex. health regions, post-secondary training institutions, public libraries, municipalities and school divisions).Eligible Participants:Must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident with a Social Insurance Number;Temporary Foreign Workers are not eligible;May be based outside of Saskatchewan during the training period as long as they are normally residents of Saskatchewan; andMay be either a new hire or an existing employee.Note: Self-employed individuals are NOT eligible.Eligible Training: Note: The application must be approved before training can begin.Must be delivered by a Saskatchewan based third party (ex. Post-secondary education institutions; private vocational schools, trade unions; and private industry trainers);Must be a minimum of 8 hours in length per trainee by the same training provider and completed within 4 months; Must result in a credential (ex. record of completion, certificate, grade, etc.); andTraining can be in-person or remote.Eligible Expenses:Tuition fees or fees charged by the training provider;Mandatory student fees;Textbooks, software and other required materials;Learning material fees; andExamination fees.Best Practices:This program cannot be combined with other Provincial or Federal grants;Employer applicants that demonstrate reliance on the grant will be prioritized above those that are less dependent on the training for their employee's employability and overall corporate performance. Training that has already been pre-paid and not yet started may be de-prioritized;Training providers must not be affiliated with the employer; andThe training provider and training can occur outside of Saskatchewan as long as employer and employee are normally residing and based in Saskatchewan; andReimbursement: 33% of funds will be disbursed to successful applicants at the start of the placement, and 67% received after final report.

        January 7, 2026Starting December 15, 2025, Indigenous partner organizations in the Indigenous Pathways initiative will be able to support up to 30 internship units per submission year, an increase from the previous limit of 12.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This program allows student entrepreneurs to grow their businesses with the intention of bringing new technology or goods to the market. It will fund 50% of a research-based internship for the student entrepreneur to expedite research and development efforts that align with the company and their graduate work. Students will receive a minimum of $7,500 for a 4-month project—duration and grant value may increase based on the needs of the startup.Note: This program is different from the Mitacs Accelerate program. It allows student entrepreneurs to work at their own companies.Grant Value: For 1 internship unit (4-6 months), Mitacs will provide 50% of wage subsidies up to $7,500. For projects less than 6 internship units, Mitacs and the employer will contribute $7,500 each ($10,000 for the internship and $5,000 for business and R&D costs). After 6 internship units, Mitacs will contribute $7,333 and the employer will contribute $6,000 ($10,000 for the internship and $3,333 for business and R&D costs).Turnaround time: 6-8 weeksEligible Employers:Early-stage businesses in approved incubators that are: Testing a new product, service, or technology; orRe-iterating an existing product, service, or technology; The participant's startup must be affiliated with an incubator for the entire duration of the placement; If a business drops out of their incubator, they can apply to the regular Mitacs Accelerate program; andMust be incorporated.Note: The applicant is both the employer and the participant.Eligible Candidates:Current undergraduate, graduate students, or post-doc startup founders.Eligible Activities:Research activities pertaining to a new project for the startup that: Addresses "the unknown" - an artifact in computer science that needs solving; Makes a new contribution to the body of knowledge in a field; Is broadly applicable;Is defined by the research community;The results are publishable in a peer-reviewed journal or conference;Builds on previous research; The level of research expected is appropriate for the level of education of the applicant (undergraduate vs. post-grad); andOther activities related to the business are welcome, but the application should focus on research and development efforts.Note: Projects in which the intern develops novel software to answer a research question or test a hypothesis are also eligible.       Grant Criteria 
      The BC Basin program will fund 75% of wages up to $17,000 for food producers (involved in one of key areas listed below) who live in the Basin area to meet the increased demand for food production as a result of COVID-19.Turnaround time: 25 business daysGrant Value: 75% of wages up to $15.40/hour to a maximum of  $17,000 totalEligible Employers : Must be registered BC corporation located in the Basin (see map below);Food producers involved in the production of any of the following (also known as "primary" food processing):Grains;Fruits, vegetables or forage; orLivestock for meat or dairy products;Have been operating for at least two years;Be able to provide a Statement of Farming Activity for 2020 (required) and 2021 (if available);Must be hiring for one of the following reasons:To maintain or increase 2022 season production compared to 2021;To maintain or increase 2022 season employment levels compared to 2021.Must provide a safe working environment in accordance with COVID-19 protocols and follow applicable labour laws; Must have WorkSafeBC coverage before the employee starts placement and be in good standing; andEmployers can apply with or without a candidate. Eligible Participants:Must live in the Basin;Be aged 15 or older before the employment start date;Be legally entitled to work in Canada; Not on another wage subsidy; andNot a relative of the owner unless supervised by someone other than the owner.Internship Details:Participants must be hired as an employee (contractors are ineligible);Be paid hourly (salary and piece-rate work are ineligible);Temporary, part-time, or full-time; The placement must take place between March 1, 2023– October 28, 2023;Mandatory Employment Related Costs must be paid by the employer;Reimbursement claim is available 4 weeks following the participant start date;The program will require a minimum 1 claim by August 5, 2022 and confirm the total approved subsidy will be used by October 28, 2022;Applicants must submit the final claim by November 30, 2022, unless an extension has been granted; andThe program may monitor the placement via virtual meetings or phone call.Map of BC Basin region:

      Best Practices:This program cannot be combined with other provincial or federal wage subsidy programs;Once a contribution agreement is signed, the applicant must commit to hiring employees to use the full subsidy awarded or contact program staff immediately if the full amount cannot be allocated;If the employer is not able to hire and will therefore not be using the subsidy, the employer must contact program staff immediately so that the funds can be allocated to another applicant;Applicants must indicate the number of jobs that will be subsidized, types of jobs, and associated wages; Applicants may apply without a participant; andDo not hire before the application is approved.Forms:Application guidelines: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program aims to accelerate the growth of innovative health technologies by funding 50% of eligible projects up to $600,000. The fund supports small to medium-sized enterprises in Alberta who are implementing projects, conducting studies, or holding clinical trials in real-world testing sites. Projects will produce studies to accelerate commercialization and market adoption.Grant Value: 50% of eligible project costs up to $600,000Turnaround time: 8 weeksEligible Applicants:Incorporated small and medium-sized enterprises (less than 500 full-time employees);Must be incorporated in Alberta and have the majority of the business and physical premises in AlbertaDemonstrate appropriate Alberta ownership with benefits flowing primarily within the province of Alberta;Less than $50,000,000 in annual gross revenue;Have a partnership with an independent clinical/user testing organization;Relationship with Testing Site; andPossess a health innovation that is ready for clinical/real-world testing, defined as:Approved by Health Canada, FDA, or equivalent; orHave Investigational Testing Authorization, Clinical Trial Application, or equivalent; orNot requiring regulatory approval, in later stages of tech development, and have design freeze; ANDPossess all other necessary certifications and/or privacy approvals.Eligible Costs:Salaries and wages for employees working directly on the project;Out-of-pocket travel expenses (up to 5% of total project costs);Equipment, materials, and supplies for the project;Licenses and software relevant to the project;Data mining and analytics; andIn-kind contributions.Note: this list is not exhaustive, the funder may allow other costs on a discretionary basis.Ineligible Costs:Staff, contractors indirectly working on the project;Exceptions may be made with approved justifications.Conferences, hotels, food, meetings, and other travel costs unrelated to the project;Rental equipment;Development costs prior to the project;Depreciation costs;Software and tech unrelated or outside the duration of the project; andIndirect overhead expenses.Note: this list is not exhaustive, the funder may restrict other costs on a discretionary basis.Program Details:Max 2 years in duration;The following emerging technology areas are high priority areas for the program:Data-Enabled Innovation: technology that creates and utilizes complex data sets to improve decision making; orDigital Tech for Business Transformation: technology that collects, senses, measures, connects, and distributes information to improve health outcomes or realize health system economic value.Must align with the objectives and intended outcomes of the program;own or have full commercial rights to a health innovation that is ready for clinical/real-world
testing, defined as:regulatory approved (Health Canada, FDA or equivalent); orholding an Investigational Testing Authorization (ITA), Clinical Trial Application (CTA) or
equivalent; ornot requiring regulatory approval (or an ITA/CTA or equivalent), and having a high degree of
technology readiness (TRL 6 to 9) and design freeze for base technology; andpossess all other necessary certification and/or privacy approvalsInclude 1+ testable hypotheses related to health innovation (informed by early experts);Focus on a technology that has potential to improve health outcomes (i.e., purely business
management or operational clinic/hospital backend software is not a fit for this program); andMust have measurable goals and performance indicators. Eligible Testing Sites:Exist as a corporate person, with up-to-date corporate filings (operating anywhere in the world);Be authorized to undertake the proposed project;Demonstrate that the relationship between the Applicant and Testing Site or does not create a conflict of interest;Be at arm’s length from the Applicant;Good credit under Alberta Innovates, InnoTech Alberta, and C-Fer Technologies; andNote: Testing Site can be based in any country that Canada does business with.

      Program provided by
      Emissions Reduction Alberta in Association with Agriculture Funding Consortium (AFC) & Canadian Agri-Food Automation and Intelligence Network (CAAIN)
     

    
      Deadline
      
        2020/08/27

      
    
    
  





    
      




  

      Grant Criteria 
      Open to sole proprietors, small and medium-sized enterprises, and non-profits in Alberta, this program will fund 50% up to $5M for tech projects focused on sustainable innovation and long-term growth in agriculture, agri-food, fibre, and forestry sectors to reduce greenhouse gases in Alberta.Note:  Applications are due August 27, 2020, at 5 pm MDTTurnaround time:  Applicants will be notified of application status in October 2020.Eligible Applicants:Operate in the agriculture, agri-food, or forestry sector anywhere Canada wide;Are one of the following: Farmers, ranchers, or individuals;Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs);Non-profits;Innovators or technology developers;Indigenous communities;Industry, industrial associations, or research and development (R&D) organizations;Post-secondary institutions; orMunicipal governments and government research labs;Have a project that meets the project criteria below;Must be willing to match contributions (1:1); andApplicants are encouraged to partner with Alberta’s post-secondary and research institutions.Note: Applicant does not need to be based in Alberta but the project must show a clear benefit to the Province.Project Details:Demonstrate a clear and justified value proposition for
reducing GHG emissions in Alberta;Innovates or improves sustainable technology to improve efficiency;Eg. Automation and digitization of operations, monitoring and detection technologies, applications of renewable energy, etc.;Examples of eligible project areas include (but are not limited to) the following:Agricultural and forest waste;Genomics for crops and livestock;Nature based-solutions;Nutrient and soil management; Tillage, seeding, and harvesting techniques; andZero carbon seeding, hydroponics, and innovative cultivation methods. Must be in one of the following stages:Pilot: Ready for field-testing;Commercial Demonstration: Approaching commercialization and being demonstrated at commercial-sized sites; orFirst-of-Kind Commercial Implementation: Design and operations of tech in its final commercialized state;Maximum of 3 years in duration from project initiation.Ineligible Projects:Insufficient GHG reduction potential; Insufficient relevance to Alberta and/or insufficient project activity in Alberta;Risk of detrimental side effects (e.g. environmental impacts);Insufficient information provided in expression of interest or not in English;Proposed development is assessed to be business as usual.Eligible Costs: Salaries and wages;Employee benefits (max 20% of the base salary);Capital assets and equipment;Materials and supplies (including PPE);Consumables (ex. fuel, lab supplies, construction supplies)Administrative supplies and overhead expenses (cannot exceed 15% of total project expenses);Insurance and utilities;Workshops and conferences (max $2,500 and $5,000 for international conferences);Travel; andIn-kind expenses.Ineligible Costs:Land acquisition;Marketing expenses;Foreign currency risk;Subscription, tuition, and membership fees;GHG validation certificates;Costs associated with hiring personnel or gaining approval from regulatory bodies;Intellectual property expenses; andGST and PST.Evaluation criteria:Best PracticesThis program can be combined with other federal, provincial,
or international funds, however, only funds directly contributed by the employer will be matched (1:1) and applicants cannot have received funding from either Emissions Reduction Alberta or Climate Change and Emissions Management Corporation (CCEMC);Applicants must request a minimum of $250,000 and a maximum of $5M;Call for expression of interest is highly competitive so ensure expression of interest is fully developed and of high quality;“Quality” means both the quality of the proposed project relative to the
evaluation criteria and the quality of the written proposal (clarity, completeness, etc.).There are no restrictions on the number of Expression of Interest (EOIs) that can be submitted by any applicant. However,
applicants are encouraged to be selective and bring forward only the most promising and highest
quality applications.A team of experts in science, engineering, business development, commercialization, financing, and GHG quantification will conduct an independent, rigorous, and transparent review overseen by a Fairness Monitor. Once approved by Emissions Reduction Alberta's Board of Directors, funding will be distributed on a milestone basis, and the progress of each project is reported on until completion. All recipients are required to produce a final outcomes report that will be shared publicly for the broader benefit of Alberta.If accepted and in line with priorities of the call, the funder will request a full application;Project start date can be delayed up to 1 year after application approval;New developmental stages of previously funded projects may be eligible; andEmissions Reduction Alberta may work with partners who can provide additional funding for projects.Technology solutions can stem from other foreign sources but MUST BE tested, piloted, demonstrated, or implemented in Alberta.ERA requires matching contributions in cash from the applicant. Other government grants and/or tax credits including the SR&ED program will not qualify as source of matching contribution.

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program offers training subsidies of up to $15,000 per trainee for businesses and non-profits in Ontario who are looking to invest in their workforce, maintain a competitive advantage. Business, technical, and soft skills for career development and maintenance training are eligible. Small companies (less than 100 employees) wanting to train new hires are eligible for 100% of funding up to $15,000 per trainee.Turnaround Time: Approximately 2-3 weeks.Grant Value: For businesses over 100 employees: 50% of eligible costs up to $10,000;For businesses under 100 employees: 83% of eligible costs up to $10,000; andFor businesses under 100 employees training and hiring unemployed individuals: 100% of eligible costs up to $15,000.Eligible Applicants:Licensed to operate in Ontario;For-profit, non-profit, or general partnerships;Must have workplace safety and general liability insurance;Must be willing to pay the training provider themselves; Should agree to offer new hires a job (during or after training) before applying; andShould be operating for at least a year.Ineligible Applicants:Government bodies;  COJG or employment service providers;Employers may be ineligible if they previously received COJG funding and meet any of the following criteria:Received a refund (overpayment) and did not return it;Has debt owed to MTCU;Did not follow through with job offers and raises as promised;Did not submit required documentation; andHas a history of abusing COJG.Eligible Trainees:Resides in Ontario;Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected persons;At least 16 years old;Can be one of the following:Unemployed (prioritized);Seasonal worker;Part-time;Full-time;Must be a current employee or set to be hired as an employee; Commission-based positions are eligible as long as they are still on payroll;Individuals in management positions in companies over 500 employees are ineligible;They are eligible if the company has under 500 employees; andMust have a significant need for this training for a long term career trajectory (whether employed by the current employer or elsewhere; International students are eligible if they have a work permit and are on payroll; andUnemployed participants may be able to continue their EI benefit while in training under COJG.Note: Business owners, including individuals with a controlling interest in the applicant business, are not eligible as trainees under COJG.Eligible Training: Under 1 year in duration;Offered by an Ontario training provider classified as one of the following;Colleges of Applied Arts and Technology;Publicly-assisted universities;School boards;Private trainers operating in compliance with the Private Career Colleges Act, 2005;Union-based training centres;Product vendors (service providers who also produce or sell the product used in training): Training cannot be how to use the product or service;Training must be unrelated to the use of the product or service;Training involving essential skills, specialized and technical skills, management and business skills, and soft skills in the areas of career development, maintenance, and refresher training; and Must be transferrable/universal skills learned.For under 25 participants or under must apply through service provider in respective area; andFor over 25 participants must apply directly through the Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities.Ineligible Training: Training that the employer legally has to provide itself;Executive training courses (MBA, CFA);Preparatory training courses (LSAT, MCAT, GMAT);Business Consulting services; Apprenticeship training; andTraining that displaces existing staff or replaces staff currently on lay-off.Note: The employer may deem many applications of over $25,000 ineligible depending on funding availability.Eligible Expenses:Tuition fees or fees charged by the training provider;Mandatory student fees;Textbooks, software, and other required materials;Equipment, clothing, tools;Examination fees; andTravel costs up to $500 (if the participant is traveling at least 24km each way).Eligible Training Provider:If the selected training is through a private trainer, then the training provider must meet the following requirements:Must have been in business and conducting training for at least 2 years at the time of application submission;Declare any conflict of interest between the employer, training participants and/or product vendor;Within the preceding 10 years, experience working in a profession relevant to the training being provided with:48 months of experience or teaching a program to prepare a student for the field (or a combination of the two); ORAt least 24 months of experience with one of the following qualifications:A Canadian bachelor’s degree (or equivalent foreign degree)A certificate of qualification issued under the Ontario College of Trades and Apprenticeship Act, 2009Status as a graduate of a college of applied arts and technology or registered private career college (or equivalent institution outside Ontario)Third-party regulatory requirements (if applicable)Program Details:Applications for 25 participants or under can apply through service providers; ORApplications for over 25 participants must apply directly through the Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities (See Forms below).Applications are assessed by priority measured by these three tiers:1. Training results in a new or higher position and this is the employer's first successful application in the last 6 months;2. Training results in a new or higher position but this is not the employer's first successful application in the last 6 months OR training does not result in a new or higher position;3. Training per trainee is below $500 and lasts no longer than 1 week OR the training is required due to legislation, regulation or policy.

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program will offer 50% (or 75% for underrepresented groups) of project activities up to $5,000,000 to businesses in Canada's agriculture, agri-food, and agri-based product industries to expedite sustainable innovation. The new clean technology will improve practices and reduce greenhouse gases to align with Canada's transition into long-term sustainability. Eligible businesses and non-profits can be in any stage of development from beginning research to pre-commercialization, but they must be able to prove their innovation will be adopted by the sector. Project activities must be completed by March 31, 2021.Note: This program is highly competitive and on its final funding year. Ensure you apply in advance of the deadline.Grant Value: 50% of project activities up to $5,000,000. Underrepresented groups (Indigenous, northern communities, etc.) may be eligible to receive 75% of project activities.Turnaround time:  within 100 business daysEligible Applicants:The following Canadian-incorporated groups in agriculture, agri-food, and agri-based products are eligible:Businesses;Non-profits;Academic institutions;Co-operatives;Indigenous organizations and associations; andGovernment bodies.Note: Applicants must prove that their innovation will be adopted in the sector in the short or long term.Project Details:Intend to generate positive impacts for land, water, and air, while reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in agricultural production;Include measurable amounts in Work Plan;Must be an innovation, as defined by the following:New invention, technology, process or service that is not currently available in the marketplace;Major adaption of existing technologies, processes or services applied in an unprecedented setting or condition; orImprovement to existing technology, process or service that significantly improves functionality (generally to the point of being patentable), cost, or performance of goods and services that are considered 'state of the art' or new to the industry;Must produce cleantech, which is any process, product, or service that improves the environment through the following:Protection activities that prevent, reduce or eliminate pollution or other negative environmental impacts;Resource management activities that result in more efficient use of natural resources;Use of goods that have been adapted to be significantly less energy or resource-consuming than industry standard;Must result in one of the following:Increased investment in clean technology for the agriculture sector;Increased development, demonstration, commercialization and adoption of clean technologies in agriculture;Improved long-term environmental performance in the sector;High priority projects innovate clean tech in one of two key areas:Precision agriculture - gathering and processing data to make decisions that will improve the sustainability, efficiency, and productivity of agricultural operations;Agri-based bioproducts - renewable products, other than food and feed, derived from agricultural resources or wastes (e.g. manure and crop residues); Benefits Canadian ag producers and key stakeholders; Projects that benefit underrepresented groups will be prioritized (indigenous communities, Northern Territories, youth);Contribution from other industry stakeholders;Innovative experimentation/testing that can lead to a new area of discovery in Clean Tech of what does and does not work; Current adoption levels and status of emissions to which the project pertains;Applications deemed complete by Sept 30, 2020, will be considered for funding support. Project activities must be completed by March 31, 2021.Innovation Continuum: Eligible Costs:Any activities regarding research and development, to technology and knowledge transfer, to commercialization and adoption:Basic and applied research, including public-private collaboration;Development of clean technologies;Piloting, evaluating, and reiterating clean technologies;Demonstration activities;Commercializing activities;Accelerating adoption of on-farm clean technologies; andIndustry awareness activities that promote clean technologies.Note: Any costs incurred prior to signing an agreement with the funder will be ineligible. After signing the agreement, costs must be incurred before March 31, 2021.Ineligible Costs:Costs incurred prior to the agreed start date;Expenses that do not provide a direct benefit to the agriculture industry;Activities related to aquaponic food production, aquaculture, seaweed, fish and seafood production, and processing;Regulation development and enforcement;Automated applications that do not result in greenhouse gas reductions or other direct environmental benefits (e.g. automated steering systems, robotic milking systems); andRenovations, site improvements, leasehold improvements, land lease or purchase, building purchase or construction.

      Best Practices:This program can be combined with other federal, provincial, municipal, indigenous, and non-governmental funding;If the employer is a for-profit or not-for-profit organization, a 10% cash contribution is required from the provincial or territorial government supporting the project;If you are grant reliant, ensure you do not incur costs until you have been approved for funding;Obtain an application package by emailing: aafc.actprogram-programmetpa.aac@canada.ca or 1-877-246-4682. program;Be aged 15 or older before the employment start date;Be legally entitled to work in Canada; andNot a relative of the owner unless supervised by someone other than the owner.Internship Details:Maximum 1 placement per company;Part-time placement (1-15 hr/week);Participants may work up to 40 hours a week on breaks;12-38 weeks and 180 to 570 hours in duration;Participants with exceptionalities may be considered for fewer hours;Must be consecutive work weeks;The earliest start date is September 5, 2023;Participant must be on payroll;Participants are to be paid hourly—salary and contract work are ineligible.Must not replace a current employee; Meets minimum wage requirements in BC; andEntry-level jobs are not eligible.Map of BC Basin region:

        Recently Changed 
        May 20, 2025Program is now accepting applications.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program offers a maximum of 70% wage subsidy of up to $7,000 to hire current post-secondary students in part-time or full-time studies. It is intended to provide post-secondary students with work experience and valuable skills to secure meaningful employment as well as increase productivity and competitiveness in the aviation and aerospace industry. Grant Value:50% of wages up to $5,000;70% of wages up to $7,000 for students in the following underrepresented groups:Women in STEM;Indigenous persons;Newcomers to Canada;Visible minorities; Persons with disabilities; andFirst-year students.Turnaround Time: 2 business daysEligible Employers:Be directly or indirectly involved in the aviation/aerospace industry;Ie. aviation/aerospace organization, supplier of goods and services for the aviation/aerospace industry.Have registered business number;Have WorkSafeBC or Workers’ Compensation Board registration;Have General Liability Insurance;Employer Liability Insurance of $2,000,000 minimum; andGeneral Liability Insurance of $2,000,000 minimum.Must have participants on payroll; Cannot be receiving other federal funding for the placement; andEmployers must apply with a candidate.Eligible Participants:Must be a current student enrolled (full-time or part-time) in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Proof of enrollment required.Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents or persons with refugee protection legally entitled to work in their placement province; andMust have a co-op, internship, or practicum as a part of their study plan during the placement term or recognized work-integrated learning in the next semester.Ineligible Participants:Immediate family members of CCAA or employer;Must not be a recipient of Employment Insurance; andApprentices.Placement Details:The position must support the aviation and aerospace industry;Full-time or part-time positions;12 hours/week minimum is encouraged;An 8-week placement minimum is encouraged;1 placement is considered to take place over 4 months;An 8-month contract can result in 2 placements for a student, and a 12-month contract may result in 3 placements.Employers can fund up to 5 participants per term;Work-integrated learning must be in the participant's study plan and span over the duration of the placement;Employers to have identified participants and confirmed placements for the application;All aviation and aerospace businesses and post-secondary institutions can be pre-approved if desired, even before the selection of one or more students, presuming student eligibility.Employers must provide a company description, including the business number, company website, and job description;Employers must develop a learning plan for the participant;Wage subsidies in this program are reimbursements following an agreed payment schedule;Advance payments are possible for small and medium-sized businesses and nonprofits if there are operational cash flow needs. Eligibility will be determined on a case-by-case basis; andSubsidies can be transferred via cheque or electronic funds transfer.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This grant cannot be combined with other federal wage subsidies. Provincial, municipal or any other funds may be acceptable;Process Best Practices:If you are searching for participants, please join the online CCAA Job Matching services for Aviation and Aerospace industry here or partner with local post-secondary institutions;Participants with a formal SWPP agreement with a post-secondary education institution is not mandatory, but highly encouraged;The application online does not allow for saving.Recommended to the internship placement details (ie. student’s start and end dates, full details of wages and employment benefits, if applicable) and all responses prepared and saved separately before applying.Forms: Program Webpage: click here
