      Grant Criteria 
      This BC provincial program provides targeted financial support for small and medium sized businesses in BC that have faced a 30% revenue loss from March 2020 to now when compared to the same one-month period in 2019. Additional support will be provided for tourism reliant businesses. Additional support will be provided for tourism reliant businesses. The goal of the program is to provide fully-funded grants to businesses to ensure they are supported through the COVID-19 pandemic for long term success.Turnaround time: 8 weeksGrant Value:Up to $30,000Additional $15,000 maximum funding for tourism-related businessesUp to $2,000 to service providers to assist in developing the recovery planEligible Applicants:Business entities including sole proprietors, partnerships, corporations, or other associations of persons;Majority share of the company is owned by one or more BC residents;Business's sole or primary operations are located and conducted in BC;Have been operating in B.C. for at least 18 months as of the date of application to this grant program;Must be registered in BC;Pay taxes in BC;Businesses must currently be in operation;Businesses affected by provincial health order are not eligible;Seasonal businesses in the appropriate season may be eligible; andMust not have announced or intended for business closure or dissolution.Announced a permanent closure to their customers;Held a closing-out sale;Listed their business for sale; orGiven notice to their employees.Must have a maximum of 149 employees on payroll in BC for at least 4 months in a calendar year;Including contracted staff prior to February 1, 2020.For sole proprietorships and partnerships that do not have staff, they must have fixed costs related to tangible assets: property, plant or equipment;Last financial statement prior to February 1, 2020 must have positive cash flow;Experienced at least a 30% revenue loss from March 2020 to present when compared to the same one-month period in 2019;Maintains a:Payroll account number with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); andBusiness license and all other operating licenses as required.Has received or applied to federal support programs including:Canadian Emergency Business Account (CEBA);Regional Relief and Recovery Fund (RRRF); orCanada Emergency Commercial Rent Assistance program (CECRA).Note: Only your B.C. revenues and B.C. resident employees employed at a B.C. location count toward the revenue and employment requirements of the program.Eligible Applicants for Additional Tourism Grant:Must meet all eligibility requirements listed above;Be able to demonstrate a significant part of the business's total demand/revenue comes from visitors; andMust be part of the tourism sector.Transportation, food and beverage services, recreation, entertainment, and travel services;Accommodation:Hotels, inns, lodges, campsites, recreational vehicle rentals, etc.; andDoes not include long-term stays, apartments, condo sub-leases, home-stay arrangement, vacation rentals.Base grant funding (based on total revenue):Pre-COVID Annual RevenueGrant AmountUp to $100,000$10,000$100,001 to $1,000,000$15,000$1,000,001 to $2,000,000$20,000$2,000,001 to $3,000,000$25,000More than $3,000,000$30,000Additional funding for tourism (number of BC resident employees):Number of Pre-COVID BC Residents EmployedGrant Top-Up Amount0-1$5,0002-4$10,0005-149$15,000Required Documents:Incorporated businesses:Central Securities Register or T2-Schedule 50 Shareholder Information;Balance Sheet, Income Statement, Statement of Cash Flows (if available) for the current year plus 2 preceding years;The monthly breakdown for the past 24 months actual monthly revenue;18 months for businesses operating less than 24 months.Notices of Assessment for 2018 (if applicable) and 2019;The first section of the T2 return (first nine pages) for 2018 (if applicable) and 2019;If applicable, payroll documents from September 1, 2019, showing  the initials, city, wage, and deductions for each employee, include one of the following:T4 Statement of Remuneration Paid;PD7A Payroll filing documents; andPayroll or cheque run.Unincorporated businesses:T1-T2125 Statement of Business or Professional Activities indicating the percentage of ownershipThe monthly breakdown for the past 24 months actual monthly revenue;18 months for businesses operating less than 24 months.Notices of Assessment for 2018 (if applicable) and 2019;The first section of the owners’ T1 return (Form 5010-R) for 2018 (if applicable) and 2019;T2125 Statement of Business or Professional Activities for 2018 (if applicable) and 2019;If applicable, payroll documents from September 1, 2019, showing  the initials, city, wage, and deductions for each employee, include one of the following:T4 Statement of Remuneration Paid;PD7A Payroll filing documents; andPayroll or cheque run.Program Details:Must demonstrate recovery plan is consistent with criteria of this program;Must clearly show implementable plan to regain solvency upon grant funding;The recovery plan may include but is not limited to:Diversifying the business;Providing new services;Accessing new customers;Upgrading physical premises of business currently in operation;May not be used retroactively;As long as it directly contributes to the business growing/recovering, it is eligible, including but not limited to:Purchasing equipment to make improvements to goods or services provided;Install new outdoor patio with social distancing barriers;Modify your physical business location.Ineligible expenses:Renovations (it does not directly help the business recover or grow).May be eligible for supporting fixed/overhead costs.Staff wages may be eligible if it is under 20% of the funding amount.Funding is provided on a one-time basis.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program allows for combining with other funding by the Government of Canada, Government of BC so long as funding received is not for the same activity;The program funding can be used retroactively until September 17, 2020;Applicants are advised to gather all the required documents as listed in the checklist prior to starting the application;A recovery plan template, guidebook and workbook are available by logging into the application; andProgram funds cannot be for costs related to reopening businesses that were ordered closed under a Provincial Health Order, or costs related to meeting WorkSafeBC safe operating guidance.How to Apply:Apply and provide information to demonstrate eligibility in the link below;If eligible, a business must develop a recovery plan. Up to $2,000 to professional service providers are available to help businesses plan for their recovery as needed;With recovery plan approved, funding is provided to the business to implement actions outlined in the recovery plan;Business must provide regular updates that account for spending and status of their recovery effort supported by the grant received; andMust agree to participate in a third-party audit at the end of the program.Forms:Application Guidelines: click hereApplication Form: click hereRequired Documents Checklist: click hereRecovery Plan Template: click here

      Grant Type

      Regions

        Recently Changed 
        The Canada Emergency Rent Subsidy (CERS) ended on October 23, 2021, and is replaced by 2 new programs - Tourism and Hospitality Recovery Program (THRP) and Hardest-Hit Business Recovery Program (HHBRP); andApplicants may still continue to apply for claim periods that are still openJanuary 27, 2022, is the last day to apply to claim period 11 (July 4 - July 31, 2021) of the CERS;Claim period 14 (Sept 26 - Oct 23, 2021) was the final claim period of CERS.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      Businesses, charities and non-profits that have been affected by COVID-19 may qualify for rent and mortgage support up to a maximum of $67,500 per location. For businesses that can demonstrate a revenue loss, the subsidy will be available on a sliding scale up to a maximum of 65%. An additional 25% (total of 90%) is available for businesses temporarily shut down by mandatory public health order issued by authorized public health authority.Organizations will need to calculate revenue loss and multiply this by a figure provided by this program to determine the rent and mortgage subsidy organizations are eligible to receive.Grant Value: Up to 90% of a maximum of $67,500 per location or up to 90% of a maximum of $270,000Eligible Applicants:Must be one of the following entities:Individuals and sole proprietors;Canadian private corporations and trusts;Partnerships that are up to 50% owned by non-eligible members;Indigenous government-owned corporations;Non-profit organizations;Registered charities;Registered Canadian Amateur Athletic Associations;Registered journalism organizations; andNon-public colleges and schools, including institutions that offer specialized services in art, driving language or flight.Meet 1 of the following conditions:Have a payroll account or have been using a payroll service provider as of March 15, 2020; ORHave a business number as of September 27, 2020; ORPurchased the business assets of another person or partnership who meets 1 of the 2 above conditions and has made an election under the special asset acquisition rules.For claim periods 1-10, there is no minimum revenue drop required to qualify for the subsidy;For claim periods 11-13, the applicant must have experienced more than a 10% drop in revenue to qualify for the rent subsidy.Eligible Expenses:Maximum $75,000 per location;Maximum $300,000 among affiliated entities;Expenses including the following:Commercial rent;Property tax (including school taxes and municipal taxes);Property insurance;Interest on commercial mortgages (subject o limits);Ancillary services to facilitate and support the use of the qualifying property (eligibility determined on a case-by-case basis).E.g. security, traffic control, janitorial or cleaning services, landscaping, waste collection, disposal and recycling, snow removal, etc.Expenses paid under agreements in writing before October 9, 2020;Real property expenses located in Canada.Note: Property taxes, utilities bills , common area maintenance (ie. condo/strata fees) are eligible ONLY if those items are included in the rental agreement.Ineligible Expenses:Residential property used by the applicant;Any revenue from renting or subleasing space on the property to entities with existing business or personal relationships (arm's length parties);Payments made to entities with existing business or personal relationships (non-arm's length); andMortgage interest expenses for rental income properties.Revenue DeclinePeriod 19 (Aug 1-28)Period 20 (Aug 29-Sept 25)Period 21 (Sept 26-Oct 23)70% and over40%40%40%50%-69%25% + (revenue decline - 50%) x 0.75(e.g., 25% + (60% revenue decline - 50%) x 0.75 = 32.5% subsidy rate)25% + (revenue decline - 50%) x 0.75(e.g., 25% + (60% revenue decline - 50%) x 0.75 = 32.5% subsidy rate)10% + (revenue decline - 50%) x 0.5(e.g., 10% + (60% revenue decline - 50%) x 0.5 = 15% subsidy rate)>10%-50%(Revenue decline - 10%) x 0.625(e.g., (30% revenue decline - 10%) x 0.625 = 12.5% subsidy rate)(Revenue decline - 10%) x 0.625(e.g., (30% revenue decline - 10%) x 0.625 = 12.5% subsidy rate)(Revenue decline - 10%) x 0.25(e.g., (30% revenue decline - 10%) x 0.25 = 5% subsidy rate)Program Details:If a lockdown period is 1 week or longer, applicants may qualify for lockdown support even if the minimum lockdown period of 1 week overlaps 2 different claim periods;Subsidies for affiliated entities with expenses over the maximum $300,000, the applicant will need to divide the maximum expenses of $300,000 equally among the various locations;The qualifying periods for CERS will align with the qualifying periods in the Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy (CEWS);Period 8 - September 27 to October 24, 2020, of CEWS will be the 1st period for which the CERS will be in effect.All applications must be made on or before 180s after the end of the qualifying period;If a deadline for a claim period was missed, applicant organizations can ask Canada Revenue Agency to review the late request to apply for the subsidy under exceptional circumstances, including:Evident attempts to apply but there were identified outages of CRA secure portals;The specific account was temporarily suspended or if there were other limitations preventing the filing of the application;Undue delay on the part of the CRA in receiving and processing the subsidy application before the deadline; andThe applicant relied upon inaccurate information provided by the CRA.Applicants may also increase a previously claimed subsidy amount within 180 days after the end of the claim period under certain circumstances, including:Unintentional or arithmetic errors in filing subsidy applications;The applicant relied upon inaccurate information provided by the CRA;Evident attempts to apply but there were identified outages of CRA secure portals; andUndue delay on the part of the CRA in receiving and processing the subsidy application before the deadline.Adjustments or late-filed subsidy applications may be requested to the Business Enquiries phone line within 30 calendar days following the later of:April 21, 2021;       Grant Criteria 
      This program aims to accelerate technology development and deployment that contribute to the 2030 Innovation Target by funding up to 50% of eligible projects to a maximum of $2 million per project. The funding is open to technology developers industry,  industrial associations, small and medium-sized enterprises, research and development (R&D) organizations, post-secondary institutions, municipalities, not-for-profit organizations,   government research labs, and individuals who are seeking funding to advance innovation-commercialization or knowledge generation.Grant Value: 25-50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $2 millionTurnaround Time: 3-6 months (depends on the project dollar size)Eligible Applicants:Be 1 of the following applicant types:Technology developers;Industry;Industrial associations;Small and medium-sized enterprises;Research and development (R&D) organizations;Post-secondary institutions;Municipalities;Not-for-profit organizations;Government research labs; andIndividuals.Not required to be based in Alberta;Must demonstrate a clear value proposition for the province; andBe in 1 of the 5 technology portfolios:Advanced hydrocarbons:Cleaner hydrocarbon production; andInnovative hydrocarbon products.Clean Technology:Renewable and alternative energy;Bioenergy; andCarbon capture, and utilization.Environmental innovation:Land and biodiversity; andWater innovation.Smart agriculture and food; andBioindustrial materials.Eligible Expenses:Labour;Materials;Capital assets and software;Travel;Sub-contractors; andOther.Note: full breakdown of eligible expenses can be found here.Program Details:The program prioritizes technology or knowledge development projects;Technology  solutions  can  originate  from  anywhere  globally  but  must  address  challenges  and  opportunities of importance to Alberta;Projects that will be researched, piloted, demonstrated, and/or implemented in Alberta with long term Alberta-based infrastructure/resources will be prioritized;Technology projects should demonstrate a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 3-7;All applicants are expected to provide a portion of the funding towards a project, which can include cash and in-kind contributions from project partners or other sources of funds;Funding made available through this Process is  provided to support the execution  of  projects  with  well-defined objectives, milestones, deliverables, and timelines;Regular project update meetings will be held with the applicant and the assigned Project Advisor to assess progress towards milestones.There are no restrictions on the number of applications that can be submitted by any applicant; andOnce projects are completed, Alberta Innovates continues to collect information from clients for up to 5-years to assess the economic, environmental, and social benefits realized for Albertans.

        The program has been extended to February 15, 2022, at 11:59 pm;The deadline was previously February 1, 2022.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This Ontario program offers agricultural operations with intensive use of labour up to $15,000 to address immediate health and safety issues related to COVID-19. Eligible reimbursements costs include modifications throughout an agricultural operation, providing personal protective equipment (PPE), cleaning and disinfection, and providing worker accommodations and worksite mobility.Grant value: 60% of expenses up to $15,000 per business or propertyTurnaround time: 10 business daysEligible Applicants:Must be a legal entity in Ontario;Has operations in Ontario;Maintains a Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) client number;Produces agricultural commodities under Farm Business Registration Number (FBRN);Be one of the following businesses:Poultry catchers/vaccinators;Professional barn cleaners;Agri-food industry organizations that are incorporated as a non-profit or similar entity under an Act of Canada, province or territory;Provides off-farm primary packing services for primary agricultural commodities;Corn detasseling services;Farm product wholesaler-distributor;Farm business involving intensive use of labour where workers work in close proximity; andAgricultural operators that provide workers with on- or off-site accommodations.Eligible Activities:Note: Each expense submitted should already have been invoiced to the business and paid for by the business.Minor modifications throughout an agricultural operation, worker/employee housing, or worker/employee transportation systems to promote appropriate safety with regards to physical distancing needs (e.g., physical barriers).Providing workers/employees with rapid COVID-19 antigen testing, personal protective equipment and other approved safety supplies for use throughout an agricultural operation, worker/employee housing or worker/employee transportation systems to prevent disease spread.Cleaning and disinfection throughout an agricultural operation, worker/employee housing or worker/employee transportation systems.Providing arrangements to support worker/employee accommodations and work-site mobility that are necessary to address immediate health and safety issues due to COVID-19.Eligible Expenses:Personal protective equipment (PPE)PPE and other safety supplies for workers/employees (e.g., masks, gloves and other protective gear).There is a limit of $7,500.00 of funding available for PPE expenses.WIFI EquipmentInstallation or upgrade of WIFI equipment on the applicant's property directly related to expanding worker/employee access to WIFI within employer-provided housing/accommodations or worker/employee common areas, to enable physical distancing. This excludes computers, tablets, smartphones or monthly WIFI/wireless communication expenses.There is a limit of $10,000.00 of funding available for new/ upgraded WIFI equipment;A strong COVID-related rationale for this expense must be provided.Physical distancing measuresRetrofits or adjustments to employee housing or workplace modifications to allow for proper health and safety measures and physical distancing;Measures that enable workers/employees to practice physical distancing: minor capital (physical/infrastructure) updates/ renovations, temporary or permanent modifications (e.g., reconfigurations, shielding, barriers, roofs, additional refrigerators, stoves, beds, mattresses, bedding, winterization), and rental of temporary structures;Agriculture/agri-food equipment/machinery that would enable physical distancing.Preventing disease spreadThird-party services to help to prevent disease spread (e.g., third-party services to administer COVID-19 testing outside of the quarantine period, perform COVID-19 related medical checks, third-party cleaning services to increase frequency and extent of cleaning, security);Medical equipment (e.g., body temperature remote sensors, thermometers and cameras; COVID-related testing equipment);Cleaning/disinfection equipment and supplies to increase frequency and extent of cleaning that would help prevent the spread of Covid-19;Vaccination costs not covered by the Government of Canada or the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP);Wearable technology specifically designed to promote social/physical distancing, as well as contact tracing for COVID-19 cases, which alerts users/wearers within a workplace who have been in close contact with individuals who have tested positive for COVID-19. This does not include funding for multi-purpose technology such as smartwatches, smart phones or other devices which include an entertainment or communication function.AccommodationsShort-term accommodations (e.g., hotel room rentals, dorm rentals, house rental/lease, trailer purchases) to enable physical distancing best practices and allow workers/employees to attend workplaces;Hotel room rentals and dorm rentals are limited to a maximum of $80/day/worker/employee;Rental or lease of housing to support worker safety related to COVID-19 for the duration of the renovations to employee housing.TransportationCOVID-related worksite mobility and transportation expenses to enable workers/employees to access the work site or vaccine clinics and transportation to/from airport to meet quarantine requirements (e.g. car rental/bus rental/taxi services).Enhanced sanitization and disinfectionIncludes only innovative sanitization and disinfection techniques and technologies (e.g. UV sterilization technologies) to help prevent the spread of COVID-19.Translation services for training, testing and vaccinationsArm's length translation services required for COVID-related training, testing and COVID-19 vaccinations.Air circulation and filtration in enclosed work environmentsNew/upgraded COVID-19 related air circulation and air filtration systems, HVAC modifications or upgrades required for enclosed work environments.Ineligible Expenses:Expenses to address usual business practices, expansion or any other non-COVID-19 related objectives (includes toilet paper, paper towel, garbage bags etc.);Expenses related to retail or other on-site sales activities;Expenses for activities/practices that are not in accordance with any standard or guideline of an appropriate authority (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Labour);Monthly WIFI/wireless communication expenses;Rental costs for new processing facilities;In-kind contributions;Legal fees; andProfessional services not necessary for the eligible activity.Note: For the full list of ineligible expenses, please review the webpage here.Program Details:Incremental expenses specifically required for the implementation of eligible activities that guard against the spread of COVID-19 are:Ordered on or after January 1, 2021, and received on or after March 13, 2021;Goods/services are received, projects are completed, invoiced, and paid for prior to the date of submission of an application or February 1, 2022.Procured through a transaction with a third-party that is at Arm's Length from the business that incurred and paid for the expense; andProcured through a process that is transparent, fair, and promotes the best value for the money expended at competitive prices no greater than fair market value after deducting available discountsApplication Process: Applicants will need to complete Transfer Payment Common Registration (TPCR) and Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) registrations before the government of Ontario can accept this submission form;Upon approval, the applicants should receive the funds in 10 business days;If the applicant currently owe any money to Ontario, they will need a description of the business' debt to Ontario is attached to the submission form;Submissions should be emailed to AgRuralPrograms@ontario.ca and not submitted via Adobe Cloud; andApplicants should retain all records relating to any payments made to the business, including all invoices and proof of payment for at least 7 years from the date the submission form was submitted.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Amounts of funding sourced from federal, provincial, and municipal governments for a submitted expense do not exceed 100% of the amount of the expense;Please download the submission form and fill out the form using Adobe software, not on your internet browser;Any payments made to the business may be subject to recovery or offset against the business' pre-existing debts to the Crown in Right of Ontario or of Canada. Ontario may charge interest on any money owing by the business at the then current rate charged by Ontario on accounts receivable; and No officer, director or employee of the business, or other beneficiaries of the expenses, is a current or former federal public office holder or federal public servant;Forms: Program website: click hereSubmission form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program provides up to $17,500 for commercial farm business operations and primary agriculture producers with less than $60,000 revenue in the 2 previous years (2018 & 2019) to purchase commercial farm infrastructure and equipment. It is intended to help the commercial farm operations achieve income growth, ensure commercial viability and strength financial stability. Be aware that the program intake timeframe is only 1 week (Dec 7 to Dec 15, 2020).Grant Value: 50% - 75% up to $17,50075% for the first $10,000 of project costs50% for costs between $10,000 - $30,000Note: For project costs of $30,000: applicants will receive $7,500 for the first $10,000 + $10,000 for the remaining $20,000 for a total of $17,500. Neither a farm business nor an applicant may apply for more than one project.Eligible Expenses:Commercial farm infrastructure and equipment, including but not limited to:New and used farm equipment from recognized farm equipment dealer;Small-scale irrigation systems;Electric, stackyard, and cross-fencing (maximum contribution: $12.00 per meter); Food packing equipment;Food safety equipment (ie. wash stations)Infrastructure to extend growing season (e.g. poly tunnels)Projects with eligible expenses of $1,000 or more; andAll businesses must purchase from vendors not related to the applicant, not affiliated with the applicant (must be arm's length).Ineligible Expenses:Costs incurred prior to approval;GST and/or interest payments;Normal and ongoing operating expenses;ie. staff salaries, maintenance costs etc.Consultant or advisory services;Productive farm units (e.g., breeding stock, perennial plants, root stock, beehives, etc.);Variable expenses for agriculture product (e.g., fertilizer, chemicals, livestock, seed, feed, fuel, etc.)Community gardens for individual consumption;Land and facilities rent;Raising domestic animals;Agri-tourism initiatives;Forestry products;Waste recovery;Horseback riding lessons;  Government program payments or other non-commodity income; andPerimeter fencing.Note: Costs incurred before approval or after the project completion date are not eligible for reimbursement.Program Details:By the time the proposed project completes, must have either:Received a Statement of Completion or Implementation from the Environmental Farm Plan Program OR;Commit to apply for and complete an Environmental Farm Plan assessment within a year of completing the Small Farm Business Acceleration Program.In-kind contributions are eligible for the farmer's cost-shared portion, these include but are not limited to:Staff hours for installation of equipment or infrastructure (limited to $20/hour);Machinery - small equipment and operator labour (limited to $60/hour);Hand tools and motorized tools of 25 horsepower or greater;Farm tractor and implements up to 80 horsepower such as skid steer.Machinery - medium equipment and operator labour (limited to $90/hour);Farm tractor and implements of 80 - 120 horsepower such as tandem axle dump truck.Machinery - large equipment and operator labour (limited to $140/hour);Farm tractor and implements greater than 120 horsepower such as excavators, loader backhoe or land scraper.Projects can include more than 1 equipment or infrastructure item as long as they meet a common purpose of growing the business;The application package must include the following documents:Small Farm Business Acceleration Pilot Program Application;Business Plan;Growth plan;Project budget and partial budget;Partial budget helps estimate the net change in income of a business as a result of the project.       Grant Criteria 
      This program provides a wage subsidy of up to $7,000 for internships for employers operating in any industry sector. Up to 70% of the new employee’s salary is offered for post-secondary students where a work placement is part of their study plan. The program aims to help to bridge the gap between formal post-secondary learning and the skill requirements of Canadian employers.Grant Value:50% of wages up to $5000 per regular participant;70% of wages up to $7,000 per participant in any of the following under-represented groups:Women in STEM or business;Indigenous students;Visible minorities;Recent immigrants (immigrated to Canada within the last 5 years);Persons with disabilities;First-year students;Students on their first work term. Turnaround Time: 15 business daysEligible Employers:Be a registered Canadian business or non-profit;Have Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) or alternate workplace insurance coverage;Committed to paying the student for the role for the duration of the placement in full;In compliance with all federal and provincial human rights and labour legislation, regulations, and any other relevant standards including the Occupational Health and Safety Act and the Employment Standards Act;Employers in all industries may apply; andMust place participants on payroll (must make CPP, EI, and vacation pay contributions).Ineligible Employers:Federal, provincial, territorial or municipal governments;Crown corporations;Hospitals;Post-secondary institutions; andMajor financial sector employers.Eligible Candidates:Registered as a full- or part-time domestic student in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Master's or PhD students are eligible;International students are ineligible.Registered in any program of study;Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or protected persons;Registered in a class with work-integrated learning (WIL) component as part of their study plan;Must send a signed document from the post-secondary institution indicating the student is registered in a program/course where a work-integrated learning component is part of their study plan (e.g. co-op document, letter, etc.);Ideally, the documents should state the school term, the program enrolled, start and end dates,  etc; andTranscripts are generally not acceptable.Cannot be a family member of the employer; andCannot be part of another Student Work Placement Program simultaneously.Note: Apprenticeships are ineligible for program funding.Placement Details:Wage subsidy will apply to gross wages between:Winter 2025 - January 1, 2025, to April 30, 2025: No funding AvailableSummer 2025 - May 1, 2025 to August 31, 2025: CLOSEDFall 2025 - September 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025: OPENFull-time or part-time;Eligible forms of Work-Integration Learning:Internships;Field placements;Part-time/short-term intensive hands-on practical experience in a setting relevant to their subject of study.Co-operative education;Alternating academic terms and paid work terms.Apprenticeships;Note: Apprenticeships in a skilled trade are not eligible under this program;Community and industry research/projects;Research that occurs primarily in workplaces, includes consulting projects, design projects, and community-based research projects.Entrepreneurship;Engage in the early-stage development of business start-ups and/or to advance external ideas that address real-world needs for academic credit.Mandatory practicum/clinic placement; andWork experience under the supervision of an experienced registered or licensed professional (e.g. preceptor) in any discipline that requires practice-based work experience for professional licensure or certification.Community service-learning.Meaningful community service with classroom instruction and critical reflection to enrich the learning experience and strengthen communities.No maximum participants per company;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Work from home placements are eligible;Placements will be counted in the term they start in;Employers can still receive funding for placements with start dates outside the academic term; andEmployers cannot postpone placements and will need to ensure placement(s) occur before the agreement end date or request an agreement extension.

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program provides up to $500,000 in funding to increase the development, scale up and expansion of B.C. agritech companies and technologies. The goal of the program is to attract and retain investments to B.C. that create jobs for British Columbians and to further build B.C's reputation as a top agritech jurisdiction. Agricultural technology, or agritech, is the use of technology in agriculture, horticulture, and aquaculture and this program supports products, services, or application improvements that result in betterment of input or output processes. Examples include: Agricultural biotechnologyFarm roboticsDronesSatellite photography and sensorsPhase trackingWeather forecastsAutomated irrigationLighting and heat controlIntelligent software analysis for pest and disease prediction or soil managementGrant Value: 75% of project activities up to a maximum of $500,000Turnaround time: up to 3 months (applicants will be notified in March 2021)Eligible Applicants:The business’s sole or primary operations are located in B.C or a company from outside of B.C. that has an intention to establish operations in B.C. within the near-term;Is registered or has the intention to establish in B.C. before March 31, 2021;Technology or agritech company or agricultural producer or agrifood company;Pays taxes in B.C. or will pay taxes in B.C;Employs a minimum of 10 B.C. residents, for a minimum of four months of the calendar year or intends to employ up to 10 B.C. residents within the near-term;Have a payroll account number with the Canada Revenue Agency;Have a Goods and Services Tax number with the Canada Revenue Agency;Have a WorkSafeBC registration number;Have a provincial Sales Tax number;Has at least 25% of total project costs secured from industry, self-funding, private-sector contribution or the federal government;In-kind contributions are ineligible.Business license and all other operating licenses as required; andDisclosure of applications to other provincial and federal funding programs will also be required.Note: For joint project proposals, only one of the B.C. producers can submit an application on behalf of the group.Eligible Activities:Business management:Hiring, training B.C.-based staff to scale operations;IT implementation/facilities upgrades which may include the testing or demonstration of an IT system or products like sensors and or data visualization within an agrifood producer’s operations; andImproving governance, best management practices.Prototype, pilot or demonstration of new technology:Developing, assessing, adapting or adopting new technology; andProductivity improvement.Commercialization of new technology, products or services:Supporting patenting;IP protection;Certification; andTesting of products.Research and industry partnerships:Applied research collaboration involving researchers, farmers, industry associations, educational institutions, technical experts, etc.; andPilot, demonstration projects.Investment attraction:Joint venture or business alliance between a B.C. company and external partner premised on anchoring and establishing an international partner’s operations in B.C.; andActivities to access new markets and customers.Eligible Costs:Capital expenditures required for the execution of the project:Purchase or lease of machinery and equipment and installation of infrastructure.Capital expenditure required for the execution of the project;Purchase or lease of machinery and equipment and installation of infrastructure;Contracted services:Professional, consulting, and/or technical services.Salaries & benefits:Project-specific cost of labour.Other direct project costs:Pre-production costs (e.g. technological developments and commercial demonstrations);Commercialization costs. (e.g. marketing, sales, customer service and support);Costs of licensing or developing intellectual property;Production of business management, marketing and promotional tools;Rental or lease of facilities;Shipping and transportation materials and services; andConstruction, operating, business and similar licenses and permits required for project.Projects that are already underway may be eligible if the requested funding is for a new phase of an ongoing initiative, so long as the work has not already been completed or has been fully funded already.Ineligible Costs:Any costs deemed not reasonable and/or not directly related to the eligible project activities;Capital expenditures not specifically required for the execution of the project;GST, sales, income and other taxes, interest and principal payments on loans;Costs incurred before approval of project or after project completion date (as specified on the approval of your application);Acquisition of land and buildings;Hospitality (e.g. meals, entertainment, gifts, etc.); andAny cost that is ineligible or unsupported under the grant letter.Program Details:Successful applicants will be required to provide progress reports on the following matters:Progress reports:Activities completed and progress made towards deliverables, as described in the Project Work Plan.Performance reports:The reports will track progress against mutually agreed upon performance measures outlined in the Contribution Agreement.Financial reports:To ensure funding is being applied to eligible costs and activities.Final report:Required detailing progress, performance and financial highlights over the project duration; andShould include contributory outcomes, economic impacts and learnings from the project.Detailed project milestones will be outlined in the contribution agreement and successful applicants will need to demonstrate that they can meet the determined milestones;Projects may subject to a final audit either by government or a third-party;Assessment Criteria:Economic potential:Number of jobs that will be created, and projected wage category of those jobs;Estimated revenue growth for the company from the project;Estimated net revenue resulting from the project for B.C.; andIndirect economic benefits such as partnerships or collaboration projects that support more than one company and create indirect employment.Intellectual Property (IP), Scalability:Identify the creation and anchoring of intellectual property within B.C;demonstrate a high probability of scalability either in terms of production growth or applications across multiple industry functions or crops.Timeframe, Budget Implications:Ability to implement the project within the proposed timeframe and within the identified budget;Demonstrated project viability through the project description, risk mitigation, market assessment and implementation readiness; andComposition of the management team and their probability of success.Priority Considerations:Applicants with:Raised seed or angel investor funding or series A funding of less than $5 million;Net revenue between $1-5 million or evidence of paying customers. Of note this does not require the company to be profitable; andRevenue or staff growth of at least 20% over the past three years.Partnerships with Indigenous businesses or regional communities experiencing high unemployment rates (based on B.C.Stats data) will be given priority; andDemonstrate sustainable or regenerative agricultural technologies will also be given priority.

Applicants may withdraw their proposal at any time with written notice; andAgritech grants are considered taxable income under the Canada Revenue Agency.       Grant Criteria 
      This program helps employers offset the cost of training for new or existing employees to gain the skills in a sector where jobs opportunities have been most impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.  Eligible participants include unemployed persons, employees at risk of losing their jobs, or employees who need training to obtain a better or different job. The program offers up to 100% of training costs to a maximum of $10,000 per person. When the type of farm activity cannot be distinguished between crop and livestock.Be in one of the following circumstances:Be unemployed but will be employed upon completion of training;Employed by the applicant employer and requiring new skills for the survival/recovery/growth of the business;Employed by another employer but working reduced hours due to COVID-19 and will be employed full-time upon completion of training.Must be Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and protected persons;Be at least 16 years old at the time of application; andEmployer provided programs.Training towards attaining a diploma or degree (in full or in part);All maintenance training (training needed to maintain current skills/certification);Simultaneous training (enrollment in another government-funded training program while participating in ETG);Repeat funding for training (funding for the same training that was previously funded by ETG); andHave started prior to the application being submitted.Eligible Costs:Tuition fees;Mandatory student fees;Examination fees, when attached to a training program;Textbooks, software and other required materials;Travel costs, only under certain circumstances; andThe mode of transportation must be economical.Meal allowances.Ineligible costs:Membership fees, subscription fees, annual fees, professional association dues;Software purchase/license for the business;Laptops, tablets, and other hardware;Equipment (e.g. boots and tools);       Grant Criteria 
      This federal challenge aims to develop new technologies to meet evolving industry requirements to ensure safe and efficient work environments for its labour force, and to increase operational efficiencies and maintain food safety standards. Proposed technologies must include advances in automation through robotics, artificial intelligence, or other forms of innovation that are scalable and suitable to each sub-sector within the processing industry, such as stunning, slaughtering; butchering; grading; cutting; and packaging.Grant Value:Phase 1 Grant: $150,000Phase 2 Grant: $1,000,000Eligible Applicants:For profit companies;Incorporated in Canada (federally or provincially);499 or fewer full-time equivalent (FTE) employees*;Research and development activities must take place in Canada;50% or more of its annual wages, salaries and fees are currently paid to employees and contractors who spend the majority of their time working in Canada*;50% or more of its FTE employees have Canada as their ordinary place of work*; and50% or more of its senior executives (Vice President and above) have Canada as their principal residence*.* Includes affiliated businesses, i.e. parent and subsidiary companies.Program Details:Phase 1:The maximum duration for any Phase 1 project funded by a grant resulting from this Challenge is up to 6 months;Cannot exceed Technology Readiness Level 4.Phase 2:Only eligible businesses that have completed Phase 1 could be considered for Phase 2;The maximum duration for any Phase 2 project funded by a grant resulting from this Challenge is up to 24 months.Proposed solutions must:Allow meat processors to integrate alternative or non-traditional methods of re-engineering current meat processing tasks, whether single worker task or multi worker tasked processes, leading to increased productivity, profitability or worker safety;Introduce a technology that utilizes automation through robotics, artificial intelligence or other advanced features;Integrate technology that is capable of running in meat processing plants considering all types of environmental conditions related to humidity and temperature; andEnsure the new technology adheres to all regulations (federal or provincial) connected to worker health and safety standards including new COVID-related protocols in meat processing facilities.Proposed solutions should:Increase accessibility, meaning that meat processing facilities regardless of scale can purchase and implement the technology in a method that is not financially prohibitiveSelected companies are eligible to receive one grant per phase per challenge;Program Process:Review eligibility criteria;Create your profile and begin proposing solutions using the "Propose a Solution" button. Please note that challenges are available for applications at various times, be sure to check the deadline to ensure your application is accepted;An evaluation process will be conducted and selected innovators could receive up to $150,000 to develop a proof of concept;Develop a proof of concept;Evaluation of the proof of concept. Successful small businesses could receive up to an additional $1 million to develop the prototype;Once the prototype is complete, participants are on the pathway to commercialization. The Government of Canada could be your first customer, or you could be ready to advance to the marketplace.Best Practices:The application is long and includes mandatory descriptions of scope, project plan,  project risks, financial proposals, implementation team, benefits to Canada, innovation, and commercialization approach. Applicants are advised to prepare well ahead of the deadline;Proposals must meet all mandatory criteria identified by achieving a "Pass" in order to proceed to Part 2. Proposals that do not meet all mandatory criteria will be deemed non-responsive and given no further consideration;For Part 2, proposals must meet the overall minimum pass mark of 50% to be deemed responsive. Proposals that do not achieve the minimum pass mark will be declared non-responsive and given no further consideration; andConsiderations should be given for the participation of under-represented groups  in the research and development of the proposed solution.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Program website: click here;Applicant Guide: click here;Application Portal: click here.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers a wage subsidy of 50% up to $50,000 for Alberta employers to hire a new highly qualified technical or business professional for 12 months. Employers must be an incorporated small or start-up company. The program is intended to enable the use of geospatial technologies in addressing local, national and global challenges.Grant Value:50% of wages up to $50,000 Turnaround time: 2-3 weeksEligible Employers:Must be a for-profit company;Incorporated and operating in Alberta;Minimum of 1 and no more than 50 full-time employees;Annual sales revenues can not exceed $5MM.Eligible Candidates:Must be living in Alberta;Must be highly educated with a Bachelors Degree or higher from a recognized university program;Be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident of Canada at the time of application;The position must be associated with the development and/or commercialization of innovative geospatial technologies;Must be added to the current and recent activity of the company, and can not be a replacement for a recently (within three months) departed employee, contractor or consultant;Can either be technical (Engineer, developer, etc.) or business-focused (sales, market, etc.);May not be related to any senior manager, officer, director or principal shareholder of the applicant company; andExecutive, co-founder, or partner-level positions are also non-eligible.Ineligible Expenses:Bonuses;Benefits; andOther expenses or fringe costs.Program Details:Placement duration: 12 months;Placement of the approved candidate must take place within 2 months of notification of award, otherwise, the application will be considered void and a new application will be required;Positions should be to serve a long-term business need(s) within the applicant company (i.e. beyond the period funded by TECTERRA);Positions previously or currently funded through any and all other TECTERRA, federal and/or provincial funding programs of any kind (partially or fully, directly or indirectly) are ineligibleSalary must align with recognized industry standards;Applications may be submitted prior to the hiring of the candidate;The placement start date of approved candidates must take place within 6 months of the award notification;Upon the start of employment and during the term of TECTERRA’s funding, the candidate must be a resident of Alberta;The application must be submitted by an Officer or a Director of the company;Reimbursements are made monthly on receipt of proof of salary payment for the candidate along with a brief monthly report;Application Process:Companies submit an online application through the online client portal here;Applications are reviewed within 2-3 weeks of submission;Receive notification of award from TECTERRA and begin the 60 day hiring period;Enter Due Diligence phase, submitting all required documents to TECTERRA;Sign a Funding Agreement;Hire the candidate.Assessment Criteria:Geospatial technology:Will the new HQP (highly skilled personnel) be associated with and add significant value to the ongoing development and/or commercialization of innovative geospatial technology?Will the HQP expand or provide new geospatial capabilities within the applicant organization?Will the HQP accelerate your go-to-market plan?Will the HQP increase the likelihood of commercial success for your product?Program Readiness:Is the job description understandable with clear short, medium, and long-term objectives?Can the applicant support the position during the placement?Can the applicant support the position after the placement?Additional Criteria:How will this type of funding assist the applicant?What is the financial impact that this HQP will have on your organization?Preference will be given to applications where the candidate’s degree is at the post-graduate level (i.e. Ph.D., Masters, or MBA).

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program provides up to $50,000 to B.C. societies, companies, and individuals to support the production of high-quality, original, interactive digital media projects, content, and software applications, aiming to position BC artists for promising new markets. Funded projects should be interactive, educational, suitable for commercial exploitation, and intended for a digital media platform, network, or device that is capable of interactivity or a gallery setting.Grant Value: Up to $50,000. Turnaround time: 14 weeks after the application deadline. Eligible Applicants:Be either:Incorporated companies;Be incorporated in BC or Canada with its head office in BC.Have a majority of the issued common voting shares held by BC residentsNon-profit societies (be incorporated under the Society Act);Incorporated under the Society Act;With its head office in BC.Collectives;Unincorporated, groups, ensembles, or collectives of three or more individual professional
artists or cultural practitioners, where the majority of members are B.C. residents.Individual creators.Has resided in BC for at least 200 of the 365 days prior to the application;Have filed income tax returns in BC for the tax year prior to the application.Maintain a harassment-free workplace;Be in compliance with the Worker's Compensation Act and applicable Occupational Health and Safety Regulations;Have a history of producing, creating, or experimenting with digital or screen-based media for interactive platforms, exhibitions, networks, or devices; and100% of the copyright of the project being developed must be owned and controlled by the lead applicant. Exceptions may be granted where co-productions or partnerships exist demonstrating that the copyright ownership granted to the BC applicant is commensurate to the BC applicant’s financial, technical, and creative contribution and control.Eligible Projects:Primarily digital and interactive;For use by individuals or groups;Interactive and allow users to make choices that impact their experience;Educational, informative, or entertaining;Suitable for commercial exploitation and/or broad dissemination; andIntended for experience by the end-user on a digital media platform, network, device that is capable of interactivity or gallery setting;Including but not limited to the following:Digital-based art installations; Interactive websites;Interactive narrative content;Virtual Reality/Augmented Reality experiences; andMobile/tablet applications and games.Eligible Costs:Market research;Labour and personnel;Technology content and design;Expenses required to put content online, including copyright clearance, documentation, design, and development;Technical and administrative expenses; Travel costs((i.e. accommodation, airfare, per diem) directly associated with building the project); andCosts directly associated with operating during the COVID-19 pandemic (i.e. PPE, testing, cleaning, etc.)Ineligible Costs:Purchase of equipment (Capital Expenses) not essential to the project;Production of a live-action film or television program;Travel costs (i.e. accommodation, airfare, per diem) not associated with building the project i.e. marketing, distribution, promotions, events or workshops; andCorporate overhead and administrative expenses not associated with the project.Program Details:Application checklist:Work plan;Budget (template provided);Production schedule (template provided); andProof of financing via bank statements or paid invoices.Additional checklist for companies:Certification of incorporation;1 page corporate profile;Links to a maximum of 3 projects within the last 3 years; andChain of title (template provided).Additional checklist for non-profits:Certificate of incorporation under the Society Act;List of board of directors;One page profiles including a mandate for the applicant, co-applicant, and service providers;Links to a maximum of 3 projects within the last 3 years; andChain of title.Additional checklist for individual artists:Bio and CV (maximum 2 pages);Links to a maximum of 3 projects within the last 3 years; andChains of title or declaration of ownership.The program is competitive and does not accept applications on a first-come, first-served basis.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices: The program does not allow for retroactive use of funds;The Work Plan should be a succinct six-pages, include images and or charts;All costs associated with the project do not have to be incurred in BC, however, featuring BC talent may benefit an application;The presence of other confirmed funding, including cash investment from the applicant, may benefit an application;An applicant may submit one application as the lead. Applicants may be attached as a service provider on several projects, however, Applicants may only have ownership in one project;The program adjudication is competitive and is based on the quality of the application. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Applications will be reviewed based on the following criteria:Experience of applicant individual, company or society and their key personnel;Diversity (as defined below);Creativity and originality of the Project;Goal Statement(which will be captured in the online application);Marketing and or distribution strategy; andProposed project budget and finance plan (revenue, grants, etc.)The Interactive Fund will prioritize applications from equity-seeking groups including attitudinal, historic, social, and environmental barriers based on age, ethnicity, disability, economic status, gender, nationality, race, sexual orientation and transgender status, etc.;Creative BC will do a look-through to the shareholders of the applicant company. If an individual is a majority shareholder in multiple applicant companies, they will be asked to withdraw all but one submission;The program cannot make exceptions based on when you found out about the fund. Late or incomplete applications will not be accepted; andCreative BC reserves the option to reduce the amount of funding per successful application should we choose to award funds to more applicants.Program website: click hereProgram FAQ: click here

      Grant Type

      Regions

      Industries

      Grant Criteria 
      This Ontario program offers agricultural operations with intensive use of labour up to 60% funding up to $100,000 to address immediate health and safety issues related to COVID-19. Eligible reimbursements costs include modifications throughout an agricultural operation, providing personal protective equipment (PPE), cleaning and disinfection and costs related to worker training and safety protocols.Grant Value: 60% funding up to $100,000 per business or propertyTurnaround time: 15 business daysEligible Applicants:Must be a legal entity in Ontario;Maintains a Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) client number;Produces agricultural commodities under Farm Business Registration Number (FBRN);Must involve intensive use of labour where workers may operate within close proximity of one another, or where the operator is responsible for providing workers with on- or off-site accommodations; andAquaculture farm businesses are not eligible for funding under this project category for the On-Farm Worker Safety Improvement Program.Eligible Activities:Retrofit or adjustments to existing operations to cover extraordinary costs associated with COVID-19 to ensure worker safety:Workspace adjustments to allow for proper safety measures and physical distancing;Enhancement to required employer-provided housing for workers as a result of COVID-19 to ensure worker safety;Support for temporary housing arrangements for workers in cases where existing facilities cannot adequately allow or be modified to allow for physical distancing;Training workers on COVID-19 safety protocols (e.g. interpretation, materials, external support.).Eligible Expenses:Modifications to the operations:Added sanitation (cleaning and disinfection) and security requirements;Adjustments to current processes and processing stations to accommodate physical distancing;Adjustment to transportation to ensure physical distancing during movement within the operation or between accommodations and the operation;HVAC modifications or upgrades;Equipment such as safety barriers (e.g. Plexiglass dividers);Purchase/rental/lease of additional on- or off-site housing and ancillary buildings (e.g., washrooms, kitchens, laundry facilities) for workers, portable or relocatable buildings, and/or installations/site modifications related to COVID-19 measures;Site modifications and/or transportation for wellness checks; andDisinfection and cleaning in the event of an outbreak.Non-disposable personal protective equipment (PPE) that were not part of normal operations before COVID-19:Body temperature screening/fever detection systems, including thermal scanners;Washing stations;Workstation dividers;Full and half facepiece respirators;Impact goggles and face shields;Face masks and coverings; andSafety glasses.Costs related to worker training and safety protocols:Interpretation services; andTraining on COVID-19 protocols.Note: Expenses must be incrementalIneligible Expenses:Expenses to address usual business practices, expansion or any other non-COVID-19 related objectives;Expenses related to retail or other on-site sales activities;Taxes, including Harmonized Sales Tax;Expenses of permits and approvals;Meal expenses.Note: Please visit the program website for the exhaustive list of ineligible expenses.Program Details:Have a written plan that documents steps in place to limit the spread of disease throughout the operation. The written plan must be supported by the relevant union or health and safety committee;Expenses must be incurred on or after March 15, 2020, invoiced and paid for prior to submission;Materials and services must be procured through a transaction with a third-party that is not related, not affiliated, or otherwise controlled by another member from the business that incurred and paid for the expense; andMaterials and services must be procured through a process that is transparent, fair and promotes the best value for the money expended at competitive prices no greater than fair market value after deducting available discounts.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Amounts of funding sourced from federal, provincial, and municipal governments for a submitted expense do not exceed 100% of the amount of the expense;Incomplete submissions or ineligible applicant's submissions will not be considered;Applicants will need to complete Transfer Payment Common Registration (TPCR) and Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) registrations before the government of Ontario can accept this submission form;Please download the submission form and fill out the form using Adobe software, not on your internet browser;Any payments made to the business may be subject to recovery or offset against the business' pre-existing debts to the Crown in Right of Ontario or of Canada. Ontario may charge interest on any money owing by the business at the then-current rate charged by Ontario on accounts receivable;If the applicant currently owe any money to Ontario, they will need a description of the business' debt to Ontario is attached to the submission form;No officer, director or employee of the business, or other beneficiaries of the expenses, is a current or former federal public office holder or federal public servant; andApplicants should retain all records relating to any payments made to the business, including all invoices and proof of payment for at least 7 years from the date the submission form was submitted.Program website: click hereElectronic submission form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program offers employers a maximum of $18,700 wage and training subsidy to provide employer-delivered, work-site training opportunities to individuals with barriers to employment or individuals with limited or no work experience. The intent is to enable unemployed individuals with barriers to employment to acquire essential skills and occupation-related skills required which will allow for meaningful participation within the labour market.Grant Value: a maximum of 100% subsidy up to $11,700 plus an additional $7,000 supplemental training subsidyTurnaround Time:Eligible Employers:Be located in Alberta;Eligible Participants:Have required Canadian work rights;Documentation indicating that the participant is in Alberta on a temporary basis cannot be accepted for job training or employment services.Be 18 years of age or older;Be unemployed;Be in one of the following circumstances:Experience barriers to obtaining and maintaining employment; ORHave limited or no experience in competitive employment; ORLacking the minimum qualifications that employers require.Seek and accept employment after completion; andParticipate in the evaluation process (i.e. surveys, focus groups, etc.)Program Details:2 streams:On-The-Job (OTJ) training stream:Maximum $390/week contribution based on the training plan;Minimum hours per week: 30;Maximum duration: 30 weeks not including breaks;An exception to the full-time requirement may be made for individuals who would benefit from OTJ training for a reduced number of hours to accommodate special needs (e.g. individuals with disabilities)Paid Work Experience (PWE) stream:Maximum contribution: 100% coverage;Hours per week: 40;Maximum duration: 3 weeks;Additional supplemental training subsidy:Maximum $7,000 per individual;Must be provided by an independent school or training organization;May be delivered:In the classroom;Through distance delivery;Accessed and completed at the worksite; orat an off-site location.Must be included as part of the participant's Training Plan based upon assessed need and is not intended to replace training that the employer has agreed to undertake as part of the OTJ training;Supplemental training is training other than that required for apprentices which is a component of their apprenticeship contract and is required by trade regulation.Employment contracts must be in place prior to employers hiring an individual in this program;Apprenticeship training opportunities can be utilized through this program when the skills and abilities of the participant are insufficient to meet the entry-level requirements of the trades; andLabour or contracted service providers will provide information about the Workplace Training position to their local Alberta Apprenticeship and Industry Training office. Alberta Apprenticeship and Industry Training can then follow up with the employer to ensure that the employee is registered as an apprentice when appropriate.Each contract is negotiated based on the needs of the individual, the nature of the job, and the complexity of training provided.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Employers are selected based on their ability to provide OTJ training or to facilitate the PWE component and their ability to provide ongoing employment after the Workplace Training contract is over;Where the participant is not a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, the employer must review and keep written acceptable documentation of this fact; Acceptable documentation include those documents evidencing a right to work as has been granted by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act;No training plan is required for the PWE, and it is expected that the participant will be hired after the program.Forms:Program website: click here

andBe focused on innovation.Eligible Participants:Graduates who have completed a master's or doctoral degree within the last year from the application date;Once hired, the participant must be willing to live and work in Nova Scotia;Cannot have been working for the employer on a permanent basis prior to application approval.Program Details:2 streams:Innovation Stream:Funding:35% of Year 1 salary;20% of Year 2 salary; and12.5% of Year 3 salary.At least 25% of work must be on:Applied research;Product and service development;Market analysis for new complex products or activity;Improvement of product quality, customer services, and business efficiencies;Process development or optimization; andTechnical feasibility studies and pilots for product launches or market entry.Advanced Innovation Stream:Funding:50% of Year 1 salary;25% of Year 2 salary; and12.5% of Year 3 salary.At least 75% of work must be on:Applied research;Product and service development;Market analysis for new complex products or activity;Improvement of product quality, customer services, and business efficiencies;Process development or optimization; andTechnical feasibility studies and pilots for product launches or market entry.The work must also have an explicit connection to export development or growth.An extra 10% of wage subsidy for the 1st year is available for both streams if the participant is a member of an  underrepresented group;Indigenous;Visible minorities;Persons with disabilities; orWomen in under-represented occupationsThe program is intended to support activities that create new opportunities for the market and for the businessAn Innovation Plan will be required to outline the projects and the activities the new employee will undertakeA separate application must be submitted for each participant;Upon approval, the contract must be signed and returned within 2 weeks;At the end of each year of the Agreement, the employer must submit a progress report against the innovation plan to outline the undertook over the year; andProof of payments paid to the graduate must be submitted on the 6th, 18th, and 30th month. Any shortfall will need to be explained.Assessment Criteria:The completeness and clarity of the application;The content of the innovation plan and its ability to articulate the research and innovation focus of the role; andThe likelihood that innovation will lead to an increase in the export of products or services.

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program offers project funding of an average of $3,000,000 to Canadian small- and medium-sized with innovative technologies that have high potential to bring quantifiable benefits to the environment and the economy. Benefits to the environment include solutions for greenhouse gas emissions, reductions in water consumption, or the reduction of water, soil, or air contamination. The program is intended to help Canadian companies compete and be world leaders in clean tech.Grant Value: Up to 40% of project costs, with average contributions up to $4,000,000 over a 5-year periodTurnaround Time: 5 monthsEligible Applicants:Be a Canadian companyPre-commercial small- and medium-sized companies;A minimum of 25% of the eligible costs funded by private organizations (in-kind contributions included);Have innovative technology that has a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 3-8;Have a business plan and market roll-out for eventual profitability and commercialization;Have product validation from a potential customer or end-use partner (see consortium partners below in Project Details);Have an Intellectual Property strategy; andHas not and will not directly or indirectly pay a broker, consultant, or advisor a success-based fee for assistance in obtaining SDTC funding.Eligible Projects:Have the potential to deliver significant and quantifiable environmental benefits;Technology must have never been demonstrated or commercialized in any other country;At least 50% of eligible project costs must be incurred in Canada.Ineligible Projects:Funding for research projects;Project financing for deployment of commercialized technologies (e.g., solar/wind farms, greenhouse construction);The purchase of proven technology from another jurisdiction for use in Canada; andIncremental modifications to existing technologies or processes.Eligible Expenses:Salaries and benefits;Purchase, installation, repair, upgrade, testing, and commissioning of equipment, materials, and products;Licence fees and permits;Shipping costs, including customs costs;Reasonable travel and conference expenses related to the project;Capital items specifically required for the delivery of the project;Including lease of land, data collection equipment, prototypes, pilot plants, or demonstration facilities.Note: The above list is not exhaustive. Please visit the program website for the full list of eligible and ineligible project costs.Program Details:Funding from all levels of government must not surpass 75% of eligible costs;The program requires a minimum of 25% private funding, which can include in-kind contributions from consortium partners;Funding will be disbursed on a milestone basis;Applicants must report the progress made on the specific technical deliverables and metrics outlined in the Contribution Agreement;All project expenses incurred during the milestone period must also be disclosed; andAdditional reporting includes the Environmental Benefits Baseline Report at the end of Milestone 1For each milestone funding disbursed, there will be a standard 10% holdback;Upon project completion, as well as a receipt and acceptance of final project reports and project financial audit, SDTC will release the final 10% holdback.SDTC requires the participation of at least one consortium partner:The consortium partner must be unrelated to the applicants (at arm's length);The partner must also be willing to actively participate in the project. This includes making in-kind contributions, providing a demonstration site and Intellectual Property; andCan be academic, government agencies, associations, industry, or others.For 5 years after project completion, the program will require fund recipients to complete an annual questionnaire to track sales, revenues, jobs created, and other commercial activities.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:The funding from this program can be used in conjunction with funds issued by other government agencies, up to 75% of total project costs;Applicants would be best suited for this program is there is Intellectual Property patents in place.Process Best Practices:Applicants are advised to email applications@sdtc.ca to set up an introductory call; andThe funding recipient should acknowledge SDTC funding in press releases and public statements about the project.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

This program is intended to increase the Government of Canada's support for the growth and scale-up of innovative SMEs.Grant Value:Up to $550,000 for standard componentUp to $1,150,000 for military componentEligible Applicants:Be a Canadian person or entity;Be either a small- and medium-sized enterprise (SME) OR sole proprietor, individual, large business, non-profit, or academic institution;SMEs and non-SMEs will have different calls for proposals.If the applicant is an SME, the applicant must meet these additional criteria:Be for-profit;Have 499 full-time employees or fewer;Have 50% or more of annual wages paid to employees and contractors who work mostly in Canada; and50% or more of its senior executives (vice presidents and above) have Canada as their principal residence.Note: These calculations include affiliated businesses that are either in or outside of Canada.Have a place of business in Canada where activities are conducted on a permanent basis with clearly defined name and working hours;80% of proposed costs must be Canadian goods or services; andHave Intellectual Property (IP) ownership or the license to IP rights from a Canadian Licensor for the proposed innovation.Ineligible Applicants:Applicants with proposal innovation be openly available in the marketplace or previously commercially sold;Applicants with proposal innovation have been previously awarded a contract by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada or Build in Canada Innovation Program (BCIP) or the Canadian Innovation Commercialization Program (CICP);Program Details:This program has 2 components with different priority areas within them:Standard component priority areas:DigitalClean technologyHealthSafety and securityMilitary component priority areas:Digital defence;Cyber operations and resilience;Fully networked command, communications, and control;Countering small unmanned aerial systems (C-sUAS);Enhanced soldier systems - close combat;Training and in-service support (ISS);       Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program provides 100% coverage up to $400,000 to industry organizations and $200,000 to groups in collaboration to recover from COVID-19. The program is intended to strengthen the supply chain and economic recovery needs, funding projects that to increase transparency on end-to-end supply chains, implement activities to improve sector resiliency, and generate new economic opportunities. Grant Value:Industry organizations - 100% up to $400,000Groups of B.C. manufacturers in collaboration - 100% up to $200,000Turnaround Time: Funding decisions will be determined by March 31, 2021Eligible Applicants:For industry organizations:A registered Canadian or B.C. industry, sector, or trade association or organization;Consortium, co-operative, not-for-profit, etc.Have operations, members, and a demonstrated record of supporting manufacturing in BC;Provide a list of members, if applicable.For groups in collaboration:Be a group of 2 or more legally registered entities;Be directly involved in or support manufacturing in BC;Entities may be for-profit and non-profit;At least 1 member must be:A for-profit entity;Be registered in BC; andHave proof of operations in BC.Maintain a Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) number;Have either a letter of commitment from all project partners that outlines proof of cost-sharing and reason for involvement in the proposal; ORA memorandum of understanding signed by all project partners that outlines the agreed-upon deliverables and responsibilities.Applicants must demonstrate certification of incorporation; andMust provide audited financial statements for the last 2 years.Eligible Activities:Must be related to manufacturing, supply chain barriers or supplier barriers;Research to identify supply-chain challenges and opportunities;Solutions to matters such as sourcing, storage, logistics, and distribution;Development of business alliances;Development of a near-term viable strategy;Development of supply chain roadmaps for emerging opportunities;Adoption of technology or best practices for supply chain management and disruption-prevention; agreement period for the grantor to issue payment.

The goal of this program is to increase the inter-provincial and international competitiveness of Nova Scotia businesses by training the workforce to adapt to new technology, machinery and equipment, or work processes.
