      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers up to $100,000 per fiscal year for an employer to provide technical and incremental training for their full-time employees. Generally, WIPSI provides up to 50% of direct training costs to eligible employers. Additional funding may also be granted for any accommodations for disabilities (100%) or some administrative costs (15%) for hosting training that are incurred upon by organizations or associations applying on behalf of their members. The goal of this program is to increase the inter-provincial and international competitiveness of Nova Scotia businesses by training the workforce to adapt to new technology, machinery and equipment, or work processes.Grant Value: Up to $100,000Businesses with 49 employees or fewer:Project minimum size is $5,000;Up to 100% of eligible training costs up to $10,000 per fiscal year; andUp to 50% of eligible training costs for amounts that exceed $10,000, up to a maximum of $100,000 per fiscal year.Businesses with 50  employees or more:Project minimum size is $10,000;Up to 50% of eligible training costs.Organizations, business associations and private sector unions:Minimum application amount is $10,000 in direct training costs;Funding may be available for administration costs as determined on a case-by-case basis.Funding may also cover other expenses like travel (up to 50%) and accommodation costs for persons with disabilities (up to 100%).Turnaround Time: 30 business daysEligible Employers:Registered and active in the NS Registry of Joint Stock Companies or incorporated by an Act of the
Nova Scotia Legislature;Over one calendar year into operations; andGenerating at least 30% of revenue from commercial activity,  unless operating in a LAE identified priority sector.Ineligible Employers:Businesses that are generating profit solely from wholesale, retail, accommodation
and/or food service; andProfessional services such as veterinarians, dentists, lawyers, advertising professionals and consultants, among others; who compete with other NS businesses.Eligible Trainees:Employees (including full-time seasonal) receiving full-time compensation while in training;Be at least 19 years of age; andLive permanently in Nova Scotia.Eligible Expenses:Registration, tuition, course fees, or examination fees;Manuals, books, and support materials;Employee travel costs (up to 50%) where training takes place at least 100 km (each way) from the employee’s regular work site;Costs for accommodations for persons with disabilities (100%); andFor organizations or associations applying on behalf of their members:Administration costs to host training (up to 15% on a case-by-case basis).Eligible Training:Training that is new and/or incremental to the employees and/or the business which will:Result in a new direction and/or expansion to the core operations;Foster skills in the workforce that will support business and/or sector growth, exportability, productivity and/or innovation; and/orCreate more inclusive, welcoming workplaces.Eligible types of training include:Information technology training;Technical training;Workflow systems and processes training; andOther training that will benefit your business or organization and that isn’t typically eligible for funding through other government programs.Ineligible Training:Legislated or regulated mandatory training;Orientation training or onboarding;Training outside the province which has comparable learning outcomes to training available
in NS;Training that could be supported under another Government program, such as the Workplace Education Initiative (WEI);Training that has already been supported by WIPSI;Informal training, and/or training by internal staff or trainers;Training included with the purchase of equipment or new business processes; Apprenticeship training;Conference hosting costs or participation fees; Professional development intended to build an employee’s skills that are considered typically
necessary to operate in their current job (e.g. qualifications or credentials); and Consulting or coaching services intended to assist businesses or organizations with the operation, including assessments to determine the need for training.Program Details:Funding agreements should not exceed 12 months;Trainers must belong to a third party, have appropriate qualifications to provide the training, and cannot be an immediate family member of the principal of the employer; A one or two-time payment schedule is selected during the application process;Applications are submitted through the Labour Market Programs Support System (LaMPSS);Reporting takes place before the first payment, at the end of the project, and one year after training ends; and requests:Annual sales/revenues;Annual training investments; andNumber of employees and total annual salaries paid.The first payment is typically made within 5 business days if all required documents are received, and final payments may take slightly longer depending on the size of the agreement; andEmployers need to fill out a survey after training is delivered and
a follow-up survey one year later.Selection Criteria:The extent to which the training project is linked to a LAE priority sector;The level of benefit the training project delivers during and beyond the project:Number of people directly benefiting from the training;How the training will increase the capability and technical expertise of the workforce;How the project will enable the workforce to better meet economic opportunities; andHow the project will increase opportunities for employees from diverse backgrounds and/or create more welcoming, inclusive workplaces.The value for money offered by the training:Likelihood of the project going ahead without WIPSI funding;Expected return on investment from the training; andThe extent to which the training leverages additional partnerships or in-kind contributions.The applicant's capacity, capability, and resources to carry out the training:The applicant's track record with similar WIPSI funded training; andThe applicant's readiness to start the training.

objectives, and return on investment for both the employer and the province; Amendments to the agreement may be possible after the project has been approved; andApplicants may have the right to appeal the decision if the application has been declined.Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guidelines: click hereApplication login: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This stream of the Invest North Program offers multiple funding options to supply a grant contribution of up to 20% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $400,000 for businesses to grow their existing operations in Northern Ontario. This contribution may also be accompanied or replaced by a repayable contribution in the form of a term loan. The goal of this program is to support projects that will result in full-time job creation or retention, and benefit the overall economic development of the region.Grant Value: 20% of costs up to $400,000Turnaround Time: 6 weeksEligible Applicants:Businesses based anywhere in Ontario who are seeking to expand existing operations in Northern Ontario; andMinimum 1 year of incorporation.Ineligible Applicants:Retail and consumer service businesses that primarily earn revenue by providing products and services directly to individuals;Accommodation & food service businesses and related business activities; andBusinesses that are primarily involved in wholesale activities.Eligible Expenses:Capital construction;Leasehold improvements;New or used equipment including capital leases;Land servicing costs;Information & communications technology (ICT) investments;Marketing for new products and business initiatives (limited to a maximum of 20% of all other eligible project costs, or $75,000, whichever is less); andTraining costs incurred with third parties (limited to a maximum of 20% of all other eligible project costs).Ineligible Expenses:They include but are not limited to the following projects, costs, and activities (some exceptions may be made where projects address a priority economic need in Northern Ontario):Ongoing operating costs including maintenance;In-kind contributions;Restructuring or refinancing of existing business operations;Business plans, strategic plans, feasibility studies, etc.;Assets acquired through operating leases;Research and development;Land purchase/lease;Rolling stock (e.g. cars, trucks & boats and motors);Project management, consulting, and administration costs;Mineral exploration, mine development, and milling operations;Working capital;Cost of inventory;Cellular and internet service projects;Capital projects or leasehold improvements to residential or personal properties;Acquisitions and buy-outs of existing businesses; andElectricity generation projects.Program Details:Funding can be provided through three options:A conditional contribution only of up to 20% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $400,000.A conditional contribution of up to 20% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $400,000, plus a term loan of up to 30% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $600,000.A term loan only of up to 50% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $1,000,000.The applicant is expected to secure the balance of funding or financing necessary to implement the project;The applicant may be required to reimburse NOHFC if assets financed by NOHFC are sold after project completion;The combined federal and provincial government funding (including any contribution from NOHFC) may not exceed 50% of eligible project costs for private sector projects;Agencies that are arms-length from government, with an independent Board of Directors, are not considered “government funding.”If the funding offer involves a secured loan over $100,000, approved applicants are required to retain the services of a lawyer; andApplications will be evaluated in 4 competitive rounds on the following submission deadlines for a detailed business plan:Round 1: April 30;Round 2: July 31;Round 3: October 31; andRound 4: January 31.Evaluation Criteria:Factors that will be considered during evaluation of applications will include but are not limited to:Job creation;Level of investment from other sources to be secured by the applicant;Strength of the applicant’s detailed business plan;Does not unreasonably impact existing Northern Ontario businesses;Net economic benefits for Northern Ontario; andOther business activities that will result in an economic development advantage for Northern Ontario.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Launch Stream of the Invest North Program offers up to 50% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $200,000 for businesses that are starting up operations in Northern Ontario. The goal of this program is to support projects that will result in full-time jobs creation or retention, and benefit the overall economic development of the region.Grant Value: 50% of costs up to $200,000Turnaround time: 4 weeksEligible Applicants:Start-up businesses in Northern Ontario;Have been operating for 6 months or less before they apply; and"Hobby businesses" where the owner intends to work at the business full-time and transition to a full-time sustainable and commercially viable business.Ineligible Applicants:Retail and consumer service businesses that primarily earn revenue by providing products and services directly to individuals;Accommodation & food service businesses and related business activities; andBusinesses that are primarily involved in wholesale activities.Eligible Expenses:Capital construction;Leasehold improvements;New or used equipment including capital leases;Land servicing costs;Information & communications technology (ICT) investments;Marketing for new products and business initiatives (limited to a maximum of 20% of all other eligible project costs, or $75,000, whichever is less); andTraining costs incurred with third parties (limited to a maximum of 20% of all other eligible project costs).Ineligible Expenses:They include but are not limited to the following projects, costs, and activities (some exceptions may be made where projects address a priority economic need in Northern Ontario):Ongoing operating costs including maintenance;In-kind contributions;Restructuring or refinancing of existing business operations;Business plans, strategic plans, feasibility studies, etc.;Assets acquired through operating leases;Research and development;Land purchase/lease;Rolling stock (e.g. cars, trucks & boats and motors);Project management, consulting, and administration costs;Mineral exploration, mine development, and milling operations;Working capital;Cost of inventory;Cellular and internet service projects;Capital projects or leasehold improvements to residential or personal properties;Acquisitions and buy-outs of existing businesses; andElectricity generation projects.Program Details:A new business will be expected to operate on a full-time basis;The entrepreneur/owner must work at the business on a full-time basis;Applicant is expected to secure the balance of funding or financing necessary to implement the project;They are required to contribute (from their own resources) an amount equal to at least 15% of total eligible project costs towards the project.Applicant may be required to reimburse NOHFC if assets financed by NOHFC are sold after project completion;They must retain the assets acquired with program funding for 3 years, or receive prior approval to dispose or move assets outside of Northern Ontario.Combined federal and provincial government funding (including any contribution from NOHFC) may not exceed 50% of eligible project costs for private sector projects;Agencies that are arms-length from government, with an independent Board of Directors, are not considered “government funding.”Evaluation Criteria:Factors that will be considered during evaluation of applications will include but are not limited to:Job creation;Level of investment from other sources to be secured by the applicant;Strength of the applicant’s detailed business plan;Does not unreasonably impact existing Northern Ontario businesses;Net economic benefits for Northern Ontario; andOther business activities that will result in an economic development advantage for Northern Ontario.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Funding from this program may be combined with federal and provincial government funding. However, funding may not exceed 50% of eligible project costs;Tourism businesses that provide accommodation services and operate as a tourist destination for local, regional and international visitors for extended stays (e.g., remote outfitter, family vacation resort) are potentially eligible;Businesses that only serve the overnight travelling public are considered ineligible (e.g. hotels and motels).Process Best Practices:To apply, a screening form is first filled out on the website, which will then prompt the applicant to prepare a robust business case with documentation on current financial and business operations;Recommended to have bridge funding between start of project and reimbursement payments, which are negotiated during project approval.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication form: click here

The goal of this program is to invest in projects that will result in full-time jobs creation or retention, and benefit the overall economic development of the region.Grant Value: Up to $5,000,000Turnaround Time: 4 weeksEligible Applicants:Canadian businesses from outside Ontario aiming to locate business operations in Northern Ontario; andBusinesses that are primarily involved in wholesale activities.Eligible Expenses:Capital construction;Leasehold improvements;New or used equipment including capital leases;Land servicing costs;Information & communications technology (ICT) investments;Marketing for new products and business initiatives (limited to a maximum of 20% of all other eligible project costs, or $75,000, whichever is less); andTraining costs incurred with third parties (limited to a maximum of 20% of all other eligible project costs).Ineligible Expenses:They include but are not limited to the following projects, costs, and activities (some exceptions may be made where projects address a priority economic need in Northern Ontario):Ongoing operating costs including maintenance;In-kind contributions;Restructuring or refinancing of existing business operations;Business plans, strategic plans, feasibility studies, etc.;Assets acquired through operating leases;Research and development;Land purchase/lease;Rolling stock (e.g. cars, trucks & boats and motors);Project management, consulting, and administration costs;Mineral exploration, mine development, and milling operations;Working capital;Cost of inventory;Cellular and internet service projects;Capital projects or leasehold improvements to residential or personal properties;Acquisitions and buy-outs of existing businesses; andElectricity generation projects.Program Details:The applicant is expected to secure the balance of funding or financing necessary to implement the project;The applicant may be required to reimburse NOHFC if assets financed by NOHFC are sold after project completion;       Grant Criteria 
      This highly demanded federal program offers employers a maximum of $22,540 to hire a digital intern and provide training for soft and technical skills. It is intended to provide post-secondary graduates (aged 15-30 years old) with work experience and valuable skills to increase productivity and competitiveness in the economy's workforce. Grant Value: 100% of wages to a maximum of $22,540Turnaround Time: 15 business daysEligible Employers:For-profit and non-profits;Have less than 500 employees;Have General Liability Insurance;Have participants on payroll;Cannot have previously participated in ICTC’s Youth Dividend program;Must have the appropriate administrative support and capacity to train and mentor the participants to enhance and maximize their experience; andMust provide support for the youth intern to complete the soft skills and technical training requirements for the Youth Dividend program.Eligible Participants:Be 18-30 at the start of the internship;Canadian Citizen, Permanent Resident or protected persons;Have completed post-secondary education and not pursuing any post-secondary studies at the time of the program;Be unemployed or underemployed (employed below their level of education, or outside their field of study, or hold part-time employment);Have not previously worked for the employer;Have a good command of 1 of Canada's official languages (minimum CLB 7); andCannot have previously participated in Digital Skills for Youth (DS4Y) program.Program Details:Minimum hours/week: 35;Minimum placement duration: 26 weeks;Maximum 1 application per employer;Has online soft skills training and hard skills training in one of the following streams:Software development;Data analysis/Data science;Business analysis; ORDigital marketing/Sales.Employers are to create and implement a learning plan for on-the-job training with the participant;There will be a mandatory online soft skills training delivered by ICTC (a total of 16 hours);The soft skills training is about 16 hours and is spread over the course of the internship. The schedule will be communicated in advance to the youth interns;The program provides youth interns with CliftonStrengths Assessments and Coaching, in addition to online facilitated training covering topics such as communicating with others and working in teams, problem-solving, giving and receiving feedback, and diversity & inclusion training.The participant must also complete online hard skills training and submit a certificate of completion (self-paced and during non-work hours) in one of the following streams: Software development, Data analysis/Data Science, Business Analysis or Digital Marketing/Sales;The amount of training time varies depending on the stream, although is approximately 35 hours in total.Reimbursements will be released in 2 installments - 1 at the midpoint and 1 at the end of the program.

      Best Practices:This funding cannot be used in conjunction with other sources of funding as the wage subsidy already covers 100% of the participant's wages;This program does not allow funding to be used retroactively as all candidates must be brand-new hires; andEmployers must advertise approved job descriptions to be eligible.Forms:Program webpage: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Market Readiness Program funds up to $250,000 to early-stage technology companies that are incorporated and are at the commercialization stage. Applicant companies will be evaluated based on the potential long-term competitiveness, value proposition, capacity to scale as well as strong Intellectual Property rights. The intent of the program is to attract additional private investment, support scalable business growth, and support innovation in Ontario.Grant Value:MR125 Stream: $125,000MR250 Stream: $250,000Turnaround Time: 3 monthsEligible Applicants:Be based in Ontario;Headquartered in the province and have at least 50% of the current company headcount in the province.Have been incorporated within the last 5 years;Have raised less than $1 million in third-party capital, excluding friends and family;Currently or previously affiliated with a university, college or research hospital campus linked accelerator or incubator, in Ontario;Be an early-stage technology company in sectors including, but not limited to:IT;Robotics;AI;Health technology;Cleantech; andAdvanced manufacturing.Has a minimum addressable market size of $100M;Has a product built;Have early market traction;Close to commercialization;Meet the stream specific eligibility criteria below:MR125 for $125,000 Investments:Be prepared to discuss the proposed terms of the current round which is being led by third party investors (Not OCE);Be past the internal beta design and development stages and work with prospective market customers to improve the offering;Be developing proprietary technology;Be defining its primary product/ market fit and establishing reasonable pricing models with a sales strategy/pipeline;Have a defined business model and financial forecasts (1-2 years); andBe raising sufficient investment to reach the next defined significant milestone(s).MR250 for $250,000 Investments:Have already raised a pre-seed or seed round and are looking for additional growth capital;Be advanced in their growth and sales strategy, showing early but consistent traction and a sales strategy that is repeatable and scalable;Have potential to redefine or disrupt a targeted industry (ie. strong IP and a differentiated offering);Be pivoting to target growth with higher momentum;Have a business model and financial forecasts (2-4 years); andHave milestones that drive a Seed extension or Series A round in the near-term future (1-2 years).Eligible Activities:Customer creation and development of scalable sales processes;Business model development activities; andInvestments for the round to be used for significant milestones for a runway up to 12 months.Program Details:Companies are reviewed through a rigorous internal pre-vetting process before being selected to proceed to an investment advisory committee for consideration;Due diligence documents will be evaluated by the IAC against assessment criteria, including:Product Offering: core value proposition, ability to address customer challenges, appropriateness of stage of development, and commercializationTarget Customers: identification and plan to access customers, willingness to pay, marketing strategyMarket and Competition: appropriateness and feasibility of the business model and pricing structure, plan to address competition and barriers to entry (e.g. regulatory), potential exit strategyTeam: ability and resources to achieve the milestones and deliver a repeatable sales processMilestones: suitability to grow customer base and/or attract follow-on investment, risk mitigation plan, clarity and feasibility of next stepsSuccessful companies must complete the following activation requirements within 30 days of investment approval:Execution of OCE’s standard funding agreement.Do not fill out this template.       Grant Criteria 
      This program provides new and existing group sponsor arrangements in Ontario up to $1,000,000 to train apprentices. A group sponsor is a sponsor comprised of two or more persons whose purpose is to act as a single sponsor to collectively provide training to apprentices with a greater breadth of skills and experience. The program seeks to foster collaboration, innovation, and inclusion in Ontario’s labour market.Grant Value: $1,000,000Turnaround Time: 2 monthsEligible Applicants:Be one of the following:Non-profit and for-profit businesses;Union affiliated organizations / Training Trust Funds;Professional / Industry / Employer / Sector Associations;Employee Organizations;Local planning groups/Community action group;Charitable Foundations;Indigenous organizations; orMunicipal governments.Be a legal entity authorized to operate in Ontario;Have proof of third-party general liability insurance coverage of a minimum of $2,000,000;The insurance policy should include:The Indemnified Parties as additional insureds with respect to liability arising in the course of performance of the applicant’s obligations under, or otherwise in connection with, the GSG program;A cross-liability clause;Contractual liability coverage; andA 30-day written notice of cancellation, termination, or material change.Maintain appropriate workplace safety standards.Note: Applicants with an existing GSG Transfer Payment Agreement (TPA) will not be eligible to submit an additional Business Case Application until they have completed their active GSG TPAIneligible Applicants:Private consultants;Other provincial government ministries;Federal government ministries or agencies;Training Delivery Agents (TDAs);Unless TDAs can demonstrate a separate and arms-length business line between in-class training delivery and on-the-job sponsor responsibilities.Any other organization that is not involved in the apprenticeship system.Eligible Expenses:Staffing;Travel expenditures for group sponsor staff;Marketing, promotion, and distribution;Mentorship and training:Including in-class, on-the-job training and overall skill updating support; andTrain-the-trainer resources to support journeypersons who train apprentices.Health and safety-related equipment:Safety harnesses, protective eye-wear, work gloves, and trade-specific personal protective equipment, etc.End-of-training and pre-exam assistance support:Journeyperson mentorship;Instructional website access; andInstructional supplies.Operational costs:Leasing of office space and legal/accounting fees.Audits:Projects over $150,000 require an audit by the group sponsor’s Chief Financial Officer or equivalent.Note: Business Case Applications must include a breakdown and description of eligible project expenditures.Ineligible Expenses:Wage subsidy for apprentices;Professional membership fees;Fundraising expenses;Profit generating activities; Expenditures associated with special events such as tournaments, conferences, receptions, festivals, parties;Capital expenses, such as renovations; andExpenditures associated with activities or operations performed outside of Ontario.Program Details:Project duration: 1-3 years;Potential group sponsors are required to demonstrate formal sponsor approval status through the ministry’s Regional Offices by the completion of their first year of funding;Failure to do so may result in holding back funds or the termination of their TPA.Organizations may not submit multiple Business Case Applications as a lead applicant. However, applicants may collaborate through more than one Business Case Application;Group sponsor responsibilities include but are not limited to:Interviewing and selecting prospective apprentices and establish a training network;Coordinating and monitoring the apprentice’s on-the-job workplace training;Submitting documentation for apprenticeship application, registration of training agreements and completion of the apprenticeship training programs;Overseeing affiliated employers who provide apprenticeship training and ensure that they are appropriately delivering apprenticeship training to the apprentice in accordance with OCTAA, its regulations and training standards;Ensuring that apprentices and affiliated employers adhere to the terms and conditions of the registered training agreements, including regulated wage rates and journeyperson-to-apprentice ratios; andSupporting apprentices through the complete apprenticeship cycle including registration, workplace-based and classroom-based training, completion, and trade certification.No expenditures can be incurred outside the start and end dates of the agreement funding period.Evaluation Criteria:How the project aligns with the overall objectives of the program (30%);Project impact (25%);Project delivery and budget (20%);Organizational capacity (15%); andLocal labour market demand (10%).

      Best Practices:Applicants are advised to clearly include itemized eligible expenses planned for key activities in the business case application; andFor additional support, please email GroupSponsorshipGrant@ontario.caForms:Program webpage: click hereBusiness case application: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      Export Development Program provides up to $15,000 to registered businesses in Nova Scotia seeking to increase sales outside of the province. The program has 2 streams that support different business needs. The goal of the program is to improve competitiveness and strengthen the Nova Scotia economy.Grant Value: eligible costs up to $15,000Turnaround Time: 2 weeksEligible Businesses:Be registered on the Registry of Joint Stock Companies;Have a permanent establishment in Nova Scotia;Have the majority of the workforce in Nova Scotia;Have fully developed exportable product(s), service(s), technology(ies) and/or intellectual property; Have a business plan and strategy to sell products/services outside of the province; andBe in good legal standing.Ineligible Businesses:Franchises;Games of chance operations and bingo halls;Personal service providers;Real estate developers, agents or brokers;Licensed liquor establishments whose primary business is alcohol sales (excepting production breweries, brewpubs, wineries, and distilleries);Distributors, agents, or traders, including retailers except where value-added products or services are part of the deliverables for the purpose of selling Nova Scotia products/services abroad;Associations;Professional service providers, except where the project represents a unique and/or strategic opportunity with potential economic benefit and/or job creation;Creative industries companies activities which are eligible under the CreativeIndustries Fund;Tourism operators;Publicly funded organizations; andNot-for-profit organizations.Eligible Activities:Travel to outside of Nova Scotia to attend a trade show or conference, or to visit clients, potential partners, or investors;Participation in an in-person or virtual trade show, mission or conference;Have foreign clients, potential partners, or investors visit the business facilities in Nova Scotia for the first time;Hire a consultant to address challenges or barriers to selling products/services outside of Nova Scotia; andPurchase of software, hardware, and/or platforms to enhance remote working productivity, e-commerce solutions, and the digitization of internal operations.Note: Eligible Activities will depend on the stream selected by the applicant.Program Details:2 streams:Travel and Trade Missions:The minimum project cost is $1,000;Eligible expenses include:Standard floor space cost or virtual booth space for a non-retail trade show;Entry-level conference registration fees for up to two representatives of the business;An airfair stipend according to the chart found here in the guidelines;International travel is permitted; The company must follow and adhere to all health protocols in all jurisdictions where the company is travelling;The company is responsible for all quarantine costs.A per diem rate of$200CAD($400 x 50%) for each approved traveler to cover accommodations and in-market ground transportation/standard car rental (up to two representatives of the business). Per diem does NOT include the trip return day. Per diem expenses are capped at 7 days per trip;Incoming client/partner/investor first-time visit eligible costs(up to two individuals) include airfare stipend and per diem rates.Hire a Consultant/ Service Provider:To address challenges or barriers to selling products/services outside of Nova Scotia;The minimum project cost is $5,000 contributes up to 50% of eligible project costs;Eligible projects include:Diversity and Inclusion Policy;Business growth, strategic, and marketing plans;Market research, feasibility or business case analysis for proposed or existing business activity;Product research, development, and design;Development plan for e-commerce platform for markets outside of Nova Scotia;Business matchmaking or lead generation in new markets;Business valuations for succession planning;Productivity, efficiency, lean, capacity improvements, sustainability and reduction of carbon footprint;Intellectual Property or Certification research or development (does not cover legal fees);Technology implementation or development;(Re)Branding for international markets; E-commerce solution improvement; andReduction of carbon footprint.Eligible project costs:Consulting fees; andMust not have existing personal or business relationship (arm's length).Consultant transportation and accommodations cost directly related to the project.Business plan and strategy must include the following:Company's target market;Distribution channels;Challenges in the target market; andSolutions to the challenges.Stream 1 and 2 applications will only be considered for projects completed between April 1, 2023, and March 31, 2024;Deliverables for project completion must be submitted online no later than 30 days from project completion;For Stream 1: claims must be submitted online within 30 days of completion of each project/trip.Successful applicants must complete the feedback survey for the Program and participate in NSBI’s annual corporate data collection process for two years following the project’s completion.Note: Any costs not listed under the eligible costs above are deemed ineligible.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Accelerating Manufacturing Scale-Up Grant Program offers 1-time funding of up to $500,000 to small and medium-sized manufacturers of all industry sectors in B.C. The program provides incentives for industry collaboration, retooling manufacturing lines, production commercialization, and localizing supply chains. The intent of the program is to accelerate innovation capacity, strengthen supply chains, diversify revenue streams, and create jobs throughout B.C.Grant Value:75% funding up to $250,000 for Individual Businesses75% funding for a minimum of $50,000 to a maximum of $500,000 for Groups in CollaborationTurnaround Time: Decisions to be announced late July 2021Eligible Applicants:All industries and sectors that manufacture or process value-added products;Individual Businesses:Sole or primary operations in BC;Has proof of manufacturing capability:T2 return - schedule 125 Income Statement Information; Must be able to start project immediately upon approval;Have operated in BC for at least 12 months;Filed income taxes in BC for either 2019 or 2020;For corporations: T2 return.Employs between 2 and 149 people in B.C. for the calendar year; andEmployee may include an employee that is full-time, part-time, contract worker, or a seasonal worker whom is employed for at least four months of the calendar year by the applicant.Have at least 25% of project funding from other sources (i.e. industry, revenue, other government funding).Groups in Collaboration:Have 2 or more small or medium-sized businesses working together on a project;One of the project partners must meet the criteria outlined above for individual businesses;Partners may be from international or from other Canadian provinces; andAll partners need to be in the manufacturing business.Eligible Activities:Prototype, pilot, or demonstration of new technology:Trialing production efficiency methods;Design and construction of a pilot project that involves a potential customer;Pilot plant commissioning, testing mechanical systems; Data collection and recording; andEquipment, capital investment.Commercialization of new technology and/or product:Supporting patenting/IP protection; Validation of product features and product performance;Preparing reports and documentation; andGetting certified/ testing of products to pass certification.Market access/marketing:Accessing co-manufacturing capacity; and Supply chain support or business development to enter new markets.Manufacturing diagnostic:Process and operational improvements to increase production capacity, profitability, and competitiveness;Technology assessment to identify opportunities to improve systems, processes, and/or equipment.Assessment should focus on manufacturing modernization, building resilience, and developing new revenue-generating opportunities.Ineligible Expenses:Day-to-day operational costs (i.e. wages and salaries);Any eligible costs incurred before the approval of the project via a grant letter;Costs eligible for a rebate from federal, provincial, territorial or municipal government sources;Depreciation of assets paid for through the program;Federal and provincial income taxes, harmonized sales tax (HST), goods and services taxes (GST), provincial sales taxes (PST), excess profit taxes or surtaxes and/or special expenses in connection with those taxes;Fines and penalties;Provisions for contingencies;Extraordinary or abnormal fees for professional advice unless approval under the program is obtained prior to incurring the cost;Costs related to infrastructure, construction, purchase of a building, land or vehicle;Equipment costs unrelated to project objectives;Costs of proposal activities administration and management;Costs of repayment of loans or other cost-share obligations; andAny costs that are not directly related to the project.Evaluation Criteria:Project overview expected outcomes and implementation readiness;Project work plan and timeframe;Project risks and mitigation strategies;Project objective alignment:Job created/maintained;Increases in production, revenue, operational efficiency etc.Alignment with government objectives:Advancing innovation and environmental sustainability (i.e. reducing GHG emissions in production or in the supply chain);Regional economic development; andPandemic preparedness and manufacturing of critical supplies.Budget.Program Details:Intake closes at 6pm PDT on May 31, 2021;Minimum funding: $50,000;Businesses are required to provide at least 25% of the total cost of purchased material, equipment and/or labour (PMEL). This contribution must be self-financed or come from other cash contribution sources, such as other government funding;In-kind contributions are not accepted as a part of the 25% cost-share, but will be considered when evaluating applications;In-house labour will have a maximum of up to 25% of the program contribution for PMEL; andAll businesses must report on project outcomes within 2 months of the project end date, or by February 15, 2022 (whichever is earlier).

              100%
              
        
    

  
    
      Grant Type
      Market Expansion, Research & Development, Capital Costs, Investment
    
    
      Grant Amount
      $20,000,000
    
    
      Regions
      All of Canada
    
    
      Industries
      Aviation & Aerospace, Environmental - Green Technologies
    
    
      Program provided by
      Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
     

    
      Deadline
      
        

          Open until filled
      
    
    
  





    
      




  

      Grant Criteria 
      The Strategic Innovation Fund (SIF) provides up to $20M in repayable and non-repayable contributions to support large-scale collaborative projects that help position Canada to prosper in the global knowledge-based economy. SIF projects advance innovation, research and development through cooperation between the private sector, researchers and non-profit organizations to promote the long-term competitiveness of Canadian industries.Grant Value: $20,000,000Funding Details:Streams 1, 2, and 3:The amount of the contribution is based on the minimum amount required to allow an eligible activity to proceed; The amount will not exceed 50% of the costs for eligible activities and the maximum level will only be considered in exceptional circumstances; andNon-repayable contributions will only be considered for eligible activities that demonstrate strong economic, innovation, and public benefits with clear strategic value or global significance.Streams 4 and 5:Contributions made are non-repayable; andContributions cannot exceed 50% of a project's total eligible costs, except for applicants that are academic institutions and networks, where the contribution provided may cover 100% of their eligible costs.Turnaround Time: 80 business daysEligibility Criteria:Business Innovation and Growth (Streams 1 to 3):Be a for-profit organization incorporated and doing business in Canada;Undertake a project in Canada;Request a minimum SIF contribution of $10 million for a proposal with total costs of at least $20 million,Provide audited financial statements (or equivalent) for the past 3 years; Be willing to make long-term commitments to Canada (e.g. job creation and maintenance, R&D investments, and other public benefits).Collaborations and Networks (Streams 4 to 5):Stream 4: Consortium applicants:May include Canadian universities, colleges, research institutes, for-profit corporations (SMEs) and non-profit organizations; andThe lead applicant must be incorporated in Canada.Networks:The lead applicant must be a non-profit organization incorporated in Canada.Stream 5: Be either a for-profit or not-for-profit incorporated in Canada;Have collaborations with Canadian universities and/or colleges, research institutes, for-profit corporations and/or not-for-profit entities;Support large-scale ecosystems that are national in scope;Undertake national collaborative projects;Request a minimum SIF contribution of $10 million for a proposal with total costs of at least $20 million;Provide audited financial statements (or equivalent) for the past 3 years; andBe willing to make long-term commitments to Canada (e.g. collaborations with public and private entities, R&D investments, co-op/work-integrated learning opportunities).Eligible Projects:Business Innovation and Growth Streams (continuously receives applications):Stream 1:Activities must be within Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) 1-9;Encourage research and development (R&D) that will accelerate technology transfer and commercialization of innovative products, processes, and services;Adaptation of research findings for commercial applications that have the potential for market disruption;Development of current products through the implementation of new technology that will enhance the Recipient's competitive capability; andDevelopment of process improvements that reduce the environmental footprint of current production through the use of new technologies.Stream 2:Activities must be within Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) 8-9;Facilitate the growth and expansion of firms in Canada;Increasing manufacturing capacity to meet demonstrated market demand;Improving production efficiency through improvements to plant and equipment; orImproving processes to increase efficiency.Stream 3:Activities must be a minimum of Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 2;Attract and retain large-scale investments to Canada;Establishing a new production facility that did not previously exist in Canada;Obtaining a production mandate for a product that was previously produced outside Canada or is being produced for the first time; andObtaining an R&D mandate which was previously held outside Canada or is being established for the first time.Collaborations and Networks Streams (competitive applications received after a call-for-proposals):Stream 4:Activities must be within Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) 1-7;Advance industrial research, development and technology demonstration through collaboration between academia, non-profit organizations and the private sector; andDevelopment by a lead Tier 1 original equipment manufacturer company of a potential new product utilizing academic research findings, conjunction with SME suppliers and research councilsStream 5:Activities should  be within Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 3-7, but may cover TRL 1-9;Support large-scale, national innovation ecosystems through high-impact collaborations across Canada;Discovery of new knowledge that aim to support the development of new technology-driven products, processes or services at early-stage technology readiness levelsTechnology demonstration, including the advancement and development of new technologies into product-specific applications at mid-stage and late-stage technology readiness levels with the goal of commercialization in areas of proven Canadian advantage.Eligible Costs:All Streams:Eligible costs are limited to non-recurring costs that are specifically related to the project, including:Direct labor;Overhead;Subcontracts and consultants;Direct materials and equipment;Other direct costs; andLand and buildings:Must be necessary and reasonable to carry out the activity to which they relate; andExamples of eligible costs include the construction of new or the expansion of existing facilities, the development of industrial landscapes and testing facilities, and investments in modern buildings.Stream 4: Eligible costs include expenditures directly related to the operation and activities of the Network:Organization of networking events;Participation in collaborative research and technology development activities;Conferences and workshops in support of collaborative R&D activities; Operation of regional offices across Canada including:Salaries;Office equipment;Professional services;Overhead;Travel; andOther operational costs as appropriate. The eligible costs of the Network-supported projects will be the amount of money the Network provides to ultimate Recipients for a given project.Ineligible Costs - For All Streams:Allowance for interest on invested capital, bonds, debentures, bank or other loans together with related bond discounts and finance charges;Losses on investments, bad debts and expenses for the collection charges;Losses on other projects or contracts;Federal and provincial income taxes, goods and services taxes, excess profit taxes or surtaxes and/or special expenses in connection with those taxes;Provisions for contingencies;Premiums for life insurance on the lives of officers and/or directors;Amortization of unrealized appreciation of assets;Depreciation of assets;Fines and penalties;Unreasonable compensation for officers and employees;Product development or improvement expenses not associated with the project;Advertising, except reasonable advertising of an industrial or institutional character placed in trade, technical or professional journals for the dissemination of information for the industry or institution;Entertainment expenses;Donations;Dues and other memberships other than regular trade and professional associations; andSelling and marketing expenses associated with the products or services or both being developed under the Contribution Agreement.Note: Ineligible costs include but are not limited to the above.Program Details:Applications are accepted on a continuing basis for Stream 1,2,3 & 5;Applications will be assessed on a competitive basis for Stream 4;To apply as a Network or Consortia (Stream 5), you must first request a consultation with SIF officials;Project activities should support the development of technology to a higher readiness level than that at which it is currently;The combined level of assistance from all governments (federal, provincial, territorial, and municipal), shall not normally exceed 75% of eligible costs, except for applicants that are academic institutions or networks for which the maximum combined level of assistance would be 100%; andRecipients must own the background intellectual property or hold sufficient background intellectual property rights to allow their project's activities to be carried out.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices:Applications should make a strong case for why government funding is needed to complete the project, as a complement to funding available from the private sector;Eligible Best Practices:The amount of funding considered for a project will be assessed in the context of the project's needs and is rarely 50% in cases where that is the limit (all applicants except for academic institutions and networks);A proposed project should meet the following criteria to ensure SIF is the most applicable Federal program to apply for:Aligned with one or more of the Economic Strategy Tables;Project benefits have a broader impact on Canadians that is not merely local-focused; Clear rationale and/or the necessary technical expertise to carry out the project activities;Leads to technological development or growth representing an incremental or accelerated leap that goes beyond expected business plans;Large-scale product development that has a broad-based, market disruption capability or clear public benefits; andProject activities and/or costs that cannot generally be financed through debt financing;Prospective applicants are encouraged to check eligibility by completing the SIF self-screening questionnaire.Forms:Program Guide: click hSereTechnology Readiness Level Scale: click hereEmail ic.sifadmission-fsiadmission.ic@canada.ca to request the SIF Statement of Interest application package and the SOI package will automatically be sent to you.

        Recently Changed 
        This program has re-opened and is accepting applications until June 2, 2022;A Diversity Enhancement stream has been introduced: publishing companies that do not meet the sales thresholds for the regular stream can apply for up to $15k in project support if they are owned by racially diverse or Francophone individuals; andSome of the COVID-19 support measures have been removed: you can no longer use the funds to cover operational expenses, and you cannot use them to cover unexpected costs incurred as a result of public health measures (lockdowns, purchase of PPE, etc) 
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The Book Fund provides up to $150,000 for Ontario-based book publishers to support business growth via business development and marketing initiatives. Funds may be used for digital projects as well as promotional and marketing activities. The program objectives are to increase revenue, create and retain jobs, and positively impact the Ontario publishing industry.  Grant Value: Regular stream: 75% of eligible costs up to $150,000;Diversity Enhancement stream: up to $15,000 for companies with racially diverse or Francophone ownership that do not qualify for the regular stream.Turnaround Time: Approval notification to be issued in AugustEligible Applicants:A book publisher:Professional activity must involve the following:Selection, development, and editing of manuscripts or draft manuscripts;Entering into contractual agreements with authors or copyright holders;Publishing books under the publisher’s own imprint, in printed or other forms;Assuming the risks associated with production and marketing.Be an Ontario-based company:Have the central place of business located in Ontario;Filed Ontario corporate taxes;Carry out 3 of the following primarily through the Ontario office:Editing;Production; andMarketing, sales, and distribution or management.Have 50% of publisher employees based in the Ontario office.Be Canadian-owned and controlled;Be incorporated for at least 2 years;Exceptions may be considered for companies with less than two years of operations.Have a minimum of 4 books published for the last 2 years;Have a minimum of 6 Canadian authored titles in print;Have at least 50% of titles published in the last 2 years be Canadian-authored;Have at least 50% of titles published in this current year be written by authors who are neither shareholders nor owners of the publishing firm;Distribute books through normal bookselling channels;Have an annual net book sales revenue of $20,000 (average for the last 2 years);Revenues from the sale of vanity titles must not exceed 25% of the corporation's total revenues;Be able to provide financial statements for the last 2 fiscal years; andBe financially solvent.Note: Companies that do not meet the sales thresholds for the regular stream may receive up to $15,000 in project funding through the Diversity Enhancement Stream if they are owned by racially diverse and/or Francophone individuals. To be eligible for this stream, the company must have been in operation at least 1 year, have an annual book sales revenue of at least $5000, have at least 1 Canadian-authored book in print, and have published at least 1 book in the past 2 years. Eligible Sales Revenue:To be eligible for inclusion in sales figures, titles must meet the following criteria:Be Canadian-authored (written by a Canadian citizen or permanent resident);Bear an ISBN given to the publisher, be published under the publisher’s own imprint or under an imprint for which the publisher has acquired publishing, management, and marketing rights;Have a minimum of 48 bound pages, except in the case of children’s books;Be free of hate propaganda, depictions of sexual exploitation, excessive violence, and denigration of an identifiable group;Not be a vanity title (a publication dependent on financial contributions from and/or initial purchase by the author); andHave substantive editorial content.Eligible sales revenue is defined as the total of the following:The revenues for eligible titles by Canadian authors sold net of trade discounts for returns and allowances; andRevenues from the sale of rights and permissions for eligible titles.Ineligible Sales Revenue:Calendars, agendas, or almanacs;Coloring books or comic books;With the exception of collections of cartoons in book form by Canadian cartoonists meeting all other criteria are eligible, as are collections of drawings, illustrations and other artwork by Canadian artists in book form.Instructional books;University or college dissertations;Conference papers or reports;Government reports or exhibition catalogues;Instruction books or manuals;Publications containing primarily maps;Workbooks, kits, activity manuals or educational games;Reference books such as directories, index compilations, compilations of statutes, rule books, or bibliographies; andPublications that are primarily musical notation.Eligible Activities: Applicants may submit only one application but may include multiple activities within the application;Must not be for routine materials or expenses which are considered a normal part of the publishing business;Be focused on driving sales and increasing publisher revenue in a tangible and measurable manner;Be completed by February 16, 2024;Eligible projects and activities may include, but are not limited, to:Research and development of a digital transformation strategy/business plan;Creation of additional marketing tools and/or materials;Enhanced advertising and co-op programs;Specialized catalogues and mailings;Consumer contests;Attending and exhibiting at international fairs, trade shows, conferences;Virtual events and exhibits are now eligible (new for 2022-23);Ontario Author tours;Website updates;Search engine optimization;Author podcasts, videos, webcasts;Book/imprint launches;Digital rights management; andExploration of alternate sales channels.Ineligible Expenses:Salaries and wages of staff not directly related to the project;Staff benefit costs;Fixed overhead costs (such as machine costs: telephone, fax, photocopier, computer);Costs for long-distance phone and fax, paper costs, couriers, and other expenses directly related to the project may be included.Occupancy costs (rent or mortgage of facilities);Additional expenses incurred due to public health measures; andHospitality. Program Details:Funding levels:Eligible Sales RevenueTotal Funding AvailableOver $1,500,000$150,000$500,01 to $1,500,00$100,00$150,001 to $500,000$80,000$20,000 to $150,000$30,000Eligible applicants may apply for funding based on their level of eligible sales revenue.For publishers with eligible sales revenues of less than $75,000, the funds requested should be proportional to sales, with total request not exceeding 33% of eligible sales revenues and in keeping with 75% of total budget;Partners may be involved in the project of successful applicants;Partners must:Be one or more content creation companies from the book and magazine, film and television, interactive digital media, or music industries that was eligible to submit an application at the immediately preceding deadline for one of Ontario Creates’ Content, Marketing or Export Funds, or the Ontario Music Fund;Be an Ontario-based organization; andBe a Canadian-owned and -controlled organization.The profit participation share of the partners should be in appropriate proportion to the ownership of the project;Realistically valued “in-kind” services may be included as part or all of the 25% costs that must come from sources other than the Ontario Creates Book Fund; andApplicants may begin incurring expenses no more than 90 days following application approval.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:The funding from this program may be used in conjunction with other sources of funding, including governmental funds and third party participation such as retail partners;Funding from non-governmental sources, including from the book publisher, should have an accompanying letter of intent indicating their commitment to the project and ability to finance the portion of the budget indicated in the application.The funding cannot be used retroactively. Expenses incurred prior to the notification of funding will not be reimbursed;Each project activity should be properly detailed and the budget should also provide a detailed cost breakdown by activity;Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin the application process early to allow ample time to compile and complete the necessary information;Applicants may begin at any time and save information as it is entered. Once saved, applicants can go back and edit and/or add information until the time when the application is actually submitted;Ontario Creates encourages applications from companies that are led by BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, or People of Colour) or Francophone individuals and applicants that otherwise meet the provincial definition of diversity;Applicants are advised to review the assessment criteria on the application guidelines pages 10 to 11 prior to submission; andPlease note that  Ontario Authors on Tour Program (OATS) is no longer a separate program but is now delivered through the Book Fund. Please review the application guidelines on page 6 regarding the delivery of this program.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

ORFor-Profit Tourism Organizations.Be incorporated in Canada for a minimum of 1 year as of the submission date;Not in default of the terms and conditions of any grant or loan agreement with any agencies of the Government of Ontario;       Grant Criteria 
      The Innovation Stream of the INVEST North Program offers up to $2 million of funding towards applied research and development projects, and demonstration & commercialization projects for new and innovative technologies. Projects will be carried out in Northern Ontario by a lead business either alone or in partnership with a public sector academic or research institution. The aim of the program is to generate net economic benefits for Northern Ontario through innovation that meets a demonstrated market need and demand.Grant Value: up to $2,000,000Turnaround Time: 6 weeksEligible Applicants:Private-sector businesses alone, or in partnership with a public sector academic or research institution;Businesses with a minimum 1 year of incorporation;For public-private partnership projects:The business is the lead applicant and the funding recipient; andThe partnering academic or research institution must have the relevant expertise and resources required by the private-sector partner to complete the proposed project.Eligible Expenses:Applied research and development activities:Direct internal technical labour costs performed in Northern Ontario (i.e., labour performed by an employee of the applicant business that has knowledge and training in a specialized complex procedure or operation that is required to complete the project);Prototyping costs (i.e., engineering and design services and component purchase, fabrication and installation costs);Product testing;Intellectual property protection costs; andResearch and development services provided by public sector partners.Demonstration and commercialization activities:Direct internal technical labour costs performed in Northern Ontario;Building or renovation costs specifically related to the commercialization of the new technology;Prototype demonstration costs (i.e., engineering and design services and equipment purchases, fabrication and installation costs);Material costs;Product certification costs;Research and development services provided by public sector partners; andMarketing costs (i.e., in-person or virtual trade show assistance and marketing material design costs) limited to 20% of total eligible project costs.Ineligible Expenses:They include but are not limited to the following projects, costs, and activities:Land;Working capital;Administrative or other indirect operating costs;Regular operating wages for employees;Costs only associated with internal efficiency purposes;Labour costs for any person that owns 10% or more of the applicant business;In-kind contributions;Business plans;Travel, accommodation, and meeting costs;Office equipment and furnishings; andVehicles.Program Details:Applied Research and Development only projects:Conditional contribution of up to 50% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $500,000.Applied Research & Development and Demonstration & Commercialization Combined or Demonstration & Commercialization only projects:Conditional contribution of up to 50% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $2 million.Innovative technology projects are defined as: “the development or implementation of ideas to produce new or improved strategies, capabilities, products, services, or processes with a strong focus on ensuring to satisfy a market need or desire”;Applicant businesses have the choice to apply for support for applied research & development or demonstration & commercialization costs under separate applications or in one combined application;If demonstration & commercialization costs are included in a project, NOHFC will not accept a subsequent application for the same technology;For prototype demonstration projects, NOHFC will consider up to three prototypes for funding in one project;Before proceeding to the demonstration & commercialization phase, the applicant must:Own, have registered a patent for, or have the rights to exploit the intellectual property associated with the technology; andBe able to demonstrate that the technology has been tested and fully validated.Evaluation Criteria:Factors that will be considered during the evaluation of applications will include but are not limited to:Innovation meets the NOHFC’s definition of Innovation;Strength of the project’s detailed business plan;Net economic benefits for Northern Ontario;Demonstrated market need and demand;Management capacity;Business’ financial position;Supply chain impacts; andLevel of risk.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program can be combined with other Federal and Provincial government funding to cover up to 75% of eligible project costs;Process Best Practices:To apply on the portal, the applicant is expected to prepare a robust project summary;The applicant may be required to reimburse NOHFC if assets financed by NOHFC are sold within the first three years after project completion; andLimited funding is available, therefore not all projects meeting the criteria will necessarily receive funding.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication form login: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Alliance Grants provides funding contributions of up to a maximum of $1 million per year to university researchers and partner organizations in collaboration. Funding may be used for salary support, materials and supplies, and activities that support collaboration and/or knowledge mobilization. The intent of the program is to encourage collaborative teams to generate new knowledge and accelerate the application of research results to create benefits for Canada.Grant Value:Option 1 - Up to 66.% to a maximum of $1 millionOption 2 - Up to 100% to a maximum of $300,000Turnaround Time: Small and medium projects - Up to 12 weeksLarge projects - up to 16 weeksEligible Applicants:Canadian university researcher to partner with one of the following organization types:Private, public, or not-for-profit.Partner organizations may be Canadian or foreign/multinational companies;Must provide supplemental information that describes the organization and enables NSERC to determine if the partner organization can be considered in NSERC’s cost-sharing calculations.Have at least 1 partner who can demonstrate the ability to exploit such research results;Must collectively support the project through cash contributions, where applicable;Each partner organization must actively play a role in the project and support it through in-kind contributions, such as:Play an active role in the project’s research activities;Utilize the project’s research results to help achieve its desired outcomes; andPlay an active role in translating or mobilizing knowledge to ensure that the research results have an impact.Note: Only Canadian university researchers who are eligible to receive NSERC funds can apply for an Alliance grant.Eligible Projects:Must be relevant in natural sciences or engineering;Cannot use an Alliance grant to support secret or contract research;Eligible Expenses:Salary support for research trainees (undergraduates, graduates and postdoctoral fellows) to perform research and related training;Salary support for technicians and research professional personnel;Materials and supplies;Activities that support collaborations and knowledge mobilization related to the project; andActivities to develop and grow the research collaborations with the partner organizations.Program Details:Option 1:The purpose of this stream is to:Generate new knowledge and/or technology to address complex challenges;Create economic, social and/or environmental benefits;Contribute to Canada’s long-term competitiveness;Support public policy;Train new researchers in areas that are important to Canada and to the partner organizations; andDraw on diverse perspectives and skill sets to accelerate the translation and application of research results.No limits on the number of applications per year;Value: $20,000 to $1,000,000 per year;Duration: 1-5 years.Option 2:In addition to Option 1 objectives, the purpose of this stream is also to:Address a societal challenge that will result in new natural sciences and engineering knowledge and societal impact;Bring together academic, partner organization, and societal perspectives and skillsets throughout the collaboration; andDemonstrate how all interested individuals will learn about and use the products, services, or policies that stem from this research.Limit of number of applications:1 within a 12-month period for researchers as applicants/co-applicants.Value: $30,000 to $300,000;Duration: 1-5 years; andNSERC will assess the relevance and potential impact of each partner organization and their proposed in-kind contributions and will give priority to funding projects that demonstrate clear relevance to the partner organizations and potential to provide economic, social and/or environmental benefits for Canada and Canadians.

      Eligible Best Practices:The program does not allow NSERC funding to be used retroactively;However, this program allows for cash contributions that were spent up to 3 months prior to the application submission to be includedApplicants and their institutions must complete the National Security Guidelines for Research Partnerships’ risk assessment form for all applications involving one or more partner organizations from the private sector;Applicants must notify NSERC:If any of the partner organizations’ cash contributions, as committed to in the application, are not received, as this may lead to a reduced award;if any of the partner organizations leave the project.       Grant Criteria 
      This program funds up to 100% of expenses up to a maximum of $20,000 for new projects in book and magazine publishing, film production and sound recording that are undertaken by businesses in applicable creative sectors. The intent of the program, offered through the Alberta Media Fund, is to support cultural industry producers that focus on developing talent and intellectual property of Albertan-based businesses.Grant Value: up to 100% of eligible expenses up to a maximum of $20,000Turnaround Time: 5 monthsEligible Businesses:Based in Alberta;Be majority owned by Alberta residents;Be a book publisher, magazine publisher, sound recording company, or film production company; andMust be primarily engaged in the production of:Books:Permanent-bound;At least 48 printed pages;In editions of at least 500 copies; andHave at least 50% of printed copies eligible for sale.Ebooks:Available through major online retailers;At least 48 pages of print equivalent; andHave at least 75% of all eBook titles for sale.Magazines/eMagazines:Are of literary, artistic or children’s interest (500 copies in print);Have editorial policies controlled by an editor/editorial board;Have a policy that the copyright for all published material resides with the author; andHave a clear distinction between editorial content and advertising.Sound recordings:Must develop, produce, license, release, promote and distribute sound recordings; andHave the production copyright of the sound recording(s) owned or licensed by the label for each recording released.Film/video:Are primarily engaged in film/video productions for public viewing; andWill create/have created a production with a running time, or combined times, of at least 30 minutes.Must be registered and in good standing with the appropriate legislation.Eligible Projects and Expenses:Projects must meet the criteria in one more of the following categories:Art production;Training and career development;Marketing; andResearch.Includes activities that support or result in the development of new cultural work.Eligible expenses include, but are not limited to:Expenses associated with art production, career training, marketing and research;Transportation and accommodation;Royalties or licenses;Editing fees;Administration and contract fees;Promotion and publicity; andProduction.Ineligible Projects and Expenses:Self-published;Corporate or agency newsletters; Corporate video productions; andExpenses that are not eligible to receive funding include:Expenses that occur before the application date; andExpenses already covered under the Alberta Production Grant, Screen-based Production Grant, Project/Script Grant or the Alberta Foundation for the Arts.Program Details:Recipients must return funds if 1) reporting requirements are note met, or 2) if portions of the grant are unused;Recipients must submit a report upon completion of the project; andRecognition requirements exist to provide credit to the delivery organization in any publicity created for the project.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Any additional support materials that may assist in the assessment process are encouraged to be submitted (e.g., press clippings, books, magazines, CDs, invitations, reference letters, reviews, and catalogues);An extension for the project completion date may be requested in writing at least 30 days in advance of the existing project completion date (only one extension allowed);Any major changes to how the grant will be used (i.e. location of the project or expected outcomes) must be approved in advance by the department;Recipients should keep any reviews, publications, invitations, and/or catalogues in which the project is mentioned for reporting purposes; andAll previous recipients must have met reporting requirements in order to be eligible for subsequent funding.Application Requirements:The application package must include:Completed application form and signed Applicant Agreement;Contact information for the primary contact for all requirements of the grant;Most recent annual financial statement approved and signed by 2 board members (other than the Treasurer) or company principal(s);Fiscal year of the company;Royalties or license fees paid to creators and license holders;Business plan with detailed description of the project, objectives, planned activities, and expected results & benefits;Project budget;Description of the company's relevant production or publishing history;Resumes of the principals;Any additional support materials that may assist in the assessment process;Most recent return to Alberta Corporate Registry; andDocumentation related to the applicant's activity in production or publishing.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This fund contributes up to $180,000 to Albertan businesses who collaborate with a European partner to launch a revolutionary product development and commercialization project that aims to bring new products and services to market, and deliver economic benefits to citizens in both jurisdictions.Grant Value: $180,000Turnaround time: 3 monthsEligible Businesses:Albertan small and medium-sized enterprises (1 to 499 employees and less than $50 million in gross revenues);Incorporated (Albertan or Canadian registration) for-profit companies, sole proprietorships or partnerships with an office and employees in Alberta.All proposals must involve an industry partner from each jurisdiction (i.e. Alberta and Europe) with an interest in commercialization;European partners can be small or medium-sized enterprises, as well as larger companies or independent research institutions; andIf European partner is too large, they will be expected to match the funding contributed by GCCIR.Ineligible Businesses:Research organizations and university institutes are welcome to participate as additional project partners on the Albertan side, however they cannot receive GCCIR funding.Eligible Expenses:Costs of Alberta-based project personnel (i.e. researchers, engineers, technicians, tradesman, project
management and support staff when involved in project activity);Monetary contributions from GCCIR can also be put towards resources from a third-party organization (e.g. consultants or contractors);Costs of instruments and equipment required for the project (except when disposed of on a commercial basis after the project is over) are eligible;Additional costs incurred directly as a result of project activity;Other project-specific expenses including materials and supplies and travel expenses for trips to Europe related to project activities (travel expenses are limited to 10% of grant funds, but the recipient can contribute further funds for additional travel that can count as the recipient’s contribution toward the project);Professional services directly related to project activities;IP management costs; andFees for service labs.Ineligible Expenses:Training courses;Administrative fees or overhead charges for administering this program;Design and production of advertising material;Sales and promotion activities;Costs associated with applying for government grants and programs; andAny expenses outside of those listed above must be pre-approved by the GCCIR prior to the actual expenditure.Program Details:All applications will be peer-reviewed and ranked by a panel of external evaluators then the final decision-making is made by the GCCIR Steering Committee;The Albertan company is expected to match GCCIR funding through a combination of cash and in-kind contributions to the project;A minimum cash contribution of 40% of the total grant amount awarded is required.Eligible cash contributions include expenses for the direct costs of carrying out the project and achieving the objectives for which the grant was awarded (e.g. IP protection costs, new staff costs, equipment, tools, chemicals, software, consultants, etc.);In-kind contributions can be management time or tools that the company already owns, management overhead, specialized skills and advice, or access to special equipment, space, or data sets. In-kind contributions will be recognized only at fair market value and need to be backed up by proper documentation (e.g. paystubs, lease agreements, etc.);Up
to 50% of  costs for existing staff can be counted as in-kind contributions by the applicant;Funding from GCCIR can be used to cover up to 50% of existing staff

grants.grant_criteria: The Ontario Tourism and Travel Small Business Support Grant provides a one-time payment of $10,000 or $20,000 to small businesses in the tourism and travel industry that have suffered a revenue loss due to COVID-19. To be eligible, businesses must not have received the Ontario Small Business Support Grant.
