      Grant Criteria 
      The Ontario Tourism and Travel Small Business Support Grant provides a one-time payment of $10,000 or $20,000 to small businesses in the tourism and travel industry that have suffered a revenue loss due to COVID-19. To be eligible, businesses must not have received the Ontario Small Business Support Grant. The intent of the program is to help small businesses in the hardest-hit sectors recover from the impacts of COVID-19 and to help create and protect jobs.Grant Value: $10,000 to a maximum of $20,000Turnaround Time: 15 business daysEligible Businesses:Be in Ontario;Have not received the Ontario Small Business Support Grant;Have 99 or fewer employees on April 30, 2021;Maintains a Canda Revenue Agency (CRA) business number;If the business does not have one, the applicant may apply for one here.Have a revenue decline of at least 20% if the business began operating or was acquired before July 2, 2019:Must compare the total revenue for 3 consecutive months in 2019 with the same 3 consecutive months in 2020.Be a tourism or travel business:Amusement parks and waterparks;Bed and breakfasts that report their revenue as business income for income tax purposes;Cottages or cabins that report their revenue as business income for income tax purposes, and not as rental income;Fireworks display services;Hotels and motels;Hunting and fishing camps;Indoor attractions intended primarily for tourists (for example, haunted houses, funhouses, and mazes);Mobile food services (for example, chip wagons, food trucks, ice cream trucks);Observation towers;Operators of rides, games, and other activities that are operated on a concession basis at waterparks, amusement parks, carnivals, fairs, and festivals;Outdoor adventure operations without accommodation;Recreational and vacation camps (for example, overnight summer camps);Recreational rental services (for example, bicycle rental, canoe/kayak rental, houseboat rental);Resorts; andTravel agents and wholesalers registered with the Travel Industry Council of Ontario (TICO).Ineligible Businesses:Have received the Ontario Small Business Support Grant;Including businesses that are affiliated with any business that received the Ontario Small Business Support Grant.Began operating in 2021 or were acquired in 2021;Are owned, operated, or maintained by the federal, provincial or municipal government or any of their agencies;Are owned by a person holding federal or provincial office or a provincial employee;Businesses in one of the following categories:Campgrounds;Caterers;Children’s day camps;Conference centers and convention centers;Event planning services;Food and grocery delivery services, including online food ordering and delivery platforms;Indoor recreational facilities and activities intended primarily for use by members of the local community (for example, instructional courses, hobbies, exercise classes, children’s activities, and play areas);Museums, galleries, aquariums, zoos, science centers, landmarks, historic sites, botanical gardens, and similar attractions;Operators of farmer’s markets and vendors, and roadside stands selling farm products (for example, corn, eggs, berries), and activities at a farm, such as pick-your-own produce or fruit, mazes, and rides, that are secondary to the farm operation;Outdoor sports and recreation facilities;Racing venues, casinos, bingo halls, and gaming establishments;Restaurants and bars (including breweries and wineries that operate a restaurant or a bar);Short-term and long-term rental properties, including those listed through Airbnb and other websites, except for bed and breakfasts, cottages and cabins that report their revenue as business income;Ineligible rentals include, for example, multi-tenant (rooming) houses and lodgings owned or leased by businesses to house employees.Ski hills; andTour and guide services.Program Details:A business is affiliated with another business if:One of the businesses controls the other business directly or indirectly; andEach business is controlled directly or indirectly by the same business, individual, or group of individuals or businesses.A business is considered affiliated with the applicant even if the business does not satisfy the eligibility criteria for this grant;If a business is applying for funding was affiliated with 1 or more businesses on April 30, 2021:Formula:[(3-month revenue of applicant business in 2019 + 3-month revenue of affiliates in 2019) - (same 3-month period  revenue of applicant business in 2020 + same 3-month period revenue of affiliates in 2020)] / (3-month period  revenue of applicant business in 2020 + 3-month period revenue of affiliates in 2020)If the revenue decline is less than 20%, neither the applicant business nor any of its affiliates are eligible for the grant;If the revenue decline is 20% or more, the grant funding is based on the aggregate monthly revenue reduction for the affiliated group;Only the applicant and no other affiliated business may apply for funding under this program;If a new business was started or acquired after July 1, 2019, that business is omitted from the calculation of the affiliated group's percentage revenue decline and the dollar amount of revenue decline;Funding from this program may be used for any purpose deemed most sensible for the business;The employee count includes full-time, part-time, and seasonal workers from payroll data;The employee count on April 30, 2021, and the calculation of the revenue loss are determined using the total number of employees and revenues of the business and all affiliated businesses.When calculating revenue loss, only  revenue from its ordinary activities in Ontario earned from arm's-length sources are calculated;Revenues from extraordinary items and amounts on account of capital are excluded.The funding will be issued via Electronic Fund Transfer; andApplications may be selected for audit.  Additional information and supporting documentation may be required to prove eligibility.Funding ModelBusinesses began or were acquired before July 2, 2019Must have 20% revenue decline when comparing 2019 revenues to 2020 revenueCompared 3 consecutive months in 2019 to the same 3 consecutive months in 2020Formula:(2019 aggregate revenue for 3 consecutive months - 2020  aggregate revenue for 3 consecutive months) /2020  aggregate revenue for 3 consecutive months)Grant amount = average monthly loss over the 3 month period to a maximum of $20,000Start and end dates of the 3 month period do not have to correspond to the first and last day of the month (e.g. June 16 to September 15 is eligible)Note: if the applicant has affiliated businesses, please see the program details section above on revenue decline calculationsBusinesses began or were acquired after July 1, 2019, and before 2021Receives $10,000 minimum grantBusinesses began or were acquired in 2021Not eligible for the grant

The grant portion of this grant may provide up to  30% of eligible costs to a maximum of $99,999.Grant Value: $99,999Turnaround time:  6 monthsEligible Applicants:Be Métis, Status, Inuit or Non-Status Indian;Be a minimum of 18 years of age;Must be an Alberta resident (minimum 6 months) and the majority owner of a business located in Alberta;Must be involved in the operations of the business;Have experience in the industry of the business (minimum six months – 1 year) and must be able to provide the service(s) offered by the business;Must contribute a minimum of 10% cash equity of the project costs;Must obtain financing through a commercial lender for the costs that are not covered by the grant;The business must generate an income for the applicant of at least $20,000 annually; andThe business must be the applicant's main source of income.Eligible Projects:Total project must exceed $20,000;Project costs must be related to the start-up or expansion of a business;Project must lead to full time employment (cannot be part time or working another position elsewhere);The applicant must show that the business is viable and sustainable in their application; andThe applicant must have the necessary licensing, safety or certification for their particular business.Ineligible Expenses:Passive investments, property, houses or buildings;Anything involving tobacco or cannabis distribution;Sale of alcohol or gambling products;Purchase of land and/or buildings;Development of any product;Paying for a patent or assisting with testing of inventions/products; andDevelopment of land (creation of roads and infrastructure).Evaluation Criteria:Credit history of the applicant;Viability of the business proposal demonstrating there is a solid, verifiable market for the product or service;Management capabilities, experience, and background of the applicant;Cash flow prospects for the business to ensure they can comfortably repay the loan;Competitive position of the business in the industry it is involved in;Level of collateral security provided for the loan; andBusiness’s sensitivity to external factors such as the economy, dependence on certain industries, etc; Contingency plans and/or alternate sources of repayment.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Additional eligibility requirements may exist for the loan portion of the program so applicants are encouraged to discuss the eligibility of their project with a MEAP officer in advance of submitting an application;If an applicant received the grant in the past, and a minimum of 2 years has passed, they can re-apply for the grant;If the applicant is a Status individual they must apply to the Status Entrepreneur Assistance Program;This program is not retroactive, therefore any costs already incurred or purchases already signed to are not eligible for grant funds; andBusiness or asset acquisitions must be arm’s length transactions (can not purchase from family members).Forms:Program website: click hereLoan and MEAP application form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Industry Development Program offers up to 75% of costs to a maximum of $60,000 to trade and event organizations in Ontario that serve the interests of 1 or more of the book, magazine, film, television, or interactive digital media sectors. The funding can cover operations-related costs, including administrative, labour, and capital costs. The intent of the program is to expand the skills, business capacity, market share, sales, and innovation of the industry.Grant Value: Up to 75% to a maximum of $60,000 (Requests for higher amounts must be discussed with the appropriate program consultant prior to application)Turnaround Time: 9 weeks after deadlineEligible Applicants:Be incorporated or not-for-profit;If the applicant is neither incorporated nor non-profit, they must contact Ontario Creates prior to submitting an application.Be based in Ontario;If the applicant is a national organization, they must:Offer significant benefit to Ontario participants; andHave at least 60% of the membership in Ontario.Be in operation for at least 1 full year;Be a trade or event organization that serves the interests of 1 or more of the book, magazine, film, television, or interactive digital media sectors; andHave commercial general liability insurance of $2 million per occurrence.Eligible Activities:Stream 1 - Business DevelopmentSupports business to business and business to consumer development activities to generate new business leads, sales, and relationships;Includes but not limited to:Marketing through new channels;Targeting niche markets;Exploiting new geographic targetsstructured 1-on-1 or group meetings with buyers and sellers;business and/or incubators with market participation; andForums connecting buyers and investors with Ontario companies.Stream 2 - Capacity BuildingAddresses challenges and opportunities or environmental changes that contribute to the capacity of the organization or its stakeholder group;Well-defined learning activities for industry professionals;Industry events at conferences, markets, and festivals and activities that a trade organization has clearly identified as a  key priority on behalf of its members and stakeholders;Activities that provide strategic and organizational efficiencies of benefit to the applicant organization’s members and stakeholders. Must take place in Ontario;Unless has significant benefit to Ontario companies.Activities in either stream must target Ontario Creates' identified clients in the book, magazine, film, television, or interactive digital media sectors;Must provide targeted business opportunities relevant to the commercial interests of Ontario companies.Eligible Costs:Administrative costs are capped at 25% of the budget, including but not limited to:Office space/rent;Utilities;Payroll service costs;Couriers;Photocopying; andOrganization overhead costs.Labour costs:In-house and contract positions at a fair market rate are eligible.Capital costs are capped at 15% of the budget:Only eligible if the equipment is required for the eligible activity;If purchased, amortization  must  be  calculated  using  the straight-line method with a prescribed useful life of 24 months;If rented, the actual rental cost; andSoftware: 50% of the cost or the amortization expense using the straight-line method with a prescribed useful life of 12 months (whichever is less).Note: All costs with the exception of labour and administration must be paid to unrelated parties.Ineligible costs:Expenses incurred outside of the approved activity period;Expenses that were not in the original budget and which did not receive pre-approval by Ontario Creates;Labour costs not directly related to the activity;Staff benefit costs;In-kind costs for staff exceeding 25% of the applicant’s contribution;Occupancy costs, unless otherwise stated in program guidelines;Real estate costs and leasehold improvements;Capital costs related to permanent structures (e.g., materials, labour, land acquisition, purchase of equipment for project construction, any rehabilitation or retrofit of existing infrastructure assets);Cost of alcoholic beverages;Fees  relating to  the compilation  (notice-to-reader),  review,  or audit of applicant financial statements;Cost of General Liability insurance (however, the cost of specific event insurance is eligible);Sales Taxes: Taxes that are recoverable by the recipient may not be claimed as an eligible cost on the Activity Budget.       Grant Criteria 
      This program provides up to $1 million to major anchor attractions in urban areas, and up to $500,000 to both major anchor attractions in rural areas and tour bus companies that service tourism attractions in British Columbia. The grant amount for each organization is calculated based on their total revenue loss after deducting surpluses and other government funding received. The goal of this program is to support eligible organizations to operate at minimal levels while COVID-19-related restrictions on travel and indoor group gathering are still in place in the province.Grant Value: Stream 1 - Major anchor attractions in urban areas: up to $1,000,000Stream 2 - Major anchor attractions in rural areas: up to $500,000Stream 3 - Tour bus companies: up to $500,000Turnaround Time:  Funds will be provided in July 2021Eligible Organizations:Businesses: The majority share of the organization (at least 51%) is owned by one or more B.C. residents.Not-for-profits: The majority control of the organization (at least 51%) is carried out by B.C. residents.All eligible organizations must:Be currently operating and financially viable before February 1, 2020:Seasonal or temporarily closed attractions may be eligible if they qualify as one of three eligibility streams and were open to visitors for at least 60 days in 2019.Have at least a 30% reduction in revenue for the period from April 1, 2020 to March 31, 2021 when compared with the same period from 2019 to 2020;Be registered to operate in B.C. and its primary operations are located in and conducted in B.C.;Not presently be in default of payment of tax obligations that arose prior to the 2020 tax year;Have taken advantage of all other applicable COVID-19 relief programs;Demonstrate a need for support to remain open and operational at minimal levels;Be market ready according to Destination BC standards; andBe willing to make best efforts to recall back to work any willing and available employees who were laid off due to COVID without reducing their wages, vacation pay or other compensation.Ineligible Organizations:Accommodation providers including hotels, lodges, motels, resorts, campgrounds and RV parks;Restaurants, casinos, and spas;Car/RV rental;Wineries;Convention centres and other event venues;Festivals and events;Marinas;Crown corporations;Golf courses; andSports teams.Program Streams:Stream 1: Major anchor attractions in urban areas:The attraction is in an urban area:The Capital Regional District (excluding communities in electoral areas: the Juan de Fuca Electoral Area, Salt Spring Island Electoral Area and Southern Gulf Islands Electoral Areas);Metro Vancouver (excluding Bowen Island);Squamish;Whistler; andThe Fraser Valley Regional District.The attraction typically operates year-round;Based on 2019 data, the attraction receives 75,000+ visitors per year;Visitors pay a fee at a specific location and participate in a particular activity, usually for less than one day; E.g.; Amusement parks, zoos, botanical gardens, heritage sites, museums, galleries, science centres, nature parks, aerial cable cars or observatories.For-profit businesses must also prove:It employed 150+ people for at least 4 months of the calendar year (based on the 2019 calendar year), including part-time, seasonal and contracted workers.Stream 2: Major anchor attractions in rural areas (business or not-for-profit):The attraction is in a rural area (any area not defined in Stream 1);Based on 2019 data, the attraction receives 15,000+ visitors per year:The attraction typically operates year-round; andVisitors pay a fee at a specific location and participate in a particular activity, usually for less than one day:E.g.; Ski operators, whale watching, museums, heritage sites, galleries and wildlife parks.Stream 3: Tour bus companies:The company is integral to the operation of tourism attractions;It primarily supports the transportation of visitors to and from tourism attractions on a regular basis;Based on 2019 data, the company handles 30,000+ visitors per year; andThe company can demonstrate that it has an ongoing relationship with and supports one or more tourism attraction.Eligible Expenses:Necessary business expenses including payroll, rent, utilities, maintenance, vehicle leases, insurance or administrative fees and licensing;Expenses related to equipment or infrastructure to comply with COVID-19 guidelines and support the safety of visitors and workers;Expenses to restart or ramp up operations when provincial health orders and restrictions are lifted;Scheduled mortgage payments (not including prepayment of principal);Operating leases in effect since February 15, 2020; Municipal property taxes; andUp to 25% of funding may be used to repay debt incurred after February 15, 2020;Excludes debt owed to the federal government (e.g. debt incurred from a COVID-19 loan program).Note: Grant funding can only be used to cover costs essential to the operation of the organization.Ineligible Expenses:Paying employees more than their regular base pay, such as executive bonuses;Paying contractors or service providers more than fair market value for services performed;Buying real estate, making investments or providing loans to others;Making payments on debt incurred before February 15, 2020 (not including scheduled mortgage payments);Repayment of debts owed to any government;Capital expenses not related to COVID-19 adaptations or maintenance of capital assets;Paying federal or provincial taxes;Paying shareholder loans, dividends and inter-company or related party transfers/payments; andPaying for operations outside of B.C.Program Details:Successful applicants will be required to:Spend the funding 6 months after payments are deposited; andProvide a report on how the funding was used 7 months after payments are deposited.Reporting and auditing requirements will be outlined for successful applicants before they agree to receive funding.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:After reviewing eligibility criteria, businesses can contact COVID.Tourism.Recovery@gov.bc.ca to receive an application package with instructions;Applicants will need to prepare to submit documents like financial statements and tax returns;If an organization has multiple locations that collectively meets the visitor threshold for their stream, they can only apply for one grant; andApplications are due by June 7, 2021 at 1 pm.Forms:Program website: click here

        Recently Changed 
        Funding has changed to cover up to 40% of a project to a maximum non-repayable contribution of $350,000 (previously $250,000);Funds are disbursed after approval of claims submitted on a quarterly basis.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      Proof-of-concept plans for trials and demonstrations that are intended to exhibit the commercial feasibility of biologically-derived natural products or technologies may be granted up to 40% funding to a maximum of $350,000. The aim of this program is to prove the commercial feasibility of these products and technologies in order to minimize risk and advance future investment in the natural products sector. Grant Value: 40% of eligible project costs to a maximum of $350,000Turnaround Time: 2 monthsEligible Applicants:Canadian start-ups or SMEs:Must have the potential to achieve 10MM- 15MM in annual revenue within a market-reasonable period; andSole proprietors are ineligible.Research institutes:Products or technologies must address an industry or sector challenge with significant market potential; andNo limit on number of employees.Be a member of Canada’s Natural Product Innovation Cluster;Have a novel pre-commercial (Technology Readiness Levels(TRL) 4-9) 'natural product or technology';Defined as a biologically-based innovation that benefit people, animals and the planet, and can be applied to a range of industries, including: Food production and value-added agriculture; Bioproducts and sustainability; Human nutrition, health and wellness; Animal health and nutrition; and Water and waste management.Have potential for: Achieving 10MM- 15MM in annual revenue within a market-reasonable period;Significant economic, social, health and/or environmental benefits;Commercialization in Canada;Spillover benefits to more than one sector;Improving the representation of women, visible minorities, and Indigenous peoples in the natural products ecosystem.Eligible Activities:Animal, field, demonstration, or human trials;Late-stage trials for naturals products, services, or technologies that derive from a biological source; andCommercial demonstration trials.Ineligible Activities:Basic research or preliminary product/technology development;Pharmaceutical trials; andTrials that are not biological in nature.Eligible Expenses:Direct materials;Direct Labour;Subcontractors/consultants;Equipment (up to 10% of budget);Other direct costs (e.g. trial participant costs and some specialized software);Indirect costs up to ~15% of costs.Program Details:The project period cannot exceed 18 months; Applicants required to contribute 60% of project costs unless leveraging other government grant funding;Contract with NPC will include project scope, reporting requirements, and key milestones to be achieved;Applications will be reviewed by NPC staff, board members, and an external industry expert on a monthly basis;Disbursement of funds takes place through reimbursement of eligible project costs upon approval of quarterly reports;Includes a written and financial claim containing invoices and proof of payment.Annual reporting required for 5 years following program period; andFor research institutes, projects must be aimed at moving a product or technology from intellectual property disclosure to near-term spin-out and/or licensing opportunities.Evaluation Criteria: The novelty of the natural product or technology; Market opportunity; Business model/commercialization strategy;Competitors; Strength of the management team/research leadership team;Need and impact of the trial; Trial design and key activities; Qualifications of the individuals and/or centres conducting the trials; andStream specific eligibility:Music creation stream must include domestic  and  multinational  record  labels and  domestic music publishers;Music industry initiatives stream must include  music  industry  trade  associations  and  music  service organizations; andLive music streams must include live music promoters and presenters.Eligible Expenses:Administrative and overhead costs;Includes staff salaries, office space, and corporate services to a maximum of 25% of the total activity costs.Labour costs (salary or contract);New positions created from the proposed activity.Capital costs;Includes the purchase of equipment, materials, and/or software.Recording,  editing,  mixing costs;Master license fees for Ontario-based recordings;Must provide evidence that the original recording was recorded in Ontario, within the past 24 months.Video Production;Includes music videos, videos for online marketing purposes, and video recording of live performances for promotion or sale.Marketing and promotion activities for new recordings and/or online performances by Canadian artists signed to the applicant company;Up to $20,000 subsidy for direct tour costs for an artist signed to the applicant company;Includes marketing, promotion, audio/visual and stage design, technical services, travel, transportation, and Canadian crew employed by the artist or applicant.Acquiring  and  registering  copyrights; andBusiness  Development activities.Includes human resources enhancement,  undertaking strategic business travel, investing in data analytics, etc.Note: Costs must be directly related to the proposed activities.Ineligible Expenses:Costs relating to international artists and producers;Staff benefit costs;Cost of alcoholic beverages or cannabis-related products; andRelated party transactions which did not receive pre-approval by Ontario CreatesNote: For the complete list of ineligible expenses, please review the program guideline.Program Details:3 streams:Music creationSupports talent development (especially emerging artists) through recording and production, marketing, touring, and publishing;Music industry initiativesSupports activities to undertake professional development, export activities, conducting industry analysis, and building regional capacity; andLive musicSupports the production and promotion of live music events featuring Canadian artists;Includes music festivals and concert series;2022 intakes:The 1st intake closes on May 5, 2022;The 2nd intake closes on September 15, 2022.  Minimum funding amount: $10,000;First-time applicants must contact the OMO at least three weeks ahead of the application deadline to discuss eligibility;Activity spending may commence  upon application submission;Costs incurred prior to approval will be at the applicant’s own risk; andThe applicant must have a valid certificate of insurance to do so.All proposed  activities  must  be  included  in  the  Activity  Budget  template  provided  in  the  application;A  company Business  Plan is required for all applicants  requesting  $50,000 or more;Applicants requesting less than $50,000 have the option to either submit a business plan or answer the business plan related questions within the application;Successful applicants must start incurring expenses no  later than  90  days following the date of funding approval;Applicants that receive funding will have 12 months to execute their activities; andActivities must be completed with all expenses incurred and all deliverables provided by the applicant’s final report date, and no later than February 15, 2024.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Access to Talent Program enables SMEs and start-ups in the natural product sector to receive up to 40% to a maximum of $150,000 towards hiring a new experienced member on their team. The individual will be expected to support a project aimed at product and technology development or pre-commercial business development. The aim of this program is to boost talent at small companies with natural products or technologies that are derived from a biological source and benefit people, animals, and the planet.Grant Value:Stream 1 - For individuals with 5-9 years of experience40% of eligible costs to a maximum of $75,000Stream 2 - For individuals with 10+ years of experience40% of eligible costs to a maximum of $150,000Turnaround Time:  2 monthsEligible Employer:Incorporated Canadian start-ups and SMEs;Up to 25 full-time equivalent employees;Be a member of Canada’s Natural Product Innovation Cluster; Have a novel pre-commercial (Technology Readiness Levels(TRL) 4-9) 'natural product or technology';Defined as a biologically-based innovation that benefits people, animals, and the planet, and can be applied to a range of industries, including: Food production and value-added agriculture; Bioproducts and sustainability; Human nutrition, health, and wellness; Animal health and nutrition; and Water and waste management.Have potential for: Achieving 10MM- 15MM in annual revenue within a market-reasonable period;Significant economic, social, health, and/or environmental benefits;Commercialization in Canada;Technological advancement and benefits to the natural products ecosystem across Canada;Spillover benefits to more than one sector; andImproving the representation of women, visible minorities, and Indigenous peoples in the natural products ecosystem.Employers do not need to have identified a candidate before applying, candidate can be chosen before or after application submission. Note: The program focus is on disruptive technologies, specifically proprietary biological-based technologies. However, the program does not invest in technologies based on software, or artificial intelligence. Eligible Candidate:Must be hired as a full-time employee;Demonstrated experience to successfully execute the project identified by the applicant that is critical to the product or technology development;Must be a new hire and not previously a full-time employee;The company can have the candidate identified at the time of application or can recruit the candidate after the application submission, but the candidate’s resume must be submitted to NPC for review and approval prior to final approval of funding.Cannot be responsible for or have other employees responding to them directly; andMust spend 100% of their time on activities directly related to the project and its key milestones.Eligible Activities :Include but are not limited to an employee:Working directly on product or technology development;Conducting pre-commercial business development;Working on the regulatory strategy and/or collecting necessary data for regulatory submissions; andWorking on product or technology scale-up.Evaluation Criteria: Novelty of the natural product or technology; Market opportunity; Business model;Competitors; Strength of the management team;Technical feasibility of the project to be undertaken;Position to be filled; Qualifications of the candidate; andKey milestones and their impact.Program Details:Funds may only be used for salary costs (any recruiting costs not included);Applicants are required to contribute 60% of salary costs unless leveraging other grants;Candidate may be identified at the time of application or can be recruited after application submission (within 3 months of approval):The candidate's resume must be submitted to NPC for review prior to final approval of financing.Eligible positions include but are not limited to:Product or technology development;Business development;Regulatory strategy and/or collecting necessary data for regulatory submissions;Product or technology scale-up;Marketing or sales strategy; andFundraising to support the growth of the product or technology.The project period is a maximum of 18 months (employment term expected to exceed this duration);The project must provide technological advancement and benefits to the natural products ecosystem across Canada;Contract with NPC will include project scope, reporting requirements, and key milestones to be achieved;Disbursement of funds takes place through reimbursement of eligible project costs upon approval of quarterly reports;Includes a written and financial claim containing invoices and proof of payment.Annual reporting required for 5 years following the program period.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program can be combined with funding from all government sources (federal, provincial, territorial, municipal) yet total assistance received may not exceed 75% of eligible costs;SMEs that are not yet members of the Natural Product Innovation Cluster can purchase a membership for $150/yr, prorated;Must provide basic contact information and a 500-word description of the organization.Applicants must contact the NPC at programs@naturalproductscanada.com to have an eligibility assessment conducted;If the assessment is successful, applicants will then be invited to submit an application;If the application is unsuccessful, applicants will be given feedback and may request an appeal within 15 days of receiving the rejection from NPC; Process Best Practices:Employee is ideally identified prior to application, but otherwise may be hired within 3 months after submission;Interested companies may visit here to learn more about the cluster and review which sectors are included in 'natural products';Employee start date can be as early as application submission date; andApplications will be reviewed by NPC staff, board members, and an external industry expert on a monthly basis.Forms:Program website: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Gearing Up program provides up to 70% a maximum of $7,000 to mining or mineral exploration employers to subsidize the hiring of post-secondary students. The intent of the program is to attract talent to in-demand mining careers and to build skills needed for a meaningful career in this sector.Grant Value: 50% of wages to a maximum of $5000;70% of wages to a maximum of $7000 for students from the following underrepresented groups:Women in STEM;Indigenous peoples;Persons with disabilities;Recent immigrants;First year students; andVisible minorities.Turnaround Time: 2 weeksEligible Employers:Be Canadian-owned or a Canadian subsidiary;For-profit companies in the mining or mineral exploration sector; andNon-profit organizations.Eligible Candidates: Be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person with refugee protection given under the law;Be registered in a post-secondary program (full- or part-time);Studying fields related to science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and/or business; andStudents in both required and optional courses with Work Integrated Learning components are eligible.Note: International student, students in apprenticeships or vocational studies are ineligible for the programProgram Details:Placements must be completed within Canada;Can be full-time or part-time;Employers are responsible for the recruiting and the selection of participants;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Businesses must match funds received and propose budgets where the business can contribute an equal portion of funds.Grant Value: 50% of costs up to $1,000Turnaround time: Up to 2 weeksEligible Businesses: Must be located in Edmonton;Must have demonstrated revenue decline as a result of COVID-19;Must have a valid business licence, unless not required by the City to have one;Only business owners or designated authorities can apply.Eligible Costs:Costs incurred after grant approval;Any goods or services a business will purchase to help them adapt or recover from COVID-19; andExpenses that fall under any of the following categories:Jobs (e.g. for contracted work from other businesses or to improve the safety of the workplace so more employees can return to work, etc.);Financial Sustainability (e.g. to replenish merchandise that expired as a result of COVID-19 restrictions, etc.);COVID-19 Impact (e.g. branded personal protective equipment, safety measures such as plexiglass installation, etc.);Partner Leverage (e.g. leveraging funds from this grant to obtain additional funding from other organizations to support larger projects, etc.);Economic Diversification (e.g. equipment purchases that allow a business to pivot or access new markets, etc.);Business Transformation (e.g. online retail, marketing efforts, online ordering & delivery services, virtual learning, etc.);Tangible Placemaking Benefits (e.g. patio set-ups, pick-up window installations, etc.);Environment Alignment (e.g. recyclable and compostable packaging and food containers, etc.); andCommunity Impact (e.g. support for community initiatives that support marginalized communities, etc.).Ineligible Costs:Rent/lease/mortgage;Payroll;Membership fees;Permit fees;Debt reduction;Retroactive costs;Insurance, and other similar expenses; Expenses that are borne through regular business operations and are not a result of or response to the COVID-19 pandemic (such as maintenance); andAny security upgrades that detract from human-oriented design or urban design principles including: Anti-loitering spikes, anti-loitering sonic devices, bars or rolling shutters on windows/doors, or opaque window wraps.Program Details:Grants are limited to 1 per business, even if the business has multiple locations;Approved applicants must submit receipts and invoices to the City within 90 days of the cheque being issued;Cheques will be mailed to the address provided in the application, and made payable to the legal name of the business after applications have been reviewed;Funding decisions made by the City are final and cannot be appealed.

        The Adoption Stream intake deadline is now June 22, 2023; andCost-shared funding available up to 40% of eligible costs to a max of $2 million per project or up to 50% of eligible costs to a max of $2 million per project where the majority of the business is owned by one or more under-represented groups. 
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The Agricultural Clean Technology Program: Adoption stream provides up to $2 million in funding to support the adoption of commercially available clean technology and processes. The priority areas include green energy, precision agriculture, and bioeconomy. The intent of the program is to promote sustainable growth and lower carbon emissions in Canada's agriculture and agri-food sectors.Grant Value:Up to 40% of eligible costs to a maximum of $2 million per project; andUp to 50% of eligible costs to a max of $2 million per project where the majority of the business is owned by one or more under-represented groups. NOTE: Under-represented groups included: Indigenous Peoples, Youth ages 35 or under, Women, Visible minorities, Persons with disabilities, 2LGBTQI+.Turnaround Time: 120 business daysEligible Applicants:For-profit organizations including:Businesses and/or corporations;Individuals or sole-proprietorships;Co-operatives or partnerships; and Indigenous groups.Must be Canadian entity and/or incorporated in Canada;Have secured your portion financial contributions for the project, per the cost-share ratios, before applying; andHave not previously received funding from the Adoption Stream.Ineligible Applicants:Financial institutions;Crown corporations;Federal government departments and agencies; Foreign governments; Not-for-profits; andAcademia including universities, colleges and researchers.Eligible Activities:The adoption of green energy and energy efficiency technologies in agriculture, including but not limited to:Energy-efficient, low-emissions equipment (e.g. commercial grain dryers);Technologies to power farms with clean energy (e.g. fuel switching, such as conversion from coal or diesel);Energy-efficient heating systems for functional on-farm structures (e.g. barns);Energy heat pumps and frequency converters; andSolar or geo-thermal systems panels and solar powered technology (e.g. ventilation, farm equipment, sensors, etc.).The adoption of precision agriculture technologies, including but not limited to:Nutrient management technologies that optimize fertilizer application;Variable-rate application technologies and GPS auto-steer guidance systemsTechnologies and systems to collect and analyze data that enable reduced fertilizer use, including soil sensors, yield monitors, remote imagery, and related geographic information systems technologies; andMethane reduction technologies that optimize livestock digestion if commercially available, for example novel feed grain processing and precision feed technology.Bioeconomy solutions that use agriculture waste and by-products to generate energy or create bioenergy products, including but not limited to:Technologies and equipment to support improved manure management and processing waste into bioenergy products and other useful outputs including: Anaerobic digester for processing agricultural waste into bioenergy;Bio-product/biomass boiler heating of farm operations/greenhouses;Implementing solutions that use agri-based products, such as bioplastics;Eligible Costs:Capital assets:capital assets are tangible assets that are purchased, constructed, developed or otherwise acquired, and are required for the execution of the project;Salaries and benefits:salaries and benefits towards installation only as directly related to completing the project activities;Contracted services:professional or specialized services for which a contract is entered into, such as consultant/expert services required for implementation of a new technology;Travel:project travel directly related to the installation of technologies and equipment supported by the Adoption Stream based on a per diem rate that includes accommodations, meals, incidentals and transportation (air or ground). Travel is limited to economy rates;Other direct project costs:other project-related costs, such as translation, permits, the rental, lease of equipment or machinery, goods and services and all related shipping and transportation costs, including freight, required to carry out the project, and materials/consumables needed to undertake the project.Ineligible Costs: Administrative costs or costs of project management and administrative staff salaries;Labour costs, other than as part of installation costs, including wage subsidies;Capital items not specifically required for the execution of the project;Costs for activities that are deemed to be part of normal business practice for any recipient;Costs related to marketing activities and business promotion;Land purchases;Travel, not directly related to the installation of equipment;Hospitality;In-kind contributions;Goodwill;Legal fees;costs to prepare the contribution agreement or related schedules; any portion of any cost that, in AAFC's opinion, exceeds the fair market value for that cost item;any cost, such as amortization that would not result in a direct, out-of-pocket expense for the recipient;costs being reimbursed under an existing federal, provincial or territorial program.Program Details:Program will prioritize project submissions that provide the highest estimates for GHG, fertilizer and/or methane emission reductions;Maximum funding across multiple projects will generally not exceed $5 million;The program focus is on supporting projects valued at $50,000 or more of total eligible project costs;In-kind contributions are not eligible under the Agricultural Clean Technology Program;Costs incurred from the date of the submission of a completed application are eligible;Payments for eligible project costs will only be made once a Contribution Agreement is signed; andApplicants will be required to provide financial, progress, and performance reports, or other reports as detailed in the contribution agreement.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:The program allows funding to be used in conjunction with other sources of government funding up to 75% of total eligible costs of the project;This funding cannot be used retroactively as only costs incurred from the date of the submission of a completed application are eligible;Process Best Practices:Applications must clearly indicate all sources of project funding, including the applicant’s contribution and other partners' sources of funding, including funding from:Government of any level;Industry associations and networks;Businesses;Academic institutions; andIndigenous groups.Assessment Criteria:Activities and outcomes proposed should align with program objectives and priorities;Supporting information on the reduction of GHG emissions and other environmental co-benefits that can be demonstrated and measured;The proposed activities and expenditures are eligible, reasonable, and required to meet the project objectives;The applicant possesses the qualifications and track record required to deliver the project;All sources of funding for the project to be supported under the project are identified;Ability to provide information on results and indicators; andAlignment with priority areas.Forms:Program webpage: click hereTo download the project application form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Canada Recovery Hiring Program (CRHP) provides a fixed rate subsidy of up to 50% of incremental remuneration paid to active employees between June 6, 2021, and May 7, 2022. This is to help eligible employers offset extra labour costs needed as businesses reopen, either by increasing wages or hours worked or hiring more staff. The intent of the program is to help businesses that have been hit hardest by the pandemic by providing a strong incentive to begin hiring as soon as possible.Grant Value:Claim PeriodPeriod 17Period 18Period 19Period 20Period 21Period 22Claim Period DatesJune 6 - July 3, 2021July 4 – July 31, 2021Aug 1 – Aug 28, 2021Aug 29 – Sept 25, 2021Sept 26 – Oct 23, 2021Oct 24 – Nov 20, 2021Subsidy Rate50%50%50%40%30%20%Note: The 1st period of CRHP is Period 17 to avoid confusion and to align with Periods in CEWS.Turnaround Time: 8 calendar daysEligible Applicants:Meet all the eligibility requirements of the Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy (CEWS):Have a Canada Revenue Agency payroll account on March 15, 2020;Are an eligible employer; andExperience a revenue drop for CEWS (more than 0% in period 17, more than 10% in periods 18-22).For more details, please visit CEWS - Who Can ApplyFor-profit applicants must meet the following additional criteria:Be a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC);Cooperative corporations eligible for the small business deduction;Partnerships where at least 50% of the partnership's interests are held directly or indirectly by employers eligible for the CRHP.Revenue drop required:Period 17: more than 0%; andPeriod 18-20: more than 10%.Note: Publicly-listed corporations are not eligible for the CRHP.Eligible Employees:Existing and new employees;Be actively employed throughout a qualifying period or a portion of the period;Be primarily employed in Canada; andArm's length and non-arm's length employees*.*Arm's length employees are those who are independent, and one does not have undue influence over the other.Ineligible Employees:Furloughed employees (those on leave with pay but do not perform any work):Must not have worked at all for 1 or more full weeks in the claim period;Must not have been on paid absence (ie. vacation leave, sick leave or sabbatical;Have received full or partial pay from the applicant for the week; andHave been in an employer-employee relationship during this time (not terminated).Eligible Expenses:Salary, wages, and other remuneration; andCertain taxable benefits, and fees, commissions or other amounts paid for services.Note: Does not include a retiring allowance or severance pay, or items such as stock option benefits or the personal use of a corporate vehicle.Subsidy Calculation:Subsidy rate = (A-B) x CA:The total amount of eligible remuneration paid to all eligible employees for the current claim period;The amount is at least:$1129;The amount of eligible remuneration paid to each employee in the respect of that week;If the employee is a non-arm’s-length employee, the pre-crisis remuneration of the employee determined for that week; andIf the employee is on leave with pay that week, $0.B:The total amount of eligible remuneration paid to all eligible employees for the base period (March 14 to April 10, 2021);The amount is at least:$1129;The amount of eligible remuneration paid to each employee in the respect of that week;If the employee is a non-arm’s-length employee, the pre-crisis remuneration of the employee determined for that week; andIf the employee is on leave with pay that week, $0.C:Period 17Period 18Period 19Period 20Period 21Period 22June 6 - July 3, 2021July 4 – July 31, 2021Aug 1 – Aug 28, 2021Aug 29 – Sept 25, 2021Sept 26 – Oct 23, 2021Oct 24 – Nov 20, 202150%50%50%40%30%20%There is no overall limit on the total subsidy amount that an eligible employer may claim;CRHP subsidy rates are flat-rate;No top-up amounts available;Does not include the refund of employer-paid portion of CPP/QPP/EI/QPIP for employees on leave with pay;Does not subtract amounts received through ESDC's work-sharing program; andThe subsidy is calculated differently for eligible arm's length and non-arm's length employees.If the employee is non-arm's length, the eligible employer's qualifying revenue for the prior reference period is deemed to be $100; andAll non-arm's length parties must jointly elect with the applicant in order to use this rule.Program Details:Applicants must claim ONLY the greater of either CEWS or CRHP for a claim period, but not both;The subsidy program offering the lower amount will be deemed to be nil.If the CRHP amount and the CEWS amount are equal for the same claim period, the eligible employer must claim the CEWS amount, and the CRHP amount will be deemed to be nil;If an application is filed for CRHP for a claim period, the applicant will not be required to submit a separate application for the CEWS for the same claim period;The deadline to apply or increase the amount of a previous claim is 180 days after the end of the claim period;There is no deadline to cancel or reduce the amount of a previous claim;Payments can be issued via direct deposit or by cheque; andIf a payment of more than $25 million is expected, the applicant must be registered for both direct deposit and for the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS).To begin the registration process, send LVTS an email at brdlvtsreg@cra-arc.gc.caNote: The program will be in place until May 7, 2022. Applicants can apply for the final claim period until November 3, 2022.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program cannot be combined with federal funding from the Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy (CEWS);As the deadline to apply for the subsidy is 180 days after the end of the claim period, the funding is retroactive;Applicants should have the payroll program account number handy for application;Applicants should keep claim records such as reduction in revenue and amounts paid to employees;To change claims to apply for CEWS instead of CRHP, the applicant only needs to apply for CEWS for the same period. The CRHP will be replaced when the CEWS claim is submitted; andThe net difference will be issued.To return an overpayment of CRHP, the applicant will be subject to interest. The applicant will be required to return the overpayment amount as soon as possible to reduce interest charges.For more details, please visit Return a Payment.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication form: click here

The aim of the program is to develop strong business or commercialization plans that demonstrate the growth potential of and attract investment for the eventual market entry of natural products or technologies (TRL 4-9), which must be biologically-based innovations that benefit people, animals and the planet.Grant Value: up to 40% of eligible project costs to a maximum of $25,000Turnaround Time: 1 monthEligible Applicants:Canadian start-ups or SMEs:Must have the potential to achieve 10MM- 15MM in annual revenue within a market-reasonable period; andSole proprietors are ineligible.Research institutes:Products or technologies must address an industry or sector challenge with significant market potential; andNo limit on the number of employees.Be a member of Canada’s Natural Product Innovation Cluster;Have a novel pre-commercial (Technology Readiness Levels(TRL) 4-9) 'natural product or technology';Defined as a biologically-based innovation that benefits people, animals, and the planet, and can be applied to a range of industries, including: Food production and value-added agriculture; Bioproducts and sustainability; Human nutrition, health, and wellness; Animal health and nutrition; and Water and waste management.Have potential for: Achieving 10MM- 15MM in annual revenue within a market-reasonable period;Significant economic, social, health, and/or environmental benefits;Commercialization in Canada;Spillover benefits to more than one sector;Improving the representation of women, visible minorities, and Indigenous peoples in the natural products ecosystem; andA project budget of at least $12,500.Eligible Activities:Costs of engaging 1+ experts (external consultant or other service providers) to assist in strengthening or revising the business or commercialization plan via any of the following:Market, Customer, & Competitive Analysis;Value Proposition;Regulatory Plan;IP Plan;Financial Plan; and Production Plan.Assessment Criteria: The novelty of the natural product or technology; Market opportunity; Business model/commercialization strategy;Competitors; Strength of the management team/research leadership team;Need for the business or commercialization plan; Technical feasibility of the project;Anticipated outcomes; and Statement of work(s) and qualifications of the selected expert(s).Program Details:Applicants may have a preferred expert(s) at the time of application or may recruit after the application is submitted;Applicants are required to contribute 60% of project costs unless also leveraging other grants;Contract with NPC will include project scope, reporting requirements, and key deliverables to be achieved;Disbursement of funds takes place through reimbursement of eligible project costs upon approval of quarterly reports; Includes a written and financial claim containing invoices and proof of payment.Annual reporting is required for 5 years following the program period.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Alberta-DT program supports digital SMEs by providing up to $50,000 to fund projects that enable businesses to build traction through customer acquisition, activation, retention, referral, and ultimately revenue. The aim of this program is to accelerate the growth of digital firms that rely on software development for their product or service offerings, in order to generate economic and social impact for Alberta.Grant Value: 50% up to $50,000Turnaround Time: 6 to 8 weeksEligible Applicants:Be a for-profit 'digital SME';An SME that relies on software development for 1 or more of its products and/or services and intends to rapidly scale in the global marketplace.Have fewer than 50 full-time employees;Have less than $1M annual reoccurring revenue;Have a founding team larger than 1;Demonstrate previous investment into the company by the founding team;Be an Alberta-based company:Physical and corporate operational presence in Alberta;Albertan ownership and incorporation;May otherwise be incorporated federally or in another jurisdiction AND extra-provincially registered in Alberta; ORBe a General Partnership, Limited Partnership, or Limited Liability Partnership AND registered in Alberta.Intent that operational benefits will flow primarily within the province.Have up-to-date corporate filings;Have not previously received Digital Traction funding;Be in good financial standing with Alberta Innovates and its subsidiaries InnoTech Alberta and C-Fer Technologies.Note: Applicants cannot concurrently receive funding from other Alberta Innovates Programs.Eligible Activities:Customer and/or client discovery;Digital market assessment and segmentation analysis;Data-driven, online market assessment testing;Product development based on client feedback;Advanced market assessment or segmentation analysis; andAdvanced sales and/or marketing strategies.Eligible Expenses:Costs incurred after the signing of the Investment Agreement;Costs incurred between arm's length entities (with no existing relationships);Wages and salaries for individuals working directly on the project:Up to $50/hour for T4 or contract employees; andUp to 50% of total funding for founder's salary costs (must have 15% equity in applicant company).Costs of materials;Acquisitions of software or information databases (prorated over the duration of project);Advertising costs for data-based marketing strategies for customer discovery purposes; Cost of sub-contractors at fair market rates;Additional direct operating costs beyond labour and materials; andAny other cost which Alberta Innovates pre-approves in writing.Program Details:The project must be completed within 1 year;The project start date should be at least 45 days from the application submission date;Businesses must provide a minimum 25% cash contribution; The project must outline 3 defined business milestones to be reached during the project to measure progress;Have the first milestone activities identified to a maximum of $15,000 (includes payment upon execution of agreement, up to $10,000);Individual milestones cannot exceed $20,000 to a maximum of $50,000 for all 3 milestones; Project milestones are based on business outcomes, with activities required to reach those milestones; TDAs will monitor the progress of the project and provide coaching to the business; Milestone activities are flexible and may be adjusted as the project progresses;An advance payment of up to $10,000 will be released once the Investment Agreement is signed by both parties; Further funding is disbursed at the completion of each milestone; andAnnual reporting to the program will be required for 5 years following project completion.The Ideal applicant will have:a minimum viable product (MVP) to test with customers;a minimum TRL 4 and at the Validating stage of development;not previously received Digital Traction funding;performed preliminary customer discovery work to inform the development;a digital technology employed in an innovative way and/or with proprietary features to allow for a competitive advantage over existing solutions;a digital technology that could scale up in one to two years, if successful;no significant capital or regulatory barriers, not addressed by the project, that may be better addressed by other funding resources;completed a lean canvas, business model canvas, or similar tools to demonstrate anunderstanding of the problem to be solved and the customer profile; anda traction roadmap or similar tool to demonstrate customer acquisition targets for the next three years and what is required to get to those targets.Note: If the application is rejected two times for an Alberta Innovates funding program, the applicant can no longer be eligible to apply for funding for that project/technology.

      Grant Criteria 
      This cost-sharing program provides up to $250,000 to businesses seeking to meet assurance requirements needed in Alberta’s livestock, crop, and apiculture industries in both domestic and export markets. The program supports solutions that address assurance issues and gaps for plant health, apiculture health, livestock health, biosecurity, traceability, surveillance, and livestock welfare gaps by funding costs related to technologies and technical, compliance, and market expertise.Grant Value: Up to $250,000Capital expenses: cost-shared at 25% grant and 75% applicant;Non-capital expenses: cost-shared at 50% grant and 50% applicant.Turnaround Time: 19 weeksEligible Applicants:Agri-processors;Manufacturer operating in Alberta;Active in the business of changing a raw agricultural commodity into a value-added product; andOperates 1+ processing facilities that are registered by federal or provincial inspection authorities;Primary producers;Must be operating in Alberta; andHas input costs of agricultural crops or livestock producing at least $25,000 worth of farm commodities annually (does not include a landlord whose only interest in the crop or livestock is that of ownership of the land).Industry organizations; andIndian bands and Métis settlements in Alberta.Ineligible Applicants:Retail businesses, restaurants, and food service establishments;Applied research organizations and research stations;Exporters;Post-secondary institutions; andMunicipalities and government agencies.Eligible Expenses:Capital expenses:Costs for specialized equipment; andCosts for specialized technologies, integrated computers and software.Non-capital expenses:Incremental costs for labour, salaried or contract services;Costs associated with surveys, sampling and diagnostics;Costs for assurance program or system development, and its implementation;Costs for new or incremental certification to third-party standards (i.e. audit services);Costs for advertising a training session and development of related
materials;Reasonable consulting and professional fees, including speaker fees related to the delivery of training sessions;Cost of developing and distributing extension documents;Reasonable costs for materials and supplies; andTravel expenses for travel within Alberta directly related to the project, as set out in the Alberta CAP Travel Expense Policy.Excludes travel expenses for individuals participating in
training sessions delivered by the applicant.Ineligible Expenses:Taxes;Financing fees and interest charges;Legal fees;Expenses for construction and/or purchase of land, buildings, roads or vehicles;Expenses incurred in transactions that are not at arm's length;Costs incurred by the applicant to prepare the application;Costs for re-certification to the expired or current level;Hosting costs e.g. for food and beverages;Costs for day-to-day operations and general office equipment including overhead, administration, salary/wage support and maintenance costs;In-kind costs from any provincial or federal government employee;Ongoing software licensing costs or fees;Costs to set up a society, association or company, and membership fees, dues and contributions; andExpenses paid to a Government of Canada department or agency.Eligible Activities:Must be related to complying with the market assurance requirements for:Plant, livestock, and bee health;Biosecurity;Traceability; orLivestock welfare.Purchase of/modifications to operational systems, technologies, processes and controls needed to meet assurance requirements;Access to expertise for the development of protocols needed to maintain market access, or gain access to a new or emerging market;Initial or incremental implementation of third party independent assurance systems; andSurveillance related to supporting assurance for market opportunities.Ineligible Activities: Stand-alone feasibility or market studies;Activities where the Gap to Market Access is not directly related to livestock, crop or bee health, biosecurity, traceability, surveillance or welfare; andEducation/extension/direct marketing to consumers.Assessment Criteria:The capacity of the project to successfully achieve its objectives;The ability of the project to effectively control risk(s) to provide assurance required for market access; and Impact of the project to provide benefits for participants, the Alberta industry, and Albertans.Program Details:Applicants must obtain all required governmental approvals prior to beginning the project; I.e. public health and safety, labour codes and standards, care and use of animals in research, wildlife habitat, and environmental protection.In-kind contributions may not be used towards the applicant’s cost-share of the total eligible expenses unless they are an industry organization; andEligible expenses are calculated based on the actual out-of-pocket cost to the applicant (i.e. cost of the eligible expense less any rebates, discounts, incentives, and/or credits, whether provided at the time of purchase or at a later date).

      Grant Criteria 
      The Jobs and Growth Fund (JGF) helps businesses and organizations access loans (at 0% interest) and grants, respectively, for projects that generate jobs and inclusive economic opportunities while advancing the transition to a green economy, future proof SMEs through digital adoption, and strengthen capacity in sectors for economic recovery and growth.  Eligible project costs may be covered up to 50% for businesses and up to 90% for non-for-profit organizations. The goal of the fund is to enhance the resiliency of critical sectors in the economy that will lead to job creation and growth.  Grant Value:  Up to $10MUp to 50% of eligible costs for businesses (repayable)Up to 90% of eligible costs for non-profit organizations (non-repayable)Up to 100% of eligible costs for Indigenous-led organizations (non-repayable)Note: The average size of projects is approximately $1.4MTurnaround Time: 12 weeksEligible Applicants:Businesses:Primarily SMEs with fewer than 500 full-time employees.Not-for-profit organizations; Indigenous organizations such as settlements, councils, not-for-profits, and businesses; Partnerships:Considered on a case by base basis; andPartners are expected to be incorporated.Eligible Costs:Include but are not limited to:Capital costs (e.g. purchase of equipment, machinery and associated costs such as installation); andLabour (e.g. salaries, benefits);Marketing;Costs related to intellectual property;Technology adoption;Technology development and commercial demonstrations;Travel and accommodations within Treasury Board guidelines;Professional, advisory, technical services.Eligible Activities:Activities that support the transition to a green economy:Development and adoption of clean technology;Help communities and businesses plan and drive clean, sustainable economic growth;Partner with organizations to create green regional clusters; andWork with organizations supporting businesses to transition to a green economy.Activities that foster an inclusive recovery:Support businesses owned or majority-led by underrepresented groups; and I.e. Indigenous peoples, members of racialized communities, women, youth, LGBTQ2, persons with disabilities, newcomers to Canada, and members of official language minority communities.Support non-for-profits providing inclusive business services to improve access to capital, mentoring opportunities and networks.Activities that preserve Canada’s competitiveness and future-proof SMEs through digital adoption:Development or adoption of digital and technological solutions to increase and promote business productivity; andInvest in technologies that help scale businesses, enhance their capabilities and increase resilience.Activities that strengthen capacity in sectors critical to Canada’s recovery and growth:Scale-up and market expansion activities that bolster traditional areas of strength;Develop emerging areas of global competitive advantage; andSupply chain adaptation and diversification in critical sectors such as food production, medical supplies and bio-manufacturing.Other types of activities that support SMEs and communities that are economically vital to communities (i.e. major employers in those communities).Assessment Criteria:Project applications should state how activities and expenses relate to the core program objectives:Transitioning to a green economy; Fostering an inclusive recovery; Preserve Canada’s competitiveness, future-proof SMEs and enhance resilience through productivity improvement and digital adoption; and Strengthening capacity in sectors critical to Canada’s recovery and growth.Program Details:All projects must start after April 19, 2021 and end by March 31, 2024;Project timeline must include milestones with measurable and trackable objectives;Businesses must apply by contacting their regional development agency (RDA); andIndigenous applicants (businesses or organizations) may be eligible to receive funding for up to 100% of eligible costs.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Poultry and Egg On-Farm Investment program provide over $250,000 in funding to chicken, turkey, egg, and broiler hatching eff producers. The funding can be used to hire contractors, constructing new infrastructure, purchasing equipment, and other related expenses. The intent of the program is to improve on-farm efficiency, food safety and environmental sustainability.Grant Value:Up to 85% of eligible costs for Youth ProducersUp to 70% of eligible costs for regular applicantsTurnaround Time: 100 business daysEligible Applicants:Be one of the following:Chicken producers;Turkey producers;Turkey breeders;Egg producers; andBroiler hatching egg producers.Be an individual and/or legal entity capable of entering into legally binding agreements or contracts;Have held quota/shares of provincial production on January 1, 2021;Be one of the following types:Poultry and/or egg producers holding quota;Poultry and/or egg producers licensed, or equivalent, by a provincial marketing agency;Atlantic Canada Hatching Egg Producers; andPoultry and/or egg producers under new entrants programs with loaned quota and/or whole-farm leases with loaned quota at the time of the calculation.Eligibility for Young Producer:Is 35 years old or younger on January 1, 2021;Is actively engaged in farming in Canada;Is either:A majority owner:Is a sole proprietor;Has majority ownership or more than 50% of the business;Led by a young producer who has:Managed the business for more than 2 years;Is working towards acquisition/successionHas an active role in strategic decision-making;Be a child's spouse or grandchild of the majority; andBe currently developing or has developed a succession plan to acquire the farm.Eligible Activities:Meet 1 or more of the following objectives:Increasing efficiency or productivity;Improving on-farm food safety and biosecurity;Improving environmental sustainability;Responding to consumer preferences (improving animal welfare, adopting alternative housing systems, transitioning to organic production, etc.)Examples include but are not limited to:The hiring of external expertise;Construction of new infrastructure or expansion of infrastructure;Building retrofits;Purchasing equipment;Shipping and installation of eligible assets, equipment, and materials; andTraining related to other eligible project activities.Eligible Expenses:Capital assets;Contracted services;Salaries and benefits pertaining to:Transportation and installation of eligible assets/materials;New infrastructure and retrofits.Non-recurring costs for equipment and operational upgrades.Note: Eligible costs must be incurred on or after March 19, 2019.Ineligible Expenses:The purchase of quota;Animal purchases (replacing or increasing flock);The refundable portion of Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/ HST);Acquisition of land or existing buildings;Marketing costs;Legal fees;On-going support costs for items such as software licenses, troubleshooting, and upgrades; and machinery maintenance or repair;Banking/credit card fees and interest charges.Note: Please see the program guide for the complete list of ineligible expenses.Program Details:Maximum funding is based on the share of provincial quota/production on January 1, 2021, as identified by the respective provincial marketing board;Applicants must register with the program prior to the application submission here;Applicants with multiple licenses will have the option to register all their licenses together, rather than registering each license separately with the program.Applicants may submit more than 1 application at a time so long as the total of funding requested does not exceed the maximum funding amount;It can take up to 3 business days to receive an acknowledgment from PEFIP that the submission has been received.Funding allocation is not transferrable to a producer that did not hold quota/share of production on January 1, 2021;Applicants are required to provide:Copies of the receipts or invoices;Copies of proof of payment;A copy of the organization's Articles of Incorporation;Proof of financing including documents or bank statements detailing an applicant's contribution towards the total project costs;Proof of activity is required when the applicant is applying for activities already completed at the Project Application submission;Copies of authorizations or permits might be required by AAFC during the application assessment or at the claim stage.The program will assess the applications based on the following:The project completion date, with the aim of providing successful applicants with their reimbursements as close as possible as to when their project was/is due to be completedProvincial and sectoral distribution, to help ensure the fair distribution of funding across all provinces and sub-sectors for each of the program's 10 yearsProject size, to help ensure the fair distribution of funding across both small and large producers for each of the program's 10 yearsPayments under $250,000 will be made in 1 payment within 30 business days;Projects with payments greater than $250,000 may require more than 1 payment per project.The program require that applicants retain records for 7 years after the date of expiration or early termination of the funding agreement with AAFC, whichever comes later.

      Grant Type
      Systems & Processes
    
    
      Grant Amount
      $25,000
    
    
      Regions
      Alberta
    
    
      Industries
      Agriculture - Crop, Agriculture - Dairy, Agriculture - Livestock, Agriculture - Tree Fruit, Agriculture - Vineyard/Wine
