      Canadian Agricultural Partnership
     

    
      Deadline
      
        

          Open until filled
      
    
    
  





    
      




  

      Grant Criteria 
      Primary producers in Alberta can receive a maximum of $25,000 for cost-shared projects relating to either on-farm irrigation system purchases and upgrades, or to new or expanded water source developments that improve on-farm water supply. The program has two streams that support each of these intended project outcomes, with the ultimate goal of reducing the challenges in water management across the agriculture industry.Grant Value: 50% of eligible expenses to a maximum of $25,000On-farm Water Supply Stream: cost shared up to a maximum of $25,000; andOn-farm Irrigation Stream: cost shared up to a maximum of $25,000.Turnaround Time: 5 weeksEligible Applicants:Must be a primary producer:Individual or a registered corporation;Operating in Alberta;Responsible for the day-to-day management and work for a crop, bee, or livestock operation;On-farm Water Supply Stream Eligibility: Responsible for input costs or agricultural crops or livestock producing at least $10,000 worth of farm commodities annually; andLiable to pay Alberta income tax or corporate tax (or claim losses) on income
from the production of farm commodities under the Income Tax Act (Canada) or
the Alberta Corporate Tax Act.On-farm Irrigation Stream Eligibility:Responsible for input costs or agricultural crops or livestock producing at least $25,000 worth of farm commodities annually; Owns an irrigated agricultural operation in Alberta; andHas not been previously approved for payment from the Program for the Parcel described in the Application.Ineligible Applicants:Research stations;Universities; Other organizations funded in whole or in part by the government; andAny applicant who has received maximum funding under the CAP Farm Water Supply program between April 1, 2018 and March 31,
2021:Applicants who received the full $5,000 for a standard incentive project are
not eligible for additional grant money toward a different standard incentive project.Eligible Projects:On-Farm Irrigation System Purchases:Low-Pressure Center Pivot System; andDrip Irrigation System.On-Farm Irrigation System Upgrades:Low-Pressure Center Pivot System;Drip Irrigation System;Sprinkler Nozzles;Pump Modifications;Control Panel Upgrade; andVariable Rate Irrigation Equipment.Standard Incentives for New or Expanded Water Source Developments:Wells;Dugouts;Spring Developments;Tie-In to a Multi-User Water Supply Pipeline;Dams;Water Source for Crop Irrigation;Unshared Water Pipelines; andCisterns.Special Incentives:Well Decommissioning;Well Pit Conversions; andWetland Assessments.Ineligible Projects:Water hauling or temporary piping costs;Repair, maintenance or replacement of existing equipment;Water source development for field scale irrigation in Alberta Irrigation Districts;Equipment used for crop production (irrigation water application equipment) under the on-farm water supply stream;Distribution of water within the farm site, except as part of an eligible project;Energy sources where an existing program addresses installation costs;Remote watering systems including tanks, portable or renewable energy sources or unburied pipelines to support livestock grazing from existing water sources or natural waterbodies;Roads and buildings except as detailed on the Program Funding List;Water treatment equipment or supplies for domestic use;Dugout and dam projects not identified on a Long-Term Water Management plan
approved by an AF Water Specialist or discussed with a Water Specialist with a
supporting Construction Sheet; andDugout and dam projects that do not follow
construction specifications in the approved Long-Term Water Management plan
or Construction Sheet.Eligible Expenses:Must be identified in the program Funding List;Must be at competitive prices that are no greater than fair market value; andMust be incurred by the applicant after the beginning of the program term;With an exception for costs identified in a Long-Term Water Management Plan: Approved by a water specialist; andConstructed and costs incurred after the approval date on the plan and after April 1, 2018.Eligible costs for select on-farm water supply projects are funded to a maximum of:$5,000 for standard incentive projects;$12,000 for decommissioned wells;$6,000 for well pit conversions; and$2,000 for wetland assessments.Ineligible Expenses:Costs for a new Low Pressure Centre Pivot System or Drip Irrigation System for irrigation expansion;Costs incurred:Before the beginning of the program on April 1, 2021; or For on-farm
water supply projects constructed between April 1, 2018 and March 31, 2021 that
were incurred before the date a Water Specialist approved the Long-Term Water
Management plan; or That were not identified on a Long-Term Water Management plan;Costs incurred for an on-farm irrigation project where proof of 10% down
payment has not been provided; andGST.Program Details:Projects must be located and operational in Alberta;Applicants must obtain all required governmental approvals prior to beginning the project; I.e. public health and safety, labour codes and standards, care and use of animals in research, wildlife habitat, and environmental protection.Expenses are cost-shared at 50% grant and 50% applicant;Minimum payment request that will be considered is
$250 unless it is for a second application submitted with respect to an approved project;Expenses are calculated based on the actual out of pocket cost to the applicant (i.e. cost of the eligible expense less any rebates, discounts, incentives, and/or credits, whether provided at the time of purchase or at a later date); andThe project end date cannot extend beyond the program end date on March 31, 2023 and all project activities must be completed by this date.Eligible Lands:All projects must be completed in Alberta;The land must be actively farmed by the applicant by the time the project is completed;On-farm Water Supply projects must be completed on:Private land; Crown Land under grazing, cultivation, farm development, or forest grazing lease disposition to an individual or a corporation under the authority of the Special Areas Act or Public Lands Act in Alberta; orIf the project is a Tie-In, on a right of way for the Multi-User Water Supply Pipeline to which the Tie-In is to be connected.On-farm Irrigation projects must be installed on a parcel that is at least:10 irrigated acres for a new surface drip irrigation system; or20 irrigated acres for a new Low Pressure Centre Pivot System or a subsurface drip irrigation system.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best PracticesFunding from this program can be combined with funding from other federal, provincial, or municipal government sources though total funding cannot exceed 100% of the expenses claimed;All on-farm water supply projects must also be complete prior to the date the application is submitted;Eligible and ineligible expenses will be updated periodically on the Funding List (not exhaustive);Applicants cannot return for refund any item that has been funded under the program; andApplicants cannot sell or trade any items that have been funded under the program for at least 3 years after the end of the project.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication guide: click hereApplication form: click here

        Recently Changed 
        Assistance to cover operational needs will only be considered on a case-by-case basis (repayable for businesses and non-repayable for not-for-profits).
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The Tourism Relief Fund in Western Canada provides up to 50% to a maximum of $100,000 non-repayable funding, or up to 75% to a maximum of $500,000 repayable funding to eligible tourism entities. Recipients must be either a key supplier/operator in visitor experience or part of a tourism cluster or an anchor product in a destination. The intent of the program is to create or enhance tourism experiences and products and to help attract more local and domestic visitors.Grant Value:Non-repayable funding - 50% of eligible costs up to $100,000Repayable funding - 75% of eligible costs up to $500,000Note: Non-repayable and repayable funding cannot be combined for the same projectTurnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants:Be located in B.C., Alberta, Saskatchewan, or Manitoba;Be in 1 of the following categories:Key supplier/operator in visitor experience;Be part of a defined tourism cluster or a tourism-dependent community (including supporting downtown cores);Provide an anchor product or service in a tourism destination.Must cater mainly to visitors, not including local residents;Be 1 of the following:Incorporated businesses (primarily small and medium-sized enterprises);Non-profit incorporated organizations;Crown corporations and related parties;Indigenous/First Nation/Métis Settlement owned businesses or indigenous organizations such as Indigenous-led not-for-profits, including but not limited to:First Nations as represented by their Chief and Council, Tribal Councils, Indigenous Representative Organizations, Métis and Inuit organizations, and Settlements, as well as Indigenous/First Nation/Métis Settlement, owned organizations.Ineligible Applicants:Restaurants;Retail sector; andHotel chains.Note: Only restaurants and Canadian-owned hotels may be considered for funding if they are an anchor product and the main attraction in the region. This will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.Eligible Activities:Development or enhancement of tourism experiences/products, including but not limited to:Creating and enhancing protocols and permanent infrastructure to meet health and safety requirements to keep businesses operating;Assisting operators reliant on international markets, such as those in downtown cores, to create innovative tourism offerings attractive to local and domestic visitors;Modernizing operations, attractions, greening initiatives, and online sales services;Supporting businesses with local promotion of tourism products, including digital and virtual reality experiences;Developing capacity for more inclusive tourism experiences (e.g. staff training to ensure a welcoming, inclusive environment to a diverse clientele, gender-neutral washroom facilities, etc.)Destination development, including but not limited to:Helping local communities to develop sustainable tourism plans based on research and market analysis, and designed to rebuild tourism confidence in communities;Supporting seasonal dispersion by equipping tourism SMEs to extend their product offering to increase visitation during the winter and shoulder seasons;Supporting destinations to implement tourism plans that create or improve local assets, facilities, and planning for key infrastructure;Supporting the development and implementation of tourism economic development recovery plans that consider possible key market reactions when travel can safely resume;Enhancing tourism services and experiences, including market readiness designed to help communities and SMEs develop experiential tourism, that will respond to visitor expectations post COVID-19;Assisting industry partners to support recovery and rebuilding efforts through coordination, and developing new offerings and/or capacity building on behalf of the sector;Implementing strategies to re-activate and animate downtown cores, main streets and business districts through activities, public art, and mixed-use spaces;Supporting scale-up and market expansion activities for key enterprises essential to economic vitality and the local business climate.Program Details:Applicants are limited to 1 successful application per year;The funding amount will be based on the minimum amount required to deliver the project;Project costs must be incurred by March 31, 2023;Priority projects are projects that:Support the Indigenous tourism sector;Is of strategic importance to the tourism sector in the region;Contribute to job creation and economic development of a region;Take place in a tourism-dependent community/region, including projects supporting downtown cores.Mandatory documents for submission:Financial statements for the past two years of normal operations, as well as interim financial statements for at least the last six-month period;If applicable, provide a project plan as to how the applicant organization will implement third-party delivery through this project;Other supporting documentation (e.g. business plan, pitch deck, confirmation of other funding sources, detailed budgets, supplier quotes, project proposal for third party agreements, marketing plan, cash flow forecasts, opening balance sheets) detailing your organization, and details about the proposed project.$50 million will specifically support Indigenous tourism initiatives;Contributions to non-profit organizations and Indigenous non-profits will normally be non-repayable; andAssistance to cover operational needs will only be considered on a case-by-case basis (repayable for businesses and non-repayable for not-for-profits).

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Program funding can be used in conjunction with other sources of government funding, so long as funding does not exceed 100% of eligible costs;The program allows funding to be used retroactively for costs incurred 12 months prior to the receipt of the application, but no earlier than April 19, 2021;Applicants are advised to check for incomplete application fields, as incomplete applications will not be assessed and will be considered ineligible for funding;The application is lengthy but will allow work to be saved.Forms:Program website (Prairie provinces): click hereProgram website (BC): click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The 2021 Festivals and Events COVID-19 Recovery Grant Program provides 25% up to $25,000 in funding to outdoor festivals and events held between July 1, 2021, and March 31, 2022. All events must be open to the public to attend with a minimum of 50 people in attendance. The intent of the program is to continue to build and inspire the community through vibrant experiences bringing people and visitors together again.Grant Value: 25% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $25,000Turnaround Time: 2 weeksEligible ApplicantsOrganizations that operate primarily in Edmonton, or has a history of significant activity in Edmonton when they also work elsewhere;Is in good standing, and not in arrears with the City of Edmonton; andHas insurance with a minimum of $2M in general liability.Eligible Events:Held between July 1, 2021, and March 31, 2022;Is either:An outdoor event located on City of Edmonton parkland, public open space, or road; ORAn indoor event hosted by an arts and performance organization that has an established funding relationship with the Edmonton Arts Council.Is either:Open to the public to attend (free entry or participation fee/charitable donation); ORA not-for-profit, ticketed, spectator event (such as concerts or performances).Be in-person with an attendance of 50 people or more;Held in compliance with all public health requirements, restrictions and guidance imposed by the City of Edmonton, Alberta Health Services - Environmental Public Health (AHS-EPH), and Alberta Health - Chief Medical Officer of Health (AH-CMOH);Held in compliance with all other permitting or licensing requirements as necessary (Edmonton Fire, Development Services, etc);Types of events include but are not limited to:Organized runs, walks and other sporting events;Cultural and historical celebrations and observances;Concerts, performances, and music festivals;Food, arts, and cultural festivals;Parades and processions;Sport and Active Recreation events / Active Living events;Not-for-profit events attracted through partnership with Explore Edmonton.Ineligible Events:Private Events Such as weddings, graduations, showers, celebrations of life, potlucks, awards ceremonies, roasts, local sports tournaments, or ‘meets';Virtual events;For-profit venues;For-profit ticketed spectator events (e.g. for-profit concerts or professional sporting events);Events intended to raise funds for specific individuals;Film productions;Protests / rallies / demonstrations / marches;Markets (including farmer’s and seasonal markets);Block parties or play streets;Promotional or marketing activities (i.e. product demonstrations, merchandise sales, launches, etc);Events that require membership to observe or participate in;Services/activities of faith organizations;Government or government agency, post-secondary institutions, or political parties;Political campaigning; andPerformances, exhibitions, or activities that promote or incite racism, hatred, or violence.Eligible Expenses:Temporary or enhanced infrastructure;Equipment required to support the safe delivery of the event (additional seating, larger tents/canopies);Additional set-up or strike time (i.e. staffing, rentals);Additional staffing/volunteers to implement health and safety protocols;Personal protective equipment (PPE);Sanitizing materials;Additional cleaning requirements;Health screening infrastructure; andAttendance registration systems or equipment.Program Details:An organization is only eligible to receive the grant once;However, if the applicant is producing multiple events before March 31, 2022, please include details about each event in the application to further outline the circumstances of the financial need.Grant funding awards will be considered based on an established formula and criteria such as:Event size, scope, and scale (including expected attendance and location capacity);Number of events proposed that will take place between July 1, 2021 and March 31, 2022;History of the event in Edmonton;The benefit to the public (cultural, recreational, or charitable significance);Public Access (free versus charged/cost to participate);Not-for-profit, charitable, or for-profit organization status;Funding need (those organizations with sufficient funds to host the event without municipal support);Receipt of funding from other City of Edmonton sources (other than the Edmonton Arts Council grants);Total number and location of events, to distribute around City of Edmonton Wards;The order of application.Funding decisions made by the City are final and cannot be appealed;However, applicants can reapply.For approved applications, the funds are issued by electronic transfer or cheque no sooner than 30 days prior to the event (with the exception of 2022 events).

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program does not allow for retroactive funding. Please do not submit an application for events that have already occurred;Applicants are advised to identify eligible expenses in the application;Please download, complete, sign, and email your signed Declaration within 24 hours of completing the online application to eventscovidrecoverygrant@edmonton.ca;The festival or event must be insured with a minimum of $2M in general liability coverage with the City of Edmonton listed as an “Additional Insured”. Depending on the size and scope of the event, additional coverage may be required;In the event of cancellation or delay due to changes in COVID-19 restrictions, the Grant funding may carry forward to a later rescheduled date;If the applicant organization has received other City of Edmonton funding, the organization can still apply for this grant;Please note that grant funding awards will be considered based on an established formula and criteria including receipt of funding from other City of Edmonton sources.Please contact EventsCOVIDRecoveryGrant@edmonton.ca or call 311 for assistance.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Processors-Selling to Export Markets Program provides funding of up to 75% of eligible costs to a maximum of $75,000 for Ontario processors to implement a market entry plan into a new export market. Eligible applicants should be manufacturers who are directly involved in the transformation of agricultural commodities, foods, beverages, or agri-based bio-products. The intent of the program is to help processors increase new market sales and create new jobs.Grant Value: Up to 75% of eligible costs to a maximum of $75,000Turnaround Time: 60 business daysEligible Applicants:Be 1 of the following:A processor business that manufactures products in a facility; ORHas 199 employees or less;Have a valid and up-to-date Premises Identification (PID) Number for the business location where the project is to take place;Includes processors of:Tobacco-based bio-pharmaceuticals or other bio-products;Health or nutrition supplements;Pet food products.An owner of an established brand or intellectual property owner that does not meet processor eligibility criteria and has an agreement for the transformation of their product(s) in Ontario; ORA new processor business that:Constitutes a legal person;Is new to the food and agri-product processing industry and has business projections that demonstrate potential annual gross business income of$30,000 or more within 3 years of applying;Files personal income taxes in Ontario;Has not filed taxes of $30,000 or more in annual gross business revenue as a food or agri-product processing business in the two years prior to applying for funding; andHas a valid Premises Identification (PID) Number (if a processing facility is established).All applicants must:Provide a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number as part of the application process, if applicable;Located in Ontario; andHas an export marketing plan (please see documents required in the program details section below).Ineligible Applicants:Restaurants and food services, including catering services;Retail food services;Packaging material manufacturers;Businesses that only wash/clean/polish primary postharvest process (including but not limited to trimming and re-sizing), sort, package, or warehouse agriculture, and food products;With the exception of quinoa.Businesses that process household waste or household waste by-products; andCigarette manufacturers.Eligible Expenses:Brand development costs (e.g., logo design, brand identity, logo and colour usage booklet);Focus group research or consumer studies expenses;In-market product demonstrations expenses;Promotional material development costs;Product introductory campaigns for international markets expenses;Sales, marketing, and promotional activities, including virtual events;Product samples (not from normal production) for market research, tradeshow, or specific events (e.g., samples made specifically for marketing purposes);Packaging design costs;Shipping costs for tradeshow materials and product samples that are not intended for resale;One-time labour costs specifically required for the project, such as third-party advisory fees; andTravel and meal costs.Note: Only expenses incurred after approval of the project are eligible.Ineligible Expenses:Salary costs for an existing export manager or for an existing position that conducts export marketing activities;Capital costs including processing equipment, machinery, hardware, and software;Product samples not related to a   new product launch or a promotional event (e.g. tradeshow);Product samples produced from normal production;Retail or food services listing fees;Cost of acquiring production or processing quota permits;Activities that support existing products in existing markets; andIn-kind contributions, such as:Salaries;Use of equipment;Materials and supplies;Use of land and facilities.Note: Please see the program guidelines for the full list of ineligible expenses.Program Details:The program assessment process is merit-based and only approves projects that best meet merit assessment criteria;Projects must be implemented and completed no later than September 30, 2022;Documents required for application submission:Market research analysis that supports entry into the specific export market;Sales targets and assessment of other potential business impacts;Implementation strategy; andQuotes or proposals for all activities that will be sourced from third-party suppliers (e.g., consultants) detailing services, outcomes, and costs.If quotes or proposal are not available then detailed explanation of estimated costs may be accepted (e.g., tradeshow costs, Facebook or Google ads).An eligible business may have a total of 2 applications under consideration for both phases of the intake;However, applications must be for unique projects with distinct and separate outcomes;A separate application must be submitted for each project.There is no limit to the number of projects that a processor can complete over the five-year span of the Partnership; However, a project can only be funded once through a single funding allocation from the Partnership.Projects that have received funding are routinely inspected;Approved funding is issued only after expenses have been incurred;There will be a 10 % holdback of reimbursement until a final report for the project is received and approved by OMAFRA.Claim packages must contain:Completed claim form;Copies of all paid invoices;Proof of payment for all paid invoices, including:Copy of front and back of canceled cheques;An electronic image of processed cheques;Statement from banking institutions; andCredit card or debit card receipt or statements.In-Kind Claim Declaration Form (if claiming in-kind contributions).Assessment Criteria:The export marketing plan is fully developed and demonstrates the need for the project;New international markets are accessed or existing international markets are expanded;Export marketing sales are increased through project activities;Relevant business impacts are anticipated and have been quantified, such as:Reduced identified risks;Job creation or retention;Increased sales and revenue;Increased profitability.Resources, experience and skills necessary to oversee and carry out the project are identified;Project work plans are clearly defined and aligned to project goals; andImpact on economic growth.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program allows funding to be used in conjunction with other sources of government funding, so long as the other programs also permit this and the total funding does not exceed 100% of total eligible costs;This program does not allow for funding to be used retroactively as only expenses incurred after approval of the project are eligible;To register for a PID Number, visit the Provincial Premises Registry (PPR) at ontariopid.com;When determining the number of employees, the applicant must report all employees who receive a T4 slip from the applicant business, either business-wide or at a specific facility (as corresponds to the question/instructions);Applicants are advised to obtain quotes where possible to support the project budget and to demonstrate best value for money when incurring eligible costs;Quotes older than 6 months at the time of submission will not be accepted.If the applicant has submitted an application by email but did not receive an acknowledgment within 5 business days, contact OMAFRA at 1-877-424-1300;All paid invoices should indicate: the payee, the payor, amount of payment, and date of payment;Successful applicants should retain all records relating to any payments made to the applicant under the Partnership, including all invoices and proof of payment for at least 7 years from the date on which payment was received by the applicant.Forms:Program guidelines: click hereApplication form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Food Processing Student Work Placement Program+ (SWPP+) offers a wage subsidy of up to 70%  to a maximum of $7,000 to food and beverage employers seeking student talent. Students may be in any post-secondary program of study and may be in a full- or part-time program. The intent of the program is to attract talent to the Canadian food and beverage manufacturing industry.Grant Value:50% of wages up to $5,000 for regular participants70% of wages up to $7,000 for underrepresented participants (see eligible participants section below)Turnaround Time: 3 weeksEligible Employers:Must be in an industry related to food, including but not limited to:Food processing;Agriculture;Food retail (ie. grocery stores);Food service (ie. food preparation and/or catering; NOT restaurants); andFood equipment/value chain (i.e. Wholesale, distribution, transportation).Registered Canadian businesses, not-for-profit, hospitals, and long-term care facilities;Committed to paying the student for the role;Willing to provide a quality learning experience to a post-secondary education student; andHave the financial capacity to pay the student for the duration of the placement in full (the wage subsidy will be administered after receiving the final pay stub at the end of the placement).Note: Restaurants are out of scope and are ineligible for this program.Eligible Candidates:Full- or part-time students in recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Graduate students (including Masters and Ph.D.) are eligible.Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or persons to whom refugee protection has been conferred under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act;Legally entitled to work in Canada in accordance with relevant provincial or territorial legislation and regulations;Undertaking a placement recognized as a Work-Integrated Learningcomponent in their studies.The placement can be required or optional, for credit or not for credit.Underrepresented students:Women in STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics);Indigenous students;Students with disabilities;Newcomers to Canada (immigrated within the last 5 years);First-year students; andVisible minorities.Note: There needs to be a relation between the participant's field of study and the role of the placement.Program Details:Positions not directly related to agriculture (ie. marketing or accounting in an agricultural company) may be eligible;E.g. The program allows students to work in accounting positions for a meat processing plant.Wage subsidy will apply to gross wages between:Summer 2025 ( May 1, 2025, to August 31, 2025): CLOSEDFall 2025 (September 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025): OPENWinter 2026 (January 1, 2025 to April 31, 2025) : Opening November 1, 2025.Minimum placement duration: 4 weeks;Maximum placement duration: 16 weeksFull-time or part-time positions;Minimum 10 hours per week;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.The employer must provide on-the-job supervision;Applications that are 2 months out from the start of term are added to a waitlist;If the employer has applied and is on a waitlist, they will receive communication approximately 45 days before intake opens to review the status of the application.Remote work options for students are available; andThe final subsidy amount will be determined at the end of the placement term upon receipt of all supporting documents.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Funding from this program can be used in conjunction with other sources of non-federal government funding (ie. provincial and municipal);This grant allows for provincial tax credits to be used in conjunction with the funding received in this program;Process Best Practices:Employers can post a job and hire students through Campus Connect at no cost.Forms:Program webpage: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Science Horizons program offered by the UNAC Green Corps initiative provides employers with a wage subsidy valued at 75% to a maximum of $28,000 for hiring youth with post-secondary education for full-time placements in a Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics related position within environmental sectors. Additional funding is available for training and support services for each new hire. The aim of the program is to boost the green economy by creating opportunities for talented youth who are unemployed or underemployed.Grant Value: Up to 75% to a maximum of $25,000 + $5,000 for training, skills development and additional wrap-around servicesTurnaround time: Up to 5 weeksEligible Employer:For-profit or not-for-profit organization based in Canada; andMust be STEM focused or doing work in sustainability/green sectors.Eligible Participants:Must be 18-30 years of age at the start of employment;Must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or hold refugee status;Must be unemployed or underemployed; Must have post-secondary education or diploma in a STEM-related field; andMust be new hires of the employer.Internship Details: Placements must start before February 15, 2022;Minimum 6 months duration;Full-time employment (30 to 37.5 hours per week);Supplemental training is provided to interns by UNAC;Must be a STEM-related position; andMust have an environmental focus within a natural resource sector and/or sub-sector.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program is funded by Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) through the Science Horizons Program (SH) and it cannot be combined with funding from the Science & Technology Internship Program (STIP) or any other federal source of funding;To get started, employers will need to have a job description prepared and email Bonita with the heading "STEM employer: company name"; andFor non-STEM-related placements, employers may consider the STIP stream of the Green Corps program at UNAC.Forms:Program website: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers funding of up to 50% of eligible expenses to a maximum of $250,000 for projects that are aimed at commercializing products or processes in a variety of key economic sectors including food processing, life sciences, manufacturing, digital arts and culture, and more. The goal of the program is to help eligible organizations commercialize the results of university or public research in a new market outside Quebec.Grant Value: Up to $250,000 per projectUp to 50% of eligible expenses for priority sectors; and Up to 35% of eligible expenses for strategic sectors.Turnaround Time: around 3-4 months.Eligible Applicants:Incorporated for-profit businesses;Social enterprises and non-profits organizations (NPOs);Co-ops;Headquartered and registered in Quebec City, Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures or L-Ancienne-Lorette;Has a product or process that has reached the commercialization phase; The first significant sale of the product/process is expected approximately within 24 months;Has proof of a) ownership of the intellectual property, or b) of the rights of exclusive use of the selected product or process; ANDOperates in one of the following priority sectors; ORAgri-food, food processing and healthy foods;Digital arts and interactive entertainment, financial technologies, artificial intelligence, smart city or other digital products and technologies (excluding services and consulting);Optics-photonics, advanced electronics, measurement and control technologies;Life sciences, biotechnologies, and health technologies;Clean technologies: water, air, soil treatment, eco-mobility, energy efficiency, renewable energies, green chemistry, residual materials, enabling technologies and sustainable development.Operates in one of the following strategic sectors:Arts, culture and heritage;Insurance and financial services;Shops located on commercial arteries;Manufacturing, materials, industrial processing, robotics and industry 4.0;Urban security; andTourism.Ineligible Applicants:Social enterprises, NPOs, and co-ops that do not demonstrate sound democratic governance;Applicants who have not been discharged from a bankruptcy judgment; andApplicants who have outstanding debts with the City of Quebec.Eligible Expenses:Professional fees, consulting services, and studies;Costs and working capital necessary for the implementation of the project;Salaries for human resources assigned to the project at an hourly rate; andPurchase or rental of goods, equipment, and assets related to the project.Ineligible Expenses:Funding for regular business operations;Financing of charitable activities and payment for volunteers;Payment of a debt or the repayment of existing loans;Replacement of government support or existing programs;Expenses incurred before the date of submission of a complete application;Any expense relating to the relocation of a business or part of its production outside the agglomeration of Quebec, unless the City of Quebec consents in writing;       Grant Criteria 
      The Storefront Improvement Grant provides funding of 50% up to a maximum of $50,000 to commercial storefronts within Edmonton for exterior renovations. The businesses must be located within the Business Improvement Areas or other Council-approved Target Areas. The intent of the program is to help Brick and mortar stores attract customers and to create lively commercial main streets.Grant Value:Mid-block building - 50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $25,000Corner building with 1 active facade - 50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $30,000Corner building with 2 active facades - 50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $50,000Turnaround Time: 4 weeksEligible Applicants:Be a property owner or someone approved by the property owner to act on their behalf;Be a storefront business located in a Business Improvement Area or other Council-approved Target Areas (see map below);Have a clear, unobstructed street-level window on the main floor for a 5 year maintenance period;The property has not previously received a Storefront Improvement Grant/Facade; andHas not commenced construction work on the storefront.Note: Home-based businesses are ineligible.Eligible Projects:Eligible projects must include at least 3 of the following storefront improvements:Redesign the storefront (ie. enlarging, adding or moving windows and doors);Upgrading windows and/or doors;Re-cladding the building with new materials (excluding painting or pressure-washing);Adding awnings or canopies;Electrical and light fixtures;Signage installation/maintenance;Permanent patio installation;Adding bike racks and/or benches;Brick power wash cleaning;Clear security films over windows and doors;Installing new permanent patios or other active street front uses on private property; andDoes not include sidewalk cafes which are located on road right-of-ways;Please see sidewalk cafes for more information.Installing new accessibility features (ie. ramps or handrails).Ineligible Projects:Reducing transparency by removing storefront windows or filling them with glass blocks;Mirrored, frosted or tinted windows;Any obstruction or visual clutter is ineligible.Digital screens, flashing signage, backlit box signage;Radically altering the design of a building with the potential for heritage designation; andRemoving ramps, curb cuts or other accessibility features.Eligible Expenses:Storefront design costs (up to 20% of the total grant);Construction expenses;Labour expenses; andCost of materials, if work is done by the applicant (ie. no contractor).Ineligible Expenses:Rolling shutters/security bars;Rolling shutters or security bars are only eligible if:The building has a policy report from the last 2 years documenting break-ins or broken windows;The security bars are painted to match the building's colour scheme or to minimize the appearance from the outside;Rolling shutters must have valence AND be painted with a mural.Permit fees;Insurance;Tools; andConsumables.Program Details:Work must be performed or overseen by a general contractor with a valid City of Edmonton business license;Applicants are responsible for the following:Managing contractors;Keeping track of invoices;Obtaining relevant permits;Requesting approval from the Program Manager for any changes in design after the agreement is signed; andGrant amounts cannot be changed as a result of project scope or cost overruns.Program Process:Application package submission, including:Application form;Building elevations showing design and materials;Conceptual drawings or renderings to support the building elevations; andA site plan that shows the property line.Application reviewDecision notificationIf approved - applicants enter a reimbursement agreement;If approved with conditions - applicants must change the design to meet the eligibility;If refused - applicants may change the design and re-apply in the next application period.Reimbursement agreementApplicants must send the following documents within 3 months of the approval letter:2 quotes from the eligible scope of the work;A cost breakdown from selected contractors;The City of Edmonton business license number of the general contractor/subcontractors;Overall budget summary of the project;A copy of all permit applications.Please note: If the above documentation are not provided within 3 months of the approval letter, the project file will be closed and the funding reallocated.Project construction commencesProjects have 1 year from when the Reimbursement Agreement is executed to complete construction.ReimbursementApplicants must send the following to the Program Manager within 30 daysafter completion of the project:All invoices and proof of payment to eligible work identified in the Reimbursement Agreement;All invoices must be paid in full;Purchase orders are not accepted as proof of payment.City of Edmonton business license number for all subcontractors;Cost summary for the work;The most recent property tax invoice indicating the property is on municipal property taxes;Permit service reports indicating the work has been completed to satisfaction of the City of Edmonton.Payment to be issued between 3-6 weeksStorefront renovations must be maintained for 5 years.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program does not allow funding to be used retroactively for projects that have already begun;The program recommends submitting elevations and a rendering in the application package for best results. The applicant will also need drawings to apply for City permits. Should the project be approved to participate in the Storefront Improvement Program, design fees can be reimbursed (50% of the architecture/design/engineering fees up to $5,000);Design principles should be improvements:For a lively pedestrian experience, not cars;Addressing all 4 seasons;Supporting the business, the building and the Business Improvement Area;Supporting accessibility;Contributing to safe streets;Increasing energy efficiency and climate resiliency of the building.Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guide: click hereApplication form: click hereFAQ: click here

grants.grant_criteria: The Matching Investment Fund (MIF) supports the development and reformulation of Canadian dairy products and ingredients, and related knowledge/technology transfer activities by making matching contributions for product development and consultation costs.       Grant Criteria 
      The Matching Investment Fund (MIF) supports the development and reformulation of Canadian dairy products and ingredients, and related knowledge/technology transfer activities by making matching contributions for product development and consultation costs. The intent of this program is to assist the growth and innovation of dairy processors and food technology centres in order to ultimately advance demand for Canadian dairy products and ingredients.Grant Value: 50% of eligible activities to a maximum of $150,000 per projectTurnaround Time:  within 40 business daysEligible Applicants:Registered Canadian:Dairy processors;Finished food product manufacturers; and Food technology centres.Involved in the development, manufacture and/or use of Canadian dairy products and ingredients.Eligible Activities:Development of new or innovative products;Reformulation of existing products;Knowledge transfer activities;Technology transfer projects;New opportunities for solids non-fat ingredients.Eligible Expenses:Consultation services and sub-contractor costs for management and market research, dairy and food science, technical services, and food processing expertise:Professional fees for specialists and experts on the many areas of the product development process; andTravel costs for consultants and sub-contractors include economy airfare and hotel.Product Development: Product analysis, trials, and technology transfer; I.e. Adoption of new or existing technologies, kitchen, lab, pilot or industrial scale tests, retrofitting of equipment, sample preparation costs, and packaging techniques.Direct labour and material costs related to the project.For further eligible activities, review the table under 'Activities and Funding Limits' here;Program Details:Consultation services are funded to a maximum of $25,000 (before taxes);Small businesses (<25 employees) are eligible for 100% reimbursement for the first $10,000 spent on a project;Includes up to $5,000 for consultation services and $5,000 for product development activities; If only one activity is involved in the project, the amount eligible for 100% funding is maximum $5,000.Funds are disbursed 50% at halfway through the project and the remaining 50% are provided after completion;A progress report with attached proof of payments is required at the halfway mark;A final written report with attached proof of payments is required at completion.Eligible Canadian dairy products (CDP) and ingredients (CDI):Made wholly or mainly from milk such as: butter, cheese, milk powders, milk protein concentrate/isolate, evaporated milk, sweetened & condensed milk, whole milk, liquid milks, cream, and yogurt;Has the potential to increase the use of raw milk components (in the case of a dairy product manufacturer) or CDIs.Projects must involve a technical challenge associated with incorporating a CDI or developing an innovative dairy product;Projects must demonstrate that the dairy product formulation or further processed product will not risk displacing existing CDP or CDI; andProjects must meet at least one of the following:Incorporates a CDI in a product formulation where no dairy ingredient(s) had been previously used;Replaces a substitute ingredient in a product formulation with a CDI, or significantly increases the dairy content of an existing product formulation;Develops and markets a new dairy product or a product pursuant to the Domestic Dairy Product Innovation Program (DDPIP); Develops and markets a new or innovative further processed product containing CDI; andIncludes technology/knowledge transfer activities having a demonstrated benefit for a company or for the Canadian dairy industry as a whole.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Applicants must demonstrate they have the financial capacity to carry out the project independent of program funding as it is disbursed as a reimbursement;Funds can be used in conjunction with funding from other government programs as long as external funds are not being used for any of the same activities as those funded by MIF;Applicants are expected to cover 50% of all eligible activities where MIF will be contributing funds.Each project must focus on development for one single product yet may include all its varieties (e.g. different flavours of the same product);Projects that emphasize the use of solids non-fat (SNF) ingredients such as skim milk powder (SMP), milk protein concentrate (MPC), or liquid skim milk will be given priority and may be eligible for an increased level of funding;Process Best Practices:To apply, interested applicants must submit a project summary form. The CDC will contact the applicant within 10-15 business days and invite the applicant to submit a detailed application if successful; andThe project start date may be re-negotiated on a case-by-case basis if eligible expenses that are submitted in application are incurred before an approval is delivered.Forms:Program website: click hereProject summary form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Canada-Manitoba Job Grant provides employers funding of up to 75% of eligible costs to a maximum of $10,000 to train and upskill new and existing employees. Training must be delivered by a third-party trainer. The intent of the program is to address the skills gap, help Manitoba employers meet business needs, and help Manitobans gain the skills they need for available jobs.Grant Value:Companies with 100 or fewer employees - 75% of eligible costs to a maximum of $10,000 per traineeCompanies with 101 or more employees - 50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $10,000 per traineeTurnaround Time:  pendingEligible Applicants:Have a Business Number issued by the Government of Canada;Licensed to carry on business in Manitoba;Be 1 of the following organization types:Private for-profit companies;Non-profit organizations;Industry associations, sector councils, groups of employers;Union halls;First Nations; andMunicipal governments.Note: There is no minimum length required for a company to be in business to be eligible for the program.Ineligible Applicants:Prior recipients of 3 Job Grants over the past 5 years;Current recipients of funding from Manitoba under another Industry Workforce Development  program such as the Industry Expansion Program, or the Workforce Development Program;K-12 schools and publicly-funded post-secondary institutions;Federal, provincial and territorial governments; andFederal and provincial crown corporations and agencies.Eligible Trainees:Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or protected persons;Full-time, part-time and seasonal employees;Unemployed and seeking training to get a job;Temporary hires/interns who are Canadian; andWork in Manitoba. Employees who reside in another province but are working in Manitoba are eligible.Ineligible Trainees:Temporary foreign workers (Individuals with a social insurance number that begins with a "9");Individuals hired on contract (ie. non-employees); andEmployees of a Manitoba company who reside and work in a different province or country.Eligible Expenses:Tuition fees;Mandatory student fees;Textbooks, software, and other required materials;Examination fees; andTravel costs for individuals residing in northern and remote communities to attend events in Manitoba delivered outside their communities or unavailable online.Travel and accommodation costs reimbursed are negotiated and not guaranteed.Ineligible Expenses:Wages of employees while in training; andExpenses for internally delivered training by a company employee.Eligible Training Providers:Be a third-party training provider;Deliver training at the workplace, online or in a classroom/training facility;Be one of the following:Post-secondary institution;Private vocational institutions;Sector councils or industry associations;Union halls; andEquipment manufacturers and other private trainers hat have the applicable curriculum, knowledge, qualification, and equipment or materials required for training.Program Details:All applications that meet the eligibility requirements listed above will be processed in the order that they are received until funding is fully expended;Applications must be for training that is taking place or has taken place within the same fiscal year;Employers can apply for funding for training that has already occurred so long as the training took place in the same fiscal year in which the application is submitted (April 1-March 31);Employers cannot apply for training that will take place in the next fiscal year.Maximum funding per employer per fiscal year: $100,000;Businesses with 2 or more locations in Manitoba can include employees from all locations in1 application;Parent companies can apply for the program for 1 or more of their subsidiaries;Subsidiaries with 100 or fewer employees cannot classify as a small employer if they are part of a larger parent company;Franchises of a national chain are considered separate companies and thus may be considered as a small employer if they have 100 or fewer employees;Companies located in another province or country are eligible so long as they meeting the following criteria:They employ individuals who work in Manitoba;Are licensed to operate in Manitoba; andHold a Manitoba business number.To submit reimbursements, approved employers must submit the following:Training plan report;Training evaluation; andProof of payment of eligible training costs (e.g. invoice and canceled cheque or invoice and Paypal receipt, etc.)To be eligible for training costs initially paid for by an employee, employers must submit documentation showing the training cost is paid, and that the employee has been reimbursed for the training cost.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:The program allows for retroactive funding so long as the eligible training took place within the same fiscal year (April 1 - March 31);Please contact the program at 204-945-3744 or mgi@gov.mb.ca should employers have the following needs:Identifying their training needs;Connecting with suitable job seekers;Completing the grant application;Information about training delivered by third-party service providers; andInformation about other available workforce development programs and services.For employers seeking funding for training delivered in-house by a company employee, please visit Workforce Development Program; andFor employees who have left the company but have participated in training funded by this program, employers can still submit expenses for the training.Employers should indicate on the training plan that the employee left the company prior to completing the training;A consent form will not be required for the departed employee.Forms:Program website: click hereEmployer Applicant Guide: click hereEmployer Application: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides a wage subsidy of up to 70% to a maximum of $7,000 to employers in the tourism and hospitality sector that hire post-secondary students for full-time or part-time placements. The goal of the program is to create employment and skills development opportunities that  benefit both students and employers.Grant Value:50% of wages up to $5,000;70% of wages up to $7000 for students from the following underrepresented groups:Women in STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics);Indigenous students;Visible minorities; Newcomers to Canada (immigrated to Canada within the last 5 years);Persons with disabilities; andFirst year students. Turnaround Time: 2 weeksEligible Employers:Registered Canadian businesses, startups, and not-for-profits related to the tourism and hospitality sector; andI.e. accommodations, food and beverage services, culinary, recreation, entertainment, culture, events, transportation, travel services, etc.Must provide a work-integrated learning opportunity for the student.Ineligible Employers:Federal, provincial, territorial, and municipal governments;Crown corporations, hospitals, public long-term care facilities, and post-secondary institutions; andMembers the House of Commons and/or Senate.Eligible Candidate:Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or has refugee status;Registered at a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution in a program that includes a work-integrated learning component;Undergraduate or graduate student;Full- or part-time student; andLegally entitled to work in Canada.Ineligible Candidate:International students; andImmediate family members, unless a clear, transparent, and fair nepotism policy is in place.Peogram Details:Applications are being accepted for placements in the following semesters:Winter 2025 (January 1, 2025 to April 30, 2025): CLOSEDSummer 2025 (May 1, 2025 to August 31, 2025): CLOSEDFall 2025 (September 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025): OPENThe work experience must coincide with a course, degree, certificate, diploma, or other recognized program offered by the student's institution;The student will need to provide proof of enrolment (e.g. a letter from a registrar) in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Ideally, the document will also demonstrate that the student’s program includes a work-integrated-learning component.Eligible placement types include:Co-op placements;Internships;Practicums;Mentorships;Field placements; and Applied projects.Placement can be full-time or part-time;Minimum 20 hours per week;4-15 weeks per semester;On-site, remote, or hybrid allowed; Participants must be placed on payroll; Students hired as independent contractors are not eligible for the subsidy;Placements must not displace an existing worker or fill a role left vacant due to a labour dispute;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Apprenticeships that are part of the designated trades governed by regulations under the Provincial and Territorial Apprenticeship Acts (Red Seal Trades) are not eligible for the wage subsidy.

      Grant Criteria 
      Stream 2 of the Indigenous Community Business Fund provides up to $7M in non-repayable funding to Indigenous community-or collectively-owned businesses who have experienced a reduction in revenue due to COVID-19. The fund seeks to support businesses that do not qualify for CEWS or other federal government relief measures by helping to cover the cost of expenses related to the operation of the businesses in addition to adaptation, planning and reopening costs of a business.Grant Value: Up to $7,000,000Note: Only in extraordinary cases will the maximum value be allotted to an applicant. Otherwise, the value is determined on a need-basis.Turnaround Time: 1 to 2 months (may vary according to Indigenous Services Canada regional office)Eligible Businesses:First Nations, Inuit or Métis community-or collectively-owned (over 50% Indigenous community-owned);For-profit;Located in the provinces;In operation since October 1, 2019;Incurred a negative financial impact due to COVID-19 OR financial support will prevent layoffs, bankruptcy or permanent closure;Has been solvent, financially viable, and not declared bankrupt prior to COVID-19;Expects to continue to operate with a reduction in revenues from the previous year over the coming months as a result of COVID-19 (in line with the terms of CEWS); andHas previously applied for federal business support and been declined, in whole or in part, OR does not qualify under business support eligibility criteria:This may include applications to more than 1 federal program depending on the requested support.Eligible Expenses:Capital lease payments for existing equipment and machinery;Salaries and benefits, At the same rate as CEWS and only if ineligible for it;Utilities;Bank charges and interest payments;Professional fees;Monthly insurance payments;Rent or mortgage, only if ineligible for CECRA;Supply and delivery costs;Operating costs or capital expenditures related to adapting the business and services;Payments for regularly scheduled debt service of an existing debt that is not related to other federal COVID-19 financial support;Other reasonable applicable operating costs; andCOVID-19-related costs associated with the adaptation, planning and reopening of a business such as:Costs required to comply with provincial health regulations;Retraining;Marketing;Technology;Professional services;Planned maintenance and repairs the business is unable to complete due to cash flow; andOther reasonable operating costs.Ineligible Expenses:Expenses not associated with the operation, adaptation, planning and reopening of a business;Refinancing or repayment of an existing loan or debt resulting from other federal COVID-19 financial support;Costs of amortization and goodwill;Acquisition of buildings;Costs for services provided by a federal or provincial government; andLoss of revenue.Program Details:Stream 1 of this program relayed support directly to communities and collectives in order to support relief measures from COVID-19 and no applications were required;Stream 2 is proposal-based and requires applicants to detail the funds required to strengthen operations or recover from COVID-19 economic impacts;Funding will be disbursed depending on the demonstrated need of the business to cover the cost of operating losses between April 1st, 2021 and March 31, 2022;Métis businesses must apply directly to the Métis organizations in their province;Businesses in the territories must apply to the Northern Business Relief Fund; andFirst Nations, Inuit or Métis community or collective may apply for funding for 1 or more community-owned businesses.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program reviews applications on a first-come, first-serve basis;Eligible businesses will need to demonstrate they have exhausted all options from other federal funding and were ineligible or declined, in whole or in part, to receive funds; Most Indigenous communities have received notice about this program, so their community-owned businesses may apply via any additional instructions received from their corresponding Indigenous Services Canada (ISC) regional office; After an application is submitted, the program will confirm receipt of the application shortly after; andDelays in responding to requests for additional information within 5 business days may result in a delayed or declined decision.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication forms: click here

      Engineering, Utilities, Tech - AI, Tech - Computer Network Security, Tech - Software & Web Development, Tech - Technology Hardware, Tech - Video Game

      Deadline
      
        

          Open until filled
      
    
    
  





    
      




  

      Grant Criteria 
      The TalentEdge Internship component of the ENCQOR 5G program provides funding to Ontario-based SMEs who carry out industry-driven research and development projects related to 5G, wireless and digital technologies. This stream of the Evolution of Networked Services through a Corridor in Quebec and Ontario for Research and Innovation (ENCQOR) program supports the hire of current students or recent graduates from undergraduate or graduate programs for up to 6 units of four-month internships. Each internship unit is funded at $10,000 for a maximum of $60,000 in funding to help SMEs leverage and retain the top talent in the province.Grant Value: Up to $60,000$10,000 per four-month unit for eligible project costs, up to a maximum of $60,000 (six units)Turnaround Time: 7 weeks (pending a signed contract for a coupled ENCQOR 5G project)Eligible Businesses:For-profit, incorporated in Ontario or Canada;Has a valid CRA business number;SME with fewer than 500 total employees;Developing 5G, wireless, or digital technology-based innovation or innovative processes;In response to an ENCQOR
5G SME Technology Development Challenge Statement; ORPreferably, using the iPaaS testbed.Has operations and/or R&D in Ontario related to the project; andHas the intent and potential to apply, exploit, and/or commercialize the results of the
project for the economic benefit of Ontario; Has the necessary expertise and resources to put the project into effect within an
appropriate time frame; andIn good financial and reporting standing with the Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI).Eligible Interns:Undergraduate level:Students in their final year of study who are registered at an accredited College or University in Ontario; or Recent graduates (within 3 years of graduation).Graduate level:Current Masters and PhD students who are registered at accredited College or University in Ontario; Recent Masters graduates (within 3 years of graduation).Institution-based internships:Must have active status at the academic institution for the duration of the internship.Company-based internships:Must be eligible to work in Ontario;Be a resident of Ontario; and Have employee status at the company for the duration of the internship.Cannot apply with a company where there is any conflict of interest, such as a company where the intern or relatives have any control as a major creditor or shareholder or governing board member;Cannot be currently enrolled in a co-op program or other equivalent job placement/employment program; andCannot be a current or past employee within the last 6 months (including consultants, contract position, part-time, etc.).Eligible Projects:Has an R&D component related to 5G, wireless or digital technologies, preferably using the
iPaaS testbed or responding to an ENCQOR 5G SME Technology Development Challenge
Statement;Proposed internship activities must be coupled with an existing ENCQOR 5G project in one of the following program streams:ENCQOR 5G Demonstration Program;ENCQOR 5G SME Technology Demonstration Program;ENCQOR 5G iPaaS Network Access.Defined project with clear activities, milestones and outcomes, to be executed within the duration of the internship (not a “first job”-type placement);Interns will receive on-the-job training;Commensurate with the intern’s experience and expertise; andIntellectual property (IP) arising from the project will be managed by the project participants;The parties are bound by the IP terms of the company
where the intern is an employee for the duration of the internship.Program Details:The applicant contribution is $10,000 ($5,000 cash + $5,000 in-kind) minimum per four-month unit;The intern MUST receive a
minimum cash compensation of $15,000 of the total $20,000 contribution per unit; and The remainder may be used for other direct project costs.Consecutive internships are allowed;All interns may hold a maximum of 3 "internship units", unless they are current PhD students in which case they are eligible for 6 units.Note: Each internship unit is 4 months long.Businesses can apply for multiple interns in the same application up to a maximum of six ENCQOR 5G internship units per company over the lifetime of the ENCQOR program;Applies to internships units only associated with the ENCQOR 5G Demonstration Program, the ENCQOR 5G SME Technology Development Program and ENCQOR 5G iPaaS access projects. Previously awarded TalentEdge Internship units from other OCI program streams do not count toward the six unit maximum;Applications will be assessed on criteria which includes:Clarity of the project description, project plan, and intern objectives; Suitability of methodology and feasibility of timeline and milestones;Intern qualifications and experience;Benefit of the placement to the intern; and Overall quality and completeness of the application.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:To apply, businesses will need to first fill out an interest form which will be reviewed in 1 to 2 business days; If the applicant, intern and
project are deemed eligible, applicants will be sent a link to OCI’s online application system,
AccessOCI, to complete the online application form and upload the required supporting documents;Company profile including CRA business number, incorporation date and number of employees (globally and in Ontario); andIntern’s CV and official transcript.All eligible applications undergo a review process where the applications are assessed against program objectives and criteria, therefore not all eligible applications will be approved for funding;The applicant must ensure it can contribute $10,000 ($5,000 cash + $5,000 in-kind) minimum per four-month unit to match every batch of $10,000 per unit that is provided by the program; OCI will release a payment equal to 75% of the grant at the start of the project and the
remaining 25% will be disbursed at project completion; andParticipants will be expected to provide project outcomes and metrics annually at a minimum.Forms:Program website: click hereInterest form: click hereFAQ: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Skills Development Funds funds employers in Ontario to provide training and wrap-around support for job seekers and existing employees.  Employers may receive up to $5,000 in wage subsidies as well as $5,000 for training stipend per training participant. Target sectors include high-demand occupations such as skilled trades, heavy-duty equipment technicians, health care, and infrastructure projects. The intent of the program is to address the growing skills gap and to facilitate economic recovery.Grant Value: Wage Subsidy - up to 50% of wages to a maximum of  $5,000 per training participant or job placementTraining Stipends - Up to a maximum of $5,000 per training participantNote: While the grant value above is noted at $376,923. This is the average amount awarded to recipients. The highest awarded amount was $7.2 million.Turnaround Time: 10 weeksEligible Applicants:Have a presence in OntarioBe one of the following organization types:For-profit organizations;Indigenous Band offices;Trade unions;Municipalities;District Social Services Administration Boards;Consolidated Municipal Service Managers; and Hospitals.Primary applicants must:Be a legal entity and authorized to operate or carry-on business in Ontario;Maintain and declare appropriate Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) or private disability insurance coverage (if applicable);Be, or must partner with a ministry-approved Training Delivery Agent (TDA), where the applicant intends to deliver apprenticeship in-class training;The following institutions can only apply as a co-applicant with an eligible organization:Publicly assisted post-secondary institutions; andPrivate career collegesNote: Entities that are not eligible to be the primary applicant may be eligible to participate in an application or project as participating partners.Eligible Activities:In-class training support for apprentices;Accessibility accommodations, tutoring, exam preparation support, mentorship programs.On-the-job support to help trainers/journeypersons provide the training apprentices need;Wrap-around support;Recruitment and retention strategies, end-of-training supports.R&D and piloting new, innovative approaches to delivering classes that are on the 2024-2025 apprenticeship in-class training seat plan;E.g. e-learning delivery, online assessment, virtual simulation etc.Purchase of equipment or supplies that support skills building or enhance in-class training;Removing barriers in education and skills training opportunities;Providing tools, and equipment to job seekers and employees;Developing virtual employment and training services; and Building capacity of training providers and supporting organizations.Eligible Expenses:Operating costs;Salary of staff conducting training;Up to 50% to a maximum of $5,000.Professional development for staff involved in the project;Marketing;A pro-rated portion of lease of real estate;Percentage of utilities.Administrative costs;Maximum of 15% of the operating costs;Legal/accounting fees;Contracting; andIT maintenance.Capital costs;Training equipment;Vehicle and Mobile Unit purchases;Employer/Participant/Apprentice and Trainer costs;Pre-screening candidates;Personal protective equipment (PPE);Disability-related services; andTravel costs.Note: Wage subsidies may not be used as a replacement for, or to supplement tuition fees.Ineligible Expenses:Executive or senior management salaries who do not directly contribute to project delivery;Regular costs related to other activities carried out by the organization;Costs already reimbursed by government funding under other Transfer Payment Agreement;Insurance;Annual membership fees to associations; andFines and penalties.Note: For the full list of ineligible expenses, please review the program guideline here.Eligible Projects:Eligible projects must meet 1 or more sub-categories in each of the following categories:Project objectives:Support and help develop a resilient workforce;Attracting investment and job creation through the development and maintenance of a stable labour force.Bridging the skill gap between unemployed and underemployed.Encourage partnerships and support innovative ideas and training solutions;Support in-demand sectors like skilled trades and construction labour to increase housing supply in the province.Be in one of more target sectors/occupations:Skilled trades, other high-skilled occupations, technical occupations, and other occupations in high demand (e.g. heavy-duty equipment technician, technology-related jobs, etc.)Manufacturing and advanced manufacturing;In-demand healthcare occupations;Infrastructure projects essential for both sustainability and fostering economic growth.Be in one or more participant groups:Women, youth, justice-involved individuals, people with disabilities, Indigenous peoples, racialized persons, immigrants, and underemployed.Note:  Projects may be multi-year projects.Program Details:Applicants are required to submit a detailed budget with their application;The budget must include all costs directly related to delivering the project, including any proposed cash and in-kind contributions being contributed to the project by the applicant and/or their partners;The project budget must clearly identify where applicable:All costs directly related to delivering the project, within market value;Any supplies delivered by non-arms-length parties must be valued at their established arms-length equivalent market value.All costs including in-kind contributions (e.g. donated space, time donated by instructors, etc.);Funding received from partnerships and/or collaborations; andOther funding sources, including federal and provincial government funding.The program may withhold up to 15% of the funding amount until project completion;Applicants who intend to deliver apprenticeship in-class training must be OR must be partnered with a ministry-approved Training Delivery Agent (TDA);Organizations can submit more than one application, however, the project activities must be substantively different;To ensure that funding awarded is used judiciously, selected applicants who receive funding of $150,000 or more from the program will be required to engage the services of a third-party auditor to assess the financial statements of the project and submit a report to the program;Entities can submit more than one application;However, each project and project activities must be substantively different;Entities can partner together on multiple projects.Project monitoring, depending on the degree of associated risk, may include:Verification of documents and other forms prior to processing;Direct contact with the selected applicant and/or participants/beneficiaries, other stakeholders, and partners;On-site/virtual visits to assess progress and achievement of activity milestones;On-site/virtual visits to verify expenditures and compliance to Agreement terms;Utilizing program/project data for informed decision-making; orProduction of a digital periodical associated with an eligible print periodical.Program Details:The number of applications if on a per publication basis;If a publication company has 2 eligible periodicals, the applicant company can submit 2 applications.Grant funding must be spent by March 31, 2022;Unspent funds may be required to be refunded.Any changes to the organization or publication(s) may render the applicant organization ineligible, including changes to:Name of the publishing firm;Title of the periodical;Periodical ceases publishing;Insolvency - Assignment in bankruptcy;
