      Grant Criteria 
      The Industrial Energy Management Program provides funding of up to 50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $40,000 per facility and up to $200,000 for multiple facilities. Eligible facilities must engage in energy-consuming processes that involve the physical or chemical transformation of materials or substances into new products. Eligible projects should have energy savings potential such as greenhouse gas emission reduction. The intent of the program is to reduce the impact of industries on the environment.Grant Value: 40% of eligible costs up to $40,000 per facility or $200,000 for multiple-facilitiesTurnaround Time: 5 weeksEligible Applicants:Must engage in energy-consuming processes that involve the physical or chemical transformation of materials or substances into new products;Have products that may be finished (ready to use or consume) or semi-finished (raw material);Be able to provide either:A GST number;An incorporation document; orProvincial business registration.Have facilities located in Canada;Be registered as a CIPEC Leader;Has the financial, management, and technical resources to fulfill the undertaking; andDoes not owe any money to the Government of Canada and is not involved in litigation or an ongoing settlement process commenced by the Government of Canada.Eligible Costs:Salaries of internal employees for work specific to the energy management system (EnMS);Professional, scientific, and technical fees specific to the EnMS;Fees for data collection, benchmarking, monitoring, and analysis services;Fees associated with training on the EnMS.Purchase of instrumentation software and metering equipment; andOther capital costs are ineligible.Fees associated with obtaining ISO 50001 certification.Re-certification or fees associated with re-certification are ineligible.Ineligible Costs:Fees for tasks started before NRCan’s approval and execution of a Contribution Agreement;Energy retrofits;Purchase and installation of equipment and systems (with the exception of the purchase of instrumentation software and metering equipment);Capital projects; andISO 50001 re-certification or fees associated with re-certification.Program Details:The project must  not involve any former public servants to whom the Conflict of Interest and Post-Employment Code for Public Office Holders or the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Service apply;Projects must be completed by March 31, 2023;Applicants must complete the Energy Planning Report Template (provided by NRCan) no later than 6 months into the project;Applicants must complete the Final Report Template (provided by NRCan) upon project completion;NRCan will withhold 10% from each reimbursement payment until it is satisfied with the final report from the Applicant; andApplicants are required to monitor and report energy performance improvement results from the project, on an annual basis for three years following the end of the project using the Annual Report Template provided by NRCan.

The program provides participants with free enrolment in BioTalent Canada's suite of Essential Skills and Technical Skills training courses, and gives them access to the BioSkills Recognition Program. The goals of the program are to connect employers to talented individuals they might not otherwise consider for roles, and to help newcomers to Canada enter the bio-economy. Grant Value: max. 75% of wages up to $20,000 per placementTurnaround Time: 5-10 business daysEligible Employers: Must be a Canadian company in the bio-health, bio-energy, bio-industrial or agri-biotech sector. No specific sector, company type, or company size is prioritized. Eligible Participants:Must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or refugee;Must be a new immigrant to Canada (in Canada 5 years or less);Must be seeking first full-time work experience in Canada's bio-economy;Must not be recipient of EI contributions;Must be legally entitled to work in Canada;Must be a new employee (not previously employed by the organization applying for funding); andMust be added to the employer's payroll (not a contractor). Internship Details: Must be full-time (min. 30 hours per week);Must be between 3 and 9 months in duration;Employer must have a nepotism policy with respect to the intern;Participant must be approved for participation prior to the start of the placement (can take up to 10 business days); Employer must develop a Formal Learning Plan with the participant prior to the start of the placement;Employer must submit monthly financial claims, progress reports, and additional data upon request;Placement Contract must be completed before the start of the placement; andEmployer may be required to provide proof of employment, employment contract, start date, and full wage and benefits.Note: There is no limit to the number of internships a company can apply for. However, each internship must support a unique participant. Participants cannot apply for a second internship.

      Grant Criteria 
      CCSIF grants provide funding  of up to $120,000 per year for 1-3 years to colleges working with public, private, or not-for-profit partners on well-defined community innovation projects. Community innovation projects are those that use new and existing ideas to solve complex community challenges, and that create positive health and/or social outcomes for communities. The goal of the program is to foster community innovation by connecting Canada's colleges and polytechnics with the research needs of local organizations. Grant Value: $120,000 per year for 1-3 years.Turnaround time: 20 weeksEligible Applicants: CCSIF is an institutional grant: the primary applicant must be employed at an eligible Canadian college or polytechnic, and is responsible for administering the grant on behalf of the institution;Colleges must be declared eligible to administer grants by at least one of the three federal funding agencies (NSERC, CHIR, SSHRC);They must offer programs that are aligned with the applied research areas identified in the proposal;Faculty members included in the proposal must be engaged in applied research;The college must provide space, facilities, and services to support the proposed project;Proposals must identify a project director who is affiliated with the college and able to undertake independent research;Partner organizations may be Canadian organizations from the private, public, or not-for-profit sectors;Partner organizations are expected to participate actively in the project, and contribute resources (cash or in kind) to support project activities; andPartner organizations should implement and/or leverage project outcomes to benefit the community and/or Canadian society.Eligible Projects:Eligible projects are those that use new and existing ideas to solve complex community challenges, and that create positive health and/or social outcomes for communities. Possible project areas include, but are not limited to:Social integration of vulnerable populations;Community development;Education and training;Climate change and/or environmental degradation; andHealth and well-being.Eligible Expenses: Overhead and administrative costs equivalent to 20% of the annual grant amount;Costs associated with hiring replacement faculty to cover teaching load of faculty members heavily involved in the research project;Salaries and non-discretionary benefits for non-faculty researchers, part-time faculty, technical and professional staff, research administrators, business development, technology, and/or knowledge transfer personnel;Stipends for college students;University students are not eligible for student stipends, and should be remunerated as technical/professional staff, or as consultants;Salaries associated with project management staff and activities; andEquipment, operating, supplies, and consulting fees up to 20% of total project budget (total budget includes grants and cash contributions from partner organizations).Note: Applicants have the option of adding a Mitacs Accelerate Internship to their CCSIF application to support the training of highly qualified personnel (HPQ). Contact a Mitacs Business Development Representative to obtain a Mitacs-NSERC joint application form, which can then be submitted with the CCSIF application through the Convergence Portal. Note: Colleges partnering with organizations and/or collectives that have a valid Canada Council for the Arts Applicant profile may request additional funding from the Canada Council by completing a Canada Council for the Arts budget form and submitting it with their CCSIF application through the Convergence Portal. Arts organizations may request up to $75,000 for up to 3 years to support their participation in the CCSIF project.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers funding to Canadian production companies producing premium, original digital video series (fiction and non-fiction) for online distribution. Successful applicants receive 75% of the cost of series production up to $150,000, plus an additional $50,000 for audience development. Series may be in English or French, and must have at least 6 episodes, with a maximum episode length of 20 minutes. Production companies must provide a license agreement or letter of commitment from an approved digital platform as part of their application, and must have secured third-party financing for at least 10% of the total project cost at the time of application. The production company must own, option, or control the copyright for the project. There are two submission deadlines in 2023: April 3 and September 26.Grant Value: 75% of production costs up to $150,000, plus an additional $50,000 for audience development.Note: The program will not take equity in any of the approved projects.Turnaround Time: 6-10 weeksEligible Applicants: Applicants must be Canadian production companies, defined as follows:A for-profit company carrying on business in Canada and a resident of Canada for the purposes of the Income Tax Act;Incorporated in Canada; andHead office is located in Canada.Note: The applicant company does not need to be incorporated at the time of application, but must be prepared to be incorporated if the application is successful.Eligible Projects: Short digital series in French or English, with at least 6 episodes at a minimum length of 20 minutes each;Second seasons of series are eligible, provided the previous season ran in its entirety, and key performance indicators are shared with and approved by Bell Fund;Series can be fiction or non-fiction, but must be original content;The production company must own, option, or control the copyright for the series;The series must comply with all policies and standards applicable to broadcasting and intellectual property law;It must be closed captioned and have described video;The production company must have a meaningful COVID-19 safety plan in place; andThe project must achieve at least 6/10 Canadian certification points under CRTC, OR be certified by Telefilm as an official Canadian treaty co-production (scoring guidelines included in Project Details form).Note: Animated series, instructional or informational content, corporate, industrial, or promotional content, and user-generated content (e.g.: vlogs, how-to's) are not eligible. Eligible Expenses: All standard digital video production costs contribute to the total used to calculate the subsidy, including:Labour costs;Producer fees (max. 10% of total);Corporate overhead (max. 10% of total);Contingency;Closed-captioning and described video;Liability and E&O insurance; andDevelopment costs.Once the project is approved, an additional $50,000 is available to fund audience development.Note: The expectation is that all budget costs will be spent in Canada, on Canadians. However, up to 25% of the budget may be spent on non-Canadian costs if adequate justification is provided. Program Details:There are 2 application intakes:1st intake deadline: April 3, 2023;Platform pre-approval deadline: March 13, 2023.2nd intake deadline: September 26, 2023.Pre-approvals for non-broadcaster and digital platforms must be completed no later than 3 weeks before the deadline. To be approved, the platform must:Be available to Canadians and demonstrate that it markets to Canadian audiences;Feature premium quality entertainment content; Feature short-form digital series comparable to those financed by the Bell Fund; andComply with the regulations, policies, and rulings of the CRTC guidelines on violence and sex-role portrayal.The minimum episode length: 5 minutes;The maximum episode length: 20 minutes;The minimum number of episodes in a series: 6;If applying for a subsequent season (regardless of Bell Fund’s involvement in the previous season) the majority of the previous season must have streamed in order to provide key performance indicators;Each company shareholder and key creative personnel involved in a project’s production team be identified in the 'Self-Identification Contact List';After the application is submitted, a link to 'Bell Fund’s Online Self-Identification Questionnaire' will be emailed directly to each individual listed in the 'Self-Identification Contact List';The questionnaire must be completed within 7 days of receipt of the email invitation. In this manner, the applicant no longer has to collect this information on behalf of others.Application packages are submitted via the Bell Fund online portal, assessed for eligibility and completion, then submitted to an independent jury for evaluation;Evaluation takes 6-10 weeks; andUpon approval, applicants submit 2 additional forms (Audience Development Plan and Audience Development Project) to qualify for a $50,000 audience development top-up.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Reconnect Ontario 2022 program provides funding of 50% of total eligible expenses up to $250,000 to Ontario-based entities in operation on or before January 1, 2021. Eligible events are those that take place in Ontario between April 1, 2022, and March 31, 2023. Events must be open to the public. The intent of the program is to provide job opportunities for Ontarians, to offer safe experiences that draw tourists and local visitors.Grant Value: 50% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $250,000Turnaround Time: Applicants will be notified in Spring 2022Eligible Applicants:Ontario-based entities;Be in existence on or before January 1, 2021;Carry at least$2 million commercial general liability insurance coverage; andNot be in default of the terms and conditions of any grant or loan agreement with any ministry or agency of the Government of Ontario.Ineligible Applicants:Governments of any level and/or their agencies;Sole proprietorships;Limited partnerships;Limited liability partnerships; andGeneral partnershipsEligible Events:Must occur in Ontario;If the event is broadcasted or is a virtual event, the event must be produced in Ontario.Take place between April 1, 2022 and March 31, 2023;Be open to the public at large without membership in a club or group;Must follow all municipal and provincial guidelines, including health and safety guidelines.Ineligible Events:Fundraising events or events with a primarily charitable purpose;Symposia, conventions, meetings, conferences, seminars, clinics, workshops, contests, and events that solely consist of an award show;Sporting events offering programming that is of primary benefit to event participants only (e.g., local hockey tournaments), and is not marketed to, or does not attract, additional visitors;Events that seek to attract only a special interest audience, restrict audiences (e.g. students only), or recruit new members (e.g., religious or political gatherings and workshops);Events of a primarily commercial nature, where the main intent of the event is to sell or promote one or multiple products, services, or sponsorships (e.g., trade fairs and shows, business events, consumer shows, artisan and craft fairs); andEvents that are receiving funding through the Ontario Sport Hosting Program, the Celebrate Ontario Blockbuster program, or the Ontario Music Investment Fund (OMIF).Eligible Expenses:Costs incurred for the delivery of the event;Costs linked to programming activities and other services accessible to the public;Cannot only benefit VIPs or invitation-only guests.Including but not limited to the following:Programming and productionPerformance fees, travel, accommodation, and booking costs to Canadianartists, musicians, and other entertainers;Note: International artists are ineligible.For eligible sporting events, programming costs related to attracting and engaging spectators;Ontario-based production costs, including audio and visual support (e.g., rental of sound and lighting equipment and rental of event venue).Promotions and advertisingPaid advertisements on broadcast, digital, print, social media;Distribution costs for printed materials.Other expensesCosts related to strengthening health and safety measures at the event;Wages for temporary/contract event staff directly related to programming and marketing of the event;Note: Wages for contract staff employed on a year-round basis are not eligible.Event security;Other costs are deemed reasonable.Note: For the full list of eligible and ineligible expenses, please see the program guideline pages 7-10 here.Program Details:1 event per application;Maximum of 2 applications per organization;Approved applicants are expected to:Report back to the ministry within 90 days following the event on the use of funds;Permit the province to verify/audit information submitted; andAgree that if the funds were not used or will not be used for the intended purpose(s), the province has the right at a future date to recover parts or all of the funds transferred.

Applicants are to create a ONe-key account and ID that may take up to 5 days. Applicants are advised to start the process early;Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides grants of up $10,000 to for-profit businesses in B. C. that had to close as a result of the December 22, 2021 Public Health Officer (PHO) orders, with additional funding (to a total of $20,000) available to businesses that must remain closed according to the January 18, 2022 PHO order. The amount of the grant scales to the size of the business, and can be used to cover rent and utilities, insurance, maintenance, and employee wages. To be eligible, businesses must have complied fully with the PHO orders. To qualify for HHBRP, organizations must have a 12-month average revenue drop from March 2020 to February 2021 of at least 50%, and a claim period revenue drop of at least 50%. Rent subsidies are capped at $75,000 per location.Grant Value: Up to 50% maximum subsidy rateEligible Applicants:Must be one of the following eligible entities:Sole proprietors; Corporations or trusts that are not exempt from income tax;Non-profits; andCertain business associations and organizations (see application guidelines for full list).If applying for wage subsidies, applicant must have had a CRA Payroll Account since at least March 15, 2020;exceptions apply in payroll provider and asset acquisition situations;If applying for rent subsidies only, applicant does not need a CRA Payroll Account, but must have had a Business Number registered with the CRA since September 27, 2020; andMust have a 12-month average revenue drop from March 2020 to February 2021 of at least 50% and a claim period revenue drop of at least 50%.Eligible Employees:Full Time, Part Time, Casual Employees  where wages,  salaries, other remuneration like taxable benefits were paid during qualifying periods;Unlike CEWS, employees on leave with pay are not included in the calculation of the wage subsidy for HHBRP;Non-resident employees are eligible if they are employed primarily in Canada and physically reside in Canada.Eligible Expenses: For wage subisdies, the following expenses are eligible:Salary and wages;Certain taxable benefits;Fees and commissions;For rent subsidies, the following expenses are eligible: Costs related to real property (buildings or land) in Canada that the applicant rents or owns and uses in the course of ordinary business activities, such as:Commercial rent;Property tax;Property insurance;Interest on commercial mortgages (subject to limits); andAncillary services (eligibility determined on a case-by-case basis).Ineligible Expenses: For wage subsidies, the following expenses are ineligible:Severance pay;Stock option benefits;Dividends;Tips customers gave directly to employees; andnon-cash taxable benefits. For rent subsidies, the following expenses are ineligible:Residential property used by the applicant;Any revenue from renting or subleasing space on the property to entities with existing business or personal relationships (arm's length parties);Payments made to entities with existing business or personal relationships (non-arm's length); andMortgage interest expenses for rental income properties.Program Details: HHBRP requires a separate application for each claim period;Applications can be submitted one of three ways:Through CRA My Business Account;By a representative, through CRA Represent A Client portal;Through a Web Form application (for business owners who do not have a My Business Account).To apply, first calculate the average 12-month revenue drop using the calculator found here;Next, calculate the subsidy amount using the appropriate subsidy calculator:For rent subsidies, use the calculator found here;For wage subsidies, use the calculator found here;Calculators require the following information: Monthly qualifying revenue amounts from the last 2 years;  Eligible staff payroll details for each week of the calculation period (for wage subsidies); Eligible expenses broken down by business location (for rent subsidies);Download or print the results of each calculator (12-month revenue drop, rent subsidy, and wage subsidy), and use them to complete the HHBRP application;Add or update direct deposit information through CRA My Business Account;Direct deposit payments will be received in 3-5 days;Cheque payments will be received in 3-8 days, plus additional time for mail delivery. Note: The CRA calculators are not saveable, and information will be lost when the page is refreshed.       Grant Criteria 
      This program supports large accommodation providers and commercial recreation businesses operating on Crown land or in BC Parks by providing one-time grants to offset certain fixed costs. Funding will be awarded in three streams: 1) property tax relief for large accommodation providers; 2) BC Hydro fee relief for Indigenous-owned large accommodation providers operating on reserve; and 3) fee relief for rent under Land Act Tenures or Park Use Permits for commercial recreation operators. The goal of the program is to support the post-pandemic recovery of B.C.'s tourism industry; to be eligible, businesses must be B.C. owned, and must not owe any tax payments from before the 2020 tax year. The application portal will remain open until February 14, 2022, or until funding is fully allocated, whichever comes first. Grant Value:Stream 1: 25% of 2021 property taxes, up to a maximum of $500,000;Stream 2: 100% of 2021 BC Hydro costs, up to a maximum of $200,000;Stream 3: 100% of fees paid for rent under Land Act Tenures or Park Use Permits on invoices with payment due dates between May 1, 2021, and April 30, 2022.Turnaround time: Funding decisions will be announced by March 31st, 2022Eligible Applicants: Businesses that are majority-owned by one or more B.C. residents;Must not owe any tax payments from before the 2020 tax year;Must be in operation (seasonal closures are acceptable, but businesses that closed permanently during the pandemic are not eligible for this retroactive funding);For Stream 1: Hotels, motels, resorts, lodges, and strata hotels that employ 150 or more people for at least 4 months of the year (including part-time, seasonal, and contracted employees);Must operate on land they own; andMust pay property tax.For Stream 2:  Indigenous-owned hotels, motels, resorts, lodges, and strata hotels that employ 100 or more people for at least 4 months of the year (including part-time, seasonal, and contracted employees); andMust operate on reserve.For Stream 3:Tourism operators that hold commercial recreation Land Act Tenures or Park use Permits;Must be in good standing; andMust have received or expect to receive invoices with payment due dates between May 1, 2021, and April 30th, 2022.Ineligible Applicants:Non-profit organizations;Educational institutions;Indoor recreation facilities; andMajor resorts and golf courses with Crown land rent based on revenue-sharing;For Stream 3, additional eligibility criteria apply. Businesses are not eligible for Stream 3 funding if they provide any of the following services, even if they also offer commercial recreation activities:Transportation (vehicle or watercraft rentals, marinas, private yacht clubs);Accommodation (hotels, motels, B&Bs);Food and beverage services (restaurants, pubs, wineries, farmers' markets); andTravel services (offices or kiosks for booking travel arrangements).Eligible Expenses:For Stream 1:25% of 2021 property taxes, up to a maximum of $500,000.For Stream 2:100% of 2021 BC Hydro costs, up to a maximum of $200,000.For Stream 3: 100% of Land Act Tenure or Park Use Permit rent fees whose payment due dates fall between May 1, 2021, and April 30th, 2022.Note: Businesses that offer commercial recreation under both a Land Act Tenure and a Park Use Permit may apply for relief for both. Program Details: Applications are submitted via online form. The following information is required:Business information, including the business number and registration number;Central Securities Register or Schedule 50 Shareholder Information;If place of residence is not clearly stated on ownership documents, a B.C. driver's license or B.C. Service Card may also be required;2020 Notice of Assessment from Canada Revenue Agency;2019 T4 Summary of Remuneration Paid;For Stream 1: 2021 property tax statement and proof of payment;For Stream 2: 2021 BC Hydro invoices;For Stream 3:File number(s) for Land Act Tenure and/or Park Use Permit;Applicants will receive a decision about their grant application by March 31st, 2022; Payments will be made by electronic funds transfer or cheque;Grant recipients may be subject to post-payment audits by the Ministry of Tourism, Arts, Culture, and Sport.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices: This program applies retroactively to specific fixed costs incurred in 2021;This program funding cannot be used in conjunction with other provincial and federal relief funding;The application process is simple, provided you have all business information, registration and permit numbers, and digital copies of supporting documents assembled before beginning the form;Ensure that your application is complete and contains all supporting documents, as Ministry decisions are final.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Ontario Business Cost Rebate Program provides funding of up to 100% of property tax and energy costs of businesses impacted by the public health measures in response to the Omicron variant of COVID-19. Eligible businesses must be subject to the provincially mandated capacity limit of 50% or lower, including temporary closures, and must pay commercial property taxes and/or non-residential energy costs directly or through the property owner.Grant Value: 50%-100% of eligible property taxes and energy bills incurred during capacity reduction or closureTurnaround Time: 3 weeksEligible Applicants:Located in Ontario;Subjected or be expected to be impacted by the provincially mandated capacity limit of 50% or lower, including temporary closures;Pay commercial property taxes and/or commercial energy costs (directly or through the property owner as detailed in their lease);Maintains a Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Number;If a business does not have a CRA Business Number, please refer to the Government of Canada webpage, How to Register for a Business Number or CRA Program Accounts.Be one of the following business types:Restaurants and bars;Personal hair or body care services (hair salons, spas, manicure salons, tanning salons, tattoo studios);Non-grocery retailers <50,000 square feet (corner stores, boutique bakers, butcher shops, fruit markets);Gyms and other indoor sports facilities (including dance studios, martial arts facilities);Places of worship;Indoor meeting and event spaces (banquet halls, conference centers, event spaces in hotels);Indoor concert venues, theatres, and cinemas;Casinos, bingo halls, and other gaming establishments;Indoor horse and car racing tracks;Indoor museums, galleries, aquariums, zoos, landmarks, historic sites, botanical gardens, etc.Indoor clubhouses at outdoor recreational amenities;Indoor businesses associated with tour and guide services;Oxygen bars;Steam rooms and saunas;Bathhouses;Teaching and instruction centers;Day camps and overnight camps;Before- and after-school programs; andPet and veterinary services.Note: Non-profit organizations and charities may be eligible if their operations/services align with the business types listed above.Ineligible Applicants:Businesses that do not pay business property taxes and/or energy costs, such as those with a gross lease or businesses operated out of residential properties;Landlords that do not own or operate a business on the applicable property that meets the eligibility criteria; andBusinesses owned by the federal, provincial, or municipal government, or those owned by a person holding federal or provincial office.Eligible Expenses:Property taxes incurred while required to close or reduce capacity due to recently announced public health measures;Municipal and provincial (Business Education Tax) components of the property tax bills are eligible.Applicants only need to apply once for the property tax component.Energy costs incurred while required to close or reduce capacity due to recently announced public health measures;Including bills for electricity and natural gas (or, where natural gas is not available, propane and/or heating oil);Rebates for the energy cost component of the program are provided based on the statement date of a submitted energy bill, not with respect to the period the business is billed for (i.e., a business may receive a rebate for November energy bill dated as of December 19, 2021 or later);Businesses are required to submit all pages of their energy bills for each month that they are subject to closure or reduced capacity due to recently announced public health measures.If a business becomes eligible for additional billing cycles, they are required to return to the application portal to submit new energy bills for each additional month they are eligibleIneligible Expenses:Arrears and Late Fees - bills may include overdue amounts not paid from previous bills;Water and wastewater costs;Third-Party Appliances and Services;Natural gas and hydro bills can include third-party charges such as the sale, service, rental, or financing of appliances (e.g. hot water tanks and sentinel lights) and energy efficiency or environmental initiatives.HST could be charged on the bill as a single combined amount for eligible and ineligible charges; andAdditional charges that are not related to the delivery or consumption of energy for the billing period in question are also ineligible.Program Details:Multi-use business properties with a component that meets the eligibility criteria and is included on the list of eligible business types may be eligible for that portion of the property;E.g. a restaurant within a hotel, the applicant would be required to separate out the eligible business type.Property tax and energy costs associated with the eligible portion(s) of the business can be based on a reasonable estimate such as how much indoor square footage the eligible portion of the business occupies compared to the total square footage of the entire business/property;E.g. if the eligible portion occupies 10% of the property, they would be eligible for 10% of the property’s property tax and energy cost.Property tax calculations example:A restaurant is eligible for 50% of their property tax costs in December because they were subject to a 50% capacity limit. In January, they are eligible for 100% of their property tax costs because indoor dining is closed:(Annual property tax / 12 months) x 50% = Property Tax Rebate for December;(Annual property tax / 12 months) x 100% = Property Tax Rebate for January  A restaurant is eligible for 50% of their property tax costs in December because they were subject to a 50% capacity limit. In January, they are eligible for 100% of their property tax costs because indoor dining is closed.Energy cost calculation example:Hotels are ineligible for the Ontario Business Costs Rebate Program, but restaurants are eligible. To calculate the payment amount for a restaurant within a hotel, the payment amount would be adjusted to reflect the square footage occupied by the restaurant. I.e. Restaurant square footage / total hotel square footage = Business Eligibility Energy Rate %:Payment = Eligible energy costs x 100% x Business Eligibility Energy Rate %. Additional billing cycles to be calculated at the same rateThe total number of eligible billing cycles available for restaurants will take into account the number of days restaurants have capacity restrictions and the % capacity limits.If the application is approved, the applicant will receive an email with information regarding payment details.       Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program helps SMEs in the advanced manufacturing sector invest in capital equipment, technology adoption, and skills development by funding 15% of the total project cost between $500,000 and $5,000,000, and by providing complementary services and support. In most cases, the funding comes as a loan, with no interest during the project period (up to four years). If investment and job/upskilling targets are met, up to 30% of the loan (up to $500,000) may be forgiven. For small companies located in rural areas, and for certain strategic projects, the funding may be awarded as a non-repayable grant. The goals of the program are to create jobs, attract private-sector investment, improve competitiveness, encourage innovation, and stimulate economic growth.Grant value:Loan portionUp to 15% of funding to a maximum of $5 million, interest-free during the project period (up to four years);If you achieve your investment and job or upskilling targets, up to 30% of the loan (to a maximum of $500,000) may be forgiven.Grant portionUp to 15% to a maximum of $500,000 for small companies in rural communities (less than 100 full-time employees and in a municipality of less than 100,000 people or a population density of 100 people per square kilometer or less.Up to 15% to a maximum of $1.5 million for strategic projects that are foreign direct investments or from companies competing against other jurisdictions or companies with significant reshoring projects.Turnaround Time: Notified July 22, 2025Eligible Applicants:For-profit businesses in the advanced manufacturing sector, including but not limited to the following sub-sectors:Aerospace;Automotive; Chemical;Information and Communications Technology;Life sciences; and/orSteel.Located in Ontario, or planning to locate in Ontario;Have at least 3 years of operations and financial statements;Employ at least 10 full-time equivalent employees;Committed to creating or upskilling at least 5 jobs; andAble to invest at least $500,000 in the project.Eligible Projects:Create jobs and build talent;Attract and encourage private sector investment;Help companies to adopt technologies to improve their competitiveness;Lead to business growth and broad positive economic impacts; andEncourage innovation, collaboration, and cluster development.Ineligible Projects:Ongoing operations including maintenance and capital replacement;Refinancing of existing business operations;Acquisitions and buyouts;Restructuring, or relocating to other jurisdictions within Ontario;Primary production;Retail;Construction (for example, residential development);Electricity generation;Waste management;Recycling.Eligible Expenses: Must be directly attributable to the project;Must be incurred and paid on or after the project start date identified in the funding agreement;Must be new investments to improve productivity, innovation, and growth, including:Project facilities and infrastructure;Equipment and machinery;One-time labour directly related to the project (ie: costs related to commissioning and/or setting up new equipment, technology, and systems for the project);Specialized labour directly related to the project (ie: research and development) for up to 2 years;Materials;Specialized expertise;Training and talent costs; andPermits and fees.Ineligible Expenses:Ongoing operational and production labour costs;Purchase of land and/or buildings;Costs associated with landscaping and staff parking lots;Purchase or lease of vehicles or other off-site equipment;Raw materials for commodity production;Preparation of funding proposal;Shareholder payments;Costs occurred outside Ontario, except purchases from suppliers;Mergers and acquisitions;Travel, hospitality, meal, and incidental expenses;Rebates, credit, or refund;Debt service; andMarketing, sales, or distribution costs. Program Details: To apply for AMIC funding, businesses must be registered on Transfer Payment Ontario (TPON);If you do not have a TPON account, you can create one using your CRA Business Number. Allow up to 5 business days for processing;Complete the Eligibility Checklist through TPON;Once the Eligibility Checklist is approved (usually within 3 business days), proceed to the application form;Include the following supporting documents with the application:A cash flow projection for the project period and loan repayment period (four years post-project completion date) showing sufficient detail for Ontario to assess the company's ability to repay the loan;Copy of articles of incorporation and/or patent letters;Corporate family tree showing parent company, affiliates, and related entities;Audited financial statements from the last three fiscal years;If audited statements are not available, contact an Ontario Government advisor; andLetters of support from project partners and financial institutions, ideally with financial commitments.If approved, applicants will enter into a funding agreement with the Government of Ontario. Funding will be disbursed after the applicant has met the disbursement conditions outlined in the agreement, including providing evidence of project financing and insurance;Successful applicants will be required to document project progress in detailed annual reports;If all investment and job creation targets are met, up to 30% of the loan may be forgiven;Funding may be issued as a non-repayable grant in the following cases:Small companies in rural areas with project budgets of $500,000; Projects with budgets of $1,500,000 that pursue one of the following strategic priorities:Foreign-direct investment;Competition with another jurisdiction;Significant reshoring.In addition to funding, successful applicants can access the following complementary supports:Advisory services, such as guidance on compliance approvals;Help with skills and talent;Health and safety support; andEnvironmental support.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:AMIC cannot be used in conjunction with other provincial funding;AMIC is not retroactive;Process Best Practices:Because the application process is quite competitive, applicants are encouraged to contact a provincial government advisor for help with their application; andProjects are assessed according to the following criteria:Alignment with the fund's goals of supporting advanced manufacturing in the province;Potential job creation and/or upskilling;The potential economic benefit to the province; andFeasibility.Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guidelines: click here

and/orRecruit 20 (or more) diverse candidates for critical high-demand roles in Canadian ocean SMEs;Seek a maximum program contribution of 65% of eligible costs (up to $600,000);Plan to conclude by March 31, 2023;Build incrementally on existing ecosystem capacity;Involve a minimum of three applicants who are Canadian entities and OSC members;Create one (or more) net-new relationships between project delivery agents;Be national in scope, with deliverables in at least 4 provinces;Have a clear execution plan, and a forecast of the project's impact after the funding period;Include a detailed, realistic budget;       Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program covers 50% of the cost of mineral exploration/ development projects undertaken by junior mining companies, up to a maximum of $200,000.  Of the total amount, $10,000 may be set aside for Indigenous engagement efforts, which will be covered at 100%. To apply, companies must have a market capitalization of less than $100 million on the opening date of the intake period, and must be registered to conduct business in Ontario. Projects must identify new mineral exploration targets, or evaluate existing targets in areas not known to host a mineral deposit with economic potential. The goals of the program are to expand mineral exploration in Ontario, promote the development of critical minerals, and increase Indigenous representation in the mining industry. Intake for the current cycle closes on February 15, 2022. Grant Value: 50% of eligible project costs, up to a maximum of $200,000Turnaround time: Funding decisions to be made within 30 days of the application deadlineEligible Applicants:Non-producing, junior mining companies registered to conduct business in Ontario;Must have a market capitalization of less than $100 million on the opening date of the intake cycle (January 10, 2022);Must be able to demonstrate the ability to cover 100% of project costs on the day the application is submitted;Must provide a valid Certificate of Insurance which includes the following:General liability insurance for at least $2 million per occurrence;A cross-liability clause;Contractual liability coverage; andA 30-day written notice of cancellation.Must be enrolled in the Mining Lands Administration System and thus able to hold mining claims in Ontario;Claims must be in good standing for the duration of the project.Must have an exploration plan and/or valid permit at the time of application and for the duration of the project; andMust have the approval of the tenure holder to conduct the project in the event of an option agreement or co-tenure holder relationship. Eligible Projects:Grassroots mineral exploration that pursues either of the following objectives:Identifying new mineral exploration targets; OREvaluating existing targets in areas not known to host a mineral deposit with economic value.Possible project components include:The establishment of a grid by line cutting;Geophysical, geological, or geochemical surveys;Overburden stripping, trenching, and test pitting;Surface overburden and core drilling for exploration purposes;Removal of material;Rehabilitation activities required by permits and/or exploration plans (such as capping and sealing of drill holes, disposing of drilling fluids, backfilling, contouring, sloping, etc.); andEvaluation activities (assaying and analysis).Projects may also include Indigenous training, hiring, and procurement initiatives, eligible to be subsidized at 100% up to a maximum of $10,000.Eligible Expenses: Costs that are directly attributable to the project and necessary for its completion, and that fall into any of the following categories:Salaries and benefits of permanent employees;Hourly wages of temporary employees;Mandatory Employment Related Costs (MERCs) such as employer contributions to Employment Insurance, CPP, etc.;Contractor, sub-contractor, and/or consultant fees related to the project, but not to the project proposal;Equipment rentals and supplies;Cost of transporting personnel, supplies, and machinery to project site;Meals and accommodation that are directly project-related;Indigenous engagement efforts, including:Salary and benefits for permanent Indigenous employees;Wages and benefits for temporary Indigenous employees;Skills training for Indigenous employees; andCosts to procure from Indigenous suppliers.Ineligible Expenses: Capital costs (land, buildings, vehicles, etc.);Infrastructure costs (buildings and facilities);Costs related to proposal development;Costs associated with celebration or entertaining (food, alcohol, gifts, etc.);Costs associated with lobbying or government relations;Allowance for interest on invested capital;Ongoing administrative and operational costs; andPrototyping.Program Details: To apply for OJEP funding, businesses must be registered on Transfer Payment Ontario (TPON);If you do not have a TPON account, you can create one using your CRA Business Number. Allow up to 5 business days for processing;Download, complete, and re-upload the OJEP application form through TPON;The application form requires the following information: Completed eligibility checklist;Company information;Direct deposit information;Project name and timeline;The total cost of the project and amount requested from OJEP (the requested amount must not exceed $200,000);Project summary, objectives, proposed activities, rationale, and anticipated results;Plans for Indigenous engagement and capacity-building (if applicable);Summary of previous mineral exploration experience;Description of the project site;Exploration plan and/or permit numbers;List of claims, leases, etc., where activities are being carried out; andStatement of the relationship between the applicant and the mining rights holder (if they are not the same entity).Include any items submitted to the Ministry as part of applications for plans or permits;Include copies of any permits issued by the Ministry; If the project does not require a Ministry permit, include a regional- and a project-scale map that meets Ministry standards;Proof of the applicant's ability to cover 100% of the cost of the project on the day the application is submitted (bank statement preferred);Proof of insurance;Successful applicants with enter a funding agreement with the Ministry;Approved projects will commence by April 1, 2022, and end by February 15, 2023;An interim report will be submitted to the Ministry at the halfway point of the project, identified in the funding agreement. If the report is satisfactory, 30% of the funding will be dispensed; andThe remaining funding will be dispensed following review of the final report, which is due February 28, 2023. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices: Applicants using TPON(formerly Grants Ontario) for the first time need to create a “ONe-key” account. Setting up an account may take up to 5 business days so allow at least 1 week to register before starting the application process; andOnce an application has been started, it may be saved or downloaded at any point and returned to later. Please refer to  Transfer Payment Ontario for instructions on how to submit the application.Forms: Program website: click hereProgram guide: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Low Carbon Economy Challenge - Champions Stream provides funding of up to 75% of eligible project costs up to $25,000,000 to a wide range of applicants with projects that reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and generate clean growth. The program has 4 streams: 1.) The Indigenous Leadership Fund 2.) The Implementation Readiness Fund 3.) The Leadership Fund 4.) The Challenge Fund. Applicants must first use the Self-Screening Tool, followed by a full evaluation of project merit. The intent of the program is to achieve GHG emissions reductions in 2030 and goals for net-zero emissions by 2050.Grant Value: $1,000,000 - $25,000,000, cost-share ranges from:25% for for-profit private sector businesses40% for regional/local/municipal governments40% for not-for-profit organizations50% for provincial governments/bodies/boards75% for territorial governments/bodies/boards75% for Indigenous communities and organizationsTurnaround Time: Final funding decisions to be announced in early July 2024Eligible Applicants:Be one of the following organization types:Private sector for-profit small, medium, and large businesses;Non-profit organizations;Provincial governments, bodies, or boards;Territorial governments, bodies, or boards;Regional/local/municipal governments;First Nations, Métis, and Inuit government, communities, or for-profit organizations;Public sector bodies or boards; andResearch, academic or educational institutions.Have not received funding from the other Low Carbon Economy Fund streams; andHave the project location confirmed at the time of application.Note: Previous applicants of the Challenge Fund may reapply for this intake so long as there is no overlap of eligible costs.Eligible Projects:Must achieve material GHG reductions;Must be tangible, measurable, achievable, and sizeable enough to contribute to Canada's GHG reduction targets;Must also be directly attributed to the project.Have incremental GHG reductions;Be beyond what is required by existing regulations, and standards.Be at a reasonable level of project readiness;Projects with outstanding feasibility studies are unlikely to be completed by March 31, 2028.Have the capacity to make use of commercially available technology;4 funding streams:The Indigenous Leadership Fund provides funding for renewable energy, energy efficiency, and low-carbon heating projects led by First Nations, Inuit, and Métis governments, communities, and organizations. Funding is available for a variety of project phases, including planning, feasibility, and deployment, along with capacity-building activities.The Implementation Readiness Fund provides funding for activities and investments that increase readiness to deploy GHG emissions reduction projects from lower-capacity entities and organizations.The Leadership Fund provides funding to provinces and territories to stimulate ambitious provincial and territorial climate action, with a focus on deploying proven, low-carbon technologies that will result in GHG emissions reductions in 2030 and align with Canada’s net-zero by 2050 goals.The Challenge Fund provides funding to a wide range of applicants to support the deployment of proven, low-carbon technologies that will result in material GHG emissions across sectors. There is now only one stream under the Challenge Fund. There will no longer be multiple streams (e.g., Champions and Partnerships).Eligible Project Activities:Energy efficiency;Stationary equipment retrofits for energy efficiency;Mobile Equipment retrofits for energy efficiency;Building envelope upgrades (insulation, windows, doors);Heat recovery.Fuel switching;Stationary equipment retrofits for fuel switching;Mobile equipment retrofits for fuel switching.Energy production;Clean electricity production for own use;Low-carbon fuel production for own use;Cogeneration or combined heat and power production;Using low-carbon fuels, but not using fossil fuels.District energy and/or heating.Non-energy related;Organics diversion;Landfill gas capture;Industrial process emissions changes;Industrial product use changes (e.g. refrigerants).Carbon capture;Carbon capture and storage;Carbon capture and utilization (excluding enhanced oil recovery).Expanding to new facilities or buildings.This may only be eligible for types of equipment, technologies, or processes.Must NOT require full construction (e.g. foundation, framing, building envelope).Note: End-user training directly related to the implementation of the project can be eligible for funding.Ineligible Project Activities:Purchase of on-road zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs);Zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) infrastructure;LED (light-emitting diode) lighting retrofits;Electricity transmission and distribution infrastructure;New fossil-fuel combustion equipment, including new cogeneration/combined heat and power production;Research and development (R&D);Routine maintenance activities; andRegulatory compliance activities.Note: For the full list of ineligible activities, click here.Eligible Expenses:Salaries;Contractors;Including general labourers.Equipment and capital assets (purchase or rental);Must cost more than $10,000 with a useful life of more than 1 year;Includes site preparation and acquiring, constructing, rehabilitation & improvement of assets;Management and professional services (external);For services such as accounting, communications, translation, audit, GHG emission reductions, and energy savings estimate verification, and results monitoring, measuring, and reporting.Materials and supplies;Assets such as tools or equipment costing less than $10,000;Office supplies are to be included in the overhead/administrative category.Overhead and/or administrative;Planning and assessments;Maximum Program contribution of 5% of the total project funding.Printing, production and production;Training fees for employees related to the project's new technologies, equipment, software, and systems;Tax (PST, GST or HST);Hospitality, travel and venues/conferences;Monetary honoraria offered to Indigenous Elders and/or Knowledge Keepers and hospitality expenditures for Indigenous ceremonial offerings.Program Details:Latest project end date: March 31, 2028;Project costs are only eligible if  they are incurred before the date when the Approval-In-Principle (AIP) has been sent to the successful applicant;Applicants may submit an application involving 2 or more entities to seek funding for a project;In this scenario, a lead applicant must be identified to be the main point of contact for the Program and be responsible for the applicationIf the project is approved, the Program on behalf of the Government of Canada, will enter into a funding agreement with the lead applicant only, who will be referred to as the “recipient;Assessment criteria:GHG merit (70% of total project score);2030 cost-per-tonne: funding requested from the program per tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent reduced in the year 2030 (50% of total project score);Cumulative to 2050 cost-per-tonne: funding requested from the program per tonne of cumulative carbon dioxide equivalent reduced to 2050 (20% of total project score).Net-Zero 2050 alignment (15% of total project score);The degree of alignment with net-zero and the role of the project in the facility’s long-term decarbonization pathway.Co-benefits (15% of total project score).Non-GHG benefits such as benefits to clean growth, the environment, Indigenous leadership, and health and safety.

      Grant Criteria 
      This federally funded program provides non-repayable contributions to help Aboriginal people and/or communities in the Coast Salish territory start, expand, or acquire businesses. Contributions are capped at $99,999 for individual business owners and $250,000 for community-owned businesses. The applicant must have a viable business plan, proof of Aboriginal ancestry, and the ability to cover at least 15% of the total project cost. The goals of the program are to increase the number of viable businesses owned by Aboriginal Canadians in the Coast Salish area, to cultivate a culture of entrepreneurship in the Aboriginal community, and to increase access to capital for Aboriginal businesses. Grant Value:Up to $99,999 for individual businesses;Up to $250,000 for community-owned businesses.Turnaround Time: 6 weeksEligible Applicants:Canadian Aboriginal individuals (Status or Non-Status, Métis, Inuk) residing in the TACC service area, which includes:Lower Mainland (to Squamish);Fraser Valley; andVancouver Island.*Canadian corporations, partnerships, associations, or other legal entities majority owned and controlled by Aboriginal individuals residing in the TACC service area;Applicant must be involved full-time in a management capacity in the proposed business project, and must possess the relevant certifications, qualifications, and/or licenses; andApplicant must be able to contribute at least 15% of the total project cost.  *Note: Northern BC, Central BC, and some parts of Vancouver Island are not included in TACC's service area, but TACC will refer applicants to other Aboriginal Financial Institutions as necessary. If your business falls outside of TACC's service area, you can access similar programming through the AFI that serves your region. Eligible Projects: Projects may involve starting, purchasing, expanding, or modernizing a business, and must create measurable benefits, including but not limited to additional revenue, new markets, and/or new job opportunities;Eligible market expansion activities include advertising campaigns, trade shows, seminars, and conferences;Eligible innovation activities include research, process and product development, productivity improvement, and investment in new technology and/or systems;The minimum project budget for starting, purchasing, expanding, or modernizing a business is $25,000; andThe minimum project budget for marketing and innovation is $10,000. Ineligible Projects:Community infrastructure projects that are unrelated to commercial enterprise;Purchase of land, buildings, and/or investment property; andBusiness activity related to pawn shops, payday loan firms, gaming operations, and/or the production/distribution of alcohol, tobacco, and sexually exploitative materials.Program Details:BEP contribution levels vary depending on the type of project the applicant submits. Higher contribution levels (60-75%) are available for business planning and market expansion activities. Capital projects (including equipment purchase, start-ups, and acquisition) typically qualify for a 25% non-repayable contribution through BEP, but may receive additional fundsthrough the  First Citizen's Fund or the NRT Equity Match grant; The First Citizen's Fund offers loans with a 40% forgiveness portion. All Indigenous entrepreneurs (Status, non-status, Métis, Inuit) can borrow a lifetime maximum of $75,000 from this fund. Applicants who have not already exhausted their First Citizen's Fund allowance can combine it with a BEP contribution;The New Relationship Trust (NRT) Equity Match Grant is offered in conjunction with TACC's other programs and is available to Indigenous entrepreneurs who are members of a BC First Nation, and who live in the TACC service area. The Equity Match Grant is a non-repayable contribution of up to $5000 that reduces the amount of cash equity the applicant has to provide to receive a BEP contribution.TACC will determine whether BEP applicants are eligible for a First Citizen's Fund loan and/or an Equity Match Grant;Combining all three programs significantly increases the non-repayable portion of the funding, but applicants who do not qualify for the additional programs can still receive a non-repayable contribution through BEP.There is one application form for all types of projects (business planning, market expansion, and capital). The  form requires the applicant's business information, a description of their project, a summary of their  business experience, an approximate budget, and the following supporting documents:Evidence of Aboriginal ancestry;Evidence of identity;Resume;Evidence of sufficient cash equity to undertake the project;Letters of commitment from other funders;Financial statements from the last three years (for projects related to existing businesses);Projected financial statements for the next three years;Copies of partnership agreements or incorporation documents;Business plan, if available; andAny additional information supporting the proposal (ie: market studies).Applications are reviewed within 10 business days, and are deemed eligible, ineligible, or sent back to the applicant with a request for more information;Eligible projects can proceed to the next stage in the application process, in which the applicant submits a detailed business plan;TACC provides a template for business plans, but can also issue funding to cover up to 75% of legal, accounting, and/or consulting fees related to the development of the plan;The business plan will be assessed within 30 business days; if approved, TACC will issue a Letter of Offer, outlining the amount and terms of the funding; Each funding agreement is unique, but typical contribution levels for various project costs are outlined in the table below; andProject financials and performance may be monitored for up to three years after the agreement is signed.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This funding can be combined with other provincial and/or federal funding programs;BEP will not fund project costs retroactively; applicants are advised not to commit any project costs before finalizing the funding agreement with TACC; andCredit rating is an important factor in the eligibility assessment; applicants are encouraged to seek a credit report before applying. Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guidelines: click hereApplication form: click here

        Recently Changed 
        Intake is now open until April 22, 2022;For this intake cycle, CMHC has launched a new Application Portal; andThe portal is easy to use and supports collaboration with consultants. The client (employer) must create the application, but once created, they can delegate it to a consultant through a simple email invite. 
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This federally funded program offers wage subsidies to help businesses and organizations create housing-related internships for Indigenous youth. Internships may be in housing administration, maintenance, construction, or tenant relations, and may range from 8 weeks to 2 years in duration. The goal of program is to provide Indigenous youth with much-needed work experience, and to create job opportunities for them in the housing sector. Grant Value: 6-12 month internships may receive subsidies of up to $15,000. The subsidy amount is negotiated for each internship.Turnaround time: 2 weeksEligible Employers:Indigenous governments and affiliated organizations (ie: band councils, tribal councils, self-governing entities);Indigenous non-profits;Indigenous-owned businesses; Non-Indigenous employers  (public, private, or non-profit) seeking to hire Indigenous youth; andEmployers must be in the housing sector. Eligible sub-sectors include, but are not limited to: Property management;Real estate;Housing research;Construction;MaintenanceRenovation;Eco-Fitting/Retro-fitting.Eligible Participants: Self-declared Indigenous youth between the ages of 15 and 30;Legally entitled to work in Canada;Must be unemployed at the time of hire;Must not be receiving Employment Insurance OR employed elsewhere while participating in HIIY;Must be a new hire;The youth is considered a "new" hire as long as they started within the last year. The start date of the subsidy will be negotiated on a case-by-case basis. Most subsidies will start after April 1, 2022, but employers who hired before this date may be eligible for retroactive funding;The youth should be hired as an employee, not a contractor;They can be identified before or after the application is submitted; andThe CMHC cannot "match" employers with Indigenous candidates, but they can connect employers with Indigenous organizations that host job boards and job fairs.Internship Details: Internships can range between 8 weeks and 2 years in length;Compensation must meet or exceed the provincial minimum wage;The position must be in the housing sector but may have any focus;For example, interns could be involved in housing administration, research, tenant relations, construction, renovation, design, or maintenance.Position may be full- or part-time, on-site or remote; andEmployers must provide the youth with any equipment, tools, and/or technology necessary for the fulfillment of their duties.Program DetailsTo be considered for funding, employers create a profile and an HIIY application through the CMHC online portal;Once the application is created, it can be "Assigned" to a consultant for completion; the employer simply enters the consultant's email address to send a Portal Invitation to them;The application, which must be completed by April 22, 2022,  outlines how many youth the employer would like to hire, what positions they would like to fill, and what they expect to pay the youth;CMHC will evaluate applications on a first-come, first-serve basis, and issue funding agreements to successful applicants;There is no cut-off date by which the employer must hire, but they should communicate with the CMHC about how the hiring process is going; Amendments may be made to the funding agreement. For example, if an employer applies to hire one youth, and ends up hiring two, they can receive additional funding;CMHC will disburse 25% of the funds soon after the hire is made, 50% of the funds at the midway point of the internship, and the remaining 25% at the end of the internship;The payment request form is simple, and there are no formal reporting requirements, but the youth may be approached for an interview about their work experience.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program cannot be combined with other federally or provincially funded programs;Requests for retroactive funding are sometimes approved. They are evaluated on a case-by-case basis;Applications are assessed on a first-come, first-serve basis; andIf an internship terminates prematurely for any reason, the employer can find another intern to fill the position.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication Guide: click hereApplication Portal: click here

Your profile must be verified before you can apply for grants. such as street dance battles, poetry slams, etc.Self-publishing or author-subsidized publishing of literary works (unless applying to a component of Creating, Knowing and Sharing: The Arts and Cultures of First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples);Activities carried out by organizations that have not paid, or do not pay, fees or royalties to artists according to the standards of the arts practice or sector.Eligible Expenses:Transportation costs;Accommodation per diem, up to 5 days per trip, at a maximum of $150 per day;Additional shipping or baggage costs directly related to the travel activity, up to a maximum of $2500;Registration fees, up to $1000.Note: Applicants cannot apply for activities that occur before the departure date or those that receive funding from another Canada Council program component.Program Details: Applicants can apply to this program twice per year, but the maximum amount they can receive for the year is $30,000;Applications are submitted through the Canada Council for the Arts online portal;The Travel application includes the following components:An overview of applicant's artistic/cultural practice; A description of the project and proposed travel activities; A budget;A list of events, partners, and/or host organizations, if applicable;A sample of past work;A letter of invitation from the event or host organization the applicant is traveling to;A letter of support from a senior professional or mentor (if the applicant is an aspiring artist).Applications are reviewed by an internal committee, and assessed for impact (60%), relevance (20%), and feasibility (20%);Successful applicants must sign a Grant Acceptance form to receive funds; andA final report is due 3 months after the completion of the activity.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Sectoral Workforce Solutions Program (SWSP) provides up to $50,000,000 to eligible applicants with projects that help key sectors of the economy to develop and implement solutions to address current and emerging workforce needs. Key sectors include agriculture/agri-food, construction, clean technology, ICT, manufacturing, natural resources, tourism/hospitality, transportation, and healthcare. The intent of the program is to help employers in critical sectors attract, retain and upskill their workforce.Grant Value: $5,000,000 - $50,000,000Note: projects that focus on Health Care Sector are exempt from this minimum funding level.Turnaround Time: Funding decisions to be announced in Summer 2022Eligible Applicants:Be 1 of the following organization types:Not-for-profit organization;For-profit organization;Indigenous organization, including:Band council;Tribal council;Self-government entities;Provincial or territorial government body such as an:Institution;Agency;Crown corporation.Municipal government.Have in-kind and/or cash contributions from sources other than the program funding equal to or more than 10% of your total project costs.Eligible Projects:Eligible projects must focus on 1 or more of the following priority areas:Building talent for the clean economy:Support workforce development needs in sectors directly or indirectly involved in the clean economy, inlcuding:Agriculture and agri-food;Clean technology;Construction (building retrofits/energy efficiency);Natural resources and environment; andTransportation.Supporting workforce development needs of workers and employers for hardest-hit sectors by COVID-19, including:Agriculture and agri-food;Construction;Information and communications technology;Manufacturing;Natural resources;Tourism and hospitality; andTransportation.Investing in the health care sector:To address challenges faced by in-demand health care occupations, for example:Skills and labour shortages;Labour mobility;Workforce mental health needs; andLabour market integration of internationally trained health care professionals.Target a minimum of 250 participants (for projects focused on the delivery of training or transition initiatives);Training and transition initiatives can take various forms of training (e.g. online or in-person), worker transition activities, upskilling, credential or certification programs, work-integrated learning or placements, job matching, recruitment, and other skills development activities;Activities could also include wage training subsidies;Projects that focus on the Health Care Sector will be exempt from this criterion.Target a minimum of 50 employers participating in and/or benefitting from the project.Particularly for projects whose focus is not on participants.Eligible Activities:Training and Reskilling, including:Development of curriculum/training tools;Online or in-person training delivery;Work-integrated learning.Solutions for Employers, including:Employer-focused initiatives, tools for recruitment, retention, or capacity building;Building employer networks, partnerships ,or consortiums;Employer strategies for sector-specific challenges.Sector-wide Standards and Tools, including:Forecasting analysis and response plans for labour market trends;Occupational standards and job matching tools;Skills recognition and certification systems;Educational or training materials.Creative Solutions, including:Innovative approaches to sector-specific issues;Promote the adoption of emerging technologies;Scaling up pilot projects for identified needs.Eligible Costs:Overhead costs;Materials and supplies;Wages and professional fees;Staff training and development;Printing and communication;Computer and library services;Digitization costs;Participants’ wage and training subsidies, completion bonuses, or other incentives;Selected capital expenditures such as a single or composite asset (e.g. computer) with a purchase value of more than $1,000; andWraparound supports to project participants, as needed.Ineligible Costs:Capital improvements, such as the construction or renovation of buildings;Consultant fees for individuals who are also receiving a salary from your organization or its partner;Contingency fees;Costs incurred to prepare for the proposal;Entertainment costs;Expenditures outside the start and end dates of the agreement;Fines or penalties;Lobbyist fees; andCosts not related to project activities.Program Details:Earliest project start date: Fall 2022;Latest project end date: March 31, 2024;The project scope should meet one of the following:Target a minimum of 250 participants * for projects focused on the delivery of training or transition initiatives;The Healthcare sector is exempt from this criterion.Target a minimum of 50 employers *participating in and/or benefitting from the project;The Healthcare sector is exempt from this criterion.Support large-scale, high-impact projects national or regional scope.Approved project activities must start within 2 months of project date;Eligible organizations may submit only 1 application for funding;Selected applicants will be asked to submit a letter confirming the cash, or in-kind contribution from a source other than the funding from this program;Assessment Criteria:Applicant capacity to understand proposed project activities;Geographical and sectoral representation;Knowledge of skills issues in a sector or across multiple sectors;The level of impact and the number of partnerships with national, provincial, and/or regional sectoral stakeholders;Involvement of equity-deserving groups in their sector(s);

grants.grant_criteria: This program provides funding to Northern Ontario employers to hire Indigenous interns who are new entrants to the workforce. Employers can receive 75% of the intern's salary (including MERCs), up to a maximum of $52,500. The intent of the program is to strengthen and develop Northern Ontario's workforce, and to provide training and career advancement opportunities to Indigenous people. As such, positions focused on retail and sales, low-skill manual labour, or low-skill clerical duties will not be considered for funding. The position must provide meaningful career development for the intern.
grants.best_practices: Eligible Best Practices:This program does not allow funding to be used in conjunction with other sources of government funding (ie. provincial and federal), including the Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy (CEWS);A fair and transparent selection process must be conducted by the organization for each position. Employers required to post a job advertisement in at least one public forum;NOHFC will require proof of the posting, including the opening and closing dates of the posting; andExceptions may be made for apprenticeship internships.If an internship candidate is hired prior to the applicant receiving funding approval and the funding application is declined for funding, the NOHFC bears no responsibility for any costs incurred by the applicant with respect to the intern;Funding for each project is determined by the NOHFC Board of Directors, and limited funding is available. Not all projects meeting the criteria will receive funding;Process Best Practices:Applications are assessed according to the follow criteria: Extent to which the position addresses a known labour shortage or supports the development of a skilled trade/profession in Northern Ontario;The potential for the position to result in a permanent, full-time job;The quality of the skill development opportunity, and the extent to which it provides specific, recognizable transferable skills; andThe quality of the training plan and proposed onsite supervision. Forms:Program website: click here

The intent of the program is to strengthen and develop Northern Ontario's workforce, and to provide training and career advancement opportunities to Indigenous people. The position must provide meaningful career development for the intern.  Grant Value:90% to a maximum of $35,000 for municipalities, Indigenous communities, and not-for-profit organizations;75% to a maximum of $52,500 for private businesses.Turnaround time: 8 weeksEligible Employers:Be either a business, municipality, indigenous community or not-for-profit organization;Located in Northern Ontario;In operation of at least 1 year;Have a minimum of 1 full-time employee;Have commercial general liability insurance with a minimum of $2 million per occurrence:For third-party bodily injury, personal injury, and property damage;Must include:Northern Ontario Heritage Fund Corporation and each of its directors, officers, agents, advisors, and representatives as additional insureds with respect to liability arising in the course of performance of the recipient’s obligations under, or otherwise in connection with, the legal agreement;cross-liability clause;contractual liability coverage; and30 days written notice of cancellation or material change.Be able to provide direct supervision to the intern.Eligible Candidates:Self-declared Indigenous person residing in Northern Ontario;A new entrant to the workforce;Legally entitled to work in Canada;Has not previously participated in a Northern Ontario Heritage Fund Corporation (NOHFC) funded internship;At least 18 years of age;Hired after application submission; andMust not be immediate family members or relatives of owners and directors.Exceptions may be made in smaller, Northern communities with a limited labour base.Eligible Expenses:Intern salary; andMandatory employment-related costs (Canada Pension Plan, Employment Insurance, and mandatory minimum vacation pay)Ineligible Expenses:Discretionary benefits paid by the employer (i.e. sick pay, group medical or dental plans);Training expenses;Computers and equipment; andTravel and accommodations expenses.Program Details:Internship must be full-time (minimum 35 hours per week); Maximum duration: 52 weeks;An extended placement period of up to 18 months will be considered for apprenticeship internships to accommodate any necessary off-site training and/or educational requirements; andA 2-year internship if the intern is required to complete a minimum number of hours of professional experience (greater than 52 weeks of full-time employment) for a certification, designation, or registered apprenticeship.A separate application for second-year funding is required.Positions must be in Northern Ontario;Remote work is eligible if the participant and the positions are both in Northern Ontario.The intern must not displace an existing employee;Internships must provide meaningful skill development to the intern; positions involving low-skill manual labour, low-skill clerical work, or retail/sales are not eligible for funding;Applicants are responsible for recruiting candidates; andEligible organizations may apply to host 2 interns.Colleges, universities, and research institutions may be eligible for up to up to 5 research positions, in addition to 2 regular internship positions.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program does not allow funding to be used in conjunction with other sources of government funding (ie. provincial and federal), including the Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy (CEWS);A fair and transparent selection process must be conducted by the organization for each position. Employers required to post a job advertisement in at least one public forum;NOHFC will require proof of the posting, including the opening and closing dates of the posting; andExceptions may be made for apprenticeship internships.If an internship candidate is hired prior to the applicant receiving funding approval and the funding application is declined for funding, the NOHFC bears no responsibility for any costs incurred by the applicant with respect to the intern;Funding for each project is determined by the NOHFC Board of Directors, and limited funding is available.
