      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program aims to promote entrepreneurship in Indigenous communities and increase the number of viable businesses owned by Indigenous people through non-repayable grants of up to $99,999, issued through designated Aboriginal Financial Institutions (AFIs) located across the country. Program details are determined by the AFIs, and may vary from location to location, but in general, the funds may be used to support proposals for starting, acquiring, or expanding a business, and to leverage other sources of funding. Consult your local AFI for application instructions (see "Forms" for directory link).Grant Value: Up to $99,999 for Individual Indigenous entrepreneurs; andUp to $250,000 for eligible Indigenous community businesses.Turnaround Time: 2-8 weeksEligible Applicants:Indigenous individuals;Businesses owned and controlled by Indigenous people;Indigenous and non-indigenous organizations and associations (except those with a religious or charitable purpose); First Nations and Inuit communities and governments;Canadian owned and controlled banks, credit unions, and trust companies;Private equity providers;Provincial and federal crown corporations; andMunicipal governments, labour organizations, and post-secondary institutions. Note: Eligibility criteria may vary between AFIs. Many AFIs only serve Indigenous individuals, businesses, and organizations in their local area.Eligible Projects:Projects may involve starting, purchasing, expanding, or modernizing a business, and must create measurable benefits, including but not limited to additional revenue, new markets, and/or new job opportunities;Examples of eligible activities include: Advertising campaigns, trade shows, seminars, and conferences; Research; Process and product development; Productivity improvement; and Investment in new technology and/or systems.Ineligible Projects:Community infrastructure projects that are unrelated to commercial enterprise;Purchase of land, buildings, and/or investment property; andBusiness activity related to pawn shops, payday loan firms, gaming operations, and/or the production/distribution of alcohol, tobacco, and sexually exploitative materials.Note: Be sure to consult your local AFI for a more detailed list of eligibility criteria.Program Details: Application requirements vary slightly between AFIs. In most cases, the first step is to submit an application form and business plan;Financial support for the creation of the business plan is available from most AFIs;Applicants must provide proof of their ability to cover at least some of the project costs (usually 10% of the total);Project financials and performance may be monitored for up to three years after the funding agreement is issued; andTo proceed with an application, consult the AFI directory to find an Aboriginal Financial Institution near you. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices:This program can be combined with funding from provincial sources;Because application processes vary between institutions, it is essential to find an AFI near you, and review the instructions for their version of the program;Indigenous business owners in BC can access this funding through the Business Equity Program at Tale’awtxw Aboriginal Capital Corporation.Eligible Best Practices: Most AFIs do not allow the funding to be used retroactively.Forms:Program website: click hereDirectory of Aboriginal Financial Institutions: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This competitive program provides grants of up to $6,000,000 in non-dilutive funding to support the development and scale-up of innovative products and processes that accelerates the reduction in greenhouse gases (GHGs). Eligible projects include technologies and business processes that are at a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) between 4-9, ranging from early stage of prototype development to an early commercialization.  Projects should fall in one of five focus areas: 1) carbon management ; 2) low-carbon hydrogen; 3) bio-energy/bio-fuels/synthetic fuels; 4) renewable natural gas; and/or 5) battery and energy storage. The primary objectives of the program are to advance projects that reduce GHG emissions, and to support BC-based innovators.Grant Value: up to $6,000,000 in non-dilutive funding.Turnaround time: Expressions of Interest are due February 10, 2023. The final stage of the application process will conclude on June 1, 2023. Eligible Applicants:Private companies, organizations, and consortia of companies based in BC;Companies must demonstrate their ability to complete the project with sound management, operational capability, and financial management; andProposals from non-incorporated entities may be considered, but in such cases additional evidence of managerial, operational, and financial capability will be required. Eligible Projects:Projects may be technologies or business processes in any of the following focus areas:Carbon management;Low-carbon hydrogen;Bio-energy/bio-fuels/synthetic fuels;Renewable natural gas; and/orBattery and energy storage.The proposed technologies/processes should be at a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 4-9;Project activities can include, but are not limited to:Demonstrations;Implementation of plans to scale technology production;Linkage of system components to create a complete solution;Development of quality and/or safety standards; andCreation of business linkages.Eligible Expenses:Wages and salaries;Consultant fees;Direct costs associated with project management;Securing of demonstration sites;Integration of system components;Pilot production; andScale-up of manufacturing.Ineligible Expenses:Enhancing normal business/operational capabilities;Purchasing capital equipment;Capital or leasehold improvements;Purchase of furniture or office equipment;Advertising or business promotion; andOverhead.Program Details: Applications proceed through a multi-stage elimination process;Stage 1 is an Expression of Interest, due February 10, 2023;Applicants complete a webform and upload a 5-minute video that introduces their project, explains its GHG emission reduction potential, and demonstrates its scalability and commercial viability;Stage 1 applications will be evaluated by CICE.  By February 24, 2023, a limited number will be invited to sign a non-disclosure agreement, and proceed to Stage 2;Stage 2 is the Detailed Proposal Submission and Review, due April 7, 2023;Applicants will work with the CICE project review team to ensure adequate technical assessments are made;A template for the proposal will be provided;Stage 2 applications will be ranked competitively. By May 12, 2023, a limited number will proceed to Stage 3;Stage 3 is the Funding Decision;Applicants will negotiate a contribution agreement with CICE by June 1, 2023, identifying obligations of all parties. The contribution agreement will include key milestones for the project;Grant funding will be paid in increments upon completion of project milestones; CICE reserves the right to reject all proposals in any competition cycle; andThe total program funding is $6,000,000, although there is no limit on how much an applicant can apply for the program wants to fund several projects therefore an applicant will not receive the full $6,000,000.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program funds large-scale projects that bring Indigenous organizations and industry employers together to create training opportunities for Indigenous people in high-demand sectors. Projects of 1-5 years are eligible for $10,000,000 per year in funding, up to a maximum of $50,000,000. Applications must be led by Indigenous businesses or organizations, and must demonstrate an ability to cover at least 25% of the total cost of the project. Projects that increase Indigenous representation in the Green Economy, Information and Communications Technology sector, Infrastructure sector, the Ocean Economy, and the Indigenous Public Sector will be prioritized. The goals of the program are to improve employment outcomes for Indigenous people by providing training in high-demand sectors, and by building respectful, inclusive workplaces in those sectors. Grant Value: $10,000,000 per year, up to a maximum of $50,000,000 for 5 year projects.Turnaround time: Results to be announced in Fall 2022Eligible Applicants: Indigenous-led organizations in Canada, including:Incorporated for-profit Indigenous controlled organizations;Incorporated not-for-profit Indigenous controlled organizations;Indigenous-controlled unincorporated organizations;Indian Act bands;Band or tribal councils; andIndigenous self-government entities. Note: "Indigenous-led" means that self-identified Indigenous people hold at least 51% of leadership positions in the organization. Eligible Projects:Projects must provide training to support the entry of Indigenous people into employment in high-demand sectors, and may include any of the following components:Job-specific education or training;Skills training and apprenticeships (ie: Red Seal certification);Job retention counseling;Job supports (ie: childcare for parents participating in labour market programming);Targeted programming (ie: programming for youth, women, or persons with disabilities);Cultural competency training for employers; andCreation of new cultural competency and/or sustainability roles (ie: Sustainability Officer).Project is no more than 60 months in duration, ending on or before March 31, 2028;Funding request does not exceed $10,000,000 per year, or $50,000,000 for the entire project;Project partners contribute a minimum of 25% of the total project cost (cash or in-kind);Project includes measures to ensure any employer partners create respectful, inclusive workplaces for Indigenous employees;Project has a sustainability plan to continue after the conclusion of program funding; ORThere is a clear plan to end the project once program funding is exhausted.Eligible Expenses:Administration and overhead costs, including:Wages and benefits;Office rent and utilities; andCosts related to the development of a sustainability plan.Office equipment and technology directly related to the project;Cost of training programs for clients;Income support for clients (ie: allowances, wage subsidies, accommodation, and transportation); andProfessional fees for services provided to support Indigenous individuals and families (including services provided by Indigenous elders and traditional healers). Note: Administrative costs cannot exceed 15% of the total funder contribution. Ineligible Expenses:Capital improvements, such as the construction or renovation of buildings; andAdministrative costs not directly related to the project. Program Details:SPF proposals are evaluated in 2 stages: first, they are screened for eligibility. Then, they are assessed for feasibility and impact;Proposals may be submitted by mail, email, or web portal, using the Grants and Online Services (GCOS) system;If using GCOS, create your account well in advance of the program deadline, as it can take up to 2 weeks to verify a new GCOS account;Complete applications include the following components:Application form;Budget Detail Template (BDT);Commitment letters from all project partners;One of the following: CRA business number; OR CRA registration number; ORProof of incorporation or registration.Applications that pass the screening stage will be subject to a competitive evaluation process, in which the following factors are considered:Organizational capacity;Alignment with program goals;Potential impact;Projects intended to serve more than 25 clients will be favoured;Clarity and feasibility of the project plan and budget;Sustainability (long-term effects of the project after funding concludes);Strength of partnerships and partner contributions; andAlignment with target sectors (Green Economy, ICT, Infrastructure, Ocean Economy, Indigenous Public Sector).Funding decisions will be announced in Fall, 2022;Successful applicants must establish a data collection system, and create a reporting plan to share data with the government; andA final report is required at the end of the project. Applicants may include professional evaluation services in the budget for this purpose. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:SPF can be combined with other provincial and federal sources of funding;The program is not designed to fund projects retroactively. Project activities cannot begin until November 2022, after funding agreements have been reached; Employment and Social Develop Canada (ESDC) may contact applicants for additional information during the screening stage. Applicants who do not respond to these requests within 5 business days will be eliminated from the funding competition;Recipients of SPF funding must award all contracts worth over $25,000 through a competitive process;ESDC reserves the right to provide funding at less than the requested amount; andProjects whose partners can contribute more than 10% of the total project cost in cash will score more points in the evaluation process. Forms:Program website: click hereApplication guide: click hereApplication form: click hereBudget detail template: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Canada Digital Adoption: Boost Your Business Technology program offers funding of 90% of eligible costs to a maximum of $15,000 as well as 0% interested loans of up to $100,000  to for-profit small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs). The objective of the program is to develop and implement a digital adoption plan tailored to their needs with the help of Digital Advisory service providers. The goal is to help Canadian SMEs boost productivity, access new markets to remain competitive in the market.Grant Value:Non-repayable funding - 90% of eligible costs to a maximum of $15,000Inclusive of a wage subsidy - up to 100% to a maximum of $7,300 to hire talentLoan - 0% interest up to a maximum of $100,000 with a 5-year term + 12 months capital postponement (total of 6 years)Turnaround Time:  Eligibility Confirmation 5-10 business daysEligible Applicants:Must be a Canadian-controlled and Canadian-owned for-profit business;Be a sole proprietor or an incorporated business;Has between $500,000 and $100,000,000 annual revenue in 1 of the previous 3 fiscal years from the date of submission;Have between 1-499 full-time equivalent employees (FTE); andFull-time employees are those who receive a T4 Statement of Remuneration Paid slip  from the applicant and work at least 30 hours/week of paid labour; andPart-time employees must be included as fractions of 1 FTE based on average labour hours compared to typical hours for 1 FTE employee.Is a business that respects human rights codes, labour, environment, and anti-corruption standards, as well as engages exclusively in legal activities.0% loan eligibility (optional portion):For loan requests made under CDAP, applicants must meet CDAP eligibility criteria and BDC creditworthiness requirements to receive a loan offer.Businesses with between $500,000 and below $5M annual revenue can request a loan of between $25,000 and $50,000;Businesses with $5M and more can request a loan between $25,000 and $100,000;Applicants apply without a Digital Advisor. Note: Only an owner or a director listed in the articles of incorporation can apply.Ineligible Applicants:Businesses that have a class of shares publicly traded on a stock exchange domestically or internationally;Majority or wholly-owned subsidiaries or branches or sales offices of a multinational corporations (MNC);Businesses whose revenue model is designed to be economically dependent on non-commercial sources such as direct government funding or private donations;Government organizations or entities with government-owned equity interests;Entities in which equity interests are held by any current member of the Parliament of Canada or any current member of the Senate of Canada;Not-for-profit entities - unions, charitable, religious, or fraternal organizations;Businesses that promote violence, incite hatred, or discriminates on the basis of race, national or ethnic origin, color, religion, sex, age or mental or physical disability nor does it trade with countries proscribed by the government of Canada; andBusinesses that have pled guilty to or been convicted of tax evasion or a criminal offense.Note: If the program determines that the applicant does not continue to meet the eligibility criteria, the program reserves the right to terminate any Grant Agreement, and recipients are responsible for paying all costs incurred to that point and in the future.Eligible Expenses:Fees, commissions, and charges by organizations providing Digital Advisory services;Applicable federal and/or provincial sales taxes applied to the fees and commissions charged by the Digital Advisors listed on the Digital Advisor Marketplace.Only expenses charged for the purpose of producing a Digital Adoption Plan for the funding recipient.Application Process:Non-Repayable Grant Application Process:Create or sign in to the portal with GCKey or Sign-In Partner;Verify the applicant's identity; Eligibility Confirmation 5-10 business days;Eligible applicants will have up to 6 months to accept the terms of the CDAP grant;If not accepted within 6 months, a new eligibility validation will be required.Upon accepting the terms of the Grant Agreement, the applicant will have access to the Digital Advisor Marketplace system;The system contains information on registered Digital Advisory service providers. Applicants must be or be partnered with Black-led, Black-focused organizations, and must be able to deliver programming in one of the BYAP target areas (Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area, Ottawa, Windsor).       Grant Criteria 
      This program funds 1-2 year initiatives that support the economic prospects of Black children and youth in Ontario through training, mentorship, and work experience opportunities. Initiatives should be sector-specific and tailored to the needs of the local population. Applicants must be or be partnered with Black-led, Black-focused organizations, and must be able to deliver programming in one of the BYAP target areas (Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area, Ottawa, Windsor). The goals of the program are to increase the skills, competencies, and credentials of Black Ontarians, cultivate Black networks, and build pathways to high-opportunity careers.Grant value: up to $463,800 (max. $231,900 per fiscal year)Turnaround time: 4-6 weeksEligible Applicants:Based in Ontario; andLegal entities that are Black-led and/or Black-focused, including:Non-profit organizations;For-profit organizations;Boards;Associations;First Nations bands;Municipalities; andPost-secondary institutions;Employers can apply with or without candidates.Note: Organizations that are not Black-led may still apply if they form a partnership or coalition with one or more Black-led organization(s). Eligible Projects:Projects may be centered on a new initiative, or may entail the enhancement or expansion an existing initiative;Must be 1-2 years in duration, and must provide training, mentoring, and/or work experiences to Black youth in one of the following target areas:Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area;Ottawa; and/orWindsor.Must contribute to at least one of the following target outcomes:Increased wellness and resilience for Black youth; Academic support and/or career preparation that will support the success of Black Ontarians in high-opportunity fields; andConnecting Black youth to caring adults in professionally relevant networks.Note: All applicants must demonstrate their capacity to offer services in French. At minimum, applicants will have a formal referral agreement in place to redirect French-speaking participants to a French language service provider, OR a French Language Services quality improvement plan outlining a 3-year strategy for improvement. Eligible Expenses:Must be budget items directly related to the provision of the Career Launch initiative, such as:Salaries, wages, and benefits;Start-up costs;Participant/client remuneration;Supplies, materials, and equipment;Web-based platforms(s);Building accommodation;Travel;Staff recruitment and training; andAllocated central administration (up to 10% of total budget).Ineligible Expenses:Expenses not directly related to the Career Launch initiative;Capital expenditures; andLand or building acquisition.Program Details: To apply for BYAP funding, organizations must be registered on Transfer Payment Ontario (TPON);If you do not have a TPON account, you must create one in order to apply. Allow up to 5 business days for validation of your new account;The application form includes the following components: Organization information (including payment information);Applicant contact information;Organization capacity;List of partner organizations;Overview of proposed initiative;Work plan for proposed initiative;Budget;Performance measurement scheme;List of organizations providing Letters of Support;Agreement to Terms and Conditions;Applicant declaration/signature.In addition to the form, applicants must include the following attachments: Proof of legal entity status (ie: certificate of incorporation, certificate of registration, etc.);Logic Model for the initiative (template provided);At least two Letters of Support;The letters must identify 1) your organization's connection to or knowledge of the target sector/industry/career trajectory named in the application, and 2) your organization's capacity to contribute to positive outcomes for Black children, youth, and/or young adults;If you are applying as a partnership or coalition, at least one of the letters must be from a partner or coalition member.Successful applicants will enter a funding agreement with the Ministry, and will be subject to monitoring and performance measurement; Funded organizations will be expected to report on the outcomes of their initiative using standardized measures outlined in the funding agreement;See Ontario's Anti-Racism Data Standards for guidelines on data collection, management, and use.Decisions about which initiatives to fund, and how much funding to provide, are at the sole and absolute discretion of the Ministry. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program can be combined with other federal and provincial sources of funding;This program is not designed to fund activities retroactively. Projects should begin in Spring/Summer 2022;You must be able to describe your initiative in terms of the Logic Model provided by the ministry:Inputs: resources invested in the initiative, such as staff, volunteers, time, money, technology, and/or partnerships;Activities: what is done as a result of that investment (ie: workshops, training sessions, internships, industry events);Outputs: number of participants reached, and products/services produced as a result of the activities;Outcomes: changes that occur as a result of the activities (ie: youth develop industry skills, increased opportunities for Black Ontarians in high-opportunity fields, etc.). Forms: Program website: click hereProgram guidelines: click hereOntario's Anti-Racism Data Standards: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers funding to Nova Scotia tourism accommodation providers for the purposes of marketing activities that will build demand in 2022. The goal of the program is to help the tourism sector recover from the effects of the pandemic. The amount of funding scales to the size of the business: operators that have  between one and five rooms available for booking by tourists can receive a one-time grant of $5000. Operators with more than five bookable rooms can receive a one-time grant of $1000 per room for the first 10 rooms, and $500 per room for each room after that. Businesses that already received funding through the Tourism Accommodations Restart Customer Attraction Program (TARCAP) will be fast-tracked for TMAP funding. Grant Value: $5000+ Turnaround time: 3 weeksEligible Applicants:Business must be a roofed accommodation, defined in the Tourism Accommodations Registration Act as follows:A building, part of a building, group of buildings, or place of accommodation that includes one or more residential units used mainly for the reception of the travelling or vacationing public; and/orA cottage or cabin.Business operator must be registered as a host under the Tourism Accommodations Registration Act;Business must be HST registered; If your business is not required to collect/remit GST/HST, or opened in 2020, 2021, or 2021 under normal conditions, you must generate at least $30,000 in annual business revenues;Must have at least one room available for booking by tourists; andMust be operating in 2022.Eligible Activities: Advertising;Package development and promotion; andInvestment in products/processes that will enhance the visitor experience.Note: Funding may not be used to provide direct discounts to customers. Program Details:Applications can be submitted by webform on the Tourism Nova Scotia website (see "Forms" below);Businesses that received funding through TARCAP do not have to submit a TMAP application unless their business information has changed; Tourism Nova Scotia will contact TARCAP recipients to confirm eligibility, then fast-track them or TMAP funding;The deadline for applications is 4 PM (AST) on Friday, March 18, 2022;Payment cheques will be sent to eligible applicants by mail.

      Grant Criteria 
      The  Short-Term Compensation Fund for Canadian Audiovisual Productions (STCF) provides up to $1.5M or 20% of the total production budget to audiovisual productions that experience an interruption or abandonment due to COVID-19. Eligible applicants must be a Canadian corporation eligible for the Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit and must not benefit from any coverage for interruptions or abandonment of filming caused by COVID-19 under any other compensation program or insurance policy. The intent minimize the impacts of the pandemic on the film industry.Grant Value: The lesser of either $1,500,000 or 20% of the total production budgetTurnaround Time: Telefilm is not subject to any time limit for processing applications,  so its response times may vary depending on the volume and complexity of the applications submittedEligible Applicants:Be a Canadian corporation eligible for the Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC);Have and apply a COVID-19 safety plan in accordance with the current applicable sanitary requirements; andHold all the copyrights in the project necessary for its development, production, and exploitation,  as well as the control of the project.For co-production, the applicant must hold these rights and control the project in proportion to its participation in it.Eligible Projects:At the time of pre-eligibility:Be an audiovisual production eligible for the Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC);Be covered  by insurance  currently  in  effect  provided  by  an  insurance  company  specialized  in  audiovisual production (comprehensive producers insurance and general liability insurance) containing an exclusion relating to COVID-19 with respect to the project subject to the application;Not benefit from any coverage for interruptions or abandonment of filming caused by COVID-19 under any other compensation program or insurance policy;Have a fully confirmed financial structure; andHave a scheduled period of filming which is planned to last more than a single day.At the time of compensation request:The project must have been the subject of a pre-eligibility agreement under the STCF between the applicant and Telefilm prior to the occurrence of any Incident;Principal photography of the project in Canada must have been interrupted by more than one day or abandoned by the applicant due to the occurrence of an Incident. The Incident must not have been the result of an omission, fault, or negligence on the part of the applicant;Project filming must have been interrupted or abandoned prior to the Fund Expiry Date;The  COVID-19 safety plan and all of the sanitary requirements applicable at the time of filming have been systematically complied with throughout the filming; andA minimum of 15% of the production budget or, in the case of audiovisual coproductions governed by treaties, 15% of the Canadian production budget, must have been incurred and contractually payable at the time of the interruption or abandonment.Eligible Expenses:Reasonable Canadian production costs incurred and contractually payable directly caused by an interruption of more than one day in filming or the producer’s abandonment of the production that occurs after the execution of a pre-eligibility agreement with Telefilm.Ineligible Expenses:Non-Canadian costs;Costs incurred outside of Canada;Expenses related to any interruption in filming resulting directly or indirectly from an event other than those referred to in subsection 5.1 above;Expenses caused by interruptions related to the tightening of the sanitary protocols by the national, provincial, or local sanitary authorities and the confinement orders/decrees;Revenue losses;Expenses otherwise covered by private insurers or other compensation programs;Producers’ fees and administrative expenses;Costs relating to an interruption or abandonment which occurred outside of Canada;Costs relating to an interruption or abandonment occurring outside the coverage period indicated in the pre-eligibility agreement under the STCF between the applicant and Telefilm; andExpenses not directly related to productionProgram Details:Only 1 application for pre-eligibility will be processed per project;Applicants must notify Telefilm in writing no later than 24 hours after an interruption in the filming of more than one day due to the occurrence of an Incident;Any claim under the STCF must be submitted within 30 days following the resumption of filming, and in all events, no more than 15 days after the Fund Expiry Date, or be subject to the refusal or non-availability of funds.

Applications are due May 9, 2022, with results to be announced in June.   Grant value: up to $1,000,000Turnaround time: Results to be announced in June, 2022Eligible Applicants:Alberta oil and gas facilities that have a facility code with an Operational Status of Active (Petrinex or equivalent);Facility must be must be owned, operated, or leased by the applicant;Must have been in operation for at least 1 year; and To the applicant's knowledge, the facility will continue to operate for the lifetime of the energy saving measures.Eligible Projects:Installation of specific energy saving measures deemed eligible in the SPEED  program guidelines. There are 60 eligible measures in total, arranged in the following categories: Air fuel ration controllers;High-efficiency engines;Pump jack electrification;Lighting controls;Onsite generation;Geothermal;HVAC;Process heating;Water heating;Food service;Motors and drives;Compressed air;Refrigeration;Lighting systems;Building envelope and windows;Agricultural lighting; andSolar air heating.The total value of incentives must be greater than $10,000; For most measures, incentives cover 50% of eligible costs, meaning that project budgets will need to exceed $20,000 to be eligible for the program;Lighting projects are subsidized at a lower rate of 25%;The proposed measures must be new to the facility and not previously subsidized under the Energy Savings for Business Program;No aspect of the proposed measures should be classifiable as routine maintenance;The participant must obtain all permits, licenses, approvals, and authorizations required by law to instal the measure;The measure must be installed after the program launch date of March 8, 2022, and must be identified in the SPEED proposal; andThe project must be completed by March 31, 2023. Note: see Eligible Measures List for technical requirements specific to each measure. Eligible Expenses:The expense must be directly related to the purchase and installation of the proposed measures;It must be incurred after the program launch date (March 8, 2022), and before the project deadline set out in the funding agreement;If the applicant undertakes installation internally, only equipment expenses will be considered eligible, and these must be equal to or less than fair market value, as determined by Emissions Reduction Alberta;If measure installation is contracted to a third party, the following expenses are eligible: Energy modelling costs;Engineering (structural, electrical, civil, geotechnical) costs;Cost to obtain permits;Cost to obtain inspections;Procurement and construction;Equipment purchase;Installation of equipment;Disposal/decommissioning of replaced equipment;Labour costs; andCost of interconnecting with electrical and/or natural gas distribution system.Ineligible Expenses:Any costs not directly related to the purchase or installation of the proposed measures;Costs to prepare or modify the facility in advance of measure installation;Aesthetic improvements;Costs related to upkeep or maintenance of equipment;Costs that are already being subsidized through other funds, subsidies, grants, etc.;GST and PST;Warranties and/or insurance;Battery or storage equipment and installation;Overhead and administrative costs;Costs to complete SPEED applications and/or documents; andTaxes that result from participation in SPEED.Program Details: The first step in the application process is to create a profile in the SPEED portal. Register your company as a participant, and select your primary vendor or engineering firm as a contractor; If your preferred contractor is not already registered in the SPEED portal, they will need to register;You only need to identify one contractor in the application. Sub-contractors do not need to be included; andApplicants wishing to complete the project internally can create a contractor profile in addition to a participant profile, and assign the project to themselves in the application. After receiving registration confirmation, continue the application by selecting the technologies relevant to your project;For complicated applications involving multiple measures, applicants are advised to consult with the Emissions Reduction Alberta Applications Assist team;Once the application is complete, the participant submits it for pre-approval; Proposals will undergo a competitive evaluation process, with fundings decisions to be issued in June 2022;Approved projects must go ahead as planned;The only way to make changes to the project after pre-approval is to submit a formal Change Request; andIf the Change Request is approved, the new incentive cannot exceed 105% of the amount originally claimed in the proposal.  After accepting the funding agreement, successful applicants will have 10 months to complete their project;Payments will be disbursed after projects are complete, and post-project documentation has been submitted to and approved by Emissions Reduction Alberta; andSite visits may be conducted in some cases. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program cannot be combined with subsidies, incentives, or grants from the TIER regulation, the repealed Climate Leadership Act, or the Pan-Canadian framework programs.Incentives only apply to costs incurred after the program launch date of March 8, 2022, and cannot be applied retroactively to measures implemented before that date; andApplications will be assessed according to the following criteria:Abatement cost, or total eligible incentive divided by tonnes of CO2 reduced over the lifetime of the measure (60 points);Feasibility and soundness of the Work Plan (25 points);Region diversity (5 points);Measure diversity (5 points);Ability of the project to leverage economic benefits and create jobs (5 points). Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click hereApplication guide: click hereEligible Measures List: click here

        March 12, 2025Program is now accepting applications for the 2025/2026 fiscal year for training that begins on or after April 1, 2025.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The B.C. Employer Training Grant provides funding of 80% of eligible costs to a maximum of $10,000 per employee to employers who support skills training for their new or current employees. Training can be taken at a public post-secondary institution or through a private training provider (additional course syllabus requirements apply), so long as training is in compliance with PTIB (see pages 15/16 of the PTIB Policy Manual here).  The intent of the program is to help British Columbians access the skills training required to adapt to the labour market’s changing job requirements, while also addressing the skills gap in the province.Grant Value: 80% of eligible training costs up to $10,000 per traineeTurnaround Time: Up to 40 business daysEligible Applicants:Be operating in B.C. for at least 1 year;Have a Business BCeID; andBe in good standing with the Province of B.C.Eligible TraineesCanadian citizens, permanent residents, or protected persons;Be either unemployed or employed by the applicant employer;Be at least 16 years at the time of application;Have no real or perceived conflict of interest with the employer.To ensure an application is not denied due to conflict of interest, employers wishing to train family members must email etg@gov.bc.ca with a clear justification for their choice of the participant following the submission of their application.Trainees could be from outside BC, so long as the employer is BC-based, is paying for the training and will continue to employ people who live in BCIneligible TraineesIndividuals employed by a company other than the employer at the time of application;Temporary foreign workers, international students, working holiday visas, or other temporary residents; andParticipants who are receiving Employment Insurance (EI) or Income Assistance (IA) without prior approval from the Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction.EI or IA recipients are advised to seek approval from the Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction prior to training.Eligible TrainingMust be relevant to the immediate needs of the business and the trainee's job;Must lead to a "better job", leading to one of the following results:Increased pay;Promotion or advancement to another position;Move from part-time to full-time employment; ORMove from temporary/casual/seasonal employment to permanent employment.Training with a start date on or after the date of application submission;Training duration must be 52 weeks in duration or less.Ineligible TrainingTraining toward diploma or degree programs;Training needed to maintain current skills/certification;Training that has already been funded for the same participant;Training that is simultaneously funded for the participant by another federal or provincial program;Ineligible training methods:Consulting;Coaching;Coaching may be permitted as part of training toward coaching certification or when coaching is needed to complement a broader skills training program.Mentorships;Trade shows;Annual meetings;Networking;Seminars;Conferences; andPaid practicums.Eligible Training Providers:Be a B.C.-based training provider;Exceptions may be considered in exceptional circumstances.Be arm's length from the employer with no real or perceived conflict of interest;Training providers must deliver training as the main business activity;Includes but not limited to the following types of training providers:B.C. public post-secondary institutions;Trade or technical schools designated by the Industry Training Authority (ITA);Private training institutions certified and designated by the Private Training Institutions Branch (PTIB);Exceptions may apply if the Ministry deems the provider is a qualified instructor and training is competitively priced.Training organizations run by a B.C. school district;Industry associations.Indigenous Elders.Only when the trainee is Indigenous; andThe request for Elder support will be assessed on a case-by-case basis. The application should identify the Elder(s) providing the supports, the associated costs, and a description of the Elder supports.Training providers must be in compliance with Private Training Institutions Branch (PTIB) (see pages 15/16 of the PTIB Policy Manual here);Examples of programs that DO NOT require approval include:A career-related program at a registered institution for which tuition is less than $4,000;  A career-related program at a designated institution for which tuition is less than $1,000; A language program at a designated institution that is no more than six months and lessthan $4,000;Any language program at a registered institution; andA commercial driving instruction program. Programs that DO require approval fall into three categories and include: Class A: Career-related programs with 40 or more hours of instruction, for which tuition is at least $4,000. A career-related program is defined as a program that has the purpose of enhancing students’ employability or ability to carry out a career occupation;Class B: Career-related programs at designated/interim designated institutions, other than Class A programs, for which tuition is at least $1,000; andClass C: Language programs at designated/interim designated institutions that are longer than six months or for which tuition is at least $4,000. A language program is defined as a program that has as its learning objective that students gain or improve proficiency in a language.Eligible ExpensesTuition feesMandatory student feesExamination feesTextbooks, software and other required materialsTravel costs, only under certain circumstances (please see Appendix C for more information)Mandatory unpaid practicums for occupational certificationsIneligible ExpensesMembership fees, subscription fees, annual fees, professional association duesSoftware purchase/license for the businessLaptops, tablets, and other hardwareEquipment (e.g. boots and tools)Participant wages while in trainingProgram Details:Maximum funding per fiscal year (April 1 - March 31): $300,000 per employer;Applications that are not assessed after 60 calendar days will be returned unassessed;Applicants must submit and appeal within 15 days of having an application denied;Applicants can have paid for training prior to applying however cannot have started training prior to applying;Each course must be applied for in a separate application;If separate payments are required for individual courses, the applicant will need to submit separate applications for each course.Employers must pay all costs in full before reimbursement claims can be made;Training should be of no cost to the trainees. If the trainee pays for any training-related expenses.Employers cannot submit Participant Information Form (PIFs) on behalf of participants;Employers must submit an “Employer Completion Report” once all participants have completed or ceased training;Once training is completed, employers must intend to hire or continue to employ participants in B.C.;Employers and participants may be contacted during or after their participation in the program to ensure that training is contributing to the objectives and expected outcomes of the program.Employers who do not submit a Completion Report may become ineligible for future funding.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program allows applicants to use other sources of grant funding to cover the training costs not reimbursed by the program (i.e. this stream covers 80% of expenses, applicants can receive funding from other sources for the remaining 20%);This program does not allow funding to be used retroactively for training that has already taken place;Priority is given to first-time applicants, small businesses, and applicants from regions and industries experiencing the greatest challenges acquiring skilled workers;Employers are expected to select training that is competitively priced;Process Best Practices:Applicants can have paid for training prior to applying however cannot have started training prior to applying;The program asks for additional information including a business case, course outlines, and/or job descriptions to determine eligibility and value for money. Applicants should be prepared to provide additional information supporting their case;Any applications with providers outside of BC needs to be justified with comparisons with at least 1 local provider;If training is not designated by PTIB, the applicant should provide the following information to the Ministry:Instructor’s resume or curriculum vitae (CV);Capacity (number of participants);Description of each course including intended learning outcomes;Total training duration and duration per course;Total cost and cost per course; Description of how participants will be evaluated;Forms:Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guideline: click hereApplication Portal: click herePTIB Policy Manual: click hereBCeID: Click here

        November 5th, 2025 :The CleanBC Custom Program has been paused and is not accepting new applications or funding studies at this time.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers energy study funding and capital incentives for fuel switching and other electrification measures. Eligible BC Hydro commercial customers can receive up to $20,000 to cover 50% of the cost of an energy study, and up to $200,000 to install measures that reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The final subsidy amount is determined by the GHG reduction potential of the project. Grant value: Up to $20,000 to cover 50% of the cost of an energy study; and Up to $200,000 for installation of electrification measures;Parent companies are eligible for up to $750,000 in incentives, which can be spread over projects at multiple properties.Turnaround time: Up to 90 daysEligible Applicants:Applicant facility must be located in a BC Hydro service area, including New Westminster; andApplicant must have a BC Hydro Key Account Manager (KAM).Eligible Projects:Project must be permanent in nature, and have the potential to generate a lifetime savings of at least 1200 tonnes of CO2 emissions at a single facility; Must involve technologies that are accessible for site inspection, and/or measurement and verification;Technologies must be commercial available, and have a reasonable adoption rate;Program administrators may grant special approval for test cases involving emerging technologies, or technologies that are commercially available but not widely used in BC. One implemented, technologies must:Create a net decrease in GHGs;Produce results that are measurable and verifiable, and that can be estimated using standard engineering calculations;Involve technologies that are not covered by other utility DSM programs (e.g.: Fortis BC's Commercial Performance Program). Project must result in net electrical load growth;Examples of eligible measures include:Heat recovery chiller;Air-to-water heat pump;Air-to-water heat pump water heater;Ground source heat pump;Air-to-air rooftop heat pump;Water-to-water heat pump;Exhaust air heat recovery heat pump;Sewage heat recovery heat pump;Electric boiler (if more efficient heat pump options are not feasible);Electric water heater (if more efficient heat pump options are not feasible);High-efficiency (>75%) HRV;Air source VRF;Water source VRF.Program Details:Applicants begin by applying for a CleanBC Energy Study Incentive. Energy studies provide detailed technical information and quantify potential energy savings, identifying the most cost-effective energy saving measures for a particular facility;Applicants who completed an energy study independently, before the launch of the Custom Incentives program, can submit the study to BC Hydro for approval. If approved, they can skip the Energy Study Incentive, and apply directly for a Capital Incentive.Customers who apply for an Energy Study Incentive must complete the study within 6 months of signing the incentive agreement. Incentive payments are issued after completion of the Study;Data from the Study should be entered into the Custom Workbook (excel workbook) provided by the customer's KAM;The Workbook is submitted to and reviewed by BC Hydro to determine eligibility for Capital Incentives;Capital Incentives are offered to support the implementation of energy conservation measures identified in the Energy Study;Incentives are calculated at $40/tCO2e of lifetime GHG savings, up to a maximum of $200,000 per facility;For heat pump rooftop units, the rate is $60/tCO2e;Eligible Northern customers (north of and including the District of 100 Mile House) will receive an additional $10/tC02e on all eligible measures installed. Incentives are capped at 50% of the incremental cost of the project, or the point at which the project costs can be repaid within 4 years;There is no limit to how many submissions a customer can make, but they cannot receive more than $200,000 in total incentives;Parent companies can receive up to $750,000 in incentives from the Energy Study, Custom, and Custom-lite programs, which can be spread across projects at multiple properties;Customers must complete projects within 18 months of signing the Capital Incentive agreement;A Post Implementation Review will be conducted to ensure the measures were installed as proposed. If the Review is satisfactory, the incentive payment will be disbursed;Program participants are required to create an ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager account, and share their account in "Read Only" mode with BC Hydro and the program administrator for the purposes of monitoring and accountability.* *Note: Portfolio Manager is a free online tool developed by the US Environmental Protection Agency that allows users to track the energy performance of buildings.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: This program is not designed to fund projects retroactively; costs incurred before incentive agreements are in place will not be subsidized;The program can be combined with some other funding sources, but third-party funding will be subtracted from the incremental project cost, thereby reducing the Custom Incentive. In addition, projects that are already eligible for subsidies through utility DSM programs (such as Fortis BC's Commercial Performance Program) are not eligible for Custom Incentives; andBC Hydro will not advance incentive payments; applicants must be prepared to cover project costs up front. Forms: Program website: click hereApplication guide: click hereCustom Workbook template: click here

        Applications are now open! Deadline for applications has been extended to July 21, 2023. 
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The Traceability Value Chain Program provides funding of 70% of project costs to a maximum of $75,000 for agriculture, food, and seafood sector organizations, commercial food hubs and value chain partners. The intent of the program is to enable businesses to meet existing and emerging market and regulatory requirements by enhancing food and seafood traceability among supply chain partners.Grant Value: 70% of project costs to a maximum of $75,000Turnaround Time: 1 monthEligible Applicants:3 types of applicants:Sector organizations:Is a registered non-profit, incorporated association, or other recognized legally incorporated entity or
formed under the laws of its jurisdiction that represents members in an agriculture, food or
seafood sector;Must be able to enter into a legally binding contract.Represents members in the agriculture, food, or seafood sector, including:Members involved in agriculture, food, and seafood producing, processing, or handling activities;Alcoholic beverage processors - wine, beer, etc.;Retail food operations;Food service operations - restaurants, cafes, etc.;Agricultural input suppliers - feed, fertilizers and pesticide suppliers, etc.; andPackaging manufacturers.Commercial Food Hub:Are commercial shared-use food and beverage processing and innovation facilities that offer food, agriculture and seafood businesses access to commercial processing space, equipment, expertise and resources.Have been in operation for a minimum of one year at the time of application; Must be able to benefit a minimum of four hub-based businesses;Commercial food hubs must be involved in two or more of the following stages of the value chain:Inputs;Production;Processing;Distribution/Warehouse;Transportation providers; andRetail.Value chain partners:Must file business or farm income taxes in BC;Must have 1 lead applicant and a minimum of 2 value chain partners;Value chain partners must be in 2 or more of the following stages of the value chain:Inputs;Production;Processing;Distribution/Warehousing;Transportation; andRetail.Eligible Value chain applicants include: Producers directly involved in growing or producing agricultural crops including harvesting, sorting, grading, washing or packing;Producers raising livestock or poultry;Operations directly involved in the co-mingling, movement or storage and warehousing of livestock or poultry, agricultural and related products along the chain (e.g., transportation company);Processors directly involved in the processing of food products;Producers and processors directly involved in growing, producing or processing of seafood products including harvesting;Retail food operations;Food service operations (e.g., restaurants);Agricultural input suppliers (e.g., feed suppliers, fertilizer suppliers, pesticide suppliers);Traceability equipment suppliers;Transportation providers; andPackaging manufacturers.All applicants must be based and operating in BC;All applicants must maintain an active 9-digital business registration number or active GST number or CRA business number; andFile business income taxes in BC.Note: Eligible participants may apply for funding each year for new eligible activities, however, priority will be given to first-time applicants.Ineligible Applicants:Sector organizations that:Are national sector organizations with non-BC based members;Represent tobacco product producers, manufacturers, or processors;Represent pet food producers, manufacturers, processors, or related facilities; andRepresent health and/or nutrition supplement processors.Commercial Food Hubs: National food hub organizations and non-BC based members of these organizations;Commercial food hubs involved in pet food production, manufacturing and/or processing;Commercial food hubs involved in tobacco and tobacco product production, manufacturing and/ or processing;Commercial food hubs only involved in health and/or nutrition supplement processing; andCommercial food hubs involved in supplying equipment.Value chain partners:Partners or participants who are not a fundamental part of the value chain;Pet food producers, manufacturers, processors, or related facilities;Equipment suppliers;Health and/or nutrition supplement processors; andTobacco and tobacco product producers, manufacturers, and processors.Eligible Expenses:Consultant services for traceability project management;Research and pilot testing of solutions (needs assessment, gap analysis, evaluation of information sharing technologies);Information technology infrastructure, equipment associated with developing/maintaining information sharing networks;Customization of common desktop applications ( Microsoft Excel or Access) specific to the traceability project;Costs associated with developing or maintaining information-sharing networks;First time training costs associated with new equipment purchases or procedures related directly to the implementation of the project;First time costs related to traceability implementation (e.g. first-time registration with GS1 for unique company prefix number, excluding identification tags, labels);Costs associated with Mock Recall (see Program Details section below for more details);In-kind activities directly related to the development and implementation of the project; andOther activities as deemed eligible prior to being incurred based on project assessment by the Province.Ineligible Expenses:Expenses, deposits, or pre-payments requested by a vendor prior to the date of the funding application letter;Expenses related to day-to-day operations;Costs that have been reimbursed or are eligible for reimbursement under another government grant program (e.g. On-Farm Food Safety, Post-Farm Food Safety, Traceability Adoption, Livestock Tag Reader Rebate);GST, PST or other items for which a refund or rebate is received; Ongoing costs or running a traceability system including consumable items (e.g. spare batteries, purchase of single use identification tags, labels, renewal fees for GS1 certification etc.);Cost of system accessories (e.g. protective cases for handheld devices, stands or attachments for traceability hardware, optional ruggedization of purchased items, etc.);Market research (e.g. product, sector, customer);Costs to meet regulatory requirements;Costs associated with planning and creation of a value chain (e.g. partners facilitation/ coordination, agreements, business planning);Scientific testing or product R&D;Expansion of production capacity; andExpenditures and activities that result in facility-level recording/storage of information without further information sharing between value chain partners.Program Details:The objectives on the program include the following: enhance information sharing and increase the adoption of sustainable, voluntary information sharing systems to improve supply chain transparency;assist participants or entire sectors to streamline operations, improve market access, substantiate product claims, or generate economic benefits for participants;increase capacity to trace animals, agri-food or seafood products and their associated attributes;increase the ability of sectors and value chains to execute emergency response procedures when required (e.g. food recall); andsupport sector and value chain commitments to the sustainable production of safe,
high-quality food.All projects must be completed by February 16, 2024;All claims must be submitted within 30 days of the completion of the project, or by March 1, 2024, whichever is earlier;Mock recall exercise:Successful applicants must be able to demonstrate that 100% of any selected product can be located;Supporting documentation must be submitted as part of the final report to show the information-sharing capability and responsiveness of the traceability system in an emergency, including:Updated mock recall procedure;Records generated by the newly implemented/expanded traceability information-sharing system documenting the outcome of the mock recall exercise;Records confirming the capability of the information-sharing system to locate 100% products along the value chain or across a sector within a 24-hour period; andAny other reports, logs, or schedules as generated by the information-sharing system.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program does not allow funding to be used retroactively for expenses incurred prior to receiving the approval letter;Applicants seeking consultant services should see the list of known consultants with traceability experience here;Consultants do not need to be on this list and will be reviewed based on experience and expertise.Applicants seeking vendors should see the list of known vendors here;If the applicant is unsure if an expense or activity is eligible, please contact the program to inquire prior to incurring the expense; andApplicants are advised to keep all invoices and receipts to evidence purchase and payment for reimbursement.Forms & Links:Program webpage: click hereApplication portal: click hereTraceability vendors list: click hereTraceability consultants list: click hereTraceability training courses: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides funding to help Canadian booksellers improve their business model for online sales. It is designed for sellers of print books seeking to improve an online store that serves as a complement to physical retail locations. To be eligible, sellers must be headquartered in Canada, and must have achieved $50,000 in new book sales in 2019 (January - December). Grant funds may be used to cover costs associated with the establishment or improvement of tools for online sale, the management and shipping of orders, and the promotion and/or marketing of Canadian books.  Grant Value: For individual booksellers, up to $1,500,000;For an affiliated group or chain of booksellers, up to $3,500,000.Turnaround Time: 7 monthsEligible Applicants:Booksellers must be at least 75% owned and controlled by Canadians;Must have headquarters and at least 75% of employees in Canada;Must specialize in the sale of new print books to the public;Must sell Canadian-authored print books;Must have a physical retail store that is open to the public:Must have been in operation since January 1, 2019;Must sell new books by a minimum of 25 publishers;Had total new book sales of at least $50,000 between in 2019 (January - December); andSell new print books to the public through a transactional website at the time the application is submitted.Note: A lower new book sales threshold of $30,000 will be applied to booksellers owned and controlled by members of an official-language minority,  Indigenous, or racialized community.  Sellers not owned and controlled by these communities, but specializing in serving these communities, may also be eligible for the lower threshold; contact the program to discuss this possibility.Ineligible Applicants:Booksellers that exclusively sell used books, discounted books, or digital books;Booksellers that do not sell any Canadian-authored titles; andEvents such as festivals or salons du livre.Eligible Expenses:Establishing or improving technological and logistical tools related to the sale of print books online;Promotion and marketing of Canadian books for online sale;Costs associated with the management and shipping of orders, including: Labour;Shipping; andPostal costs.Costs associated with the development of official-language minority markets;Translation of marketing materials;Capital and salary expenses that are directly related to the development of online sales capacity; andExpenses must be incurred between April 1, 2022, and March 31, 2023. Ineligible Expenses:Expenses not directly related to the development of online sales capacity; andDividends, bonuses, or other extraordinary compensation to shareholders or owners.Program Details: Application forms must be requested from the program by email;A complete application package includes the form and the following supporting documents:Financial statements of the last year of operation, if available;Financial statements are mandatory if your business had more than $1M sales in 2019;For organizations with more than one store, a list of all eligible stores, including their physical address and websites (if applicable);For organizations that have never submitted a funding application to Canadian Heritage, a copy of incorporation papers, partnership agreement, or the business number and registration documents (for sole proprietorship);For publicly traded companies, a Geographical Analysis Report dated between January 1, 2022, and March 31, 2022; andA disclosure regarding the participation of any former public office holder or public servant subject to the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector and the Policy on Conflict of Interest and Post-Employment. Data on sales of Canadian books must be included with the application. andIf applicable, negotiate an intellectual property and/or non-disclosure agreement with the student team (templates available from BCIT).Eligible Projects:Project scope: 400 hours;Participation fee: $500;The participation fee is waived for non-profit employers.Any IT or software project that can provide learning opportunities to computing science students;Examples of suitable projects in each of the program's focus areas are:Computing Systems Technology:Web application using a framework such as React or Angular and a programming language such as Node js, Python, Java, PHP, or GO;Mobile application for Android or iOS using a framework such as Flutter;Scalable Cloud Application with public cloud providers such as AWS or Azure;Web or Mobile game.Computer Information Technology:Projects involving DevOps, Scripting, Cloud Integration, Machine Learning, and/or Web Development.Systems Software Developer:Web or Mobile projects with a database backend.Full Stack Web Development:Web development projects. Projects that are time-sensitive or mission-critical are not suitable for the program, since students are still in training;Applicants may submit projects throughout the year, but the cut-off for consideration for each semester is as follows:Fall semester: submit by August 11;Winter semester: submit by December 1;Spring semester: submit by March 23.Projects received after the deadlines will be saved for the next term;Large projects may be divided into phases for students to work on over several consecutive terms;       Grant Criteria 
      This Call for Proposals seeks innovative pre-commercial prototypes that address one of the following challenge areas related to Canada's oceans: 1) coastal resilience; 2) navigation and ocean communications; 3) autonomous surface and subsurface vehicles; and 4) aquaculture, blue carbon, and ocean pollution remediation. Successful bidders will receive a Government of Canada contract for the purpose of testing their prototype. Some prototypes will then qualify for the Pathway to Commercialization initiative, under which they could be selected for government contracts of up to $8M. Grant value:Standard component: $550,000Military component: $1,150,000Turnaround time: Proposals are due April 26, 2022. Adjudication time depends on the number of proposals submitted. Eligible Applicants: For-profit businesses with fewer than 500 full-time equivalent employees (FTEs);Not-for-profits, large businesses, and universities may apply as partner organizations, but the application must be led by a small or medium-sized enterprise;Must have a place of business in Canada where activities are conducted on a permanent basis;At least 50% of employees must work in Canada;At least 50% of wages, salaries, and fees are paid to employees and contractors who work in Canada; andAt least 50% of senior executives principally reside in Canada.The applicant must own or have a license to the intellectual property associated with the proposed innovation.Eligible Projects:Proposed innovations must be within the scope of one of the Standard or Military component subject areas (see "Program Details" below);Innovation must be pre-commercial, defined as:Not currently available for sale;Not previously sold on a commercial basis.At least 80% of the proposed project costs must be attributable to Canadian goods and services;The proposed innovation must not have been awarded a grant under the Build in Canada Innovation Program (BCIP) or its predecessor, the Canadian Innovation Commercialization Program (CICP), nor under any other Innovation Solutions Canada (ISC) Streams;If the innovation has already been submitted to any of the above programs, the proposal must be withdrawn (or the bid expired) before it can be resubmitted for the Oceans CFP;A bidder can participate in more than one of these programs if their proposals are for significantly different projects. Significant difference is defined as:A distinct product and/or service that has undergone a completely separate R&D path, or that diverged early in technology development;Significant modifications have been made to the application of the previous technologies (or components of the technology) that were not possible in the previous phase of development;A significant improvement in functionality, cost, or performance.The bidder's financial proposal must not exceed $550,000 (for Standard component proposals) or $1,150,000 (for military component proposals). Ineligible Projects:Projects will not be eligible for ISC funding if they can be described in any of the following ways:Incremental improvements on existing commercial technology;Technologies following a normal course of product development (ie: new versions or releases of existing technologies);Innovative aspects of the project are not quantifiable, or are not adequately described in the proposal. Eligible Costs:Applicable direct and indirect costs that are properly incurred and/or allocated in performance of the contract, including:Direct material costs;Direct labour costs;Overhead and administrative costs (max. 15% of total eligible costs);Selling and marketing expenses associated with the contract; andResearch and development expenses as outlined in the contract.Ineligible Costs:Interest and/or losses on investments;Legal, accounting, and consulting fees in connection with financial reorganization, security issues, capital stock issues, obtaining of patents and licenses, and prosecution of claims against Canada;Taxes;Contingency provisions;Premiums on life insurance;Amortization and/or costs associated with depreciation of assets/facilities;Fines and penalties;Unreasonable compensation for officers and employees;Product development not directly associated with he contract;Entertainment and hospitality expenses;Donations;Membership dues; andCompensation in the form of dividend payments, or based on changes in the price of corporate securities, stock options, stock appreciation rights, etc. Program Details: Applications are submitted via secure web portal using GC Key or a participating Sign-in Partner;The deadline for the Oceans CFP is April 26, 2022;Proposals must respond to one of the four challenge areas identified in the CFP:Coastal Resilience: Short- and long-term solutions that can assist with forecasting, situational awareness, climate assessments, marine sector decarbonization, and emergency response along Canada's coastlines. Acceptable innovations include:Flood prediction and forecasting systems;Nature-based solutions for flood and erosion risk management;Climate change impact assessment and adaptation solutions;Space-based Earth observation technologies and related applications;Electric vessel charging infrastructure;Low carbon shore side infrastructure;Coastal Bathy-topo Lidar, point cloud from imagery, bathymetric sonar, imagery, sampling, etc.; andSolutions to address sedimentation at points of entry.Navigation and Ocean Communication: Solutions that can enhance the current capabilities of ocean navigation and communications. Acceptable innovations include:Solutions to assist with ice navigation;Navigation systems for autonomous vessels that travel in ice and other harsh environments;Sensor technology;Weather routing technologies;Technology the can predict, automate, and/or disseminate the real-time detection of marine mammals using active sonar operations;Route optimization technology;Sea floor mapping solutions;Artificial Intelligence and SWARM systems for navigation; Vessel situational awareness technologies; andUltra energy efficient sensors, data storage, and communication technology.Autonomous Surface and Subsurface Vehicles: Autonomous marine vehicles that will enhance the capacity and safety of Canada's ocean operations. Acceptable innovations include:Small unmanned submarines and subsurface vehicles;Marine Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS);Remotely Operated Under-water Vehicles (ROVs) and Autonomous Under-water Vehicles (AUVs);Ship launched Unscrewed Aerial Systems that can transition between functional theatres;Configurable under-water vehicles with sea floor mapping capabilities;SWARM systems;Improved fuel, energy rejuvenation, and battery systems for autonomous vehicles;Ultra energy efficient sensors;Remote control centres to manage autonomous vehicles;Storage, maintenance, and infrastructure for autonomous systems; andMobile remote control facilities.Aquaculture, Blue Carbon, and Ocean Pollution Remediation: Short- and long-term solutions that can make the ocean economy more sustainable. Acceptable innovations include:DNA based technology to understand ocean biodiversity;Sensing solutions that can assist in the detection and monitoring of ocean pollution;Seaweed aquaculture, either harvested to generate energy or sunk to capture carbon;Aquatic waste management solutions;Solutions for the transportation of CO2 from source to sink;Sediment remediation solutions;Remote sensing technologies to detect and monitor marine biodiversity;Solutions that provide autonomous monitoring capability over extended time periods;Large scale pollution scanning technologies; andRisk impact assessment methodologies using Space based Earth observation.Successful bidders may be eligible for additional funding under the Pathway to Commercialization initiative;If your innovation is market-ready (TRL 9+) at the end of your ISC testing contract, it will be assessed for feasibility and may be added to a government source list, where it will remain for three years. During this time, the government may issue contracts of up to $8M to purchase the innovation. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices: The program may consider supporting eligible costs incurred before the signing of the funding agreement, up to a maximum 20% of total eligible costs. Costs incurred before the submission of the proposal will not be supported.ISC contracts can be combined with other provincial and federal sources of funding, provided the total amount of government funds does not exceed 100% of the project costs;Applicants will be required to inform the Minister or equivalent of the relevant department of all secured funding;Proposals pass through a competitive, multi-stage evaluation process, during which they are assessed according to the following criteria:Technological readiness and safety;Alignment with CFP challenge areas;Quality of the applicant's IP strategy;Organization capacity of the applicant;Financial capacity of the applicant;Economic benefits that will result from the project;Risk mitigation plan;Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion outcomes;Quality of the commercialization strategy; andAdoption potential.For a detailed overview of the criteria and associated point system, see the program website. Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

Eligible events must take place in Ontario and be open to the public at large without membership requirements. A minimum of 10,000 tourists is expected for the program. The intent is to help Ontario gain international exposure, attract more tourists and generate a significant economic impact for the province.Grant Value: Up to 20% of eligible operating expensesNote: While the grant value above is noted at $0, it is because the rate fluctuates per applicant.Turnaround Time: 3.5 monthsEligible Applicants:Be one of the following organizational types:Ontario municipalities;For-profit organizations that have event management as part of the organizational mandate;Non-profit organizations that have event management as part of the organizational mandate.Legal entities that have been in existence for 1 year or more at the date of submission;Have a Canadian business bank account conducting business in Ontario; andHave the organizational capacity and fiscal prudence to host a successful Blockbuster event.Applicants should ideally have proven national/international event management experience.Eligible Events:Must occur in the province of Ontario;Be open to the public at large without membership in a club or group;Be either:A major one-time national or international event;A major event that recured infrequently in Ontario.Cannot recur annually or travels nationally or internationally to host destinations.Have cash operating expenses totaling $1 million or more;Is of a size and scope sufficient to draw tourists to Ontario and generate significant economic impact for the province;Should draw a minimum of 10,000 tourists.Is of national and/or international prominence, attracting significant media exposure across Canada and/or globally; andCarries at least a $2 million commercial general liability insurance coverage for the duration of the Agreement.Ineligible Events:Events that are still in the bidding process;Amateur sporting events funded under the Ontario Sports Hosting Program;Recurring events on an annual or biennial basis;Events that attract special interest audiences;Events that recruit new members; andTrade fairs or events that are primarily commercial in nature (conventions, meetings, seminars, clinics, etc.).Eligible Expenses:Expenses must relate directly to specific expenditures incurred during the delivery of the proposed Blockbuster event, including but not limited to:Programming and production;Paid advertisements;Event security;Accessibility services.Ineligible Expenses:Event staffing and administration/overhead costs;Consulting costs;Mobile and website development/upgrade costs;Any expenses that will be covered by in-kind revenues or in-kind services;Alcohol or cannabis-related products;Audience surveys, research or economic impact studies;Competition prizes.Note: please see page 8 of the program guideline for the full list of ineligible expenses.Program Details:Maximum of 2 applications per organization;Maximum of 1 application per event;As part of the application, applicants must submit the following documents:Application form (completed and electronically signed and dated);Incorporation documents (does not apply to municipalities);Applicant organization's most recent, audited financial statements (must be prepared by a Chartered Public Accountant CPA);An economic assessment report; andMarketing plan.Applicants must report back to the ministry within 90 days following the event on the use of funds, service deliverables  and outcomes achieved using the Celebrate Ontario Blockbuster final report form; andIf the funds were not used the province has the right to recover parts or all of the funds transferred.
