      Grant Criteria 
      This program supports the development of independent Ontario-based magazine publishers by providing grants of up to $75,000 to support strategic initiatives that enable publishers to achieve business development and marketing objectives. Funds may be used to support promotional activities that increase sales, and/or to implement measures that improve the efficiency and productivity of the publisher.  The goals of the program are to enhance revenue and create more jobs the Ontario publishing industry. Grant Value:Standard stream: 75% of eligible costs up to $75,000Diversity Enhancement stream: up to $15,000 for companies with racially diverse or Francophone ownership that do not qualify for the regular stream.Note: Publishers that do not meet the sales thresholds for the regular stream may receive up to $15,000 in project funding through the Diversity Enhancement Stream if they are owned by racially diverse and/or Francophone individuals. To be eligible for this stream, the publisher must have been in operation for at least 1 year, have an annual sales revenue of at least $5000, and circulation of 1500 (for print publications) or (for web publications), a minimum website engagement of 5000 unique monthly visitors OR a membership/subscriber base of 1500. Turnaround Time: Funding decisions to be announced in August 2023.Eligible Applicants:Independent Canadian-owned and -controlled magazine publishers that are based in Ontario;For affiliated companies and subsidiaries, only one application per parent company is allowed;Must be actively publishing at the time of the application;Must derive more than 50% of revenue from magazine sales and related brand extension (ie; events, trade shows, website, television properties);Must pay Ontario corporate taxes;Must be at least 75% owned and controlled by Canadians;Must have a minimum sales revenue of $20,000; andMust be financially solvent and in good standing with Ontario Creates at the time of application.Note: Group projects involving multiple magazine publishers are eligible, as long as all participating publishers meet the eligibility criteria. Eligible Content:For publishers of print magazines, the following eligibility criteria apply: Must have undergone a full 12-month publishing cycle and business year by the time of application;Must have published at least two editions;Must be actively publishing at the time of application;Must include a clearly displayed masthead or equivalent with a named editor;Must be primarily edited, designed, and published in Ontario;Must have an editorial function and a named editor;Must contain at least 75% Canadian editorial content on average (textual and/or graphic content created by Canadian citizens or permanent residents);Must have an editorial calendar for the ideation, creation, and publishing of content;Must present editorial content from more than one person;The majority of the content must be original;Issues must be published under a common title and at regular intervals, no more than once a week, and no less than twice a year;Must clear distinguish between advertising and editorial content, and contain at most 70% advertising in all issues published in the previous 12 months;Must have a publishing revenue stream (ie: subscription, advertising sales); andMust have achieved the following circulation benchmark in the most recent 6 months:2500 copies per issue for single applications;1000 copies per issue for group projects involving more than one magazine. For digital magazines, the following additional criteria apply: Must maintain the availability  a substantive amount of editorial content (including articles, videos, photo essays, and infographics);For web-based magazines, have a valid, live URL address specific to the magazine title;For app-based magazines, have an application currently available for download; Must have achieved one of the following circulation benchmarks in the most recent 6 months:For open-access, web-based service: maintain a minimum of 15,000 unique monthly visitors;For application-based circulation: maintain a minimum of 10,000 active subscribers;For closed-access (subscription, paywall): maintain a minimum of 2500 active subscribers. Ineligible Content:The following content is ineligible for Magazine Fund support:Promotional content published by companies whose principal business is not magazine publishing;Editorial content that is predominantly reproduced from previous issues of a publication, or from other published or online sources;Content that incites hatred against an identifiable group;Sexually exploitative content, or content that is criminal or excessively violent in nature; andContent that is contrary to public policy in the opinion of Ontario Creates.Eligible Expenses:Costs directly related to activities that drive sales and increase publisher revenue, OR that improve operational efficiency and productivity, including:Relaunch/rebrand activities;Promotional campaigns and media kits;Special issues;Launching of a new magazine (for established publishers);Redesign or upgrade of website;Enhancement of online and/or mobile magazine formats;Podcasts, videos, webcasts;Digitization of back issues;Optimization of online content;Exploration of alternate sales channels;International business development activities, including travel;Enhancing internal workflow/backend processes, including CRM implementation;  andDevelopment of digital transformation strategy and business planFor digital projects, capital expenses (ie: hardware, software) can be funded up to 15% of the total project budget. Ineligible Expenses:Ongoing operational costs;Salaries and wages of staff not directly related to the project;Fixed overhead costs (ie: telephone, photocopier, computer);Occupancy costs (ie: rent); andHospitality.Program Details: Applications must be submitted through the Online Application Portal;Publishers may submit a single application for a project related to one or more magazines titles, OR up to two applications for projects relating to different titles;Projects must involve new activities that are not already under way at the time of application; Funding for successful applicants will be proportion to sales revenue (see table below);Realistically valued “in-kind” services may be included as part or all of the 25% costs that must come from sources other than the Ontario Creates Book Fund;Applicants may begin incurring expenses no more than 90 days following application approval; andProjects must completed by February 16, 2024.Eligible Sales RevenueTotal Funding Available per ApplicantOver $2,000,000up to $75,000$500,001 to $2,000,000up to $65,000$140,001 to $500,000up to $40,000$20,000 to $140,000*up to $35,000*Note: For publishers with eligible sales revenues of less than $75,000, the funds requested should be proportional to sales, with total request not exceeding 33% of eligible sales revenues and in keeping with 75% of the total budget;

      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers cost-matching contributions of up to $10,000,000 for pre-commercial recycling, upcycling, and waste management initiatives. Funds may be used to support field-testing and scale-up of prototypes, commercial demonstrations, and/or development of a product in its final commercial form. The goal of the program is to accelerate Alberta's transition to a low-emissions economy by advancing innovations that support economic diversification and reduce the impacts of material production, processing, and disposal.Grant Value: 50% of eligible project costs up to $10,000,000.Note: The minimum funding contribution is $500,000.  Turnaround Time: Expressions of interest are due May 26, 2022;Funding decisions are to be announced in December 2022 - January 2023. Eligible Applicants: Individuals;Innovators and technology developers;Small and medium-sized enterprises;Industrial facilities owners/operators;Industrial associations;Indigenous communities;Think tanks and/or post-secondary institutions;Not-for-profits;Municipalities; andConsortiums (collaborations and partnerships are encouraged). Note: Applicants do not have to be based in Alberta, but project proposals must have a clear value proposition for the province. Eligible Projects:Innovative technologies that have the potential to deliver greenhouse gas benefits across the entire material value chain and product life cycle, such as:Transformative solutions for waste stream processing and value recovery;Novel technologies for product recycling, reuse, remanufacturing, and upcycling;Enhancement of cross-sector symbiosis such as cascading use of energy and materials between industries;Lower-emissions substitutes for products with high resource, energy, emissions, and/or waste footprints; andCircularizing the flow of carbon through the economy. Specific technologies that are well aligned with this challenge include, but are not limited to:Solutions for treatment and upcycling of solid wastes and waste water;Novel mineral sources and high value material extraction from waste streams/products;Metals and minerals recycling and reuse;Solutions for agriculture and food waste reduction and/or upcycling;Advanced plastics recycling and circular plastics technologies;Green materials (ie: hemp, novel cement chemistries, novel plastics, etc.);Feedstock substitution (ie: biogenic inputs, recovered materials, industrial symbiosis, etc.);Digitization and automation of product manufacturing and logistics; andCarbon dioxide conversion or utilization.Projects should be in one of the following stages of development: Field Pilot: Technology or innovation is ready to be field-tested in an operational environment. Commercial Demonstration: Technology or innovation is approaching a final commercial product and representative systems have been built.First-of-kind Commercial Implementation: Technology or innovation is ready for first-of-kind commercial deployment. Proposed initiative must be incremental to business-as-usual activities.Ineligible Projects:The following types of projects are ineligible for the Circular Economy Challenge:Business-as-usual technologies and practices, such as:Waste heat recovery;Biogas/biofuel production;Renewable natural gas;Anaerobic digestion;Composting; andSpreading of biosolids/other waste as fertilizer.Standalone studies of product/material life cycle impacts; andSoftware approaches to waste tracking, sorting, and management. Eligible Expenses:Incremental expenses that are directly related to the proposed initiative or project, including:Salaries and wages (including MERCS but excluding bonuses and commissions);Stipends/bursaries for research students involved in the project;Contractor fees;Overhead that is directly related to the project (max. 15% of total eligible expenses);Capital assets (ie: property, equipment), pending ERA approval;Materials;Costs associated with preparing progress reports for ERA;Costs associated with publishing results/research related to the project, pending ERA approval;Travel to present the project at a conference (max. $2500 for national conferences, $5000 for international conferences); andWith ERA approval, a vehicle allowance of $0.505 per km for project-related trips made in a private or company vehicle.Ineligible Expenses:Purchase of land;Memberships, subscriptions, and tuition fees;Costs associated with GHG validation and verification;Cost of obtaining approval from any regulatory body;Costs associated with hiring personnel;Product marketing;Costs associated with protecting intellectual property;Costs associated with entertainment or hospitality;Note: Hospitality expenses related to workshops, seminars, and other knowledge-sharing activities may be deemed eligible; andGST and PST. Program Details:Applications must be submitted via ERA's Emissions Reduction Information Management System (ERIMS);Late and/or incomplete applications will not be considered;The application consists of an Expression of Interest document (max. 10 single-spaced pages; template available through ERIMS) and a Project Information webform;Letters of Support from partner organizations are optional. If included, all letters should be merged into a single PDF attachment;Applications will undergo a competitive review process, with a shortlist to be determined by July, 2022;Shortlisted applicants will have until September, 2022, to submit detailed proposals;Final funding decisions will be announced in December 2022 orJanuary 2023. Projects must commence within 120 days of funding approval, and must be completed within three years;Funding recipients will be required to report on project outcomes, achievements, and lessons learned, including GHG reductions, job creation, and other environmental, economic, and social benefits; andERA may require funding recipients to take part in knowledge-sharing events and activities. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This funding may be combined with other federal and provincial sources of funding. However, ERA will only match unencumbered cash contributions. Government funding will be taken into account in the ERA's risk assessment of the project, but it will not be eligible for cost-matching;This program is not retroactive. Costs incurred prior to the funding agreement will not be reimbursed, and will not be eligible for cost-matching from ERA.Projects are evaluated according to the following criteria:Innovation potential (25 points);Feasibility (20 points);GHG and non-GHG benefits (35 points); andMarket and value proposition (20 points).Reasons for projects to be rejected include, but are not limited to:Insufficient GHG reduction potential;Technology or approach is not feasible in Alberta;Project site is not in Alberta;Detrimental side effects (environmental, economic,  social);Insufficient information provided;EOI not written in English;EOI is not sufficiently readable or comprehensible;EOI does not conform to submission standards;Project is inconsistent with the intent or scope of the Challenge; andProject is assessed to be business-as-usual.During the submission process, applicants may allow ERA to share their application with other trusted funding partners. Allowing the application to be shared is not mandatory, and will not affect the ERA's evaluation of the project;Projects that have received ERA or CCEMC funding in the past are not eligible for the Circular Economy Challenge. However, funding may be considered for a new phase of development that builds on and sufficiently advances the previously funded project.Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guide: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Canada-NL Job Grant provides up to 100% of training costs to a maximum of $15,000 to Newfoundland and Labrador employers to help offset the cost of training for existing and future employees. The training must be 12 months or less in duration and may be delivered in any format so long as the training takes place within the province. The intent of the program is to help Newfoundlanders and Labradorians upskill while helping employers address the skills gap.Grant Value:Existing employees: Up to 33.33% to a maximum of $10,000 per yearUnemployed individuals: Up to 100% of training costs to a maximum of $15,000 per yearNote: Contribution percentages for this program are determined based on the size of the business (see Program Details section below).Turnaround Time: Within 30 business daysEligible Employers:Have an office location/base in Newfoundland and Labrador;Be one of the following organizational types:Private-sector businesses (incorporated, sole proprietors and general partnerships);Non-profit organizations;Industry associations;Employer consortia;Unions; andIndigenous governments and organizations.Maintain a Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) business number;Be in good standing with the Registry of Companies and Deeds; andBe able to provide a Letter of Attestation.Ineligible Employers:Crown corporations;Government agencies;Boards and commissions; andMunicipalities.Eligible Trainees:Be legally entitled to work in Canada;Be residents of Newfoundland & Labrador;Existing employees; andUnemployed individuals.Must be hired by the employer no more than 30 business days prior to the training date;Proof of unemployment is required from participants, acceptable documentation includes but is not limited to:Record of Employment;Recent Notice of Termination from the last employer;Confirmation of Employment Insurance; andConfirmation of Income Support.Note: An individual leaving their current job to accept employment with a different employer is not considered an unemployed participant.Eligible Training:Training must take place within Newfoundland and Labrador (except under exceptional circumstances);E.g. highly specialized/technical training not available in the province.Be 12 months or less in duration;Be delivered in any format (online, classroom-based, or workplace-based);Be delivered by a provincially recognized third-party training provider:Public or private post-secondary training institutions;Private trainers approved and operating in compliance with the Department's Private Training Regulations Act;Union-based training centers; andProduct vendors with manufacturer-recognized training certifications.E.g. Microsoft Systems, Cisco Systems, etc.Eligible Expenses:Tuition fees and fees charged by the training provider;Mandatory student fees;Textbooks, software, supplies, and other required materials;Examination fees;Travel costs (please refer to program guidelines for more information); andWages or wage replacement (ONLY if the employer is a small business training an existing employee).Ineligible Expenses:Travel outside the province, unless in exceptional circumstances;Conferences;Training delivered by the employer or an employee of the business (e.g. mentorships);First-aid training; andWorkplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) training.Program Details:Employer contribution percentages to training costs:Large businesses with 50 employees+ must contribute at a minimum of 1/3 of training costs, unless the trainee is an unemployed individual;Small businesses with 50 or fewer employees must contribute 1/3 of training costs.Small businesses may elect to provide their trainees with wages or wage replacements up to 50% of the require contributions as an alternate form of contribution for the grant;In other words, if the employer is required to contribute $1000 to training costs, they can pay the trainee wages of up to $500 instead of using the funds for the training costs.Employers may apply for more than 1 grant;The Letter of Attestation for unemployed individuals must include the following:The date of hire, or anticipated date of hire;The state that the individual will be hired upon completion of the training.The Letter of Attestation for existing employees must include the following:Must state that the employer will continue to employ the individual upon completion of training;Must state that the employee will have increased or enhanced skills related to their current position or for advancement with the employer.The employer must provide contact information for all the employees identified as training recipients and participating in the training within 7 days of approval.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Accelerating CCUS Technologies call provides funding of up to 50% to a maximum of $2.85M for research and development projects for CO2 Capture, Utilisation, and Storage (CCUS) technologies. Project proposals must be submitted by a project consortium, consisting of a minimum of 2 eligible applicants from at least 2 participating countries/regions. The projects must also include higher Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) of 5 and above. The aim of the program is to commercialize carbon capture technologies to reduce the global carbon footprint.Grant Value: 50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $2.85MTurnaround Time: Funding decisions to be announced in late December 2022Eligible Applicants:All categories of applicants, including:Technology developers;Industry;Industrial associations;Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs);Research and development (R&D) organizations;Universities;Municipalities;Not-for-profit organizations;Government research labs; andIndividuals.Have at least 2 eligible applicants seeking funding from at least 2 participating countries/regions;Lead applicants must be the main contact point at the national level;All consortium applicants must have the required expertise to undertake research and development.Applicants are not required to be located in Alberta, but all applicants must demonstrate a clear value proposition for the province.Applicants must demonstrate how the proposed technology or application thereof is an innovative solution for emissions reduction in Alberta.Eligible Projects:Carbon capture: production of a pure CO2stream from combustion and/or processes at the point of emissions;Carbon capture and transportation networks: integrated approaches combining multiple capture points and transportation infrastructure to link multiple specific capture sites to a common network;Point-to-point transportation via pipelines, ships, trains, or trucks with a single input CO2stream;Direct carbon conversion: implementation of a process that directly absorbs carbon into a product at the point of emissions such as the creation of CO2-based products (e.g., fuels, chemicals, building materials);Permanent Storage: captured CO2is transported to a geological storage site and then injected deep underground where it is permanently stored;Utilization to Storage via Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR)/Enhanced Gas Recovery (EGR): the captured CO2is transported to an oil field and is used to stimulate more oil production, with the CO2then being stored in the oil-depleted reservoir;Offshore CO2storage: injection of CO2into deep geological formations beneath the seabed (e.g., depleted oil and gas reservoirs and saline aquifers) for permanent storage;Clean Hydrogen Production: low-carbon hydrogen production from fossil sources combined with CCUS;Carbon dioxide removal (CDR):Biomass Carbon Removal and Storage (BiCRS)/ Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS): utilization of biomass as an energy source and the capture and permanent storage of CO2produced during the conversion of biomass to energy;Direct Air Capture (DAC): production of pure CO2stream from ambient air;In-situ carbon mineralization: CO2captured, compressed and stored in reactive geologic formations where CO2in the fluid form mineralizes to produce water-insoluble calcium or magnesium carbonates, such as in basalts offshore.Program Details:Proposals shall be submitted to the ACT Secretariat via email at act-ccs@rcn.no as a single PDF file;Projects must commence within 3 months of receiving ACT funding approval;Projects must be completed within 3 years;No project partner can have a share of more than 70% of the project's work plan activities.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices:Alberta is home to the Alberta Carbon Conversion Technology Centre (ACCTC), a real-world testbed for carbon capture and conversion technologies. Applicants are strongly encouraged to consider piloting or testing their technology at the ACCTC.Forms:Program webpage: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This cost-sharing program helps businesses in Nova Scotia make accessibility-related improvements for customers, clients, and employees. Funding is available in five project categories: Built Environment, Accessible Communication Services, Assistive Devices, Universal Design Capacity Building, and Accessible Transportation.  Funding caps and conditions apply to each category (see Grant Criteria); the maximum grant amount per applicant across all categories is $100,000.Grant Value: Up to $100,000 Turnaround Time: 12 weeksEligible Applicants:For-profit businesses that are registered and operating in the province of Nova Scotia;Business must be open for use by all community members, with reasonable rates and operating hours;Member-only businesses are not eligible.Ineligible Applicants:Franchises, unless locally owned;Residential rental properties;Member-only businesses; andNon-profit agencies and municipalities. Eligible Projects: Projects are eligible if they have not already received business accessibility funding in the current fiscal year, and fit into one or more of the following  categories:Built Environment - Removing physical barriers to make it easier for persons to access business services. Grant will cover 2/3 of eligible expenses up to a maximum of $50,000;Accessible Communication - Ensure all customers, clients, and employees can access information related to the business. Grant will cover 2/3 of eligible expenses up to a maximum of $30,000;Assistive Devices - Ensure employees and customers with disabilities have the devices they need to do their jobs/access the place of business. Grant will cover 2/3 of eligible expenses up to a maximum of $30,000. Accessible Transportation - Improve accessible transportation options for employees and customers via access to shuttle services, fleet vehicles, and taxis. Grant will cover 2/3 of eligible expenses up to a maximum of $20,000.Universal Design Capacity Building*- Develop universal design capacity within the professional-technical services community and train disabled persons in this field. Grant will cover up to 1/2 of eligible expenses.Only recognized educational institutions and organizations that deliver training to the business community are eligible to submit projects under the Universal Design Capacity Building category. Eligible Expenses: Built Environment Improvement to physical premises, including curb cuts, accessible parking, accessible bathrooms, automatic door openers, and barrier-free paths of travel;Facility renovations/enhancements that meet or exceed the accessibility requirements of the building code;New construction projects that exceed the accessibility requirements of the building code;Design and permit fees; andAudit and certification fees. Accessible Communication Accessible web design;Accessible signage (analog and digital); Assistive technologies to enable the blind or the deaf and hard of hearing to communicate with the business;Conversion of commercial documentation into braille or other formats;Fire alarms for the deaf; andCaptioning of commercial videos.  Assistive DevicesPurchase and installation of movable equipment, such as page-turners, adaptive switches, voice-recognition programs, and specialized door levers; andCosts associated with training employees to use the devices.Accessible TransportationConverting an existing vehicle to a wheelchair-accessible commercial shuttle; orThe difference between the cost of purchasing a wheelchair-accessible commercial shuttle service vehicle and a traditional commercial shuttle service vehicle. Universal Design Capacity BuildingTrainer fees and resources;Cost associated with hosting training events;Project management costs; andMarketing and promotion. Note: Features and improvements required by law, legislation, or the Nova Scotia Building Code are not eligible under this grant. Program Details:Applications can be submitted by mail, fax, or email;A complete application package includes;Description of the business;Description of the physical premises, including drawings/sketches/plans;Description of activities that take place on the business premises;Summary of the proposed project;Copy of lease agreement or proof of ownership; List of other funding sources;Proof of insurance;Proof of registration as a for-profit entity;Detailed estimates;For projects totalling less than $10,000, include two quotes;For projects totalling more than $10,000, include three quotes;Justification of vendor selection;If using skilled labour as an in-kind contribution in your application, provide proof of the skilled labourer's certification;If applying for assistive devices, identify the purpose and explain the expected results of installing the equipment. For assistive medical devices, include proof that the devices are not covered under medical insurance plans; andEngineered drawings, maps, and illustrations to demonstrate the scope of the project. Applications will be evaluated by the Business ACCESS-Ability Grant Review Panel;The Grant Review Panel will make approval recommendations to the Minister of Communities, Culture, Tourism, and Heritage;Funding recipients must notify the program coordinator of any post-approval changes to the project; andRecipients must submit a final report within 30 days of completing the project. 

      Best Practices & Forms

Other funding sources must be declared by the applicant, and may affect the amount they are eligible for through the Business ACESS-Ability program;Applications are evaluated according to the following criteria:Applicant's commitment to equal opportunity and inclusive communities;Ability of the business to create a welcoming commercial environment and employment opportunities for persons with disabilities;Implementation of universal design principles; andDegree to which the project creates barrier-free travel from public curb to interior amenities. Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guidelines: click hereApplication form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This federally funded loan program provides up $5,000,000 in repayable contributions to help BC businesses improve productivity, commercialize technology, and/or accelerate their growth in domestic and international markets. Applicants must be high-growth businesses that have been operating in BC for at least 2 years. The program will prioritize the advanced manufacturing, clean tech, ICT,  health/bio-science, natural resources,  ocean technology, and value-added agriculture sectors. Projects must result in increased revenue, export sales growth, and job creation. Grant Value: 50% of eligible project costs up to a maximum of $5,000,000 per projectNote: Companies may submit more than one project per fiscal year, in which case they can receive up to $10,000,000 in repayable funding.Turnaround Time: 90 business days from submission of the full applicationEligible Applicants:Incorporated for-profit organizations that have been in operation for at least 2 years;Must have staffed facilities located in British Columbia;Must be a high-growth business, defined as 20% revenue growth year over year;For companies applying with a pre-commercial technology, other factors will be used to measure growth, including the number of jobs created and investment dollars secured.Must have evidence of confirmed funding at the time of application;At least 50% of project costs must be covered by non-governmental sources of funding. Evidence of this funding must be provided at the Expression of Interest stage.Note: Preference will be given to SMEs with fewer than 500 employees. Eligible Activities:Activities that support business growth through job creation, increased revenue, and/or growth in export sales, such as:Productivity improvement: Acquiring, adapting, and/or adopting new technologies and processes;Process re-engineering;Improving manufacturing capacity;Business Scale-up:Market development and/or expansion;Adopting best practices for management;Business opportunity development;Technology Commercialization:Late-stage product development to grow/diversify markets;Technology demonstration (for technologies that are Technology Readiness Level 7-9).Preference will be given to proposals from the following strategic sectors:Advanced manufacturing;Clean technology;Information communication technology;Healthcare and bioscience;Natural resources;Ocean technology; andValue-added agriculture/Agritech.Ineligible Activities:Any activity that does not result in job creation, increased revenue, and/or growth in export sales AND/OR is not approved by PacifiCan. Eligible Costs:Incremental costs that are directly related to project activities, including: Capital costs (ie: equipment, machinery);Labour (wages and benefits);Marketing costs;Cost related to intellectual property (ie: registration); Technology development and commercial demonstrations; andProfessional, advisory, and technical services. Ineligible Costs:Costs deemed unreasonable, non-incremental, and/or not related project activities, including:Basic and applied R&D (Technology Readiness Level 1-6);Land and buildings;Salary bonuses and dividend payments;Entertainment/hospitality expenses;Refinancing of existing debts;Amortization or depreciation of assets; andLobbying activities. Program Details:Applications pass through two stages. In the first stage, companies submit an Expression of Interest via the PacifiCan Application Portal. In the second stage, PacifiCan invites companies with the most promising EOIs to submit a full application;There are two Expression of Interest intakes in 2022;Intake one is open from June 15, 2022, to July 27, 2022;Intake two will open in November, 2022 (dates TBD); andCompanies may submit one project per intake cycle.The earliest possible start date for projects is the date the Expression of Interest is submitted;Projects may be up to 3 years long;The minimum project cost is $200,000, and the maximum project cost is $5,000,000;At the Expression of Interest stage, the following documents are required:Financial statements for the last 2 years, as well as interim statements for at least the last 6 months;Supporting documents (ie: business plan and pitch deck) that explain the project and show how your company is high growth;Confirmation of other funding sources, such as bank statements, unused portions of lines of credit, letters of intent, funding agreements, and/or signed term sheets;The following are NOT acceptable sources of funding: Forecasted revenue from future activities;Accounts receivables;Commitments to raise equity or obtain future bank financing; andScientific Research & Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credits. BSP does not provide funding up-front. Successful applicants submit claims for reimbursement on a quarterly basis;After the project concludes, there is a 1 year grace period. Then, the loan is repaid in equal monthly payments over 5 years;Payments are interest-free as long as they are received on time; andThere is no penalty for early repayment. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:You may combine this program with other federal and provincial sources of funding. However, at least 50% of project costs must be covered by non-governmental sources. This means that leveraging other government sources of funding will decrease the amount you receive from the BSP program;Funding is retroactive to the start date of the project, which is considered to be the date on which the Expression of Interest was submitted. You cannot receive retroactive funding for expenses occurred before this date;Applications are evaluated on their ability to achieve program objectives, and on their relative strengths in the following areas:Market potential;Management capability;Financial capacity;Economic benefits; andAgency priorities.A strong business plan that clearly identifies how the productivity or efficiency savings will enable the company to grow is essential; andApplicants are advised to exclude SR&ED costs from their applications, as these may decrease the amount of funding available from BSP. Forms:Program website: click hereApplicant Guide: click hereExpression of Interest Help Guide: click here

      This program supports BC-based businesses, non-profits, and public entities looking to deploy commercial zero-emissions vehicles, including medium- and heavy-duty on-road vehicles, rail, marine, aircraft, and off-road equipment. andThe vehicle must be purchased or leased in Canada. Infrastructure:Electric charging infrastructure (Level 2 and above);Must have cUL, cETL, or CSA certification;Must be new and purchased/leased for a minimum of 5 years;Must be a permanent installation that will be operational for at least 5 years;Hydrogen fuelling infrastructure;Hydrogen dispensed must meet the quality standards of SAE International;Must be operational for at least 12 months;Technology must be approved for use in Canada;       Grant Criteria 
      The Wine Sector Support Program provides up to $25 million in non-repayable funding to Canadian wine producers and primary agricultural products used to produce bulk wine. Funding will be determined based on the total litres of eligible wines produced in the previous year. Eligible wine products include grape wine, fruit wines, sake, and other primary agricultural product-based wines. Eligible applicants must have generated a minimum of $50,000 in total sales in the previous fiscal year. The intent of the program is to improve financial resilience and the competitiveness of the sector.Grant Value: Up to a maximum of $25,000,000 per fiscal year (April - March)Note: The funding will be determined based on the total litres of eligible wines produced in the 2024-2025fiscal year. The per litre payment rate will be provided once the application intake period for the fiscal year has closed.Turnaround Time: 100 business daysEligible Applicants:Be a for-profit licensed winery that produces eligible wines in Canada for commercial sale, including:Grape wine;Other fruit wine;Sake;Other primary agricultural product-based wines.Have grown, produced, or owned the primary agricultural products used to produce wine, including:Grapes;Berries;Other fruits;Dandelions;Rice;Sap.Be one of the following organization types:Businesses and corporations;Sole-proprietorships;Partnerships;Co-operatives;Academic Institution.Hold a valid wine license issued by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) valid at the time of application and up to or after March 31, 2026; andHave generated a minimum of $50,000 in total sales of all wine produced in Canada in the previous fiscal year.Note: To produce wine means to bring it into existence by fermentation. The person who initiates the fermentation process will be the producer of the wine. Under the Program, wine is produced when it has completed initial fermentation.Ineligible Applicants:Ineligible wine products include:Cider;Mead;Wine that originates from processed inputs, such as:Juice;Concentrate;Syrup;Must (juice that contains skins, seeds, and stems).Wine products that were produced before April 1, 2024; Wine products you packaged, but did not produce; andWine product(s) that have an excise duty exemption available beyond June 30, 2022, the wine product is not eligible for support through this program.Program Details:Program aims to help wineries across Canada who are facing a range of hardships from: climate catastrophe;urging inflation; labour shortage; and competition from major wine producing countries that dominate wine sales in Canada etc.Eligible wine is bulk wine produced in Canada between April 1, 2024 and March 31, 2025;Only the portion of wine that is produced and originated from domestic and/or imported primary agricultural products will be considered in grant payment calculations;The grant provides 80 cents per litre, which means a winery that produces 100,000 litres of wine a year could collect $80,000;Each applicant may only submit 1 application per year to the program;Packaged wine that was produced before April 1, 2024 is not eligible for support under the program; andApplicants will receive an acknowledgment within 1 business day for online applications. If the application form (PDF) was submitted by mail or fax, it could take longer to receive the acknowledgment notice.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides funding of up to $1,500,000 to businesses, municipalities, and non-profits undertaking economic development projects in Southwestern Ontario. Businesses can receive grants or loans for projects that allow them to expand operations in the region through equipment upgrades, training initiatives, and hiring. Municipalities, industry associations, and economic development organizations may submit community development projects that advance regional economic priorities. Grant Value: Business Projects:Loans for 15% of eligible project costs up to $5,000,000. Loans are interest-free during the project period (up to 4 years). Projects that achieve investment and job targets may have up to 30% of the loan forgiven;Grants for 15% of eligible project costs up to $500,000, available to businesses in rural areas with fewer than 100 employees;Grants of up to $1,500,000 for strategic projects that are foreign direct investments or for companies competing against other jurisdictions.Community Development Projects: Grants for 50% of eligible costs up to a maximum of $1,500,000. Turnaround Time: 60 business daysEligible Applicants: Must be located in or planning to locate in  Southwestern Ontario*;For Business Projects:Must have at least 3 years of operations/finance statements;Employ at least 10 people, or 5 people if the business is based in rural Ontario;Must commit to creating 5 new jobs (or increase staff by 30% for companies with fewer than 15 employees); andMust invest at least $500,000 in the project (or $200,000 for rural businesses).For Community Development Projects: Municipalities, economic development organization, or industry/sector association;Must invest more than $100,000 in the project; andMust have private sector support. *Note: Southwestern Ontario includes: Brant, Bruce, Chatham-Kent, Dufferin, Elgin, Essex, Grey, Haldimand, Huron, Lambton, Middlesex, Niagara, Norfolk, Oxford, Perth, Simcoe, Waterloo, and Wellington. Eligible Projects:Must consist of new activities that are not part of the applicant's normal operations;For Business Projects:Allow the applicant to expand operations in Southwestern Ontario  through system or equipment upgrades, implementation of training initiatives, adding new staff, or a combination of the three.For Community Development Projects:Boost economic and business development and job creation by investing in infrastructure or implementing strategies to advance regional development priorities. Eligible Expenses:Must be directly related to the  project;Must be incurred after the project start date identified in the Funding Agreement;Must not be ongoing operational or production costs;May be in any of the following categories:Project facilities and infrastructure;Equipment and machinery;Specialized expertise (ie: consulting fees);Training and talent costs;Permits and fees;And, for Community Development Projects:Municipal infrastructure;Business attraction costs. Program Details:There are 4 intake periods per year. Upcoming intake windows are as follows: Application period 10: July 12 - August 25, 2022; CLOSEDApplication period 11: October 6 - November 17, 2022; CLOSED decision will be notified by February 16, 2023;Application period 12: January 12 - February 23, 2023;Application period 13: April 27 - June 15, 2023. Projects may be up to 4 years in length, and may occur over 5 fiscal years;They must have the potential to attract investments and create jobs in Southwestern Ontario;To apply, complete the program eligibility checklist through Transfer Payments Ontario (TPON); Program staff will review the checklist to confirm that your project is eligible. If it is eligible, you will be invited to complete a full application;A complete application consists of the following:Completed application form;Cash flow forecast;Copies of Articles of Incorporation;Corporate family tree (for Business Projects);Three years of financial statements (audited preferred); andLetters of support (optional). 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program does not provide retroactive funding. Only costs occurred after the project start date identified in the Funding Agreement will be considered eligible;This program cannot be combined with other provincial sources of funding. Combination with federal sources may be permitted;Applicants should contact a regional advisor prior to submitting their application;Applications will be evaluated against the following criteria:Potential to attract investment;Jobs created (number and quality);Broader economic and social benefits that will result from the project; andFeasibility (applicant has the appropriate financing, human resources, and experience to complete the project). Forms:Program website: click hereApplication instructions: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The BC Climate Agri-Solutions Fund (BCCAF) provides funding of up to 70% to a maximum of $75,000 to registered and licensed farms to adopt beneficial management practices in the areas of nitrogen management, cover cropping, and rotational grazing. Applicants must be reviewed and approved by a Professional Agrologist prior to application or as part of the project approval process. The intent of the program is to store carbon, reduce greenhouse gases, and improve the biodiversity and soil health of BC farms.Grant Value: 70% of eligible expenses to a maximum of $75,000Turnaround Time: 8 weeks after submission (latest 1 month after the application close date)Eligible Applicants:Have farm status in BC;Registered,  licensed, and/ or  certified  to  conduct  business  in  BC;Must be reviewed and approved by a Professional Agrologist prior to application or as part of the project approval process.Note: If an application has not been reviewed by a Professional Agrologist prior to submission, then the application will undergo an additional technical review.Eligible Costs:Nitrogen Management:Regular fertilizer and inhibitor price;Plan, assessment, design work, and consultancy fees;Cost of other agronomic support/technical training;Soil testing and soil mapping costs;Maximum of $25,000.Offsetting the higher cost of synthetic fertilizer substitutes (manure, compost, digestates);Offsetting higher prices of fertilizer in the spring if applicable;Seed and planting costs to increase legumes in rotation;Cost of fertilizer application equipment and  equipment  upgrades  to  allow  for  banding, side dressing, and injection;If transitioning to manure,  costs associated with spreading, using hoses or equipment for shallow incorporation (to avoid volatilization).Cover Cropping:Costs related to agronomic services;Seed costs with regionally and commodity-appropriate seed;Cost of planting.Rotational Grazing:Costs related to rotational grazing infrastructure (e.g. cross fencing, wildlife-friendly fencing, temporary fencing, and waterers, including remote watering systems when powered by renewable energy);Improved pasture composition (seeding costs for alfalfa, sainfoin, etc.);Grazing management plans, technical assessments, or engineered designs.Note: The only form of worker compensation that is eligible for cost-sharing is fees from external contractors. Farm employee wages are not an eligible expense, nor are fees paid to contractors who have any ownership stake in the farm.Program Details:Maximum cost-shared funding for each of the following categories:Nitrogen Management – $30,000;Cover Cropping – $30,000;Rotational Grazing – $20,000.Maximum of $75,000 in funding across all intakes;Approved projects will have 3 months from their project start date or until January 30, 2025 (whichever comes first) to incur the costs of their activities and submit a final report with cost documentation (receipts/invoices);Project activities and implementation must be completed before June 20, 2025;No extensions will be considered.This program will not accept in-kind contributions, only cash costs;Funding is intended to increase new adoption of BMPs. Farmers cannot receive funding for a BMP if it is already in use;Communications and marketing activities, including public announcements and social media posts regarding project funding must be pre-approved by the IAF communications team.  Contact communications@iafbc.ca for more information.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program does not allow applicants to use program funding in conjunction with other sources of government funding for the same eligible activities (ie. stacking is not allowed);This program does not allow funding to be used retroactively for beneficial management practices already in use;Payments made prior to the project start date are also ineligible.If you are not able to complete your project within the allotted timeframe, you may re-apply in the next funding window.The program is not able to grant extensions to approved projects in this program;Applicants are advised to start the application process as soon as possible as it can take up to 2 business days to validate your organization in the registration stage;Eligible farms do not need an Environmental Farm Plan (EFP) to apply to BCCAF. However, the program does encourage BC farms to complete an EFP. Booking an EFP appointment can be done here;To apply, applicants will need the farm/ranch soil order number. To get the number visit the Government of Canada’s Soils of Canada site; andApplicants are encouraged to include only activities that they are confident will be completed on time and within budget limits. If projects cannot be completed within the timeframe applicants are encouraged to apply in the next intake window.Forms:Program webpage: click hereApplication portal: click here

area of the post-farmgate food production supply chain (i.e. not focused on agricultural activities);Have a specific piloting or demonstration opportunity for a technology or solution that has yet to be commercialized;Have a technology or solution that is at Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) 3 to 7;Technology Readiness Level definitions.Have no other active CFIN-funded projects (approved projects with a signed Master Project Agreement and who have yet to submit their final report);Have adequate financial means and operational capacity to carry out the project;Lead Applicants:Must be led by the project.Note: Project partners are mandatory for the program, but partnerships do not have to be finalized at the Letter of Intent stage.Eligible Activities:Large-scale technology demonstrations;Development and advancement of new technologies.Eligible Projects:Must propose to demonstrate new industry processes, new product categories, new knowledge, or a new application of science;Food product development initiatives, such as the development or iteration of a new brand or product formulation in an existing category (e.g. a new protein bar) are not eligible under the program.Be in one of the below priority areas:Smart Product and Process Development;Food Ecosystem Sustainability;Agile and Safe Supply Chains.Must be carried out in Canada;Be incremental and new; andWould not be undertaken to the same extent without CFIN funding.Eligible Costs:Be necessary to carry out the approved project activities;Be non-recurring and incremental to the day-to-day business activities;Be in one of the following categories:Direct labour;Subcontractors and consultants;Direct materials;Equipment;Land, building, and building improvement;This may include the acquisition costs, construction of new or the expansion of existing facilities, the development of testing facilities, investments in modern buildings, building and land leases (the incremental cost of leasing land during the approved project activities), and permanent building improvement.Other direct costs.Note: Applicants must clearly demonstrate how any outlined costs are directly tied to demonstration activities.       Grant Criteria 
      This program funds innovative plastic recycling and plastic waste reduction projects in BC. Projects may involve reuse, recycling, or re-manufacturing of plastics, implementation of circular business models, or community-based micro-recycling and capacity-building activities. The goal of the program is to reduce plastic waste and develop BC's circular economy. Grant Value: 33%-66% of project costs for Post Consumer Recycled Plastics and Circular Economy Innovation categories;20%-80% for Indigenous Projects and Regional Plastics Innovation categories;Projects under $150,000 may receive up to 100% of project costs covered.Note: Please see the Program Details section for the expected project range.Turnaround Time: 20 business days (Expression of Interest shortlist)Eligible Applicants:All categories:Businesses and non-profits that are owned by BC residents and that operate primarily or solely in BC;Must be registered and pay taxes in BC; andMust have a Federal business number, GST number, and WorkSafe BC number. Regional Plastics Innovation category: Micro-enterprises and small enterprises (employ no more than 10 full-time employees and have generated no more than $100,000 in gross revenue in the previous fiscal year);Must be located and registered within communities located outside of the Metro Vancouver and Capital Regional Districts;Communities with populations under 25,000 located within the Metro Vancouver and Capital Regional districts can request an exemption during the EOI application process. Note: BC-based subsidiaries of organizations that maintain a corporate headquarters outside BC will not be eligible for the program.Eligible Expenses:Costs that are directly related to the proposed project, including but not limited to:Capital expenditures;Salary costs for project-specific labour;Retrofit costs;Contractor and/or partner organization fees;Installation costs;Freight or transportation charges; PPE;Marketing & media-related expenses (only eligible for the Circular Economy Innovation and Indigenous Projects categories); andEducation, outreach, and capacity-building activities (only eligible for the Indigenous Projects category).Ineligible Expenses:Costs that are not related to the project, or that were incurred before the signing of the funding agreement;General operating expenses;Marketing and media-related expenses;Salary costs for general staff;General website or IT upgrades;Website hosting fees;Credit card processing fees;Shipping costs (including packaging for shipping);Real estate;Purchase or lease of private vehicles;Labour costs associated with ongoing operations;Travel and hospitality for staff or contractors; andStructural renovations not specific to the project. Program Details: The fund will support projects that fall under four main funding categories including:Post-Consumer Recycled Plastics:Increase BC's processing capacity to produce more plastic products with PCR plastics and packing manufacturers;Increase the use of PCR plastic in plastic manufacturing; Support PCR plastic product and reuse research, design, and testing, that increase the use of PCR plastic; andExpected Project range: $250,000 to $1,200,000, 66% of costs funded.Regional Plastics Innovation Category:Provide development support and project financing for start-up and early-stage companies in rural communities;Projects funded under RPI will address the same outcomes as other funding streams;Eligible organizations must:Employ no more than 10 full-time employees;Have generated no more than. $100,000 in gross revenue in the previous fiscal year;Located in communities with a population under 25,000.Expected Project range $100,000 to $250,000.Circular Economy Innovation Category:Develop the growth and commercialization of reuse business, to support the phase out of single-use and plastic items;Develop the growth of repair businesses, to extend the life of products and materials and reduce plastic waste;Develop tools or products that connect consumers with circular economy businesses or organizations, including reuse and repair businesses that result in the reduction of plastic waste; andExpected Project range $150,000 to $750,000, 66% of costs funded.Indigenous Projects Category:Support projects led by individuals, communities, businesses, and organizations which self-identify as First Nations, Métis, and/or Inuit;Support plastic waste reduction activities that prevent or eliminate waste through reuse and repair models, and through remanufacturing, value-add processing, and recycling processes; andBuild capacity around the circular economy and plastic waste reduction which are led by Indigenous people, communities and businesses.Expected Project range $75,000 to $150,000.Applications proceed through 3 stages:Submit Expression of Interest (EOI) web form to determine eligibility;Develop and submit a detailed grant proposal that explains how you will use the funds;Negotiate and sign funding agreement.Applications are assessed on a first-come, first-served basis;There is a limit of 1 application per business;Where appropriate and necessary, funds may be issued to the grant recipient as soon as the application is approved;Successful applicants will be required to submit reports every three months until the project conclusion;The "start date" of the project is the day the funding agreement is signed by all parties;Projects must be completed by February 28, 2026; andGrant recipients must agree to participate in audits and follow-up surveys.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program does not provide retroactive funding. Project activities must begin after the application is approved;This program can be combined with other provincial and federal sources of funding;All sources of funding should be declared on the application;Applicants should confirm with program officers if they are planning to combine with program with other CleanBC programs;Meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee that an applicant will be funded; andApplications are assessed in the order received, so applicants are encouraged to apply early if possible. Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guideline (general): click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Digital Transformation Grant (DTG) is designed to assist small businesses with the adoption of technologies and provides advisory support as well as funding of up to $2,500 to permanent 'brick-and-mortar' establishments that are open to the general public for walk-in and onsite purchases of goods and services. Eligible businesses must have between 1-50 employees and cannot be franchises, wholesalers, or manufacturers. The intent of the program is to increase the capacity of businesses through digital transformation.Grant Value: $2,500Turnaround Time: 5-14 business daysEligible Businesses:Registered businesses in Ontario and/or incorporated;Permanent ‘brick-and-mortar’ establishments;Wholesalers and manufacturers are only eligible if the business has a dedicated commercial space where members of the general public (i.e., consumers, can walk in and purchase products or services).Employs 1 - 50 employees;Sole proprietors are considered to be the 1st and possibly the only employee of the business.Is open for business/operating at the time of application (not a start-up);Must be owned by Canadian citizen(s) or permanent resident(s); andMust be owned by Ontario resident(s) who are 18 years of age or older.Note: Businesses do not have to be in zoned commercial core or main street areas to be eligible.Ineligible Businesses:Businesses supplying digital services to other businesses (e.g. website design/development, SEO, programming);Franchises (including those individually owned and operated);Wholesalers and manufacturers;Wholesalers and manufacturers are only eligible if the business has a dedicated commercial space where members of the general public (i.e., consumers, can walk in and purchase products or services).Not-for-profit or charitable organizations;Businesses renting office space on a  temporary basis (month-to-month);Shared workspaces such  as a hot desk or dedicated desk;Purely online businesses or distributors;Home-based businesses; andPrevious Digital Main Street Ontario Grant Program recipients who received a DTG from July 1, 2021, to March 31, 2022 (inclusive).Eligible Costs:Digital Marketing:Hiring a consultant/agency/person to execute digital marketing initiatives.Website:Redesign, and improvement of the existing website;Development of a new website;Accessibility compliance.Software:Graphic design software;Productivity software (LastPass, Hootsuite,  Dropbox, etc.);Social media software (Hootsuite, Buffer, etc.);Security software;Other software as indicated by the program.Digital Training:Ongoing digital training courses (in-person/online).Hardware (limited to $1,000):POS systems;All hardware must be deemed necessary (as determined by the program in its sole discretion).Note: For software subscriptions or social media advertising costs, approved applicants can pay for a year or more in advance OR can include up to 6 months' worth of month-to-month subscription or advertising costs.Ineligible Costs:Business owner’s salary or current employee salary for executing the project;Purchases made prior to grant approval;Microsoft Office or equivalent;Website hosting;Domain name renewal;Software subscription renewal;Signage and printing including LED/digital signage;Logo redesign and rebranding;Unnecessary or excessive equipment (or equipment business already has and wants to upgrade);iPhones or cell phones of any type, no exceptions;Costs of land, building, or vehicle purchase.Program Details:All applicants must complete the following BEFORE applying:The Digital Main Street Assessment;Passing the pre-qualification quiz;The online training;Developing a Digital Transformation Plan.Businesses with multiple locations:Businesses with multiple locations are only eligible to apply for one Digital Transformation Grant.Owners of multiple businesses:Owners with multiple businesses may only apply for one Digital Transformation Grant.Should grant funds still be available after the deadline and all eligible applications have been processed, the application portal will re-open in January 2023 and remain open until September 30th, 2023 (or until grant funds are fully exhausted).

      Best Practices & Forms

      Grant Criteria 
      The CleanBC Building Innovation Fund (CBBIF) provides $500,000 - $1,000,000 in funding to manufacturers and technology developers to commercialize new energy-efficient building technologies, designs, and practices. The program has 5 different streams, all of which are seeking innovations with a minimum Technology Readiness Level of 3 or higher. The intent of the program is to reduce the province's greenhouse gas emissions.Grant Value:Material, Component & System Manufacturing Stream: 60% of eligible costs, $500,000 - $1,000,000Digital Technology Solutions Stream: 60% of eligible costs, $500,000 - $1,000,000Demonstration Projects Stream: 80%-100% of eligible costs, $500,000 - $1,000,000Open Call for Innovations Stream: 60% of eligible costs, $500,000 - $1,000,000Information Sharing & Market Transformation Stream: Up to $500,000Turnaround Time: Within 2 months of the application deadline (February-March 2022)Eligible Applicants:For-profit organizations registered in BC, including but not limited to:Builders;Developers; andManufacturers.Non-profit organizations that have operations in BC, including but not limited to:Industry associations;Universities; andSocieties.BC local municipal and regional governments; andFirst Nations governments and organizations.Eligible Projects:Be located in BC;Must advance innovations in building designs, construction practices, systems, materials, products, or technologies;Must reduce carbon emissions or improve energy efficiency;Have a minimum Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 3;Both retrofit and new construction applications are eligible;Projects may be for any building type; andProjects may be programs.Must include an overview of potential participants and program structure, an expected participation rate and an indication of market needNote: Project proposals must be within the minimum and maximum funding range specified for each stream to be considered.Ineligible Projects:Non-innovative investments that only meet the minimum performance/code benchmark, such as:Routine building or equipment maintenance; orInvestments with minimum performance benchmarks.Projects in which construction has already begun on a given building.Eligible Costs:Energy performance modeling, design, testing, analysis, and engineering services;Product certification and regulatory costs;Development of building components, materials, and technologies (TRL 3 or higher);Development of digital tools including software;Consulting services related to project management;Professional and technical costs required to plan and conduct project activities;Capital costs for related equipment, components, machinery, or retooling;Training of personnel on related equipment or processes;Costs related to the development of documentation, case studies, and public dissemination of information;In the case of a program, incentive disbursements for the above-noted eligible costs;Existing staff costs within the applicant’s organization that are related to project implementation;Organizational overhead and administration costs that are related to project delivery.Maximum of 10% of total eligible costs.Note: Demonstration projects (stream 3) are limited to incremental costs of innovative energy efficiency or low-carbon aspects of the project.Ineligible Costs:PST and GST;Overhead and administration costs that are un-related to project delivery;Costs incurred prior to the signing of a definitive agreement;Existing staff costs within the applicant’s organization that are unrelated to project implementation;Land and building acquisition;Legal costs.Program Details:Funding Streams:Material, Component, and System ManufacturingTo support investment to diversify and expand existing product lines or commercialize new product lines.Digital Technology SolutionsFunding for technology development for new or improved digital solutions.Demonstration ProjectsProjects that involve the construction or renovation of a discrete building and the demonstration of innovative technologies/materials within that building;Must include robust plans for documentation, case studies, and public dissemination of information;Preference will be given to projects with multiple novel technologies or applications that align with the goals in the CleanBC Roadmap to 2030.Open Call for InnovationsFor all other types of activities not covered by other funding streams, including but not limited to research projects, product development, and product testing and certification.Information Sharing and Market TransformationDevelop, synthesize and disseminate a variety of information-sharing materials (e.g.,  case studies, research reports, informational videos, etc.) and undertake related activities (e.g. workshops);Note that the application and evaluation criteria for this stream are separate from the other streams. Interested parties should contact program staff for more details.Each applicant can submit up to 2 applications with no overlapping scope per intake;For-profit organizations must contribute at least 20% of the total eligible project costs;For in-kind contributions to be eligible, they must:Be an eligible cost (see eligible cost section);Be essential to the project's delivery;Be verifiable;Staff hours must be broken down by task and must be assigned hours;The hourly rates must be based on salary and not consulting charge-out rates.Be confirmed by the program staff before or during the application evaluation stage.Funding will be disbursed in two installments, following the completion of the identified deliverables.It is anticipated that all funding will be disbursed before March 31, 2022.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Applicants may stack funds from other programs.       Grant Criteria 
      The Project Development Fund will provide funding for the development of independent film and television productions, on a project-by-project basis, in the form of a non-recoupable development advance. Applications will be evaluated on a first-come, first-served basis until the budget has been fully designated for the fiscal year. Funding is based on a commitment from an eligible triggering agent. Grant Value: Up to $50000Note: The program does not take equity in any of the projects.Turnaround Time: 8 weeks.Eligible Applicants:Must be a company incorporated in British Columbia or Canada with its head office in British Columbia. A majority of the issued common voting shares must be held by BC residents;The applicant company may own 10% or less of the shares of a broadcaster;The applicant company may have 10% of its shares owned by a broadcaster or by a distributor;100% of the copyright of the project being developed must be owned, optioned, or controlled by the applicant; and,The market trigger must be at arm's length from the applicant company.Eligible Triggering Agents:Eligible applicants may apply to Creative BC for a total non-recoupable development advance of up to 50% of the committed cash amount from one of more of the following Triggering Agents for the development of an eligible project An arm’s length bona fide distribution entity (Canadian and international distributors);National Film Board of Canada (NFB co-productions only; 100% owned and controlled NFB productions are not eligible); A licensed public or private broadcaster (Canadian and international broadcasters);Over the top (OTT) subscription-based services (Netflix, Crave, Amazon, Hulu, YouTube Premium originals, Vimeo On-Demand originals);Telus Originals (Small Program Production Agreement);Bell Fund Slate Development; and Telefilm Canada Feature Film Fund (CFFF) Development Program.Eligible Projects:Feature films, destined for theatrical release (live action or animated);Televisions movies, pilots, televisions series and mini-series (live action, animated, variety, human interest, lifestyle and performing arts and entertainment);Short films and web series (live action or animated) (Limit of 10 short films and web series during fiscal year); andDocumentaries and docudramas for television broadcast or theatrical release.Eligible Expenses:Acquisitions of rights including option payments and license fees for platforms or formats;Research including the creation of a report, bible, outline and/or treatment; Writing of script stage including editing and various breakdowns (i.e. outline, treatment, first draft, second draft, final draft and polish and applicable fringes);Production of a demo-tape including, but not limited to, creation of a sizzle reel, presentation pilot, webisode or storyboards;Creation of a character model pack (for animated projects);Polishing, packaging, and a casting phase including creation of a casting reel;Travel costs necessary for creative work (e.g. interviewing, demo-taping and travel by/to/from the director); andAudience Development and Community Outreach Plan. Program Details:The program has an application submission fee of $105:Total development funding available to each eligible applicant(including affiliated related companies) may not exceed $50,000 in the fiscal year 2023/24;The total development funding available to an eligible project for the fiscal year 2023/24 is capped at $10,000;Except for television series, which include dramatic, animated, lifestyle, or documentary, which are capped at $20,000; and,The maximum 3 cumulative funding an eligible project can receive throughout its development history is $30,000, except for television series which are capped at $50,000;Eligible applicants must have a written agreement with one or more of the Triggering Agents confirming their commitment
to provide a development advance for the eligible project;Applications must be submitted to Creative BC no later than 30 days after the date that the BC applicant receives the letter of commitment or agreement with the Triggering Agent.Exceptions to the 30 days may be given. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:If a producer should receive funding from Telefilm’s CFFF Development Program above the $30,000 threshold for one project, they are not eligible to apply for the Telefilm Development Top-Up for that project; The program is not retroactive.Process Best Practices:Applications must be submitted to Creative BC no later than 30 days after the date that the applicant receives the letter or commitment or agreement with the Triggering Agent.Forms:Program webpage: click hereApplication form: click here

The intent of the program is to support the promotion of BC projects in development, securing broadcast sales and stimulating co-production opportunities within international and domestic markets.Grant Value: funding between $1,000 and $2,500Turnaround Time: Applicants notified 3 weeks prior to the commencement of the market applied for.Eligible Applicants:BC resident producers who:Have a track record in the domestic film and television industry;Have been pre-selected to attend a particular market site; Have experience producing domestically owned and controlled digital media content.BC residents are Canadian citizens or Permanent Residents who have resided in BC for at least 200 of the
365 days immediately preceding the date of application and who have filed income tax returns in BC in the
taxation year prior to the date of application.Ineligible Applicants:Producers with only Executive Producer, Co-Producer, and Associate Producer credits.Eligible Expenses:Per Diem - $60 per day in Canada and $80 per day outside Canada;Accommodation - up to $300;Registration Fees (if applicable);Return airfare (based on economy fare);Ground transportation (rideshare, rental car, vehicle fuel costs, taxi, shuttle bus, transit costs, etc.);Design and printing of marketing materials, payable to third parties (e.g. brochures, pitch packages, one sheets, etc.) capped at no more than 20% of the approved direct travel costs; and,Overhead allowance is capped at a maximum of 10% of the approved direct travel costs (to cover related long distance, in-house photocopying, courier costs and administrative expenses).Eligible Market Sites:Markets and conferences that provide BC producers with significant exposure to current market intelligence; opportunities to enhance existing or establish new relationships with international broadcasters, distributors, co-producers and co-financing partners and insights and opportunities for digital media content development and planning.Immersions and other initiatives designed to assist BC producers in acquiring the skills and contacts needed for the successful exploitation of their projects in an international marketplace.Program Details:Individual producers are eligible for support to attend a maximum of four market sites over two fiscal years. One producer per company or project may apply for support to an individual market site;After attending the market, producers are required to submit a final report within 30 business days in order to receive the full funding . This report must include the following:  A narrative report on market activities outlining meetings held, intelligence garnered, co-venture or coproduction deals initiated, rights acquired and financing secured and/or pending; andA final cost report with PDFs of supporting invoices and receipts.
