      Grant Criteria 
      The Sport Hosting Program will provide project-based funding of up to $1,000,000 to help applicants deliver major sports events in Ontario. Supporting sports events will ensure Ontario remains an attractive destination for sport hosting and provides opportunities for local communities to build their capacity to host future events. Grant Value: up to $1,000,000.Turnabout Time: 90 days after application submissionEligible Applicants: Must be legal entities;Have been in existence for one year or longer as of the application date;Not in default of the terms and conditions of any grant or loan agreement with any Ministry or agency of the Government of Ontario;Cannot self-endorse their own application for the Program; andMust be an eligible applicant under one of the three streams of the Program.Stream 1: Provincial/ National Sport Organizations;Eligible Applicants:Provincial Sport/Multi-Sport Organizations recognized under Ontario's Provincial Sport Recognition Policy; Endorsed by the relevant National Sport Organization funded by Sport Canada; National Sport Organizations funded by Sport Canada; andEndorsed by:The relevant Provincial Sport/Multi-Sport Organization recognized under Ontario's Provincial Sport Recognition Policy.Stream 2: Event Host Organizations;Eligible Applicants:Ontario municipalities;Not-for-profit organizations (including Universities and Colleges);Indigenous organizations, First Nation, Metis, or Inuit communities;Endorsed by:The relevant Provincial Sport/Multi-Sport Organization recognized under Ontario's Provincial Sport Recognition Policy; orThe relevant Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Sport funded organization; or The relevant sports body associated with the National Sport Organizations funded by Sport Canada. Stream 3: Emerging Sports;Eligible Applicants:Ontario municipalities;Not-for-profit organizations (including Universities and Colleges); andIndigenous organizations, First Nation, Metis, or Inuit communities.Endorsed by: The relevant Association of IOC Recognized International Sports Federations. Eligible Requirements:Take place in the Province of Ontario;Be open to the public at large without membership in a club or group; andOccur at most once a year. Eligible Events:Events for athletes identified as part of the high-performance and athlete competition pathway plans for the sport;Where the event start date falls within two years of the application date, you. must wait for the appropriate application intake date if the event is taking place more than two years away;National Events:Events that are sanctioned by the National Sport Organization or the International Federation. Include representation from no less than six provinces/territories including Ontario. A country may replace a province; orIs the National Championship for a specific sport, in a specific age group as confirmed by the National Sport Organization or the International Federation. Ontario must be represented in these Championships;International Events: Events that are sanctioned by the International Federation, as per the International Olympic Committee, International Paralympic Committee and/or Panamerican Sport Association; andIncludes representation from no less than two countries, including Canada and one country from outside of North America. An exemption will be provided to events for Canadian National Teams as confirmed by the National Sport Organization funded by Sport Canada.Ineligible Events:Professional sports events;Events where the Government of Ontario is being asked to assume or underwrite any contingent or other liability such as deficit or revenue and rights fee guarantees; andEvents that are charity in nature including activity that has a solicitation of present or future donations of cash or non-cash gifts, or the sale of goods or services to raise funds, whether explicit or implied. Program Details:One Application per festival or event;Sports are eligible for funding twice per calendar year, with a maximum of one international event per calendar year for all 3 streams;The Government of Ontario's financial contribution to the hosting of an event may be up to, but will not exceed, 35% of the total event budget. This includes funding support provided by other provincial programs ( e.g., Tourism Event Marketing Partnership Program) or agencies (e.g., Ontario Trillium Foundation);Stream 1 and 2:National Sport Hosting events are eligible up to $100,000;International Sport Hosting events are eligible up to $1,000,000;Stream 3:National Sport Hosting events are eligible up to $20,000;International Sport Hosting events are eligible up to $75,000;The event start date must be no less than four months before the application deadline;Applications will be accepted for event start dates that are up to two years away from the application deadline; The Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Sport will review applications within 45 days of submissions and provide and outcome to all applicants within 90 days of their application; andApplication deadlines are the 2nd Monday in January and July of each year at 5:00pm EST. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program is stackable with other provincial programs however, the total funding combined with other programs may not exceed 35% of the total event budget;All applicants interested in seeking provincial funding to host a sport event must provide the following documentation when submitting their application through Transfer Payment Ontario:Application Form;Budget;Endorsement Letters;Sanctioning Letter;Projected Economic Impact Report;Letter of Deficit Guarantee; andIncorporation Documents;Successful applicants will be required to:Sign a Province of Ontario Funding Agreement with the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Sport that will outline the terms and conditions for receiving funds;Carry at least $2 million commercial general liability insurance coverages;Obtain the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Sport's approval for any change proposed to the event budget;Use the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Sport branding in all of its promotional materials and acknowledges Government of Ontario funding for the event on all promotional materials that identify and describe the event as set out in Ontario's Logo Usage Guidelines; andPermit to the Province to use the event's brans and logos for non-commercial promotion and communication. Forms:Program webpage: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Music Industry Initiatives program is one of the Amplify BC programs funded by the province of BC to support the growth and development of BC's music industry with funding up to $60,000. The program supports initiatives that grow and develop BC's music ecosystem. Successful projects will build the capacity of B.C.'s music industry through training, knowledge sharing, collaboration and creating new business opportunities.Grant Value: between $2,000 and $60,000 up to 75% of project expenses.Turnabout Time: 4-6 weeks.Eligible Applicants: Active in the music industry in BC;Headquartered in Canada, or located in and eligible to work in Canada;New companies, this program will fund start-ups that are newly registered companies in addition to existing companies;Collectives, projects can be run by an informal group of people. One individual does need to take lead in order to take legal responsibility for the funds; andCollaborations are welcome in this program, primary individual is required to take responsibility for the funds.Ineligible Applicants: Municipalities and other levels of government are not eligible.Eligible Activities:Industry conferences, panels, workshops, forums, and events;Opportunities for training, mentorship, professional development, and fostering new talent;Community infrastructure, services, or digital platforms that provide broad industry benefit;Projects that increase the capacity of underrepresented groups in BC's music industry;Resources, policies, or manuals to share best practices in the areas of business, harm reduction, sustainability, equity, etc;Collaborative business initiatives, showcases, trade missions, or export activities; andResearch projects that develop knowledge to benefit those working in music. Ineligible Activities:Events such as ceremonies, award shows, fundraisers, luncheons, receptions, mixers, galas, and parties;Live music presentations are not eligible through this program;Entrepreneurial activities that primarily benefit one company and its artist roster, clients and/or business partners; andBusiness travel to attend industry events and conferences. Funding for business travel is available through Music BC. Eligible Expenses:All costs required to deliver the project, including salaries and wages.Ineligible Expenses:Capital purchases or operating costs not specific to the project, including utilities, corporate overhead or salaries. Program Details: Individuals, collectives and companies or organizations without financial statements can receive between $2,000 to $20,000;Companies or organizations with financial statements in the form of a compilation engagement, review engagement, or audited statements can receive between $2,000 to $60,000;This program will fund activities and related expenses between January 1, 2023, and September 1, 2024;A minimum of 25% of the total budget must come from other sources which can include personal or company investment, earned revenue or in-kind contribution;Projects that serve underrepresented groups may request 100% funding if no other revenue sources are available;The program encourages applications from underreoresented groups;Research projects may also request a higher percentage of funding if other revenue sources are unavailable; andSuccessful applicants will receive an advance payment of 60-80% and the remaining funds after completion and approval of the final report.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Marquee Event Fund provides support to municipalities and organizations in Ontario for the hosting of large-scale, high impact events that meet the ministry's definition of a marquee event. The objective of this fund is to support events that will draw significant tourist attendance to Ontario and increase tourist expenditures with funding up to 50% of eligible cash operating expenses.Grant Value: Up to 50% of the eligible cash operating expenses.Note: While the grant value above is noted at $0, it is because funding amount is based on a variety of factors, including evaluation score, funding availability within that fiscal year, demand on the program, etc.Eligible Applicants:Be legal entities and have been in existence for 1 year or longer as of the application submission date;Have a Canadian bank account at a Canadian financial institution conducting business in Ontario;Not be in default of the terms and conditions of any grant or loan agreement with any ministry or agency of the Government of Ontario;Ontario municipalities that have identified hosting major events as part of their tourism strategy; andFor-profit or non-profit organizations that have event management and/or hosting as part of their mandate.Eligible Events:Occur in the province of Ontario;Be open to the public at large without membership in a club or group;Meet the ministry's definition of a marquee event;Ineligible Events:Events that are still in the bidding process;Amateur sporing events that are receiving funding under the Ontario Sport Hosting Program;Events that recur in Ontario on an annual or biennial basis; Events that seek to attract only a special interest audience or recruit new members (e.g., religious or political gatherings and workshops); andTrade fairs, events of a primarily commercial nature (e.g., consumer shows, symposia, conventions, meetings and conferences, seminars and clinics, etc). Eligible Expenses: Must directly relate to specific expenditures for the delivery of the proposed event and must not include costs that would have otherwise been incurred by the applicant;Must be linked to programming activities and other services that are accessible to the public;Event security;Accessibility services and improvements to comply with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act 2005. Programming and Production:Performance and appearance fees paid to artists, musicians, professional athletes, entertainers, and presenters, including travel, accommodation, and booking costs;Programming costs, including interactive, experiential, and/or accessible programming;Production costs, including broadcasting, audio, and visual support (e.g. rental of sound and
lighting equipment and rental of event venue);Insurance for artworks specific to the event/exhibit;Media Buys (to promote the event):Media buys targeting Ontario audiences residing 40km or more from the event location;Media buys targeting out-of-province tourists;Eligible Media buys, in market noted above include:Placement of targeted paid advertising (e.g., broadcast, digital, print, social);Purchase of out- of- home advertising space (e.g., billboard, transit shelter space purchase);Geo-targeted digital and social media advertising buys; andDistribution costs for printed materials.Ineligible Expenses:Administrative and overhead costs (e.g., rent, telephone, insurance, computers, utilities, maintenance costs);Salaries, travel costs and expenses for permanent staff as well as for event/project staff;Hospitality costs, excluding those for artists, performers and presenters;Volunteer costs, other than those specifically for training for the event;Fees paid to consultants;Event hosting licensing fees/bid fees;Site and visitor services costs, other than event security and accessibility services and improvements to comply with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005;Permit and licensing fees;Membership and subscription fees;Translation costs;Insurance costs;Legal, audit or interest fees;Budgets deficits;Marketing creative, production, staff, or consulting cos;Media buys in Ontario targeting in-province attendees who travel less than 40 kilometres from
the event;Printing of publications, production of television programming, digital assets, videos, DVDs, USB
keys;Mobile application and website development and upgrades;Promotion-based activities, booking/packaging costs, media familiarization tours,
hosting/payment to media/bloggers.
7
Other Ineligible Expenses; Audience surveys, research or economic impact studies;Alcohol or cannabis-related products;Capital costs (e.g., construction materials, motorized vehicles, land acquisition, purchase of
equipment, stages, fixed or portable seating, lighting structures, computers/notebooks,
depreciable assets);Capital repayments;Repayments to other funding programs;Competition prizes, prize money, and monies paid to competition participants as well as awards,
trophies and medals;Any costs for gifts, gratuities, honoraria, or other items of personal benefit; Harmonized Sales Tax or refundable expenses (e.g., security deposits);Any costs incurred for events held outside Ontario;Any expenses that will be covered by in-kind revenues or in-kind services or funded by another
source;Any costs related to transactions by organizations directly affiliated with the applicant or
between enterprises under common ownership or control; andAny expenses not directly paid by the recipient organization (i.e. by the organization
directly receiving the funding).Program Details: Applications must be submitted at least 4 months prior to the event start date;1 application per event between the Reconnect Ontario program and Reconnect Ontario - Marquee Event Fund;There is a maximum of 2 applications per organization and this must be for two separate events;Applicants are eligible to apply for up to a max of 50% of eligible event cash operating expenses;The value of in-kind expenses is not included in the determination of event cash operating expenses; andThe operating expenses described must be for the event itself and not the operating expenses of the applicant organization.

creation/retention, new revenues, new customers, follow on investment and productivity
improvements).Eligible Expenses: Technology Demonstration Project costs related to the adoption of the digital technology outlined in the DMAP;Costs related to website search optimization;NOTE: The plan cannot be solely for website search optimization.Costs related to installation of a technology platform;Cost of back-office solutions to support a technology strategy;Costs of social media advertising, note plan cannot be strictly social media advertising;Costs related to the creation of customer databases;Development of new technology;Salaries for technical staff directly related to the demo program, this means one-time labour expenditures;Upgrading existing technology site for added functionality, re-design of an existing site is not eligible;Equipment expenses must not be more than 20% of budget;Software including: Softwares to track and manage product inventory, as well as fulfill and ship orders;Software for product databases;Software to track sales, market to customer, offer discounts, maintain a loyalty program;Software to simplify marketing;Cyber security software of certifications;       Grant Criteria 
      The Housing Supply Challenge provides up to $150,000 in funding to fund activities that will support the adoption of innovative construction solutions. Eligible applicants may be for-profit, or non-profit so long as the entities are incorporated. The intent is to increase the capacity to increase the supply of affordable and environmentally-friendly housing.The number of housing units created in the Challenge time frame isn’t part of the evaluation. A building (or multiple units) may be created or renovated as part of the challenge. This is only if the purpose is to test refinements, adaptations, or new ways of applying a process, technique, system, or material solution so that it can be replicated or scaledGrant Value: Up to $150,000Turnaround Time: Funding decisions will be issued between April 13, 2023, to July 2023Eligible Applicants:Be a legal entity incorporated in Canada;Be one of the following organization types:For-profit organizations;Housing developers, builders, construction professionals, general contractors, technology companies, start-ups, architects, etc.Non-profit organizations (ie. housing providers, associations, research centers, etc.);Indigenous governments, organizations, and groups;Canadian post-secondary institutions;Provincial, territorial, Indigenous, municipal, local, and regional governments.Not be in default under any previous Stage or Round of the Housing Supply ChallengeNote: Organizations/individuals associated with CMHC, Evergreen, and Innovation 7 are ineligible to apply.Eligible Activities:Research (e.g. scaling opportunities);Data collection or acquisition (e.g. data acquired while testing a prototype);Testing construction systems (e.g. , testing a building component in a wall);Public engagement and consultation (including honoraria for consultation relating to reconciliation and community consultation costs);Obtaining insurance, consulting, or professional services related to the development of the solution (e.g. testing with industry members who will use or be impacted by the solution);Certification processes (if the timeline is possible within the Challenge);Administrative costs (e.g. staff time spent addressing regulatory dependencies);Training (e.g. applicable if required for the Applicant`s solution to be feasible and viable, to contribute to reconciliation efforts, to build skills for working with vulnerable populations, to provide educational support to residents who need to learn how to use new climate-compatible housing components in order for the solution to be fully operational);Business and/or marketing plan development;Development of plans for prototyping and demonstrating an adaptation of a construction innovation; andPresentation costs for demonstrating a construction innovation.Program Details:Applicants may submit no more than 1 application per Round of the Housing Supply Challenge;No minimum number of units is required for the program;Application process - 3 stages:Initial proposalOnly 25 applicants will be shortlisted to proceed to stage 2;Important dates:Launch: December 1, 2022Submission deadline: April 13, 2023, 2:00 pm ETEvaluation and shortlisting: April 2023 to July 2023Notification of results: From July 2023 to December 2023Design & FeasibilityApplicants shortlisted for Stage 2 would be eligible to receive no more than $150,000 in Incubation Funding to fund the further development of their solution;Applicants in this stage will receive an applicant guide and evaluation criteria for Stage 2;Applicants have 5 months to develop their application package;Only selected recipients will move on to Stage 3;Important dates:Participants shortlisted: July 2023Initial design & feasibility: 5 months in durationFinal submission deadline: December 2023Submission deadline: December 14, 2023, 2:00 pm ETEvaluation and shortlisting: December 2023 to March 2024Notification of results: March 2024ImplementationApplicants selected at the end of Stage 2 may be eligible to receive funding to implement the selected solution;Have 12 months for implementation;Duration: March 2024 to March 2025.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Summer Experience Program (SEP) provides funding of up to $3,812 to eligible not-for-profit organizations, municipalities, Indigenous organizations, and First Nation communities to create meaningful summer employment opportunities for students. The objective is to provide quality, supervised work experience for students in summer positions that develop skills that are career-related and transferable to the general labour market.Grant Value: Funding up to $3,812Turnaround Time: Applicants will be notified mid April.Eligible Applicants: Not-for-profit organizations that have been incorporated for at least 1 year; Municipalities;Indigenous organizations; and First Nations communities. Eligible Students:All students must be currently enrolled in a secondary, or post-secondary institution or within six months
of graduation and have reached the age of 15 upon commencement of employment;Students must be employed full time for a minimum employment contract length of 232 hours or 32 days
at 7.25 hours per day;Proof of student enrolment must be provided to the employer;Students must be residents of Ontario during the period of employment;Students must be eligible to work in Canada and have a Social Insurance Number (SIN); andStudents should be living in Ontario at the time they start work.Employer Responsibilities:The employer is responsible for ensuring CPP, EI and other mandatory contributions are made to the appropriate level of government;Student statutory holiday compensation must be in accordance with the Employment Standards Act (ESA);Provisions for student's sick time should adhere to the employing organization's sick time policy for students;The Summer Experience Program application form includes Terms and Conditions that must be adhered to by all applicants that receive a SEP grants; andWhen all employee turns 18, employers must start deducting and submitting Canada Pension Plan contributions.Program Details: If an applicant is successful then a once off instalment of $3,812 will be paid;Recipient organizations must keep Ministry staff informed of any changes that affect the SEP position;Overtime is accepted on an occasional basis however it is not funded by the program;Students must got through a competitive process each year (e.g. students must apply for the position and be screened in). Rehiring a student without going through a competitive process is not allowed;The student's interest and career goals should relate to the job for which they have applied;Wherever possible, consideration should be given to hiring students from the local area. Funding received from the SEP cannot be used for relocation expenses; Final report is to be submitted by September 15, 2023;

Eligible projects include the commercialization of innovation or the adoption of an innovation by a startup or SME, prioritizing critical sectors, diverse organizations and equity-deserving entrepreneurs that are investing in clean inclusive growth.Grant Value: Up to $100,000 for SME stream and up to $25,000 for start-up stream. Turnaround time: Approximately 30 business days after submission.Eligible Applicants: SMEs:A registered industrial for-profit incorporated business, partnership or cooperative;Located in southern Ontario;Having fewer than 500 full-time equivalent (FTE) employees; andHaving $100,000 to $100 million in annual revenue declared in Canada during its last complete tax reporting year (or during the last 12 months for monthly and quarterly filers).Startups: A registered for-profit incorporated business, partnership or cooperative;Located in southern Ontario;Formed on or after January 1, 2020; andAt the pre-revenue/prototype stage to early commercialization stage.Eligible Costs: New incremental labour;Expertise;Capital; andNon-capital.Ineligible Costs:Activities in support of regular maintenance and/or ongoing operational costs;Cost incurred prior to the eligibility date as defined in the Contribution Agreement;Costs of land, building or vehicle purchase;Refinancing;Costs of intangible assets such as goodwill, whether capitalized or expensed;Depreciation or amortization expenses;Interest on invested capital, bonds, debentures, or mortgages;Bond discount;Losses on investments, bad debts and any other debts;Fines or penalties;Costs related to litigation;Non-incremental wages;Fees for administrators, including payments to any member or officer of the Recipient’s Board of Directors;Opportunity costs;Hospitality and entertainment costs;Costs of individual membership in a professional body (e.g. professional designations); andLobbyist fees.Program Details: This program has two streams one for SMEs and one for Startups. technology application that will satisfy the need of an eligible applicant; andThe clean technology to be implemented must be at minimum Technology
Readiness Level (TRL) of 8 or greater.Technologies must help food and beverage processors embrace automation in their
facilities, reduce waste and energy consumption, significantly reduce their carbon
footprint, and transition towards a net-zero future. Eligible Projects: Projects that support the adoption and integration of new clean technologies into the applicant's operations;This funding could be used to fund advisory, acquisitions, and commissioning costs related to the new clean technology; andThe project must be conducted in collaboration with a clean technology provider.Three scenarios that may lead to an eligible project include:Food and beverage processors ready to adopt and integrate a clean technology with an
identified clean technology provider;Food and beverage processors with an identified clean technology need, but no
established provider; andProven clean technology providers looking for an adopter in the food and beverage
processing industry.Demonstrate the impact of project financing on reducing the applicant's carbon footprint and/or transitioning to a green economy and net-zero future;Provide a Project Milestone Plan that demonstrates how implementation will be achieved beginning no earlier than June 10, 2022, and ending no later than March 21, 2024;Generate outcome with significant positive benefits to southern Ontario including but not limited to, revenue generation, jobs created and maintained, attracting new investment, generating IP, etc.Eligible Activities: Product integration/adoption. Activities that support the applicant's ability to integrate or adopt new clean technologies into their operations including equipment costs;Regulatory compliance. Activities that focus on supporting access to specialized technical services, certifications, regulatory requirements, etc;Internal employee labour. andIn-kind contributions.Program Details: Total funding for this program is $1.5 million from June 2022 through to March 2024;Final intake is open and deadline is October 6, 2023;If funding is not exhausted then there will be rolling intake;The program enhances competitiveness of the food and beverage processing and clean technology sectors; The program helps de-risk the adoption and integration of clean, or net-zero, technologies in souther Ontario;       Grant Criteria 
      The 2 Billion Trees program aims to motivate and support new tree planting projects. Over the course of 10 years, by 2031 up to $3.2 billion will be invested in tree planting efforts to support provinces, territories, third-party organizations and Indigenous organizations plant two billion trees across Canada. Grant Value:Up to $40 million per fiscal year; ORUp to 50% of eligible project costs for regular applicants or up to 75% of eligible project costs for Indigenous-led projectsTurnaround Time: Approximately 6 months. Eligible Applicants: A municipal or local government or one of their agencies, or a regional municipal organization;A not-for-profit organization registered in Canada, such as a charitable organization, volunteer organization, community, professional, industry or other association, land conservation organization, or non-government organization;A for-profit organization (legally incorporated or registered in Canada);An Indigenous organization (for-profit and not-for-profit) or community; andOrganizations looking to be project aggregators. Potential aggregators should describe their concept of operations in their project description. Ineligible Applicants:Individual landowners;Provincial and Territorial Governments;Federal Government Departments; andCrown Corporations.Eligibile Expenses:Salaries and benefits, and employee recruitment and training;Professional, technical, and capacity building services;Community and landowner engagement;Purchase or lease of land for nurseries to grow seedlings;Translation, production, printing, publication and distribution, and media services;Contractors, such as for tree planting and silviculture;Materials and supplies, such as seeds and trees for planting;Transportation;Facilities;Machinery and equipment;Travel expenses including accommodation and venue expenses; Honoraria and ceremonial costs where Indigenous recipients or Indigenous partners are involved; andOverhead expenditures, provided that they are directly related and essential to the conduct of the project, up to 15% of eligible expenditures. Eligible Projects: Contribute to incremental planting and associated management of trees and forests. Activities must be in addition to that which would occur without the initiative, and not legally required, such as following commercial activity or as a condition for impact assessment approval;Contribute clear benefits in terms of net carbon sequestration and greenhouse gas emission reduction in the period up to 2050, and seek to minimize GHG emissions in the early years. Examples of carbon sequestration considerations include: Selecting planting sites where no or minimal vegetation removal is required;Purchasing seedlings from local nurseries and minimizing the distance travelled for planted, monitoring and maintenance, thereby reducing transportation emissions;Limiting intensive site preparation activities, such as salvage harvesting after an insect infestation, trenching, or vegetation removal, all of which can cause substantial emissions early in the project;Reducing the use of pesticides/herbicides; and Limiting equipment use.Seek to achieve human well-being and environmental co-benefits;Contribute to planting that is ecologically suitable or otherwise appropriate for its location, given site conditions (this includes not planting on sites that naturally would be non forest ecosystems, such as natural grasslands or wetlands); and Result in permanent additions to forests, improve existing forests, or allow for permanent protection of forests.Ineligible Projects: Projects that help organizations that have a legal obligations to regenerate forests, such as a legal obligation to regenerate after harvesting under sustainable forest management regimes; andProjects that regenerate forests on private lands as part of business-as-usual commercial forestry activities.Program Details: Max funding through the Tree Planting streams is $40 million per fiscal year, for a maximum of 8 fiscal years (for a total of 320 million); The maximum that NRCan contribution for eligible project costs is 50% of eligible expenditures;For Indigenous-led projects the 2BT Program will consider up to 75% of eligible costs for the tree planting projects;Apply by January 16, 2025, for a decision by July 2025;Apply by May 15, 2025, for a decision by November 2025;Apply by September 18, 2025, for a decision by March 2026;There are currently 3 streams under the 2 Billion Tree Program:Mass Planting Stream;Small-Scale Planting Stream;Urban/ Suburban Stream;Mass Planting Stream: Must plant an average of 500,000 seedlings/trees per calendar year (January to December) in each year in which planting occurs. Projects can include Long-Term-Planting Work;Allow for planting to occur across multiple sites, as long as the average number of trees planted per calendar year, in years which planting occurs, is equal to or greater than 500,000;Can include forest or tree restoration portions of work involving riparian zones, habitat restoration and
other ecosystem improvement projects;Cannot be located in urban and suburban areas;When preparing a Mass planting Stream proposal, please consider the following: Choice to pursue afforestation, reforestation or both;choice of seed sources, variety of tree species of trees planted and their ability to survive and grow in the climate that may exist over the next century; co-benefits resulting from chose tree plating activities including permanence.Small-Scale Planting Stream:Must plant an average of 50,000 trees per calendar year (January to December) in each year in which planting occurs;Allow for planting to occur across multiple sites, as long as the average number of trees planted per calendar year, in years in which planting occurs, is equal to or greater than 50,000;Can include forest or tree restoration portions of work involving riparian zones, habitat restoration and other ecosystem improvement projects;Cannot be located in urban and suburban areas;Must have clearly defined planting sites;When preparing a Small-scale Planting Stream proposal, please consider the following: Choice to pursue afforestation, reforestation or both;choice of seed sources, variety of tree species of trees planted and their ability to survive and grow in the climate that may exist over the next century; co-benefits resulting from chose tree plating activities including permanence.Urban/ Suburban Stream): Must plant an average of 10,000 trees per calendar year (January to December) in each year in which planting occurs;The program recommends collaborative project proposals in order to meet this threshold, as needed;Allow for planting to occur across multiple sites, as long as the average number of trees planted per calendar year, in years in which planting occurs, is equal to or greater than 10,000;Must be located in and around urban areas, population centres or communities;Must have clearly defined planting sites;When preparing a Urban/Suburban Stream proposal, please consider the following:Choice of seed sources, variety of tree species of trees planted and their ability to survive and grow in the climate that may exist over the next century;Co-benefits resulting from chosen tree planting activities including permanence.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Workers in Transition program consists of wage and training subsidies for people wishing to transition from their current industry to one that is within the electricity sector.  The program provides funding up to $15,000 which will be paid to employers who hire people from different industries looking to move into the electricity sector. Grant Value: Up to 50% of wages or $15,000.Turnaround Time: Up to 5 business days.Eligible Employers:Canadian-owned companies;Companies that are involved with the generation, distribution, and transmission of electricity renewables;Supporting organizations that aid in that goal may also be eligible.Note: Employers working in renewable energy and/or solar energy are eligible.  Eligible Applicants: Candidates must be Canadian citizens, permanent residents or hold refugee status in Canada;Must be legally able to work in Canada according to the laws and regulations of the province or territory; andIndividuals looking to transition from another industry into the electricity sector.Ineligible Applicants:Individuals with an open work permit or study permit are not eligible; andIndividuals that have previous experience in the electricity sector. Program Details:  This program is to help individuals transition from their current industry to one that is within the electricity sector (generation, distribution, transmission);The wage subsidy covers up to 50% of the wages up to $15,000 per application; Although there is no extra incentive for training, third-party contracted training that the employer had to arrange and pay for is an eligible expense that can be part of the wage subsidy total amount; Other wrap-around support like, accommodation, transportation, remote work support or child care supports may also be eligible as part of the wage subsidy total amount on a case-to-case basis; andPositions need to be full-time, however there may be some flexibility here as some jobs get hours based on what work is available.

      Best Practices: Funding is retroactive to April 1, 2023;This program cannot be used in conjunction with other government funding programs; Candidates don't have to be identified before applying for the grant (spots can be filled after an employer gets approved); Employers must create an account to apply for funding;Once application is approved and contract is signed the employer must complete a learning plan for the candidate; andOnce learning plan is done that is when employers can start submitting claims generally every 30 days.Forms:Program webpage: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Comprehensive Energy Saving (CES) program offers a financial incentive of up to $250,000 to participants that install eligible measures from a minimum of two distinct CES core categories that meet the minimum incentive requirements. Projects must occur within Alberta and meet project timeline requirements. The objective of the program is to upgrade existing buildings with new energy-saving installations to help drive Alberta to a net zero greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions target.Grant Value: Up to $250,000 per CES core category or up to 50% eligible expenses.Turnaround Time: 5 business days.Eligible Applicants:Eligible participants must meet all the following requirements:Carries on a business or is acting on behalf of an Indigenous community. A business includes, but not limited to: Non-profits;co-operatives;Sole proprietorships;Partnerships;Corporations.A privately owned entity and is not a Public Authority; andReceives 50% or less of its annual revenue from a Public Authority.e.g. a participant that receives 25% of their funding from a Public Authority is eligible.Eligible Facilities: Must meet the following 6 requirements:The facility is located in Alberta;The applicant must own or lease a facility; If an applicant leases the facility, permission
must be obtained from the landlord.The facility has been in operation for one year or
more;The facility meets at least one of the following:used solely for commercial or industrial
purposes (the facility’s electricity rate class is
“non-residential”),
E.g., a facility on farmland with a nonresidential electricity rate class is
eligible;is comprised of only common areas of a multi-unit residential dwelling, or is a remote industrial facility with an
applicable facility ID;The facility is not a Large Emitter or has opted into
the TIER Regulation at any time during the term of
the participant acceptance; andThe facility will operate for the lifetime of the
Measure.Eligible Projects: All projects must meet the following four conditions to be eligible: Projects must consist solely of installing Eligible Measures from a minimum of two distinct CES Core
Categories and meet the minimum incentive requirements in the Eligible Measures List;The Measures must be installed at the same Eligible Facility1
, as set out in the Application Summary;The Participant has not already received an incentive through this CES Program or a previous
component of the ESB Portfolio for the Eligible Measures included in the Eligible Project; andIs submitted as part of an Application before the application deadline contained in this CES Guidebook.Eligible Contractors:All projects must assign a contractor, they can be an external third party, or internal to the business providing they have the appropriate qualifications.Basic contractor requirements: Be a registered business in Alberta; Have a current certificate from the Workers’
Compensation Board (WCB) or evidence of WCB
exemption;Have commercial general liability insurance with at least $2,000,000 for each occurrence, automobile insurance with at least $2,000,000 liability and professional liability insurance with at least $1,000,000 per claim; andProvide warranties for work on projects as applicable.Eligible Measures: On-site Generation and Renewables;Lighting;Space, Process, and Water Heating;Cooling and ventilation;Compressed air;Refrigeration and food services;Motors ad drivers; andBuilding envelope and windows.Eligible Expenses: Expenses that are incurred for the purchase or installation of Eligible Measures;Expense should not have been previously submitted and received an incentive earlier;Eligible measure is fully installed and in commercial operation and the expenses have incurred prior to project completion date; Eligible Contractor is a third party to the participant the expense is one of the following:energy modelling costs;engineering costs;permit costs;inspection costs;procurement and construction costs;equipment purchase costs;installation equipment costs;installation labour costs; andcosts of interconnecting with the electrical and/or natural gas distribution system; andEligible Contractor is not a third party to the participant: the expense is less than or equal to the fair market value of the Eligible Measure equipment only. Labour and installation costs cannot be included.Ineligible Expenses:Expenses that are not directly required to purchase or install the eligible measure; Costs where the applicable eligible measure is not installed and in commercial operation;Costs to repair or refurbish existing or used equipment; Costs to prepare or modify the eligible facility;Costs for aesthetic improvements;Costs to operate, maintain or upkeep equipment;GST or any other provincial sales taxes;Costs to purchase warranties or insurance;Costs of battery or storage equipment and installation;Overhead, administrative or internal costs;Costs to complete Program documents;Costs for energy modelling, unless incurred as part of the installation of an eligible measure; andAny costs that have received financial incentives funding, subsidies or grants from nay other third party.Program Details: Project duration is up to 6 months;Depending on the project, the cap ranges from 25-50%;The submission deadline is March 31, 2023 with projects needing to be complete by March 31, 2024; andFunding will be allocated on a first-come,  first-served basis once a Participant receives a Pre-Approval Notice.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Heavy-duty Vehicle Efficiency Program offers up to $50,000 on qualifying fuel-efficiency equipment. The program consists of two parts: a course and an application-based incentive program that provides rebates on qualifying fuel-efficiency equipment. The aim of the program is to reduce heavy-duty on-road commercial vehicle greenhouse gas emissions in BC.Grant Value: Up to $15,000 per vehicle or up to $50,000 per fleet.Turnaround Time: 2-4 weeks.Eligible Applicants:Have one or more heavy-duty commercial vehicles in their fleet (a vehicle with a gross vehicle weight greater than 11,794kg) that is licensed and insured to operate in BC;Have a current National Safety Code (NSC) certificate with a satisfactory rating;Conduct business in BC;Have a terminal located in BC; andHave a company delegate take and pass the CleanBC Heavy-Duty Vehicle Efficiency program course  (August 1, 2023 to August 31, 2025) prior to taking possession of fuel-saving equipment. Program Details:Only fuel saving equipment purchases and taken possession during the program year is eligible for rebate (September 1, 2024 to August 31, 2025)This program consists of two parts: a course and an application-based incentive program; At least one company representative must complete and pass the CleanBC Heavy-Duty Vehicle Efficiency Program course within the program year prior to applying for program incentive rebates;All fuel-efficiency equipment approved through the program incentives must be purchased and installed in BC by a BC-based facility/ company as follows: Within the program year; andInstalled or taken possession of after participating in and passing the program course.Provide a completion application, which includes:A current copy of your company's National Safety Code (NSC) carrier profile demonstrating a "satisfactory" rating;A copy of the applicant's Certificate of Incorporation or business registration; andDocumentation that qualifying the equipment/device has been purchased and installed (e.g. Bill of Sale, insurance documents, lease agreements)Program Course: The course is free of charge and its aim is to teach participants the impact of climate change;The course will include the following:An overview of CleanBC's GHG emissions reduction legislation and the BC road transportation industry's role in BC's emissions reduction target;Fuel-efficiency management practices that carriers can adopt to reduce their fuel consumption such as driving techniques, installing aerodynamic devices, utilizing wide tires and/or reducing idling time;Why and what should be included in a company fuel management program for any size of fleet;Participation in group exercises to apply course lessons;An open-book quiz (a grade of 80% is required to pass the course); andA course handbook.Once the course is successfully complete, participants are eligible to apply for CleanBC Heavy-Duty Vehicle Efficiency Program Incentives.  Rental Companies: This applies to rental companies that own and rent commercial vehicles with a gross vehicles weight greater than 7,257kg;The rental company must have at least one rental office in BC, and only vehicles that are rented from and maintained in BC, are eligible to apply for Program incentives;The rental vehicle for which incentive funding is being applied for (tractor or trailer) must be:Part of the rental company's short-term rental fleet (rented for a period of 30 days or less, long term rentals will not be considered);Returned, after each rental, back to the BC rental company's terminal; andMaintained in the rental company's short-term rental fleet for a period of no less than one year from the time the Program incentive dollars are issued.Motor Carriers: Each eligible company with distinct NSC number and corporate registration must send their own representative to complete and pass the CleanBC Heavy-Duty Vehicle Efficiency Program Course in order to apply for Program incentives;Eligible companies can apply for the Program Incentives for their owner/operator vehicles as long as the owner/operator operates under the applicant company's NSC, AND the applicant company can demonstrate it has the support of the owner/operator, by way of a letter of support, for the application pertaining to their vehicle.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: This program is not retroactive, equipment/vehicles cannot be purchased before at least one company representative has completed and passed the CleanBC Heavy-Duty Vehicle Efficiency Program course;This program cannot be stacked with other federal and provincial funding;Participants must have at least one company representative take and pass the CleanBC Heavy-Duty Vehicle Efficiency Program course;Process Best Practices:By accepting the rebate applicants agree to maintain the qualifying equipment which the rebate was granted for a period of no less than one year from the date the rebate was granted; andBCTA reserves the right to audit vehicles in which program incentive rebate have been awarded for a period of up to a year after the program incentive rebate has been awarded.Forms: Program Webpage: click hereCourse Registration: click hereList of Qualifying Equipment and Incentives: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The program provides up to $250,000 in funding to SMEs to commercialize their products, achieve optimal market position, increase revenue and potentially expand into global markets. The program is designed to de-risk the commercialization process by providing funds and coaching to SMEs. Grant Value: Up to $250,000.Turnaround Time: 3-4 weeksEligible Applicants: For-profit organizations that are either:Incorporated;General partnerships registered in Alberta;Limited partnerships registered in Alberta; orLimited liability partnerships registered in Alberta.Be Alberta-based;Have a significant physical and corporate operational presence in Alberta;Have appropriate Alberta ownership; andDiscernible intent that operational benefits will flow primarily within the Province of Alberta;Exist as a corporate person, with up-to-date corporate filings;Be authorized to undertake the proposed project, and execute a grant with Alberta Innovates on the standard terms; Have fewer than 500 full-time employees;Have less than $50,000,000 in annual gross revenue; andMust be in good standing with Alberta Innovates or its subsidiaries (InnoTech Alberta, C-FER Technologies).Eligible Partners: Exist as a corporate person, with up-to-date corporate filings; Be authorized to undertake the proposed project; Demonstrate that the relationship between the Applicant and Partner/ Strategic Partner/ Service Provider/ Collaborator does not create a conflict of interest; Be at arm's length from the Applicant;Must not have a conflict of interest with the applicant.Provide a letter indicating the Partner's/ Service Provider's/ Collaborator's intention to participate in the Project at the time of application; Have the financial capability to purchase or enter into a distribution agreement of the product upon Project completion of a demonstration;Show tangible resources committed to the Project; andMust be in good standing with Alberta Innovates or its subsidiaries (InnoTech Alberta, C-FER Technologies).Eligible Projects: Show that the product is a viable technology at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 to 8; Be stepped with critical "go/no go" milestones with measurable target outcomes; Be completed within an 18-month term; Have the participation of at least 1 International Project Partner(s); Outline the financial contribution required by Applicant; and/or Comply with other criteria that Alberta Innovates may develop from time to time. Eligible Expenses:Labour costs, directly related to the project;Costs of materials;Acquisitions of property;Acquisitions of software or information databases;Direct operating costs;Technology transfer to the Applicant from an Alberta public sector research organization;Travel expenses if they are a necessary part of accomplishing the project and also have to be pre-approved by Alberta Innovates; andAny other expense pre-approved by Alberta Innovates in writing.Ineligible Expenses: Any cost incurred prior to the project start date;Any costs which have been or will be funded by other government funding;Transactions between related persons; Provisions for contingencies;Allowance for interest of debt;Losses on investments, bad debts and expenses for collection charges;Losses on other projects or activities outside the Alberta Portion of the Project;Fines and penalties;Unreasonable compensation for Project labour; Costs for professional training and development;costs related to land and buildings;depreciation and amortization charges;Advertising costs;Costs associated with applying for government grants and programs;Costs of internships or support for students of knowledge institutions;Basic professional services, fees and disbursements, such as ongoing routine accounting, tac and legal business requirements; Routine testing and maintenance; Costs relating to meals, entertainment, hospitality, alcohol and gifts;Federal and provincial income taxes, goods and services taxes; and Any other costs deemed ineligible by Alberta Innovates.Program Details: Funding is provided to support SMEs to find and enter a partnership with an "International Project Partner" for further product development or to pilot the technical and business merits of their product with the goal to prove the product value, and advance commercialization;Objectives of the program include: Have applicants build a relationship with an International Project Partner for collaborative development and testing, leveraging industry knowledge or access to new distribution channels;Establish an early to late-stage pilot;Form long-term business partnerships that extend market access;Provide access to new capital sources;Increased global competitiveness.The support of a technology development advisor is required for the ITP. They provide guidance and coaching and assess the Applicant's ITP readiness;Project Activities may include:Developing and testing technology;Piloting in an operational or test environment to move towards commercialization.Alberta Innovates will match the applicant's contributions for eligible project costs to a maximum investment of $250,000; andThe applicant's matching funds must be in the form of 50% cash and 50% in-kind contributions;E.g. Alberta Innovates investment of $250,000, Alberta SME $250,000 (50% cash and 50% In-Kind) and International project partner $250,000 (50% cash and 50% In-Kind).

      Grant Criteria 
      The BC Manufacturing Job Fund provides funding of up to $10 million to manufacturers to conduct business/project planning as well as invest in new manufacturing infrastructure, technology, and processes. The program has 2 funding streams: the Project Readiness stream and the Capital Investment stream.  The intent of the program is to boost productivity, increase competitiveness and support clean and inclusive growth.Grant Value:Project Readiness stream: Up to 50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $50,000Capital Investment stream: Average of 20% of eligible costs to a maximum of $10,000,000Turnaround Time: 4 weeks after the initial proposalEligible Applicants:Registered for-profit manufacturing businesses in BC;Have established operations (at a proposed project location or elsewhere);Have an established employee base;Be in a viable financial position.Have a business plan and/or financial records demonstrating the ability to pay off short-term debts;Not in foreclosure or for sale;Paid taxes in the last fiscal year.Eligible Projects:Be located in B.C.;Contribute to long-term regional economic growth, sustainability, and/or diversity;Be financially viable and leverage market demand;Create, maintain, or diversify job opportunities for local workers;Have a high degree of readiness and bring direct benefits to communities; andDemonstrate alignment with program goals (see Best Practices section below).Eligible Expenses:Stream 1 - must be related to business and project planning to prepare for investment:Business plans;Market assessments;Operational plans;Financial plans and costing;Risk analyses; andOperational technical assessments.Stream 2 - must be essential to project delivery:Capital expenditures including equipment, machinery, technology, and construction materials;Wage or contract costs for net new and project-specific labour;Material transportation costs;Installation and implementation costs; andOther time-limited costs directly related to project implementation.Ineligible Expenses:Costs unrelated to the project;Operating costs (core staff salaries, bonuses, repayment loans, fines/penalties, etc.);Acquisition of land and existing buildings;With the exception of First Nations/Indigenous-owned enterprises acquiring or buying into existing manufacturing operations).Early research, concept development, scoping, prototyping, and feasibility studies (Technology Readiness Level 1-7); andCosts eligible for tax rebates and other rebates.Program Details:Stream 1 - Project Readiness StreamFocus on final-stage business, project planning, and operational & technical assessments;Early-stage R&D, concept development, and scoping are not eligible; andShould ideally begin the project within 3 months of funding approval.Stream 2 - Capital Investment StreamFocus on investing in new or renovated manufacturing equipment, infrastructure, technology, and processes;Projects must be initiated within 1 year of project approval; andApplicants in this stream will be asked to submit project documentation that outlines the project budget, and other potential and secured funding sources, and demonstrates project viability.Successful recipients of Stream 1 may apply for Stream 2 when ready;Receipt of Stream 1 funding does not guarantee approval through Stream 2.Process and timelines:Submit high-level proposal - 4-week turnaroundSubmit a detailed application - turnaround time will vary depending on the funding stream and complexity of the projectFunding Decision - within 12 weeks of the submission of the full application, depending on project complexity and applicant readinessFunding Agreement and project implementationSuccessful applicants will be required to report on progress and provide documentation throughout the term of the Agreement using templates provided by the program:Progress updates tied to funding release, including activities completed and progress made toward deliverables and program outcomes;Financial reports provide information to ensure funding is being applied to eligible costs;The final Report will describe the process, performance, outcomes, impacts, and key learning from the project.The program will prioritize projects that meet the following criteria:Projects within the forestry sector;Projects located in rural, remote, or forestry-dependent communities;Projects that have a high degree of readiness, need, and direct impact; andProjects that are Indigenous-led or benefit Indigenous peoples.

      Grant Criteria

and Any other costs deemed ineligible.Program Details: Program objectives include: Sustain, grow, and optimize productivity, and reduce the cost of production of Alberta's agri-food and bioIndustrial industries;Add value to enhance new commodities in the agri-food and bioIndustrial sectors;Increase environmental sustainability and social benefits for Albertans.The key outcomes of the program include: The development, and advancement of innovations that will lead to a strong agri-food and bioIndustrial sectors and a value-added resource industry in Alberta, one that helps our province become a global leader in environmental, social, and governance performance. Improved economic prosperity and social well-being in Alberta;Reduction of negative environmental impacts. Strategic focus areas include: Data and digital solutions;Autonomous systems;Agricultural biotechnology;Food processing innovation;Biofiber utilization;Value-added biomass;Green construction.Areas that are out of scope include: Bioenergy, biochar, and biofuel applications;Marketing and/or new agri-food product development.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Canadian Mining Work Placement Program provides wage subsidies of up to 70% of participants' wages to a maximum of $10,000 ($15,000 for equity-deserving groups) to hiring organizations that offer meaningful work placements that support a productive, safe, and highly skilled supply of labour. The intent of the program is to enable participants to practice new skills and competencies acquired from occupational training and provides the opportunity to work towards obtaining certification under MiHR's Canadian Mining Certification Program.Grant Value: Regular participants -70% of wages up to $10,000;Equity-deserving groups - 70% of wages up to $15,000.Note: equity-deserving groups include: women, persons with disabilities, Indigenous peoples, racialized communities, newcomers, and 2SLGBTQIA communities.Turnaround Time: 3-5 business days for the initial application.Eligible Employers: Hiring organizations that provide work placements in support, operations, and production-level positions in the mining sector; andEmployers can submit the initial application without a candidate but must have one to be approved.Eligible Participants: New workers - the program provides funding to newly trained talent to practice newly acquired skills and competencies from recent and relevant occupational training;Existing workers - the program offers funding to existing workers to upskill and explore advancement in new careers, and to practice newly acquired skills and competencies from recent and relevant occupational training; andWorkers Employed by Contractors: contractors must provide proof that they are contracted to conduct work at a mine or work site. Program Details: The program offers wage subsidies to hiring organizations that offer meaningful placements to workers in support, operation, and production-level positions; Positions must be involved with the mining sector, including but not limited to: Frontline Supervisor;Industry Trainer;Diamond Driller;Minerals Processing Operator;Underground Miner;Surface Miner; Hoist Operator.The objectives of the program include to: Equip participants with on-the-job training and work experience to allow them to practice their newly acquired skills in mines or work sites; Provide funding to hiring organizations to provide work placements to build competency in new talent entering the sector;Expand the labour pool of skilled, competent and experienced workers for the mining industry to meet their labour demands; andIncrease the recognition of skills and competencies of the existing workforce by providing a credential through the Canadian Mining Certification Program.Separate applications must be submitted for each occupation type as well as for each operating mine or work sites; Participants and their supervisors must complete a midpoint and a final evaluation to outline their satisfaction level, feedback, and the participant's employment status following the work placement; and Participants and supervisors will be required to complete the following eLearnings: Intercultural Awareness Training, Indigenous Awareness Training, and Gender Equity in Mining Works Training. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best practices: The program is retroactive to November 7, 2022;This program can be stacked with other provincial funding but must not exceed 100% of wages;The program cannot be stacked with other federal funding. Separate applications must be submitted for each occupation type as well as for each operating mine or work sites; andParticipants and their supervisors must complete a mid point and a final evaluation to outline their satisfaction level, feedback, and the participants employment status following the work placement.Forms: Program Webpage: click hereProgram Overview: click hereEmployer Application: click here

        November 19th, 2025Grant amount doubled from $25,000 to $50,000 for three prior monthly grant winners. 
      

      Grant Criteria 
      Amber Grants are comprised of 4 women's business grants broken out by category, including the Monthly Amber Grant, the Startup Grant, and the $50,000 Annual Amber Grant. To be considered for all these grants, applicants only need to apply once and will then be considered for all the grants which they are eligible for. The intent of the grants is to help women-owned businesses across Canada and the United States.Grant Value:Monthly Amber Grant: $10,000 for the top prize, $1,000 for 4 of the top 5 finalists (monthly)Business Category Grants: $10,000 (1 winner per month)The Startup Grant: $10,000 (1 winner per quarter)The Non-Profit Grant: $10,000 (1 winner per quarter)$25,000 Annual Amber Grant: $50,000 (3 winners per year)Note: Application to the Monthly Amber Grant allows applicants to receive an additional $10,000/$25,000 if eligible for the 3 categories- totaling a maximum grant value of $10,000  (monthly)+ $10,000 (Business Category)+ $10,000 (startup or non-profit, if applicable) + $50,000 (annual).Turnaround Time:Monthly Amber Grant: the 5 finalists will be announced by the 15th of the following month. The winner will be announced by the 23rd of the following monthThe Startup Grant: winner will be announced in March, June, September, and December of each yearThe Non-Profit Grant: winner will be announced in March, June, September, and December of each yearAt the end of the year, three of the 36 Business Category Grant winners is selected for a $30,000 year-end grant.Eligible Applicants:Eligibility across all grants:Businesses, startups, and non-profits must be at least 50% women-owned;The applicant must be a minimum of 18 years old;Be based in Canada or the United States.Additional eligibility for the Startup Grant:Be in the"idea phase" of business; ORHave less than $10,000 in sales.Additional eligibility for the Non-Profit Grant:Be a non-profit business/organization that benefits the community.Additional eligibility for the Business Category Grants:Be in the business category of the month:January - Skilled Trades;February - Health and Fitness;March - Food & beverage;April - Sustainability;May - Mental & emotional support;June - Business Support Service;July - Animal services;August - Haircare & skincare;September - Education & child care;October - Creative arts;November - Technology;December - Fashion & interior designers.Note: Applicants who fall under these specific business categories automatically become eligible (once per year) for the monthly $10,000 Business Category Grant. The same application remains active for the Category grant until the month of your category.Program Details:The deadline for the Monthly Amber Grant is at 11:59 pm Eastern Time on the last day of each month;The $50,000 Annual Amber Grant will be awarded to 3 of the previous Monthly Amber Grant winners;Applicants only need to apply once to be considered for all the grants they are eligible for;Applicants will be charged $15 for the application fee upon submission;Applicants will receive an email confirmation after the application is submitted;Details on the process will be included in the confirmation email.If the application does not get selected, it will not roll forward to the following month;Applicants who have not been selected will not be permitted to apply within 3 months of the application submission;Applicants who have not been selected should only reapply when something significant has changed in the business model or circumstances. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices:Applicants are advised to check the junk/spam folder after submitting the application if the confirmation has not appeared in the inbox;Application tips for applicants:Take every opportunity to answer the "why" and the "how" behind the business and be upfront about the challenges where possible;Whenever possible, show how resourceful you can be in making that prize money stretch as far as possible;Facts and figures should be included to provide the best answer;Applicants should err on the side of lengthier responses to maximize the chance to tell the story about the business;Do not try to sound "corporate" in the application;Applicants are advised to provide a social media profile from the company (ideally Facebook); andSave a copy of your responses to help recall what you reported.Forms:Program webpage: click hereApplication webform: click hereFAQs: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The pilot podcast program will support the development, production and promotion of podcasts by BC-based content producers by providing up to $15,000 in funding. Ultimately this program will improve the competitive position of BC-based podcast producers in domestic and international markets.Grant Value: Stream 1: Podcast Pipeline for Development - Up to $10,000Stream 2: Podcast Connect for Production and/or Promotion - Up to $15,000Turnaround Time: Approximately 8 weeks.Eligible Applicants Applicant companies must be a registered society, a non-profit organization or companies incorporated in British Columbia or Canada with its head office in British Columbia;The applicant company must have been established for at least one year;Must have the appropriate experience to ultimately bring the project to fruition; andKey personnel involved in the project must have been a resident and paying taxes within BC for the 2 years preceding.Program Details: Stream 1Provides up to a max of $10,000 in funding; The podcast pipeline will help to get your documentary or narrative storytelling podcast pitch into great shape;Eligible activities under this stream include:Research and pre-interviews;Conceptualizing;Drafting outlines;Building characters;Constructing chapters and episodes; andRecording audio samples.Chat, news, and discussion programs are not eligible for this stream. Comedy is allowed as part of narrative storytelling.Stream 2Provides up to a max of $15,000 in funding;This stream is divided into two parts:Part 1. Support eligible applicants that have some pre-existing or supplementary content that they would like to get into a podcast format, Podcast Connect will help bring added value to whatever it is that your organization already has going on;Eligible activities include:Transforming archive materials into a podcast format;Supplementing a pre-existing commercial property (e.g. books, magazines, TV programs etc.) with a concomitant podcast;Companion podcasts for film and television.Part 2. This stream can also help connect with your audience via increased promotional activities, if you already have a podcast but need to promote it, apply to this stream for marketing support;You can apply for both parts of stream 2 at the same time;The review and analysis of each application will consider: Program eligibility;Viability and market potential;The existing number of podcast subscribers;Creative evaluation.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Advance Payments Program (APP) provides loans of up to $1,000,000, of which the first $250,000 are interest-free. Eligible applicants include corporations, cooperatives, and partnerships that produce their own agricultural products. The intent of the program is to help agricultural product producers access additional cash flow for the growing season.Loan Value: $1,000,000 - the first $250,000 is interest-freeTurnaround Time: within 10 business daysEligible Applicants:Be one of the following organization types:Corporation;Cooperatives;Partnerships.Produce and own the agricultural product, including but not limited to:Crops;Grains and oilseeds;Fruits and vegetables;Livestock (cattle, hogs, sheep, bison, rabbits, red deer, boar, goats, elk);Certain breeding animals intended to be marketed during the production period (cattle, goats, sheep, hogs);Bees intended to be marketed during the production period;Fur pelts and cervid antler velvet; andHoney and maple syrup.Be responsible for marketing;The applicant must be:Canadian citizen or permanent resident; andThe age of majority in the province of operation.Note: If the agricultural product is not listed above, applicants are advised to contact a program administrator.Ineligible Applicants:Agricultural producers with:livestock for slaughter;Animals under supply management (e.g. dairy cows, poultry);Breeding animals.Program Details:Cash advance calculations:Based on 50% of the anticipated market value of the eligible agricultural products the applicant will produce or have in storage.Repayment period:18 months for most products;24 months for cattle and bison;The repayment period can vary depending on the agricultural product.Applicants may have more than 1 advance outstanding;However, the total advances cannot exceed $1,000,000.The agricultural product on which the advance is based is always required as security;Applicants must repay the advance as the agricultural product(s) are sold;Proof of sale may be required with each repayment.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices:For questions about advances, the Program Administrators will guide applicants through the application process and will advise applicants of any administration fee they may charge and explain the terms of repayment.Forms:Program webpage: click hereList of Program Administrators: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      NGen will fund up to $2.96 million to support collaborative, business-led projects that are aimed at de-risking, commercializing and scaling-up innovative manufacturing capabilities in Canada. The objective of this program is to strengthen the competitiveness of Canada's manufacturing sector, drive more innovation and investment in advanced manufacturing technologies in Canada, generate new commercial opportunities for Canadian companies in global markets, grow world-leading Canadian enterprises, and develop a modern and inclusive workforce with the skills to excel in advanced manufacturing.Grant Value: Maximum funding up to 35% and will be capped at $2,960,000. Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants: Be and NGen member;Be incorporated in Canada and have value-added presence in Canada beyond a sales office; A for-profit organization;A not-for-profit organization that facilitates and funds research and development on behalf of the ecosystem and whose funding and/or revenue is received primarily from the private sector or industry organizations;A non-federal Crown corporation whose funding is derived from commercial activities; An Indigenous organization. Eligible Projects: All projects must demonstrate the development and application of an Advanced Manufacturing Technology or Process; A limited percentage of product research and development will be permitted;Eligible projects must also meet NGen's four core strategic criteria:Transformative: project must confer significant competitive advantage to Canadian industry;Collaborative: project must demonstrate meaningful collaboration with a minimum of two Canadian industry partners;Applied: project must have a short to medium path to commercialization, and generate significant commercial and economic benefits;Enduring: project must provide broader benefits to Canada’s advanced manufacturing ecosystem.Projects need to include manufacturing and technology
