      Grant Criteria 
      The Reshaping Energy Systems program is seeking to fund technology pilots, demonstrations and first-of-kind commercial projects that represent opportunities to help place Alberta's energy systems on the pathway to net-zero emissions.Grant Value:Maximum funding $10,000,000; andMinimum funding $250,000.Turnaround Time: Final decisions announced December 2023.Eligible Applicants: Small and medium enterprises;Research and Development organizations;Universities;Municipalities;Non-for-profits organizations;Government research labs; Individuals; and Collaborations are also welcome.Eligible Project Areas: The following is a non-exhaustive list of example technologies that ERA believes could represent compelling opportunities for this call of applications: Electricity transmission and distribution (T&D) innovation, including:Innovative medium - and high - voltage direct current (DC) solutions; Novel materials for wire (conductor) replacement and other solutions for T&D capacity additions and/or efficiency improvement;Line monitoring and dynamic line rating technologies;Supporting technologies for cross-border electricity interconnections;Non-wires alternatives for T&D; andGrid T&D controls and digital solutions. Innovative low-emissions solutions for grid services(e.g. innovation approaches to providing spinning reserve, frequency regulation, and other ancillary services);Innovative solutions to enhance grid reliability and resilience;Smart grid, microgrid, and grid edge solutions including novel distributed energy resources and solution for remote, rural, and/or indigenous communities;Solutions to integrate net-zero and net-zero-ready building with the broader energy system, including:Building-integrated renewables;District energy systems;Novel grid-interactive building technologies such as demand response, control aggregation/coordination, virtual power plants, and smart heat pumps;Innovative solutions for liquid and gas pipeline networks, including electrification of compressors/engines;Energy storage technologies, including:Storage of electricity via chemical, mechanical, electrochemical, or other means;Thermal energy storage.Digital solutions for energy management, including artificial intelligence/machine learning for grid management, advanced controls for energy end-use optimization (facility -or- system-level), industrial demand response and other demand-side-management solutions;Novel zero-emissions vehicle infrastructure (battery electric vehicles, hydrogen vehicles, etc.) including:Innovative charging solutions (multifamily residential, battery storage enabled, etc.)Innovative fuelling stations (hydrogen, etc.);Vehicle-to-grid and similar technologies.Solutions for clean fleets (e.g. transit, city services, corporate/service fleets, school busses, micromobility, and others.)Projects that are in the construction/expansion of technology production, manufacturing or fabrication facilities are eligible but must have a strong case for how the investment will support emission reduction in Alberta. Ineligible Projects:GHG detection, quantification, measurement, and monitoring;Software platforms related to tracking, estimation, or monetization of energy use, emissions credits, efficiency opportunities, and similar;Efficiency upgrades (for buildings, industry, vehicles, etc.) that do not directly feature an element of energy systems integration;Purchase of low-emissions vehicles without a component of energy systems technology/infrastructure innovation;Technologies that primarily produce or generate electricity, heat, fuels, etc.; these technologies are the focus of other planned ERA funding programs in the near future;Hydrogen production, blending, or use use for heat/industrial processes; this will be the focus of other planned ERA  funding programs in the near future.Eligible Expenses: Labour costs directly related to the project;Employee benefits up to 20% of base salary of those directly related to the project; Costs associated with preparing ERA required reports;Purchase or use of Capital assets, such as property, plant, and equipment that are required for the delivery of the project;Consumables such as industrial gas, construction, or laboratory supplies used during the project are eligible but must be documented;Raw materials, tools and software;Consultant labour costs directly related to the project;Travel and attendance to relevant conferences to present on the Project(Capped at $2,500 for Domestic and $5,000 for International conferences);Reasonable expenses as per the Government of Alberta's Travel, Meal and Hospitality Expenses Policy;Parking, Economy airfare and taxi costs relating to travel; andVehicle rental or mileage for project required travel.NOTE: All expenses must be declared and approved in the application process. If an expense is not eligible it does not mean the whole project is ineligible. Program Details: Funding must be matched on a 1:1 basis with funding coming from the applicant and/or project partners towards eligible expenses; All applications will be evaluated on the following criteria:Innovation Opportunity (30);Implementation Plan (15);GHG and Non-GHG Benefits (35); andMarket and Value Proposition (20).Successful applicants must commence work on the proposed project within 120 days of funding approval;In certain circumstances the project start date may be extended for up to 12 months;Max length of the projects funded under this call is 3 years from initiation, plus one additional year for operational time where applicable;Funding will be disbursed on a milestone completion basis;Deadline for the submission of Expression of Interest is June 15, 2023 at 5 p.m. Mountain Daylight Time; Expression of Interest Shortlist notification will be Early August 2023; andProject must be TRL 7 by the end of the project.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Interested applicants are advised to attend the information webinar held on April 24, 2023 from 2-3pm Mountain Daylight Time (UTC-6h);Funding made available through this call is provided to projects with well-defined objectives, milestones, deliverables, and timelines;Successful applicants must commence work on the proposed project within 120 days of funding approval. Applicants must demonstrate how the proposed technology or application thereof is an innovative solution for emissions reduction in Alberta; Technology solutions can originate from anywhere globally however, it must be demonstrated and implemented in Alberta during the project; Project does not be a TRL 7 before project start but must be at least TRL 7 by the end of the project; andAlthough they can fund up to $10,000,000 this will be under rare circumstances and the max funding will generally fall at $7,000,000. Forms: Program Webpage: click hereExpression of Interest Guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Canadian Agricultural Loans Act program guarantees loans of up $500,000 to farmers and agricultural co-operatives. The program is intended for direct producers in the agriculture sector that are seeking to purchase the purchase, repair, construction of buildings and machines. The purchase of tools, machines, and breeding livestock is also eligible under this program.Loan Value:Up to $500,000 for the purchase of land and the construction or improvement of buildingsUp to $350,000 for all other loan purposes, including consolidation/refinancingNote: maximum of lender's prime rate plus 1%Turnaround Time: 15 business daysEligible Applicants:Must engage in one of the following:The production of field-grown crops, cultivated and uncultivated, and horticultural crops;The raising of livestock, poultry, and fur-bearing animals;The production of eggs, milk, honey, maple syrup, tobacco, fibre, wood from woodlots, and fodder crops;The production or raising of any other prescribed thing or animal.Must be one of the following organization types:Sole proprietors;Partnerships;Corporations; andCo-operative association.Must have a majority (50% + 1) farmer membership.The program allows farmers of all types to be eligible, including:Existing farmers;Beginning farmers (that is, less than 6 years of farming);Start-up farmers;Farmers taking over the family farm; andPart-time farmers.Note: Greenhouses are eligible under the programEligible Lenders:Chartered banks;Credit unions;Caisses populaires;Alberta Treasury Branches; andAny other organization designated by the Minister.Eligible Activities:Purchase of land;Construction, repair or alteration of any building or structure on a farm;Purchase, installation, alteration, major overhaul, or major repair to/of:Tools, implements, apparatus, and machines of any kind not usually affixed to real or immovable property;Machinery and apparatus for the generation or distribution of electricity, whether or not affixed to real or immovable property.Purchase of breeding livestock that will provide a long-term improvement to a farm operation including:Horses and other equinesCattle, sheep, goats, and other ruminants;Swine, poultry, bees, and fur-bearing animals;Any other prescribed animal.Erection or construction of fencing or works for drainage;Clearing, breaking, irrigating and reclaiming of land;Conservation of soil, prevention of soil erosion by the planting of trees and shelter belts;Repair or overhaul of fencing where the cost is $2,000 or more;Purchase and the planting of trees for syrup production and the purchase and planting of fruit trees, Christmas trees, and ginseng, where the cost is $2,000 or more;Construction of a road or driveway on a farm;Land transfer tax, survey, appraisal and legal costs relating to the purchase of additional land;Purchase of shares for inter-generational farm transfers; andConsolidation/refinancing of loans.Note: A loan for the purchase of shares in a farm or farming operation can be financed under the program for up to $350,000.  These loans can be amortized for up to 10 years.Ineligible Activities:Improvements to the family dwelling;Quota purchases of any kind;Operating loans and loans for the purchase of short-term feeder livestock; andConsolidation of a lender's ordinary loans.Program Details:Eligible amount of the loan:Existing farmers - Loans to existing farmers must not exceed the lesser of 80% of the appraised value of the property for which the loan was madeBeginning farmers - Loans to beginning farmers must not exceed the lesser of 90% of the appraised value of the property for which the loan was made.Application process:Approach an eligible lender as listed above;The lender will go through its loan application process and determine the financing best suited for the applicant;The lender may then register the loan with the CALA program through either the online loan registration system or by mailing the forms and registration fee in.Registration fee:0.85% of the amount of the loan;This fee must be submitted to the "Receiver General for Canada" at the time of loan registration.Administration fee:An administration fee may also be charged by the lender. For loans up to $250,000, the administration fee is capped at 0.25% of the amount of the loan (to a maximum of $250). For loans over $250,000, the administration fee is capped at 0.1% of the amount of the loan.Repayment terms:15 years for land purchases. Lenders may amortize loans for longer than 15 years provided a balloon payment is scheduled for the loan at the end of the 15 year period. The remaining loan amount could then be refinanced under the Canadian Agricultural Loans Act (CALA) for a further 10 years.10 years for all other purposes.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices:The lender organization will go through the loan application process and determine the financing best suited for the applicant's needs, which may or may not include a loan under the Canadian Agricultural Loans Act program.Forms:Program webpage: click here

The goal is to address gaps in BC's food processing sector to increase food production and economic growth by supporting facility upgrades, new equipment, expanding processing capacity and training. Grant Value: The program provides cost shared funding of up to 75% of eligible costs;The program contribution for approved projects is: Minimum of $100,000;Maximum of $1,000,000. For approved projects with only Training-related activities the program contribution is: Minimum of $50,000;Maximum of $100,000.Turnaround Time: Applications will be reviewed June 6, 2023 and July 18, 2023.Eligible Applicants: Established food and/or seafood processing business, with:Minimum of two years in operation;Minimum of $500K gross annual revenues.Established commercial food hub, commissary kitchen, and other shared-use commercial food processing facility; andIndustry group or association.Ineligible Applicants:Retail food services or operations;Processors/manufacturers of pet food, except where provides value-add to waste from
food supply;Processors/manufacturers of Cannabis-infused food products and beverages;Restaurants and food service, including catering services;Packaging material manufacturers;Processors/manufacturers of health products or nutritional supplements;Processors/manufacturers of alcohol-based beverages and ingredients meant for alcohol-based beverages; andNew entrant businesses.Eligible Activities/Expenses: Purchase and install new or upgraded/expanded facilities and infrastructure and equipment.Capital investments in new and upgraded/expanded facility/infrastructure (e.g. new cooler/freezer, production room expansion).Eligible costs include costs for renovations, site improvements, construction,
and other related costs.New/upgraded equipment/machinery to increase production capacity or support
product line expansion.Purchase and install new technology and systems.  New innovative technologies, software, advanced automation such as robotics, digital or Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology and systems that would increase processing capacity (e.g. AI, automated sorters, logistic or distribution software, supply chain and logistics solutions). Eligible costs include costs for facility changes, upgrades and modifications
required for installation of advanced automation or manufacturing
technology or equipment.Applied Research & Development (R&D) for new and improved products, lab analysis, packaging etc.R&D for new and improved products using technology, access to laboratory
equipment for food and ingredient development and analysis such as pH, shelf-life,
microbiology testing, sensory analysis, ingredient and nutritional analysis, and applied
research support and expertise (private or academic institutions).Training that supports infrastructure or equipment upgrades or adoptionSpecialized training and up-skilling of resources. Production staff, operational staff
upgrading on new skill set, new equipment, new processes or systems and also
includes specialized expertise such as food scientists, food engineers, software
developers and implementation training.Note: Please see the Best Practices section for details on eligible expenses that have already been partially paid.Ineligible Activities: Operational labour;In-kind activities;Equipment, facilities, and technology investments that do not enhance processing
productivity;Early-stage business or feasibility planning;Market development and marketing activities;Individual business support for food safety and other certifications processes; andCosts related to existing operations (limited to new investments to increase processing
capacity and improve businesses productivity).Program Details: For the initial launch of the program the Ministry has some priority requirements that will take preference:Eligible Participants:Established BC-based food and seafood processing businesses (highest priority);Projects that will positively impact the use of BC inputs;Companies/organizations that currently use BC inputs or will increase procurement once the project is completed;Companies/organizations that do not currently use BC inputs and/or will not increase procurement once the project is completed.Commodities Group 1 (highest priority)Seafood;Meat;Fruit and Vegetable.Group 2Plant-based protein;Dairy;Bakeries and tortilla;Beverages;Grain and oilseed milling.Group 3Sugar and confectionary;Other foods.Applications are being accepted on an ongoing basis starting April 26, 2023;Applications are reviewed quarterly with the priority sectors taking precedence;The review dates for each application bath for 2023/2024 fiscal year are June 6, 2023 and July 18, 2023; Project start dates for Batch 1 will be July 18, 2023; andProjects must be completed within 24 months. Additional dates will be added depending on fund availability;Successful applicants are expected to complete the activity and financial reports at regular intervals to ensure projects are on-track;Applications that match the priority criteria will be offered funding first; andApplications that are not successful will not be brought forward to the next review batch, these applications will need to re-apply for future consideration.

an FBRN or have a letter from the Indian Agriculture Program of Ontario;Food processors;Aquaculture businesses pursuing international marketing activities;Fish and seafood processors pursuing international marketing activities;Industry organizations.Maintain either:Maintain a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (CRA BN); ORSocial Insurance Number (SIN).Only if the applicant has been found eligible to participate in the program and is eligible to receive program payment.Be in compliance with:Environmental-related requirements of the law;Labour-related requirements of the law;Tax-related requirements of the law;Material compliance with all other requirements of the law.Note: The applicant company and all its staff must be at arm's length from federal public servants and the legislative branch of government.Eligible Activities:Market Analysis and Planning:Third-party advisory services to complete market analysis, life cycle analysis and/or a marketing plan.Must be for a new product or for new markets and existing markets.Third-party advisory services to investigate the regulatory or certification standards.Includes food product labels, preparation of nutritional panels and other required label information.New Product Development:Third-party advisory services for new product development activities, including:Regulatory review for new products;Ingredient, material or packaging sourcing;Formulation developmentScale-Up trials;Shelf-life determination;Testing or analysis to verify and complement the development process of:Nutritional, microbial, chemical, allergen or sensory/consumer.Marketing Products:Third-party services for implementation of a business or marketing plan to access or expand into new markets, including:Brand development;Focus groups and or consumer studies;Product demonstrations;New promotional material development (e.g. ads, brochures, videos, website development/update, social media posts, tradeshows andBe in full compliance with government laws and regulations. Ineligible Applicants:Not-for-profit organizations and associations;Government employees, Crown corporations, municipalities, towns, and cities;Educational institutions; andConsultants, representatives, brokers, agents, or related service providers. Eligible Expenses: Tradeshow/mission registration;Booth exhibit space and basic furnishing (i.e carper, power, Wi-Fi, display case, table and chairs);Economy airfare to/from Manitoba;Accommodations;Event marketing material translation;Interpreter services;Market research related to the market of interest; andRelevant trade preparedness training. Ineligible Expenses: Ground Transportation;Shipping costs;Development of marketing materials other than translation;Virtual tradeshows/missions;Conferences that do not have a tradeshow component;Company labour at the booth;Per diem, food and meal costs;Cost of goods or samples;Cost of extra baggage; andSponsorship.Program Details: The maximum funding per trade event is $20,000 with a lifetime limit of two times per specific tradeshow or trade activity;An applicant may receive support for multiple applications per fiscal year, to a combined annual maximum contribution of $30,000 per fiscal year;50% of eligible expenses for exhibiting in a tradeshow or participating in a business mission with a business-to-business meeting component outside of Manitoba;30% of eligible expenses for participating, but not exhibiting, in a tradeshow outside of Manitoba; companies must have a clear objective for attending and a business agenda developed;Available for up to 2 representatives per company per event; Reimbursements will be issued by cheque to the applicant company;Companies must submit the following documents within 30 days of their return to Canada:Expense Claim form;Receipts of their travel costs;Invoices for accommodations;Invoices for the tradeshow event, including registration costs, booth costs, and furnishing costs;Invoices for marketing material translation;Invoices for interpreter services for the trade event;Invoices for approved market research fees;Invoices for approves trade preparedness-training fees;Having a post-event meeting with a Government of Manitoba program administrator and completed an evaluation form outlining the business generated by the visit;Pictures of their booth at the tradeshow;       The Creative Export Export Development Stream provides funding to a maximum of $90,000. Eligible applicants must be Canadian-owned and controlled, have 1 full-time employee, and have a maximum of $10M in annual revenues in the current or previous fiscal year. The intent of this stream is to help Canadian organizations to enter international markets where they currently have little to no sales.Grant Value: $90,000 (The maximum request for funding from this stream is 90K for a 1-year project and 180K for a 2-year project.)Turnaround Time: 26 weeksEligible Applicants:Incorporated under the laws of Canada, a province or territory;For-profit or non-profit organizations;Canadian-owned and controlled;Have a maximum of $10 million in annual revenues in the current or previous fiscal year;Have at least 1 full-time employee (minimum 30 hours/week);This employee must receive pay, and this should be verifiable through the financial statements provided.Have a market-ready project at the project start date;Content must be fully developed and ready for sales (ie. the content must be fully developed).Must hold intellectual property rights for the content;Have a project that is expected to generate export revenues or lead to generating export revenues;Be in one or more of the following creative industries:Artistic craft;Audiovisual;Design (limited to exhibit design, fashion design, artistic product design, public art design, urban design);Music;Performing arts;Publishing (books and periodicals);Visual art;Interactive digital media (in combination with at least one of the industries listed above).Video game creators are eligible.Have a minimum total project cost of $15,000; andBe able to fund a minimum of 25% of the project costs through private sources.Note: The applicant must hold intellectual property rights for the content within the scope of the project, if applicable.Eligible Activities:Export planning activities:Limited to a maximum of $30,000 of the total requested amount;Including but not limited to:Development of an export plan or market entry strategy;International marketing plan;Export pricing strategy;Market research on target export markets;Planning of distribution and logistics;Help to find a broker or distributor, including international distribution channels;Business services and advice;Legal services (e.g., contract support, intellectual property);Tariffs, certification requirements, regulations and insurance advice; andE-business or online strategy (this may include an online international plan, sales or online security advice).Market development activities:Limited to a maximum of $40,000 of the total requested amount;Including but not limited to:Travel-related expenses (bringing delegations of international buyers to Canada or Canadian buyers to international events);Bringing delegations of international buyers to Canada must demonstrate a benefit to multiple Canadian creative companies/organizations;May apply for single or multiple trips within 1 application.Structured activities designed to develop and maintain international business-to-business relationships (i.e., one-on-one meetings, facilitated meet-and-greets and other networking activities);Purchase or rental of trade show or exhibition space/floor;Venue rentals and related expenses;Conference registration or participation fees;Marketing material (e.g., pamphlets, business cards, samples), including printing and digital marketing costs;Advertising costs; andInternational market readiness activities:Limited to a maximum of 10% of total funding requested;Including but not limited to:Versioning expenses;Dubbing expenses;Translation and interpretation expenses;Fees relating to intellectual property protection (e.g., copyright licensing, patents, trademarks, industrial design, geographical indications);Shipping and handling expenses;Insurance expenses;Website development, including software and programming expenses and search engine optimization;Product photography and videography, including product styling; andInitial e-commerce platform development.Export training and mentorship activities:Including but not limited to:Export training;Networking activities;Matchmaking services;International business advisory services; andMentoring.Must have a minimum of 30 hours of training;May be for both executives and artist training;Activities under this category must clearly demonstrate how the project aligns with the program objectives and demonstrate how the training/mentorship responds to industry needsTraining and mentorship must be provided by recognized professionals from Canadian companies/organizations in the creative industry.Applicants will be required to provide a copy of the diploma, biography and/or curriculum vitae of each of the principal teaching staff.Note: Each application can include multiple project activities. andExpenses relating to lobbying, public relations, policy development, and influence.Project Details:Project activities may span up to 24 months, Earliest project start date: April 1, 2025;Latest project end date: March 31, 2026;Maximum of 1 application per deadline;Including entities or subsidiaries of a parent company.This limit allows applicants to submit an application to both the Export Development stream and Export-Ready stream for different projects.Applicants may apply for the program for a maximum of in 3 out of 5 fiscal years;If you have already received funding from Creative Export Canada for 2 years since 2020, then you would only be eligible for 1 year of funding;The condition is set for the program, and applies to both streams.  This means that if a recipient received funding from the Export-Ready Stream in the last 5 fiscal year (2020-21 to 2024-2025), it cannot be for more than 3 fiscal years of support.No limits on how many markets the applicant can choose to enter for the application;Evaluation criteria:The project’s viability and potential for export revenue generated in the targeted market(s);The project’s potential to expand sales into international markets and/or develop international business networks; andThe applicant’s demonstrated capacity to achieve the expected outcomes of the project through (can be a combination of) experience, expertise, collaborators, partners, or service providers.Special considerations may be given to applicants:Located outside of Vancouver, Toronto, and Montreal;Whose company/organization and/or proposed project supports or empowers Indigenous peoples;Whose company/organization and/or proposed project supports or empowers members of equity-deserving communities; The greater focus will be placed on projects that aim to reach product commercialization within their allotted timeframe. Grant Value: Grant value is set at $4.1 million however this is the average across Protein Industries Canada programs as there is no set maximum a project can receive however the program will reimburse up to 45% of eligible costsTurnaround Time: Approximately 6-8 weeks.Eligible Applicants: Applicants must be a member of Protein Industries Canada;Must be a consortium of a minimum 3 Protein Industries Canada members, at least one of which is a Small or Medium Enterprise with 499 or fewer employees;Each member of the consortium must contribute to the project in a meaningful way;At least 2 members of the consortium must contribute financially to the project;A consortium may include academic or research institution(s). custody, sustainability and food safety of Canadian crops and ingredientsIngredients (50%) - the development, scaling and optimization of plant-based ingredients:Testing and scaling of new and novel ingredient manufacturing processes;Improved rates of protein extraction and nutrient density;Reduced water and energy requirements in ingredient manufacturing processes;Optimized ingredient manufacturing processes for Canadian crops and Canadian conditions;The development of new and novel ingredients and co-products from Canadian crops; andImproved processing efficiency in the manufacturing of plant-based ingredients. Products (25%) - the conversion of Canadian-made ingredients and co-products into the consumption-ready goods: The creation and commercialization of consumer-ready food products that align with consumer needs, expectations and trends, including clean-label, sustainable and nutritious products;The creation and commercialization of value-added animal feed products; andThe creation and commercialization of new industrial bio-products derived from the co-products of protein extraction and ingredient manufacturing.Technology program projects are required to document an IP rationale as part of their project proposals (template will be given to applicants submitting a project application;All applications will also be required to report on the IP assets generated by their project; andPrior to signing the final Master Project Agreement every member of the consortium will be required to complete a detailed financial assessment, including submitting the last two years of accountant-prepared financial statements and their current organizational structure.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program aims to meet the needs for new tools and technologies by co-investing in collaborative projects, comprised of consortia of two or more partner companies, that utilize artificial intelligence to help grow Canada's plant-based food, feed and ingredients ecosystem. Grant Value: Grant value is set at $4.1 million however this is the average across Protein Industries Canada programs as there is no set maximum a project can receive however the program will reimburse up to 45% of eligible costsTurnaround Time: Approximately 6-8 weeks.Eligible Applicants: Applicants must be a member of Protein Industries Canada;Must be a consortium of a minimum 2 Protein Industries Canada members, at least one of which is a Small or Medium Enterprise with 499 or fewer employees;Each member of the consortium must contribute to the project in a meaningful way;At least 2 members of the consortium must contribute financially to the project;A consortium may include academic or research institution(s). Not mandatory but encouraged;At least two partners must be Canadian companies or multi-national corporation that are legally entitled to do business in Canada with a significant Canadian business operation; andAt least one consortium member should represent a target customer or user of the new technology solution.Eligible Activities: Technology Leadership- activities in this area include:Advancing platform technologies central to future competitiveness; and Building a technology advantage for the Global Innovation Cluster.Partnership for Scale - activities in this area include: Projects that serve a target group of members to support their growth including increased domestic demand for Global Innovation Cluster products and services or by facilitating expansion;Linking start-tips with strategic partners;Offering business mentoring, consulting and coaching;Supply chain development or integration efforts for Global Innovation Cluster SMEs with local anchor firms; andWorking with public entities that provide access to capital and financing.Diverse and Skilled Talent Pools- activities in this area include: Recruitment campaign to repatriate Canadian talent to the Global Innovation Cluster;Development of curricula linked to industry needs and workforce integration programs for students;Development and promotion of specialized certifications in areas of technology leadership;Retraining programs for existing workforce;Assessment of Industry's workforce current or anticipated needs; andBuilding awareness of industry demand for skilled talent across stakeholder groups.Access to Innovation- activities in this are include: Support for access to specialized technical services;Installation of and access to dedicated laboratory or cutting-edge equipment; andAcquisition and assertion of jointly held intellectual property. Global Advantage- activities in this area include: Global Innovation Cluster promotion;Investment attraction to the general region of Global Innovation Cluster;Studies to identify new global markets for Global Innovation Cluster products and services;Participation in or leadership of trade missions to key markets;Development of regulatory or policy proposals to enhance technological advantage; andDevelopment and promotion of new international standards that incorporate the Canadian approach. Program Details: There are 3 streams under this program, the Project Stream, the System Stream and the Community Stream; Project Stream: This stream is designed to help individuals companies within the plant-based food, feed and ingredient ecosystem incorporate AI as a core business function;This requires collaboration with one or more entities within the AI ecosystem.Example of a project within this stream is a food manufacturer that wants to employ AI in the form of imaging technology and process automation for food safety and/or quality assurance.System Stream: This stream will focus on overall sector competitiveness and will require multiple partners from the plant-based food, feed and ingredient ecosystem; andAn example of a project within this stream is a consortium of plant-based food companies that are looking to iterate new products faster and improve consumer acceptance.Community Stream: This stream will help ensure that benefits of AI application in the plant-based food space are achieving societal benefits. This stream will focus on the nexus between plant-based foods and human health, as well as between plant-based foods environmental health; andAn example of a project in this stream could be a collaboration between national health advocacy agencies along with a number of plant-based food companies to use AI to design food products that help achieve certain health outcomes or to address health concerns.Protein Industries Canada will require all project participants to report on the IP assets generated by
their project, which may include patents, trade secrets, trademarks, copyright, data sets and other
types of intangible assets.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: This program does not allow for funding to be used retroactively;All projects are required to pay a project administration fee to Protein Industries Canada. This fees will be 4% of the total eligible reconciled project cost; and This program can be stacked with other sources of funding. Forms and Links: Program Webpage: click here.Program Guidelines: click here.

      Grant Criteria 
      This call for innovation focuses on forestry residue management, with the aim to identify high impact projects that accelerate the reduction of global greenhouse gases and enable a net-negative emissions future. There is no max or minimum of funding amount but the total program budget is $6 million with the intention of funding several projects. Grant Value: Grant value is set as $0 as there is no max amount of funding however total budget for this call is $6 million and the program is looking to fund several projects. Projects under $750,000 will be prioritized. Turnaround Time: Initial EOI deadline August 18, 2023;Initial application selection August 25, 2023;Detailed proposal submission deadline September 15, 2023; andSuccessful applicants will be announced October 20, 2023.Eligible Applicants: Companies with solutions relevant to BC;Consortia of companies working together to complete a project are acceptable and welcomed however a single lead company should be the applicant; andCompanies located in BC but will allow participation of companies outside of the province with presence or a project in BC.Eligible Projects: Commercially viable pathways for collection, transportation, and management of forestry residue, including opportunities for slash and thinning by-products to reduce wildfire risks;Diversification of utilization solutions to derive energy value from forestry residue, such as biogases, advance biofuels, and other scalable end-use products; andProposals that align forest management with carbon-based innovations, such as nature-based solutions, bioenergy with carbon capture utilization and storage (BECCUS), and other potentially negative-emission technologies.Eligible Expenses: Any expenses directly relating to the project including: Salaries;Consultants;Reasonable direct costs of project management;Secure demonstration sites;Build prototypes;Integrate system components;Demonstrate pilot production; orScale up manufacturing. Ineligible Expenses: Anything that will enhance normal business operational capabilities; Purchase equipment that is indirectly related to and not core to the proposed innovation;Perform capital or leasehold improvements;Purchase furniture and other equipment to be used in the routine course of business; andAdvertising or other forms of business promotion. Program Details: Projects must start within 6 months of signing a contribution agreement. Projects generally last between 18 months and 2 years;Project funding will be: Aligned with a contribution agreement between the proponent and CICE that will be negotiated as part of the final award process;Paid against completion of milestones; and Withdrawn in the event projects are significantly delayed or milestone objectives are

      Grant Criteria 
      Through this program, primary and Indigenous producers, conservation groups, water purveyors and Indigenous communities will have access to cost-shared funding to adapt to climate change by investing in water infrastructure. Stream 1 offers up to $1 million in funding for the improvement, rehabilitation, expansion, or new construction of water storage systems for farms(including agricultural dams).Grant Value: Stream 1: 50% up to $1 million.Turnaround Time: Up to 60 days after deadline.Eligible Applicants: Incorporated and individual producers;Agricultural and conservation groups;Irrigation/improvement districts and local/municipal governments that supply water to agriculture; andIndigenous Communities and Indigenous Producers.Ineligible Applicants: Non-agricultural individuals or groups;Provincial and federal governments; andCrown Corporations.Eligible Activities: Activity 1: Rehabilitation and upgrades of agricultural dams and resevoirs to meet regulatory requirements:Dams with deficiencies where the dam owner have not been ordered to make repairs or lower the reservoir;An assessment by the Dam Safety Program staff would be legally required before the work begins and when upgrade is completed;Increasing the size of the storage will require an authorization from the Ministry of Forests.Eligible Costs: Construction, materials, machinery/equipment (gates, valves, etc.) and other costs associated with the construction;Pumping systems and watering troughs to keep livestock out of the existing reservoir are recommended and are eligible costs, provided the reservoir is deemed to provide a secure source in periods of extended drought;Other professional services associated with project supervision.Ineligible Items: Water Distribution system; andUsed Materials.Regulatory Requirements: Water licence for the proposed use, (e.g., irrigation) of the water source (i.e., aquifer, stream);Water licence for the proposed storage volume;Assessment/approval/authorization from the Dam Safety Program staff of the Ministry of Forests;Change approval to make changes in and about a stream (if applicable); andEasement (if applicable).Activity 2: Improvement, expansion or new construction of dugouts and storage facilities for irrigation water and livestock watering, including rangeland:Producers on low flow water supplies will often install a dugout to enhance supply by augmenting water supplies during times of shortage;Lining of dugouts to improve water holding capacity; andInstallation of pumps and watering troughs to improve livestock watering and protect stream health.Eligible Costs: Construction, materials, liner, pump, intake, machinery/equipment (e.g., gates, valves, etc.) and associated fittings and controls;Power supply to farm property line as required;Solar or wind power supply for remote livestock watering systems;Planting of trees and snow fencing to facilitate snow collection and melt;Dugout aeration systems (wind or electric compressors);Pumping systems and watering troughs to keep livestock out of the existing dugout are recommended and are eligible costs, provided the dugout is deemed to provide a secure source in periods of extended drought; andOther professional services associated with the project supervision.Ineligible Items: Water distribution system;Used materials; andDugouts with design specifications that are legally considered as dams according to the Dam Safety Regulation (DSR).Regulatory Requirements: Water licence for the proposed use, (e.g., irrigation) of the water source (i.e., aquifer, stream);Water licence for the proposed storage volume;Change approval to make changes in and about a stream (if applicable); andEasement (if applicable).Activity 3: New Construction of resevoirs and large storage facilities:New storages will require an authorization from the Ministry of Forests;Water use will need to be licensed for each purpose; andNew storages will require an engineering plan.Eligible Costs: Construction, materials, machinery/equipment (gates, valves, etc.) and other costs associated with the construction;Pumping systems and watering troughs to keep livestock out of the existing reservoir are recommended and are eligible costs, provided the reservoir is deemed to provide a secure source in periods of extended drought; andOther professional services associated with the project supervision.Ineligible Items:Water distribution system; andUsed materials.Regulatory Requirements: Water licence for the proposed use, (e.g., irrigation) of the water source (i.e., aquifer, stream);Water licence for the proposed storage volume;Assessment/approval/authorization from the Dam Safety Program staff of the Ministry of Forests;Change approval to make changes in and about a stream (if applicable); andEasement (if applicable).Ineligible Activities:Activities or costs incurred prior to approval (no retroactive approval permitted);In-kind activities;Activities to support non-agricultural water use;Activities not directly related to agricultural water use;Purchase of farm equipment and related accessories or attachments;Activities that are not compliant with federal, provincial, or local/municipal regulations;Financial compensation for lost income, production or land or other associated losses due to water shortages, government orders, or other reasons;Activities to remove land from the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR);Purchase of land or easement;Regular or on-going operating or maintenance activities;Training or educational courses;Financing charges, loan interest payments, bank fees and related charges;Activities currently receiving funding from other funding sources; andGST and other taxes/credits reimbursed to applicant.Program Details: Deadline for application December 18, 2025;An initial payment (50%) will be made by IAF to all projects upon signing of their contribution agreement, however IAF may reduce this advance based on project/applicant risk;Interim and final payments will not be initiated by IAF until reporting requirements are satisfactorily met by the client; Interim and final payments will be made based on actual expenses reported and payments will be made in arrears;All reports require a final report and a minimum of 20% of approved funding will be retained by IAD, pending submission of final reporting; andIf permits are pending/under review but the application is otherwise complete, IAF will proceed to consider and adjudicate the application, however any approval will be conditional until all required documentation is received.

If not, they are only eligible to apply for Stream 3 funding;Applications must meet all technical, environmental, and regulatory standards and/or requirements, as applicable;This program allows for stacking with other funding sources up to 100% of project costs. Process Best Practices:Applications for funding should be complete at the time of submission, if any required documentation is not submitted with the application, it will be returned to the applicant requesting missing information.Forms and Links: Program Webpage: click hereApplication Portal: click hereProgram Guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The African Swine Fever Prevention and Preparedness investment aims to enhance efforts to prevent African swine fever from entering Canada and prepare for potential outbreak. The Welfare Slaughter and Disposal Stream will provide non-repayable contributions to projects that focus on processor retrofits and regional preparation for welfare slaughter and disposal. The program offers up to 85% funding of total eligible costs up to $1 million. Grant Value: Provincial, Territorial and municipal government applicants may apply for funding up to 60% of total eligible costs; All other eligible applicants may apply for funding up to 85% of total eligible costs; andThe max contribution for a project with generally not exceed $1 million over 3 years. Turnaround Time: Approximately 100 business daysEligible Applicants:For-profit organizations that exist to make a profit. They can include: Corporations; andPartnership.Not-for-profit organizations that operate solely for social welfare, civic improvement, pleasure or recreation, any other purpose except profit. They may include: Sector council; andCorporation. Provincial/ Territorial/ Municipal governmentsIndigenous (First Nation, Inuit, Metis). They may include:First Nations, Inuit or Metis community and/or government;First Nations, Inuit or Metis association;First Nations, Inuit or Metis not-for-profit organization; andFirst Nations, Inuit or Metis for-profit organization. Academia organizations involved in providing education or developing educational materials or tools. They may include: Private university and college;Public degree-granting college; andPublic degree-granting university. OtherIf none of the other selections apply, select 'other' and specify the organization type.Eligible Activities: Program will prioritize projects that support the pork industry's ASF prevention and mitigation efforts;Processor retrofits and regional preparation for welfare slaughter and disposal:Evaluation of technologies for destruction and disposal;Processor retrofits;Preparation for carcass disposal;Creation of engineering designs for retrofits and disposal sites;Development of transportation strategies for slaughter and disposal, including truck washes;Development of contingency plans;Purchase of slaughter and disposal equipment and provision of training on proper usage;Welfare slaughter and disposal exercises; and Other activities that support the objective of the program.Eligible Costs:In the case of for-profit organizations, administrative costs do not apply to their projects however all other organizations administrative fees will be calculated at a 10% flat rate:Project management costs;Salaries;Administrative office supples and expenses;Audit fees;Bank fees; Insurance; Legal fees; Administrative information technology products and services including maintenance; andOther overhead type expenditures. Salaries and Benefits;Contracted Services:Inspection;Project management to undertake activities; Consultant/ expert services;Installation/ construction;Financial auditing;Environmental assessment; and researchTravel:Per diems (meals, incidentals and taxis);Accommodations;Transportation, such as airfare; andHospitality.Capital Expenditures:Capital Assets are tangible assets that are purchased, constructed, developed or otherwise acquired and:are used in the production or supply of goods, the delivery of services or to produce program outputsare not intended for resale in the ordinary course of operationsbetterments (which are expenditures relating to the alteration or modernization of an asset that appreciably prolong the period of usefulness of the item or improve its functionality)the cost of which is considered to include the purchase price plus other acquisition costs, such as installation costs, freight charges, transportation insurance costs, duties, and the non-refundable portion of provincial sales taxes, GST/HST or other value-added taxeshas a useful life in excess of one (1) year and a per item cost greater than $10,000Other Direct Project costs:shipping;printing;conference fees/registration fees;construction material costs;translation; andcosts related to production of materials/documents/marketing plans. Program Details: The expected outcomes of this stream are: Increased sector readiness for ASF outbreak;Sector, including processors from underrepresented and marginalized group, is prepared to mitigate the impacts of an ASF outbreak; andIncrease resiliency of the Canadian hog sector. Applications must demonstrate how the proposed project will promote industry preparedness for ASF, as well as provide clearly defined targets and performance measures.

language, including instrumental works; and This program does not support commissions, or the
creation of new works prior to recording;Music video production including: official music videos, pre-recorded and live-streamed

streamed videos must continue to be available after the live stream as a permanent

        2024/05/24

      
    
    
  





    
      




  
      
        Recently Changed 
        Applications are open for a limited third intake; andThe expression of interest deadline is May 24, 2024.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The program will invest up to $5,000,000 in non-repayable funding for projects that modernize, scale and increase regional capabilities and capacity for small vessel construction and either boat and ship dry dock or, overhaul, refit, maintenance and repair infrastructure in British Columbia. The program funding is provided through two capital investment streams. Grant Value: Stream 1: 50% of capital costs up to $500,000;Stream 2: 25% of project capital costs up to $5,000,000.Turnaround Time: 10-15 business daysEligible Applicants: Businesses and for-profit organizations of all sizes that as of the date of the applications to the program:Operated in the marine, maritime and/or ship building and repair sector;Have been operating in B.C. for at least 24 months;Have an existing footprint in the province of British Columbia;Can demonstrate being a viable operation trough positive cash flow or have net positive assets; andAre not currently preparing the business for closure, dissolution, bankruptcy or sale. Organizations can apply individually, or in collaboration with other eligible applicants, if the primary applicant is an eligible entity.Eligible Projects: Must be located in B.C;Contribute to short to long term regional economic growth, sustainability and/or social benefits for British Columbians; andMust demonstrate a clear and justified value proposition to fulfilling one or more of the expected program outcomes. Eligible Project Costs: Eligible costs are those that are essential to project delivery, including: Capital expenditures (equipment, machinery, technology and construction materials);Construction of buildings or other facilities on existing land owned or controlled by applicant;Professional, contractor and subcontractor fees;Freight or material transportation costs;Installation and implementation costs; Other costs directly related to project implementation; andWorkforce development costs for up-skilling or micro-credentials directly related to supporting
and/or the operation of the delivered project.Ineligible Project Costs: Costs not directly related to the project;Costs for which the recipient is eligible for a rebate from government sources, including taxes;Early research, concept development, scoping, feasibility studies, and prototyping including basic
and applied Research and Development (Technology Readiness Level 1-7);Extraordinary or abnormal fees beyond customary market rates;Entertainment and marketing costs;Operating costs (ex. Core staff salaries, bonuses, repayment loans, cost-share obligations or
refinancing debts, fines or penalties, membership fees, dues, taxes, depreciation of assets, etc.);Cost related to the development of the Program application; andAcquisition of land.Program Details: Stream 1: Aimed at smaller projects and/or smaller boat and shipyards to support equipment and facility modernization and help improve their efficiency, productivity and competitiveness in areas including: overhaul, refit, maintenance, and repair of large and small vessels, including small vessel construction; andIncluding relevant up-skilling or micro credentials required for new or updated technology.Stream 2: Projects that address the wide-spread need for increased dry dock and wharfage proponents to increase capacity for more overhaul, refit, maintenance, and repair activity; andIncluding relevant up-skilling or micro credentials required for new or updated technology.Successful projects should align with the expected program outcomes: Modernize, scale, and expand industrial maritime infrastructure in B.C;Attract new market demand and investment;Establish B.C. as a leader in innovative and high-value maritime activity;Stabilize and grow well-paying, high-quality and inclusive jobs;Provide opportunity for high-value knowledge based clean made-in-BC technologies; and Contribute to decrease of harmful air emissions. The program supports projects that have a high degree of readiness and can ideally begin within less than
six months of approval.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices: This program can be stacked with federal grant funding;Stacking with other provincial funding may be permitted up to a max provincial contribution of 50% of the total project costs;This program does not allow for funding to be used retroactively;Projects should begin within 6 months of approval; andThere is no restriction on how many applications that can be submitted by any applicant however, funding is limited so projects submitted should be selective.Forms and Links: Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereApplication Portal: click here

Each consortium must be industry-led with at least 1 Canadian-SME and at least 1 potential customer. Projects must have a total cost of at least $3,000,000 and be completed by December 31, 2025. The intent of the program is to share the total investment required for Canadian tech companies to strengthen their intellectual property, refine commercial plans & product development roadmaps and address adoption & procurement requirements in their target markets.Grant Value: 35% of the total project costs, minimum project cost of $1 millionNote: There is no cap on project size, however, the total budget is $20M for 10-15 applicantsTurnaround Time: 1-2 weeksEligible Applicants:Must have a consortium of at least 3 organizations, including:At least 1 Canadian small & medium-sized business (SME);At least 1 organization representing a potential customer of the proposed A.I. solution;Applicant organizations may be one of the following organization types:For-profit;Non-profit that funds research & development and where funding is received primarily from private-sector organizations;International organizations;Non-federal Crown corporations whose funding is derived from commercial activities; andCommunity organizations aimed at improving social health and well-being must meet all 3 of the below conditions:Promote the adoption of AI solutions by community institutions (excluding for-profit organizations);Do not aim to generate profit for for-profit organizations; andInclude at least one not-for-profit organization.Have an artificial intelligence technology solution around Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 7;Eligible Expenses:Must be incremental to regular business undertakings;Must be directly related to the execution of project activities;Work must be performed in Canada unless otherwise pre-approved;Be one of the following expense types, including:Wages, salaries, including Mandatory Employment Related Costs (MERCs);Contractor and subcontractors;Cannot exceed 35% of the total eligible project costs.Equipment costs (purchase, rental, operation and maintenance);Materials and supplies;User fees;Incremental room or facility rentals;Travel costs;Dissemination and publication costs;Insurance costs required to comply with the MPA insurance obligations;Foreign costs (costs incurred outside of Canada);Must first be pre-authorized on an exceptional basis.Costs related to the project Intellectual Property (IP);Legal, accounting, and consulting fees related to executing commercial agreements between project partners.Maximum of $20,000 per SME per project;Only SMEs are eligible to claim this expense type.Ineligible Expenses:Routine administration and operation costs;Discretionary employee benefits (e.g. dental, extended health, insurance premiums, pension, bonuses, etc.);Taxes, fines, penalties, cancellation fees;Purchase or construction of buildings or land;Legal, accounting and consulting fees in connection with litigation or financial reorganization or extraordinary or abnormal fees for professional advice;Honoraria, gifts, donations and entertainment expenses.Program Details:Eligible projects costs: at least $3,000,000 with no maximum project size;Project duration: maximum 2 years and completed by December 31, 2025;Other government sources of funding must be disclosed to the program and included in the project budget;All project teams are required to track project expenses, substantiate them with evidence, and regularly report on their actual and forecasted project costs;The program will not take equity in the solution or organization receiving funding; andThe program reserves the right to adjust its co-investment rate and the right to withdraw commitments to co-invest if:Projects no longer meet the requirement of the program; and/orThere are unapproved or substantial changes in the project proposal.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides funding of 50% up to $250,000 towards Third-Party Fleet Energy Assessments and Truck/Trailer Equipment Retrofits. This stream aims to increase the knowledge and capacity of the on-road freight transportation sector to adopt energy efficient measures tailored to operational needs by providing financial support.Grant Value: 50% up to $250,000Turnaround Time: 90 business days.Eligible Applicants:Businesses;Industry associations;Research associations;Standards organizations;Indigenous and community groups;Canadian academic institutes; Provincial, territorial, regional, or municipal governments or their departments or agencies where applicable;Be operating in Canada; andHave one or more heavy-duty vehicles for business use in their fleet that are licensed and insured to operate in Canada.Ineligible Applicants: Softwood lumber companies and those that are vertically integrated with softwood lumber companies.Eligible Activities:Have been in service for a minimum of 1 year; andBe within the eligible vehicles' weight classes:Class 2B - Between 3,856 kg and 4,536 kg; Class 3 - Between 4,536 kg and 6,350 kg;Class 4 -  Between 6,350 kg and 7,257 kg;Class 5 - Between  7,257 kg and 8,845 kg;Class 6 - Between 8,845 kg and 11,793 kg;Class 7 -  Between 11,793 kg and 14,969 kg;Class 8 - More than 14,969 kg.Ineligible Activities: Vans;SUVs;Pickup trucks;Public transit buses;School buses; and Off-road vehicles. Program Details: The program provides funding for two types of activities including:Thirds Party Fleet Energy Assessment Grant; andTruck/Trailer Equipment Retrofits.Third-Party Fleet Energy Assessment Grant:Applicants can hire a third-party energy assessment company of their choosing to complete the Fleet Energy Assessment;There are two types of assessments that will be eligible for funding:Basic Third-Party Assessment, this assessment explores fleet retrofits and small-scale logistical best practices projects(50% of costs up to a max of $20,000); andEnhanced Third-Party Assessment, this assessment explores more complex and large-scale engine re-power, alternative fuel truck purchase, and logistical best-practice projects(50% of the cost up to $40,000).Truck/Trailer Equipment Retrofits:To be eligible for this applicant's fleet must undergo a Fleet Energy Assessment before they purchase any new fuel-saving device(s) and the assessment must analyze and recommend the devices that the applicant plans to purchase.Retrofits include: Aerodynamics Retrofits;Anti-idling Retrofits;Auxiliary Power Units Retrofits;Tire Retrofits;Other devices. A full list of retrofits and contributions can be found here.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Program can be stacked with other federal funding however it must not exceed 75% of the total project costs except in the case where the recipient is: An Indigenous organization;An Indigenous owned or partially owned project;A not-for-profit organization; orA provincial, territorial, regional, or municipal government or their department or agencyIn the above cases, the total Canadian government funding authorized will not exceed 100% of total project costs.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Youth in Manufacturing Initiative provides employers funding of up to $2,500 to hire youth aged 16-20 for short-term placements. The intent of the program is to offset the training cost of hiring youth and to build the talent pipeline in manufacturing.Grant Value: up to $2500.Turnaround Time: a few days at most.Eligible Employers: A registered Canadian business or organization operating in one of the four Atlantic Canada Provinces: New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island;A member of Canada's manufacturing sector or a related sector;Commitment to a minimum of 12-14 hours of participant training during the work period; andCommitment to provide participants with 8-10 weeks work (80-120 hours).Eligible Candidates:Between 16-20 years old at the program start;Legally entitled to work in Canada; andReside in Atlantic Canada (NB, NL, NS or PEI).Program Details: Seasonal  employment is eligible for funding;Eligible employers can apply for funding to support any position across all areas of the organization, including but not limited to: Production;Design;Supply Chain;Finance;Office Administration;Sales and Marketing; andHuman Resources. Employers can apply without a candidate a place will be held for a limited time to allow for recruitment;Placements can range from 8-10 weeks;Required to complete the program successfully:Mentorship training completed by a current employee;Manufacturing Foundations and Lean Fundamentals training completed by the participant; andRegular check-in surveys completed by the participant and employers.Participant will gain valuable knowledge and micro-credentials by completing two online self-directed training programs during their term;EMC's Manufacturing Foundations( approx 6 hours) certifies that the participant has developed an authentic understanding of what it takes to be successful in manufacturing and will demonstrate employability soft skills in a manufacturing workplace.Lean Fundamentals (approx 6-8 hours) certifies that the learner has developed an understanding of the principles of Lean thinking in a manufacturing environment.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program does allows for funding to be used retroactively within one month of the participants start date;Stacking may be permitted depending on the scenario, stacking eligibility needs to be confirmed with the provincial, territorial or municipal program and EMC;Participants that have previously worked with the firm in a short-term capacity can be hired if all other eligibility is met; andEmployer cannot hire their spouse, sibling or child as an employee under the program. Forms & Links:Program Webpage: click hereApplication Portal: click here

          open until filled
      
    
    
  
Wages covered by grant in percent.




    
      




  

      Grant Criteria 
      This program will be funding  demonstrations towards innovative wood-based building systems and technologies, schematic design and bio-products used in the design and construction of infrastructure that have low greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The main goal of the program is to prioritize direct funding to areas of high growth potential that target low carbon/GHG emissions.Grant Value: Schematic Design 50% up to $400,000; and Innovative building solutions for wood construction and advanced bio-based products 50% up to $1,000,000.Turnaround Time: Initial EOI 14 to 45 days;Full Project Proposals:Window 1: Apply by September 30, 2023 for decision February 29, 2024;Window 2: Apply by December 31, 2023 for decision by May 31, 2024;Window 3: Apply by March 31, 2024 for decision by August 41, 2024; andWindow 4: Apply by June 30, 2024 for a decision by November 30, 2024.Eligible Applicants: For-profit organizations;Not-for-profit organizations; Indigenous organizations and groups;Canadian academic institutions; andProvincial, territorial, regional and municipal governments.Eligible Projects: Schematic Design: A project to develop the design of a new wood or wood-hybrid infrastructure or existing infrastructure targeting the early design stage;The project must be linked to an actual project in Canada; andThe approaches submitted must be related to the use of wood and the mitigation of GHG emissions associated with the design of the actual project.Innovative building solutions for wood construction:A project to deploy innovative wood-based construction methods, technologies, processes or assemblies to address specific sustainability, construction processes or innovation goals; andThese innovative building solutions for wood
construction are targeting new or existing wood or wood-hybrid infrastructure projects that
are shovel-ready or under construction.Advanced bio-based products: A project to deploy the use of advanced wood-based products in existing or new construction to replace conventional construction materials in building to lower the buildings carbon footprint. e.g use of wood fibre insulation, wood-based cladding panels, etc. Eligible Activities: R&D to support the schematic design/system/technology/bio-product and code
compliance (fire, seismic, acoustics, building envelope, connections, durability, etc.),
including engineering design, testing and modelling;Additional engineering/design efforts associated with the innovative technology, system,
bio-product or schematic design, including construction drawings and preparing plans
for deconstruction;Development and implementation of construction fire safety and moisture management
strategies/plans associated with the design concept/system/technology/bio-products;Consultation efforts as part of the integrated project delivery approach/process;Cost of innovative wood-based building technology/system and bio-product;Case studies, replication factsheets, cost analyses;In-situ testing, instrumentation and monitoring of structure performance associated with
the innovative building system and/or technology and bio-based products;Code analysis and the preparation and detailing of alternative solutions, including
feasibility, engineering, and scientific studies;Costs associated with the validation of the design concept, engineering calculations and
analysis, product and system testing, and other demonstrations that may be required to
support the approval of the project by Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ);Virtual design and construction; and GHG emission mitigation documentation, including LCA and Environmental Product
Declarations.Eligible Expenses: Salaries and benefits of staff;Professional/consulting/technical services;Data acquisition and technical equipment/materials;Technical software and licences;Travel expenses, including accommodation, meals, and allowances (based on National Joint Council rates) subject to the program’s pre-approval;Expenditures related to demonstration projects, including, but not limited to, permit fees, construction documentation, design, engineering and testing costs, and other related expenditures;Overhead expenditures, provided they are related to the conduct of the project and can be attributed to it (overhead expenditures may be included in the total project cost to a maximum of 15% of eligible expenditures); and GST, PST or HST, net of any tax rebate to which the recipient is entitled.Ineligible Expenses:Costs related to the applicant’s office equipment and office rental;Professional fees of accountants, notaries, and lawyers, (except those related to the
taking of patents and their verification by a third party);Land purchase and related costs (e.g., professional fees for the notary public, zoning
changes, brokerage, surveyor and publication fees, transfer fees for the purchase of
land, easements or rights-of-way, and other costs related to the acquisition of land);Loss of profits, loss of production, or other losses caused by activities related to the
realization of the project;The cost of building materials other than those related to testing and the innovation of the project;Ongoing operating costs (e.g., electricity consumption, operation, maintenance, networking fees, and subscription fees); andCosts incurred outside the Eligible Expenditure Period, including those for preparing
this application.Program Details: The proposed project must constitute an advancement of wood use
as a low-carbon building material;It must also demonstrate the degree of building innovation and
novelty through the use of new innovative wood or bio-based products, building technologies and
systems, and advanced design concepts;All eligible expenses must be incurred and paid on or before March 31, 2026;However, completion of physical work paid for by the recipient or recipient’s partner(s) may extend past the program’s end date up to a maximum of 2 years.Preference will be given to projects with the lowest carbon footprint and will apply innovations in more than one category.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices: Program does not allow for retroactive funding;This program can be stacked with other sources of funding as long as the total contribution does not exceed 100% of project costs; andPreference will be given to projects that provide the lowest carbon footprint and will apply
innovations in more than one category.Forms & Links: Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Accelerating Hydrogen challenge will invest up to $25 million in later-stage pilot, demonstration, and first-of-kind projects. The aim of the program is to build a strong pipeline of hydrogen technologies across Alberta's value chain including hydrogen production, storage, transmission, and end-use.Grant Value: Max funding $7 million, minimum funding amount $250,000.Turnaround Time: Shortlist decision announcement November 8, 2023.Final decision March, 2024. Eligible Applicant: Innovators;Technology developers;Indigenous communities;Industrial facility owners/operators;Industrial associations; Small and medium sized enterprises;Research and development organizations;Universities municipalities;Not-for-profit organizations;Government research labs; andIndividuals. Eligible Projects: Proposals are invited for technology solutions in all areas of the hydrogen value chain including production, transportation, storage, end use and enablers;Projects of interest include, but are not limited to:Low-Carbon Hydrogen Production:Next-generation solutions for producing hydrogen from methane;Electrolytic production of hydrogen from water and clean electricity; andOther emerging alternative hydrogen production pathways including photolytic hydrogen, bio-hydrogen, etc.Novel Hydrogen Infrastructure:Hydrogen pipeline technologies including coatings and treatments;Novel hydrogen storage;Hydrogen distribution and delivery solutions;Hydrogen safety and infrastructure enablers; andHydrogen districts, clusters, and similar.Novel Hydrogen Carriers:Liquid carriers such as ammonia, methanol, or synthetic fuels;Metal-organic frameworks and similar; andPower-to-gas and other hydrogen-based energy storage solutions.Hydrogen in Industry:Substitution of low-emissions hydrogen as an industrial feedstock, chemical input, or fuel; andHydrogen fuel cells and turbines for production of power and/or heat for commercial or industrial applications.Hydrogen in Transportation:Novel hydrogen fueling infrastructure;Hydrogen-fueled heavy-duty vehicles and equipment (transit, freight, services, mining, construction, agriculture, etc.); andHydrogen for rail and aviation.Eligible Costs: Labour Costs;Equipment Costs;Materials and Supplies Costs;Consulting/Sub-Contractor Costs;Travel Costs; Overhead CostsNOTE: A full breakdown of the Eligible costs can be found hereIneligible Costs:Hiring of Personnel;Regulatory Approval;Land;Marketing;Entertainment;Protection of Intellectual Property; andGST and PST.NOTE: A full breakdown of the ineligible costs can be found hereProgram Details: All projects must demonstrate a clear and justified value proposition for reducing GHG emissions or enabling the transition to a net-zero economy in Alberta;Technology solutions can originate from anywhere globally but must be demonstrated or implemented in Alberta during the project;To be eligible for funding projects must start at a minimum of TRL 7;There are no limits to how many applications an applicant submits.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program does not allow for retroactive funding;The program allows for stacking of funds; Process Best Practices:Collaboration between multiple organizations is eligible and encouraged for this opportunity;Successful applicants must commence work on the proposed projects within 120 days of funding approval; andTechnologies with indirect or enabled emissions reductions are eligible, provided a strong case can be made for how the technology will support emissions benefits.Forms & Links:Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereApplication Portal: click here

The intent of the program is to help small businesses boost their growth and meet their business needs.Grant Value: $15,000 per category (within Canada) + $40,000 per category (globally)Turnaround Time: Winners within Canada will be announced on or about November 14, 2023Eligible Applicant:Be located in Canada (excluding Quebec);Have between 0-50 employees;Be a paying Zero subscriber (either directly, or via Zero accounting/bookkeeping) at the time of entry;Be operating on a for-profit or non-profit basis.Program Details:Limit of 1 entry per contest category per small business;Award categories & scoring criteria:Innovating for Sustainability (total points available: 15)Does the applicant demonstrate a clear plan or path toward becoming a more sustainable business? (5points)Does the applicant outline the positive impacts sustainability will have on their business? (5points)Does the applicant show how sustainability is a long-term part of the business strategy or goals? (5points)Innovating with technology (total points available: 15)Does the applicant demonstrate a clear plan or path towards digitalizing parts of their operations or incorporating new technology into their business? (5 points)Does the applicant explain how new emerging technologies will positively impact and change the way they operate or serve their customers? (5points)Does the applicant show how innovation is a long-term part of the business strategy or goals?(5points)Strengthening community connection (total points available: 15)Does the applicant demonstrate how they bring people together and make an impact on their local community? ( 5points)Does the applicant show specific plans or a path toward contributing to philanthropy or social good? (5points)Does the applicant show how community and impacting their local community is a long-term part of their strategy or goals? (5points)Upskilling for the Future (total points available: 15)Does the applicant demonstrate a clear plan or goals around upskilling themselves or their employees? (5points)Does the applicant show how they will benefit from training and development for themselves or employees? (5points)Does the applicant show how upskilling and professional development is a long-term part of the business strategy or goals?
