      Grant Criteria 
      Stream 2 of the Green Freight Program provides funding up to 50% of project costs to a maximum of $5 million towards fuel switching, engine repowers, and purchase or low-carbon alternative fuel. Grant Value: Up to 50% of project costs to a max of $5 millionTurnaround Time: within 100 business days.Eligible Applicants: Valid incorporated or registered entity in Canada including:Companies;Industry associations;Research associations;Standards organizations;Indigenous and community groups;Canadian academic institutions; andProvincial, territorial, regional, or municipal governments or their departments or agencies where applicable.Have completed a fleet energy assessment that recommend the actions proposed in their application.Eligible Vehicles:Have been in service for a minimum of 1 year; andBe within the eligible vehicles' weight classes:Weight ClassGross vehicle weight rating (GVWR)Class 2B Between 3,856 kg and 4,536 kg Class 3 Between 4,536 kg and 6,350 kgClass 4  Between 6,350 kg and 7,257 kgClass 5  Between  7,257 kg and 8,845 kgClass 6 Between 8,845 kg and 11,793 kg Class 7  Between 11,793 kg and 14,969 kgClass 8 More than 14,969 kgIneligible Vehicles:Vans;SUVs;Pickup Trucks; Transit Buses; andOff-road Vehicles.Eligible Project Activities: There are two types of eligible project activites:Repowers:Must submit a list of technologies/ equipment;Repowers must be permanent modifications, demonstrated the capacity to reduce diesel consumption of medium and heavy duty vehicles, and reduce GHG emissions by switching the fuel used to a lower-carbon alternative.Purchase of alternative fuel vehicles:Must make a commitment to use a minimum average of 40% renewable or non-fossil fuels is required to be considered for funding;The program will only provide funding for the incremental cost of the new vehicle that utilizes lower-carbon fuels versus purchasing a standard truck.Eligible Expenses:Professional Services;Capital Expenses;In-kind contributions limited to installation of equipment; and GST, PST, and HST.Ineligible Expenses: Other In-kind contributions; andCost occurred outside the eligible expenditure period.Program Details:Program funding will be allocated for stream 2 from April 2024 to March 2027;Applicants must demonstrate at least 50% secured funding for the total cost of the project; andMust show engagement with an equipment and/or vehicle supplier and have quoted estimates of their project costs including delivery dare of the equipment.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program does not allow for retroactive funding;Program can be stacked with other federal funding however it must not exceed 75% of the total project costs except in the case where the recipient is: An Indigenous organization;An Indigenous owned or partially owned project;A not-for-profit organization; orA provincial, territorial, regional, or municipal government or their department or agencyIn the above cases, the total Canadian government funding authorized will not exceed 100% of total project costs.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click hereApplication Form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The program provides funding up to $150,000 to assist small food processors in scaling up operations to increase productivity, business opportunities and competitiveness as well as support existing licensed Farm Gate Plus and Abbatoir operations to scale up and strengthen local meat supply chains.Grant Value: Up to 75% of eligible project costs Minimum funding of $25,000 up to a max of $150,000.Turnaround Time: 30 days.Eligible Applicants: Established food and/or seafood processing business, with: Minimum of two years in operation;Minimum of $100k gross annual revenues and a maximum of $499k gross annual revenues. Applicants will be required to provide documentation that proves how they meet the small food processor revenue criteria; andProcessors that materially transform a product.Established commercial food hub, commissary kitchen and other shared-use commercial food processing facilities:Facility not required to meet minimum or maximum gross annual revenues but must be in operation for minimum of one year;Projects must fit within one priority commodity group;Projects must intended for shared use and benefit multiple business tenants within the facility;Individual business tenants within these types of facilities are also eligible to apply as an established food and/or seafood processing business if they meet the criteria detailed above. Ineligible Applicants: Retail food services or operations;Fruit and vegetable packers, except when conducting other eligible forms of food processing on the same premises. Only processors that materially transform a product / included under NAICs codes 311 or 312 are eligible;Processors/manufacturers of pet food, except where provides value-add to waste from food supply;Processors/manufacturers of Cannabis-infused food products and beverages;Restaurants and food service, including catering services;Packaging material manufacturers;Processors/manufacturers of health products or nutritional supplements;Processors/manufacturers of alcohol-based beverages and ingredients meant for alcohol-based beverages;New entrant businesses;Animal feed processors; andNon-BC-based businesses.Eligible Activities/ Expenses: Purchase and install new or upgrade/expanded facilities and infrastructure and equipment which includes: Capital investments in new and upgraded/expanded facility/ infrastructure (e.g. new cooler/ freezer, production room expansion)Eligible costs include costs for renovations, site improvement, construction and other related costs.New/upgraded equipment/machinery to increase production capacity or support product line expansion;Related training and upskilling to support adoption and implementation;Training costs must be provided by an external organization or company and can only be claimed with an invoice.Purchase and install new technology systems which includes:New innovative technologies, software, advanced automation such as robotics, digital or Artificial Intelligence technology and systems that would increase processing capacity;Eligible costs include costs for facility changes, upgrades and modifications required for installation fo advanced automation or manufacturing technology or equipment;Related training and upskilling support adoption and implementation;Training cost must be provided by an external organization or company and can only be claimed with an invoice.Applied Research and development for new improved products, lab analysis, packaging etc.R&D for new improved products using technology, access to laboratory equipment for food and ingredient development and analysis such as pH, shelf-life, microbiology testing, sensory analysis, ingredient and nutritional analysis, and applied research support and expertise;Activities to support product development or adaption of new products must be commercialized and launched before February 1, 2023;Related training and upskilling to support adoption and implementation;Training costs must be provided by an external organization or compny and can only be claimed with an invoice.Ineligible Activities and Expenses:In-kind activities;Operational labour or staff wages not directly related to the implementation of project activities;Equipment, facilities, and technology investments that do not enhance processing productivity;Planning or training specific projects not directly related to acquisition of infrastructure or equipment;Internal expenses for general staff training;Regular capital expenditures, machinery costs, and general operating expenses made in the ordinary course of business;Early-stage business or feasibility planning;Market development and marketing activities;Individual business support for food safety and other certifications processes; andActivities related to the development of products that include alcohol, tobacco, or cannabis.Examples of Eligible Projects:Build, upgrade or expand infrastructure(new cooler or freezer, production room expansion);Purchase and installation of equipment or machinery (including IT systems) to increase production capacity or support product line expansion, including specialized training related to the use of the equipment and/or machinery; andActivities or equipment to support development of a new product development or adaptation of existing products to meet the needs of customers in different markets.Program Details: BC processed food definition:The final product undergoes one or more of the following activites performed in a commercial food and/or beverage manufacturing facility located in BC, for the purpose of sale and distribution:General physical alterations: grinding beef, milling wheat, crushing tomatoes, shredding cheese, chopping cucumbers, etc.;Extending shelf life: freezing, canning, drying, pickling, smoking, fermenting, etc; andCombining ingredients to make a new product: Baking muffins, making pizza, blending juice, mixing salad greens, etc.The following are not considered Food processing:Cleaning;Washing;Bagging; andPackaging and/or wrapping. Application intake opens September 21, 2023;Application deadline is November 2, 2023 at 4:30pm PST;Funding notification to applicants as well as earliest project start date December 1, 2023;Project must be completed by February 1, 2026;Project length can be no longer than 24 months;Funding will be allocated across Commodity groups as follows: Commodity GroupsFunding AlocationProject Funding LimitCost-shared ratioGroup 1: Seafood, meat, fruit and vegetable processors$1 MillionMin $25k to $150k Max75%Group 2: Plant-based protein, dairy, bakeries and tortillas, beverages, grain and oilseed milling processors$650kMin $25k to $150k Max75%Group 3: Sugar and confectionary, and other foods (snack food, coffee and tea, flavoring syrup and concentrate, seasoning, dressing and prepared sauces) other food manufacturing processors$350kMin $25k to $150k Max75%

      Grant Criteria 
      The Food Security Emergency Planning Preparedness(FSPP) Fund provides up to $2,000,000 for agricultural producers, industry association and local authorities to develop emergency plans and preparedness strategies with a unique focus on food security and agricultural resiliency, including investment in training and proactive procurement of equipment or infrastructure in anticipation of emergency events.Grant Value:Stream 1: Up to 100% to a minimum of $25,000 to a maximum of $150,000;Stream 2: Up to 75% for individual businesses, and up to 100% for industry associations to a minimum of $50,000 to a maximum of $2,000,000.Turnaround Time: Up to 2 months.Eligible Applicants:Stream 1: BC Local Governments;BC First Nations;BC-Based Agriculture and Agri-Food Industry Associations; andBC-Based Seafood Associations;Stream 2: BC-Based Industry Associations;Individual producers/processors are not eligible to apply for funding under FSPP. Industry Associations are encouraged to apply on behalf of producers/processors to put projects forward that have a broader sector benefit/impact.Primary Processors; andAncillary Service Providers that have a direct role in supporting agricultural emergency preparedness and response (Ancillary service providers are those who provide service directly to agriculture producers, which could include veterinarians, mass carcass disposal, providers or livestock and poultry feed, and agricultural transportation services.).Note: Eligible primary processors are those involved in the initial processing of agricultural products, such as abattoirs for livestock and poultry.Eligible Activities and Costs: Stream 1: Planning:Development of an agriculture industry association Emergency Plan for emergency events that may impact their sector;Development of a local authority or First Nation agriculture emergency plan ( or an agriculture component of a broader emergency plan) to support agricultural producers within their geographic area of jurisdiction; Development and Training staff, volunteers, or Contractors who will activate or support the agriculture-related emergency plan; Training Programs related to emergency response an d activation of emergency plans in support of agriculture;Development of tools, policies, protocols, and procedures for response to or management of emergency incidents related to agriculture;Hiring of staff or contractors to conduct agriculture emergency planning activities; and Exercising of agriculture emergency plans. Stream 2: Preparedness, Infrastructure and Equipment:Procurement and installation of Equipment or Infrastructure required to support emergency response actions in support of agriculture (but does not include prevention and mitigation);Upgrade existing equipment or infrastructure used to support emergency response actions in support of agriculture;Short-term operational costs associated with equipment or infrastructure (such as training or insurance) required to support emergency actions in support of agriculture;Procurement (purchase, rent, lease) of equipment required for response to emergencies affecting agriculture;Developing/establishing contracted response activities versus using the funding for actual operational response activities (i.e. the funding is not for operational response but for preparedness); Training and exercising to utilize existing or acquired response equipment;Research of response options/methods, including procuring scientific, academic, or other research specialists to conduct research or advance new methods for improved disease outbreak response, such as depopulation methods.Ineligible Participants and Activities:Individual producers and/or processors. Exceptions are provided to Primary Processors involved in the initial processing of agricultural products, such as abattoirs for livestock and poultry;Non-agricultural individuals or groups (including Seafood/Aquaculture);Provincial and federal governments;Crown Corporations Activities or costs incurred prior to approval(no retroactive approval permitted);Prevention and Mitigation projects;Projects eligible for funding or compensation under public or private insurance programs or qualify for an AgriRecovery framework; andIn-kind activities.Program Details:Applications will be open for 90 days, with all applications being reviewed and processed together following the intake closing date;Applications will be evaluated based on priority categories which can be found here;All projects must be completed by January 15, 2026; andIAF will complete adjudication within 60 days after the application intake deadline.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Food Storage Distribution and Retail program provides funding under 2 streams, stream 1 up to a max of $3 million and stream up to a max of $150,000 to support food system partnerships in BC to advance practice, processes, infrastructure , and collaborations that will strengthen and streamline food system logistics, storage and transportation and address supply chain bottlenecks.Grant Value:Stream 1: Min $100,000 up to a max of $3 million; andStream 2: Min $25,000 up to a max of $150,000.Turnaround Time: Earliest final decision January 1, 2024.Eligible Applicants: Stream 1: Input suppliers;Producers;Processors;Co-packers;Distributors;Wholesalers;Independent retailers;Industry associations; Commercial food hubs; andIndigenous nations and organizations.Stream 2:Only independent grocery retailers are eligible to apply.Ineligible Applicants:Non-independent retailers (e.g., national/chain retailers);Manufacturers of alcoholic beverages;Pet food, cannabis-infused products, and/or nutritional supplements;Restaurants and food service, including catering services;Provincial or federal agencies;Non-B.C. based businesses; andNew entrants, with less than two years of operations.Eligible Activities and Expenditures: Eligible project activities and costs are those that support improvements to regional distribution networks and shared storage capacity, and/or improvements to operational capacity of independent grocery retailers;  Including purchasing, developing, or upgrading equipment, facilities and infrastructure;Project activities must clearly demonstrate alignment with the program goal and objectives. This can be by: Having a direct impact on rural, remote and/or Indigenous communities (areas that are more prone to being cut off from their food supply during emergencies or have difficulty accessing food affordably due to high costs/challenges of transporting food to those communities);Supporting the role of independent grocers in providing access to affordable food in rural, remote, and/or indigenous communities;The purchase, development, or upgrade of facilities, equipment or infrastructure that support stronger food system partnerships; andThe establishment or development of food system partnerships.Ineligible Activities and Expenses: In-kind activities;Any costs not specifically required for the execution of the project;Equipment, facilities, and infrastructure investments that do not support B.C.’s food supply chain and address supply chain bottlenecks;Direct income support;Core operational expenses;Existing operating expenses;Staff wages not directly related to the implementation of project activities;Regular capital expenditures, machinery costs, and general operating expenses made in the ordinary course of business;Export subsidies;Direct advertising/promotion;Costs related to activities that directly influence or lobby any level of government;Research and development-specific projects;Planning or training specific projects; andIndividual business support for food safety and other certification processes.Eligible Projects:Stream 1: Regional Distribution Networks and Shared Storage:Warehousing and storage facility improvements that reduce costs and increase food volumes, such as shared facilities at key nodes along the supply chain;Innovative transportation models that reduce costs and increase food volumes, such as shared transportation networks that pool shipments;Partnerships to improve collaboration within the supply chain and increase food supply to specific communities, including through direct sourcing or bulk purchasing ingredients (by processors) or produce ( by independent retailers) and freight optimization;Practices and processes that strengthen supply chains, and increase food availability, such as mobile grocers, inventory management, or aggregation initiatives; andImplementation of technologies that improve the efficiency of the food supply chain, such as digitized inventory management.Stream 2: Independent Grocery Retailers:Purchase of equipment that improves the operational capacity of independent grocery retailers to enable to them to increase the supply of affordable food to local communities, such as cold storage.Program Details: All projects can be 24 months in duration and must be completed by February 1, 2026;EOI deadline for Stream 1 is October 26, 2023;Notification for an invitation to apply for Stream 1 is November 24, 2023;The deadline for Stream 1 application is December 21, 2023.Stream 2 application deadline is November 9, 2023;The earliest Project Start date is January 1, 2024; andFunding will be awarded based on eligibility and alignment with program priorities, subject to available funds.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program can help eligible employers to receive a financial subsidy up to $3,500 to offset onboarding, on-the-job training and wage costs for participants aged 16-24 and up to $2,500 for participants in high school.Grant Value: Up to $3,500 (if not in high school, not enrolled in post secondary education or training); andUp to $2,500 for participants in high school.Turnaround Time: within 1 week of receiving all documentationEligible Employers: Must operate in B.C.; andMust be part of the manufacturing sector (NAICS 31-33).Eligible Candidates: A resident of British Columbia (Canadian Citizen, Permanent Resident or Protected Refugee); Eligible to work in Canada;Aged 16-24; A current high school student OR in a post-secondary program that does not have an integrated learning/co-op component; andParticipants who have previously worked with the employer in a short-term capacity are eligible if all the eligibility requirements are met.Program Details: Placement duration is typically 6-16 weeks;Hours worked can be somewhat flexible:High school participant hours required: 240 hours;Youth not in high school, post-secondary or training hours required: 320 hours.Program Training: All youth participants must complete EMC micro credential training, including:Manufacturing Foundations; andLean Fundamentals.In additions to the youth training, employer receives mentorship training for one employee per placement; andParticipants receive ongoing support from EMC staff through regular check-ins during the placement, and EMC tracks and supports mentor training.Employers can apply for funding to support any position across all areas of the organization including but not limited to: Production;Design;Supply Chain;Finance;Office Administration;Sales and Marketing; andHuman Resource.Employer can apply for funding before securing a participant, and funding will be held for a limited time while the employer recruits;Mentorship in Manufacturing:The mentorship in manufacturing  training program explores workplace mentorship, emphasizing the importance of positive relationships and employee engagement in manufacturing;Participants will learn how to be effective mentors, identify teaching opportunities, and develop mentees;The mentorship in manufacturing training program includes:Introduction to Mentorship;What it means to be a mentor;Mentorship in Manufacturing;Mentorship for new employees;       Grant Criteria 
      The Emerging Innovators Challenge will provide funding  up to $5 million to Alberta based projects to de-risk projects and reduce the time it takes to get them to market. This call is seeking technology scale-up, pilot demonstration, and first-of-kind projects that are led by SMEs and have the potential to catalyze emerging emissions reduction solutions across several areas on the pathway to a carbon neutral economy.Grant Value: Up to 50% with a minimum of $250,000 and a maximum of $5,000,000.Turnaround Time: EOI shortlist notification early February.Eligible Applicants: Lead applicant must be a SME;Indigenous owned enterprises; orNot-for-profit organizations.Eligible Projects:A non-exhaustive list of example technologies that ERA believe could align well with the Challenge include: Digital solutions for logistics, agriculture, energy, and industry, including robotics, automation, and Artificial Intelligence /machine learning;Software-based solutions for managing energy and GHGs, provided they directly enable other emissions reduction technologies;Technologies to reduce waste (agricultural, plastic, food, etc.) and enhance recycling/value recovery;Advanced materials and manufacturing, including biomaterials and critical minerals; Novel low-emission buildings technologies;Precision agriculture and other novel practice-based solutions;Vented and fugitive methane abatement;Omics and other life-sciences-based solutions to reduce GHGs;Detection, measurement, and quantification of methane, N2O, and other GHGs from agriculture, oil & gas, and other sectors; andMeasurement and enhancement of nature-based carbon sequestration (soils, forests, etc.).Ineligible Projects: Hydrogen (this program runs concurrent with ERA’s Accelerating Hydrogen Challenge and
Alberta Innovates’ Hydrogen Centre Of Excellence Competition 2);Zero-Emission Vehicle infrastructure; Business-as-usual energy efficiency retrofits/audits; Technologies previously eligible for ERA’s Energy Savings for Business Program and
SPEED/ETP program streams.Program Details: EOIs are invited for projects that will advance technology to the stages of field pilot, demonstration, or first-of-kind commercial implementation by project completion;Applicants must demonstrate how the proposed technology or application is an innovative solution for emissions reduction in Alberta;Successful applicants are required to commence work on proposed project within 120 days of approval;Projects must be demonstrated or implemented in Alberta however, the applicant does not need to be Alberta based, Albertan businesses will be priortized;EOI shortlist notification Early February 2024;Full Project Proposal deadline Late April 2024;Full Project Proposal Oral Presentation Late May 2024;Final Funding decision June 2024; andTechnologies are not required to directly reduce GHG emissions provided that there exists a strong case for their overall contribution to enabling emissions reduction. Evaluation Criteria:Innovation Opportunity: 20%;Implementation Plan: 20%;GHG Benefits: 30%;Non GHG Benefits: 15%; andMarket and Value Proposition: 15%.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Program does not allow for funding to be used retroactively;Program does not allow for stacking as the program requires the applicant to match the funding amount given; andAlberta businesses will be prioritized however businesses outside Alberta can apply as long as the project is demonstrated and implemented in Alberta.Links & Forms: Program Webpage: click hereApplication Portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Get BC Working program offers a wage subsidy incentive of up to $3600 to employers that hire and train eligible individuals in jobs offering long-term employment. Positions lasting longer than 6 months will be prioritized.Grant Value: Up to $3600 wage subsidy + up to $1000 for short-term training.Note: The maximum wage subsidy is negotiated and will be based on the hourly rate paid to the participant, the job duties, the position and hours/week.Turnaround Time:  Within a few business days (Varies depending on the speed of correspondence from applicants).Eligible Employers:In operation for at least one year; andIn good standing with WorkSafeBC.Eligible Candidate:Be a B.C. resident (living in BC as a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, recent immigrant, or a protected person);Legally entitled to work in Canada (student visa, study, or closed permit not eligible);Unemployed or under-employed (working unstable or irregular hours such as on-call work or casual labor, working for unreliable wages, and/or working for earnings that cannot support an individual or their family);Seeking long-term employment; Facing challenges to obtaining employment; andOpen work permits are accepted however student visa, study or closed work permits are not eligible.Program Details: Placements must be a minimum of 3 months;Preference will be given to placements that are 6 months and longer; The program strongly prefers placements with full-time hours (30/week), but may allow for part-time placements on a case-by-case basis;If the placement only provides part-time hours, the program will first speak with the employer and the participant to find out why the role is only part-time. The program will need to know if it is part-time because that is what the employer needs or if that is what the participants want.Placements cannot be for seasonal work; Full time students are not eligible Criteria for training subsidy:The training must be delivered by a third party;Participants must receive a certificate after completion;The training needs to match the participant's job duties; andThe training must receive prior approval by the program before the training start date.Must have identified the candidate before applying;Positions can be in person or remote;Applicants can apply for up to 2 hires; andThe program will complete monthly check-ins with the employer and hire.

      Eligible Best Practices: Program does not allow funding to be used retroactively,  candidate cannot start before funding agreement is signed.Cannot be stacked with other provincial or federally funded labor market programs (Applicants can apply for further wage subsidy support from other sources once Get BC Working funding has been used); andCandidate must be identified before applying.Forms & Links: Program Webpage: click hereApplication Form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The program aims to help eligible applicants  to lead projects that will enable commercialization of innovative agriculture, agri-food, and agri-based products and technologies. There are two project types Market Validation which provides funding up to $30,000 and Product Development with provides funding up to $150,000. The aim of the program is to enhance competitiveness and the leadership position of Ontario in the agriculture and agri-food sectors.Grant Value:Market Validation: Maximum funding of $30,000; andProduct Development: Minimum of $50,000 and to a maximum of $150,000.Turnaround Time: Successful applicants notified Spring 2024.Eligible Applicants:Must be located in Ontario;Must have project activities that take place in Ontario with project partners located in Ontario;Must have projects that address the OMAFRA ket research priority areas and the Initiative objectives;Must be operating in the agriculture, agri-food, and agri-based products sectors, including technology or equipment suppliers to the sector; andMust have a product/technology/service that in unique to Ontario.Eligible Projects & Activities:Market Validation:Conducting market research to determine the size and quality of the market
opportunity;Comprehensive market analysis and competitive landscape assessment;Customer discovery research to determine industry needs and to identify optimal
industry partners;Beta-testing early-stage technologies before transferring to industry (Technology
Readiness Level 5+);Demonstrating proof of relevancy using a prototype made within the cost constraints
determined by the market;Generating data (proof of concept) from a novel technology to support filing a patent
application; andDetermining the technical merit, feasibility, and commercial potential of a technology,
which could involve demonstrating proof of relevancy.Product Development (Technology Readines Level 6+):Prototype creation;Field testing and/or pilot testing prototypes/devices that have never been used outside
the lab (does not cover human medical testing);Removing any barriers to a market launch or private sector adoption;Evaluating a significant advancement to an existing product, process, or service;Testing or optimizing a minimum viable product that best meets the needs of
customers;Evaluation and testing of late-stage technologies to support a regulatory approval
submission;Exploring and advancing the certification of a product or process by a reputable
association;Developing a new product for animals or agriculture based on existing technology for
humans or non-agricultural purposes; andCreating and utilizing an academic-industry research centre at an industry partner’s site
to co-develop and implement process improvements directly applicable to industry.Eligible Project Costs:Salaries that directly relate to the project;Costs of consultants, professionals, and legal fees, including Intellectual Property costs directly related to project activities;Equipment and capital expenditures directly relating to the project;Materials and supplies directly related to project activities;Travel; andIndirect costs.Note: further breakdown of eligible costs can be found on page 9 here.Ineligible Project Costs:Costs incurred in preparing a proposal;Normal costs of establishing, expanding, or operating a business or organization;Goods or services provided by federal or provincial government departments or
agencies;Deposits (prepayments) for which goods or services are not yet fully received;Costs of membership in a professional body;Purchase of land, building, or facilities;Purchase of vehicles, transportation equipment, mobile material handling equipment
(powered or unpowered), and construction and agriculture machinery;Financing charges, loan and lease interest payments, bank fees and charges, fines, or
penalties, as well as debt restructuring or fundraising;Interest on invested capital, bonds, debentures, or mortgages;Bond discount; Costs related to litigation;Opportunity costs;Costs of conference or tradeshow admission if not exhibiting or presenting;Gifts and incentives;Permits and approvals;Costs of intangible assets such as goodwill, whether capitalized or expensed.Taxes, including Harmonized Sales Tax;Any refund or rebate the applicant receives or is eligible to receive;Costs to obtain goods, services, or both, where those goods, services or both were not
obtained from an entity operating at Arm’s Length from the recipient;Costs for which the recipient is eligible to receive a credit, rebate or refund;Costs related to the recipient’s ordinary business operations; and Any costs related to submitting reports to Bioenterprise.Program Details:Project duration is up to 18 months;Projects must be completed by September 30, 2025;Required reporting:Claims and interim progress reports;Final reports; andAnnual client surveys post project completion for up to 6 years.

      Grant Criteria 
      The GoodSpark grant awards funding of $20,000 to successful small business applicants. The mission is to contribute to improving the economic and social well-being of people and communities.Grant Value: $20,000Turnaround Time: Winners will be announced in March 2024.Eligible Applicants: Be Canadian-owned and operated and have its head office located and operating in 1 of the following provinces: BC, AB, MB, SK, ON, NB, NS, NL & PEI;Have a minimum of 1 employee up to a maximum of 50 employees;Have a Canadian/provincial business registration number in addition to a registered business name;Sole proprietorships, partnerships, and corporations are all eligible;Been in operation for at least 1 calendar (on or before November 1, 2022);Not be religiously or politically affiliated;Not be owned directly or indirectly by any employees, board member, agent, advisor or team member or DesJardin;Not be a franchised operation;Not be a prior recipient; andNot be a charity, non-profit organization, or organization receiving government funding on an ongoing basis for its operational expenses. Program Details: Small business applicants must select between one of the following options when completing an application to indicate how the grant would be used:Sustainable development - A project aimed at achieving 1 or more sustainable development objectives;Health and well-being - A project that invests in health and overall personal well-being;Innovation - New initiatives to help modernize the small business; andCommunity Impact - A project that positively influences the vitality of the community of the community through the mobilization and involvement of the small business.Applications must be submitted by December 3, 2023.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Only one application can be submitted per small business; andMust ensure that the grant will be used for one of the 4 project areas stated above.Forms & Links: Program webpage: click hereApplication guidelines: click hereApplication form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The CanExport Associations program provides funding of up to 50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $250,000 to industry, trade associations, business councils, and chambers of commerce. Applicant organizations must be incorporated as a Canadian non-profit. The funding is to support new or expanded international business development activities related to commercial export for the benefit of an entire industry.Grant Value: Up to 50% to a maximum of $250,000Turnaround Time: Funding decisions to be sent via email in mid-March 2024Eligible Applicants:Be incorporated as a Canadian non-profit organization;Confirmed by articles of incorporation.Have sufficient private revenues to cover the remaining 50% of the proposed project costs;Confirmed by 2 years of financial statements.Not selling products sold by the organization's members;Be one of the following organization types:National industry or trade associations;National bilateral chambers of commerce and business councils;National horizontal/multi-sectoral trade organizations with specific focussed mandate;E.g. National trade organizations representing companies majority owned by underrepresented groups in trade (e.g. Indigenous, women, LGBTQI+).Ineligible Applicants:Funded entirely by any level of Canadian government;Accessing other federal funding programs with similar objectives to CanExport;Do not have a commercial export focussed mandate and/or do not represent member companies looking to export products/services; andRegional organizations at the provincial or municipal level.Eligible Activities:Non-travel activities that promote international business development such as:Export training support (e.g. training on intellectual property protection);Creating or updating a strategy for international business development or market diversification;Gathering market intelligence (custom research, reports, and studies);Translating, adapting, or creating marketing tools and materials; andParticipating in virtual international trade shows, networking sessions, meetings, or conferences.Visits to foreign markets;Organizing international trade missions for SMEs in relevant industries;Organizing incoming delegations of foreign buyers to Canada; andIn-person participation to international trade shows, networking events, meetings, or conferences (as an exhibitor or advocate on behalf of the relevant industry).Eligible Expenses:Market information (E.g. purchasing market intelligence reports to develop market diversification plans or strategies);Consultant fees (E.g. business consultants, market specialists, or IBD specialists);Professional services (E.g. writing, editing, graphic design, marketing, translation, or interpretation);Advertising (E.g. web site development targeting foreign customers, or targeted materials to promote trade opportunities for Canadian industry);Printing, mailing, and shipping fees;Renting rooms and equipment for meetings; andTravel expenses (ie. economy airfare, per diem, ground transportation, visa fees, and registration fee for trade shows and conferences).Program Details:Maximum 1 application per fiscal year (April - March);New applicants must register the intent to submit an application once the intake opens by emailing CanExportAssociations@international.gc.caReturning applicants may use the existing access to CanExport Associations online system;The program will assess applications based on the following: The ability of the project to diversify Canadian exports outside the U.S.;Anticipated commercial results (what will be measured and how);Incrementality (ie. how does this build on the applicant's core activities);Benefits to Canadian businesses;Performance and past results;Effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:The program fundingFunding from this program can be used in conjunction with other sources of government funding (ie. stacking is allowed up to 75% of eligible costs);Applicants are strongly encouraged to discuss their proposed activities with CanExport Associations program officers. Regular communication will help identify early ineligible activities or expenses, missing or incomplete sections, and expense estimates that seem inaccurate.Program officers can also make recommendations on areas of the application that could be improved.CanExport Associations does not make advance payments. Applicants must have sufficient cash flow to fund their proposed activities in their entirety, prior to reimbursement.Forms:Program webpage: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Tourism Growth Program provides repayable and non-repayable funding to for-profit and non-profit organizations in the tourism industry. Eligible applicant organizations must have been in operation for at least 2 years in BC. Project activities must take place between March 29, 2023, and March 31, 2026. The intent of the program is to grow and develop local tourism projects and events.Grant Value:For-profit organizations: interest-free repayable funding of up to $250,000Maximum of 50% of capital costs and maximum of 75% on other eligible costsNon-profit organizations: non-repayable funding of up to 65% of eligible costs to a maximum of $250,000Maximum of 90% for all eligible costsTurnaround Time: within approximately 90 business days after the intake closing date.Eligible Applicants:Be legal entities such as the following organization types:Incorporated small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs);Have been in operation for at least 2 years in BC;Must be a financially viable business;Only restaurants or accommodations that are an anchor for a tourism community are eligible.Non-profit organizations, including tourism associations;Post-secondary institutions;Indigenous-owned businesses or Indigenous organizations;Including sole proprietors.Municipal and provincial governments or related entities.Eligible Activities:Must be incremental value (ongoing operating costs are ineligible), including but not limited to:Improving and/or creating innovative tourism offerings;Digitization, automation, or technology integration that enhances productivity, sustainability, efficiency, and competitiveness;Promotion of tourism products, including digital and virtual reality experiences;Develop capacity for inclusive tourism experiences;E.g. enhancing the accessibility of tourism assets, staff training to ensure welcoming, inclusive environments to a diverse clientele, etc.Supporting destinations to implement tourism plans that create or improve local assets, facilities or infrastructure.E.g. Destination Canada's Tourism Corridors Strategies.Eligible Expenses:Infrastructure upgrades, such as trail development and leasehold improvements, etc.;Costs incurred in designing new or improved tourism products and services;Purchase and/or rental of machinery and equipment directly related to the authorized project;Professional services (project implementation, design, and engineering services);Costs related to community engagement and planning such as facilitation and rental of meeting space;Marketing costs (e.g. design, promotional materials, advertising, digital media content, products demonstrations, participation at trade shows, website development, design, and improvement) are eligible in the case that they are associated with a larger project that is not solely marketing; andAcquisition of new technology that will improve performance and productivity.Ineligible Expenses:Purchase of any assets for more than the fair market value of the said asset;Salary bonuses and dividend payments;Entertainment expenses;Motor vehicles that can be licensed for off-site use;Land and building acquisition;Ongoing operational costs and hospitality.Program Details:All project activities must be completed and costs must be incurred by March 31, 2026;Proposed projects are expected to produce strong economic outcomes in the tourism sector. Applicants are required to report on the following:Number of communities supported, jobs created, jobs maintained, revenue growth, entities supported, and number of visitors.Only applications demonstrating the highest merit and fit with program objectives will be considered for funding;Successful applicants will need to meet project cash flows as there is a minimum capacity to reprofile any unused funds;Successful applicants will be required to submit claim information and periodic progress reports for at least 2 years;Repayment terms:No security or collateral will be taken;No penalty for early repayment;1-year grace period followed by equal monthly or quarterly installments;Repayment terms to come, please stay tuned.Assessment criteria:Level of impact (number of jobs created & maintained, increase in visitors, revenue growth, etc.)Lasting impact (benefits after the lifespan of the proposed project);Alignment to community or regional tourism strategies;Strong leverage (seeking 50% or 65% or less from the program).

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:The program funding may be used retroactively for costs incurred as early as March 29, 2023 or as early as 1 year prior to application submission (whichever comes later);Note that project costs incurred by the applicant in the absence of a signed funding agreement with PacifiCan are incurred at the sole risk of the applicant.The stacking limit from other government sources (ie. using program funding with other sources) cannot generally exceed 50% of eligible capital costs and 75% for other eligible costs.Forms:Program webpage: click hereProgram guidelines: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The BC On-Farm Technology Adoption Program provides cost-shared funding up to $100,000 to eligible participants to adopt new technologies on-farm that will enhance profitability, productivity, and/or efficiency. The goal is to strengthen B.C.'s agriculture sector through supporting the adoption of new technologies on-farm.  Grant Value: Up to 65% of eligible costs, a minimum $1,000 to a maximum of $100,000Turnaround Time: Funding decisions will be announced June 2025Eligible Applicants: Be B.C. based;Be registered, licensed and/or certified to conduct business in British Columbia;Have a minimum of 2 years in operation;Make no less than $50,000 in annual revenue during the previous 2 years from the production of primary B.C. agriculture commodities;For farmers who experience crop loss and revenue impacts due to weather or other factors outside their control will have exceptions to this requirement;In the above cases, farmers must reach the $50k threshold for 2 of the past 5 years.Be one of the following applicant types:Agriculture producer of primary agriculture commodities (i.e., farmers, growers, or ranchers); andIndigenous businesses, communities, and organizations that are majority-owned by Indigenous individuals or communities (at least 51%) and produce primary agricultural commodities or engage in traditional food production practices.Ineligible Applicants: Operations that grow, process, or handle health or nutrition supplements;Operations that grow, process, or handle cannabis;Operations producing or processing per food or food not intended for human consumption;Food processors, wholesalers, distributors, farm input suppliers, restaurants, and other food service establishments;Unlicensed, unregistered, or un-inspected facilities;Food packing operations located off-farm; andAquaculture and seafood production/processing businesses.Eligible Expenses:Technology that reduces the hours spent on a particular task;Technology that increases the productivity per worker, e.g., implementing a new piece of equipment that has advanced capabilities to speed up the pace of the worker or increase the output from the worker by streamlining specific actions that the worker takes, such as how the autonomous picking platform works; and/or Technology that reduces workforce, e.g., from 4 staff to 3 staff by implementing a piece of automated equipment.Technology Examples:Autonomous Equipment/Robotics: technologies that operate independently and adapt to their environment. Machinery: technologies that perform specific tasks with minimal but some human interaction. Smart Sensors and Monitoring Equipment: devices that collect and analyze data in real-time to optimize agricultural processes, enable faster decision making, remote control or management, or otherwise result in labour savings.Artificial Intelligence (AI): AI and machine learning technologies enable systems to adapt and make decisions as well as predictions, or otherwise result in labour savings.Farm Business Management Tools: technologies that assist in planning, analyzing, and optimizing the operational aspects a farm and result in labour savings.Other Technologies: New and emerging technologies that do not fall under the categories above, but that would result in substantial labour savings when implemented.  Program Details: This program supports the adoption of commercially available, labour-saving technologies on farms. These technologies should be new to Canada, B.C., a specific commodity sector, or a region. The goal is to enhance farm profitability, productivity, and efficiency;The technologies or equipment must be new to the applicant, viable, and commercialized (TRL 9);This would include technologies that are readily commercially available, and/or have been successfully tested and proven to work in its final form or iteration under real-life and operational conditions.Assessment criteria:Impact on labour savings, productivity, efficiency, and/or profitability;  The type of technology/innovation being purchased (with a higher emphasis on applications that will result in technologies/innovations being purchased and installed that are entirely new to B.C. and/or a specific commodity sector); and  The project budget and timeline.  If an application is approved, the Applicant will be informed of the details of the decision and any associated terms and conditions via email (ie. June 2025);If an application is not approved, the Applicant will be notified of the decision by email and will be provided an opportunity for additional feedback should they wish to request it.   

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: This program does not allow for funding to be used retroactively; This program allows for stacking as long as the applicant contributes the minimum contribution amount; andProcess Best Practices:Applicants can submit more than one application as long as the applications are for different technologies.Forms & Links: Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereApplication Portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Food Safety Program (FSP) provides funding of 70% to a maximum of $25,000 to agriculture, food processing, transportation, warehousing, and distribution businesses funding to improve food safety practices and systems. The program has 2 streams, one for on-farm organizations and one for post-farm organizations. On-farm applicants must be able to demonstrate farm status while post-farm applicants must be provincially or federally licensed to operate. The intent of the program is to enable the agrifood sector to meet existing and new food safety regulatory requirements nationally and internationally.Grant Value: Up to 70% to a maximum of $25,000Turnaround Time: 4-6 weeks after workplace submissionEligible Applicants:Be one of the following organization types:Corporation;Cooperative association;Non-profit;Society; ORIndividual.Have an active 9-digital business registration number or GST number from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA);File business or farm income taxes in BC;Be based and operating in BC;Operate an agrifood business that produces/processes/handles food, commodities, or beverages for human consumption;Be registered with the BC Premises Identification Program if the applicant raises animals;Stream 1 - On-Farm applicants:Farmers or growers producing crops;Producers or ranchers raising animals;Packers or co-packers handling food.Stream 2 - Post-Farm applicants:Processors, transporters, warehouses, distributors, packers and importers;Processing facilities (beyond basic washing, grading and packaging);May be located on or off a farm premise and not covered by a certified on-farm food safety program.Food hubs (shared-use food and beverage processing facilities that offer food and agriculture businesses.Ineligible Applicants:Health or nutrition supplements;Pet food or food not intended for human consumption;Retail, restaurants, or other food service operations; andAquaculture and seafood production, processing, or handling businesses.Eligible Activities:Category 1- Food safety assessment:Gap assessment of food safety risks and traceability capacity:Impact of the project on improving food safety and traceability and controlling food safety risks;Impact of the project in addressing identified business needs or opportunities;Costs for an onsite gap assessment by third-party accredited auditors to identify opportunities for food safety (including traceability) improvements;Development of a food safety work plan outlining the actions needed to implement a HACCP-based food safety program, including traceability planning.Category 2- Food safety improvement:Develop traceability plans and implement written food safety programs:Equipment purchases and/or facility modification for food hazard reduction;Capped at $20,000 per applicant per term.Third-party consultation/advisory to develop or improve written food safety policies, and procedures;Incremental third-party accredited staff training - online or in-person;Validation of food safety process control measures;Baseline or incremental laboratory analysis; andThird-party audited OFFS/HACCP Certifications.Category 3 - Food Safety Certifications Completing final audits which lead to successful certification or registration in nationally or internationally recognized food safety programs;Final audit and certification costs by a third-party which lead to a certification in the following accredited, national, and internally recognized food safety certification programs are eligible:British Retail Consortium (BRC);Food Safety System Certification (FSSC) 22000;Global Red Meat Standards (GRMS);International Food Safety Standard (IFS version 6);PrimusGFS;Canada G.A.P.;Safe Quality Food (SQF 2000);Global GAP.Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) Recognized Food Safety Plans:Preventive Control Plans (PCPs) as per Safe Food for Canadians Act (SFCA);Food Safety Enhancement Program (CFIA’s FSEP);Canada Grains Council;Canadian Cattlemen’s Association Verified Beef Production;Canadian Cervid Alliance;Canadian Hatching Egg Producers: Canadian Hatching Egg Quality;Canadian Herbs, Spice and Natural Health Products Coalition;Canadian Honey Council;Canadian National Goat Federation: On-Farm Food Safety Program;Canadian On-Farm Food Safety Working Group;Canadian Pork Council: Canadian Quality Assurance Program;Canadian Sheep Federation: Food Safety Farm Practices: Canadian Verified Sheep Program;Canadian Trucking Alliance;Responsible Distribution Canada;Chicken Farmers of Canada: On-Farm Food Safety Assurance Program;Dairy Farmers of Canada: Canadian Quality Milk;Egg Farmers of Canada: Start Clean-Stay Clean;Ontario Veal Association: Veal Quality Assurance Program; andTurkey Farmers of Canada: On-Farm Food Safety Program.Note: Approval for full equipment purchase may be considered if equipment upgrades are more costly than buying new equipment.Program Details:Pre-approved applicants will work with the program's Technical Program Advisor (TPA) to develop a work plan;Project end date: within 5 months of approval;Successful applicants must complete a final report prior to receiving funds from the program;To ensure appropriate acknowledgment, all communications and marketing materials, including public announcements or social media posts, must be pre-approved by the IAF Communications Team.Details on correctly acknowledging funding can be found on the project resource hub;Materials can be submitted via the IAF Client Portal.

and Overhead.Program Details:Project length up to 12 months;Program will require projects to have milestones;Funding will be required to be a 2:1 contribution; andApplications must be submitted by a member of the senior management team.Stream Eligibility:Stream 1: De-risking of emerging technologies and venture creation:Be either an emerging venture with intellectual property (IP) developed in Ontario, or an early stage, private health science SME based in Ontario;For emerging ventures, high potential for company creation with operation in Ontario; andSeeking support with IP management, company creation, technology de-risking. Stream 2: Strengthening technology commercialization:A private, health science SME based in Ontario;Demonstrates that the technology solves a critical problem and a market exists for the product/service;Company owns or has license agreement(s) in place for intellectual property associated with the technology;Demonstrate that the completed project advances the company toward a significant value creation event; andProvide 2:1 cash matching funds for the overall commercialization project to advance technology proof-of-concept, validation, demonstration, testing, and/or deployment.Stream 3: Technology adoption:A private, health science SME based in Ontario;Successfully completed an initial pilot/validation study with supporting data;A market-ready product/service, ready to commercialize at scale;Raised dilutive funding or generating annual recurring revenues; andProvide 2:1 matching fund for an adoption project to have the technology evaluated by a healthcare organization.

Summer months are defined as May 1 to September 1. The intent is to increase youth and domestic seasonal worker employment in the agriculture sector in BC.Grant Value:Minimum 250 hours worked: $1,500Minimum 500 hours worked: $3,000Note: Funding amounts may be prorated for hours worked between 250-500 hours.Turnaround Time: 3 weeks or lessEligible Applicants:Legally permitted to work in Canada;Student visas are eligible.16 years old or older;Be enrolled in full-time studies in the current academic year and intend to return to full-time studies in the fall;Must be accepted to full-time enrolment in a secondary or post-secondary institution.Enrolled in a designated educational institution.Canadian secondary schools, universities, colleges, and certain other educational institutions;Canadian educational institutions certified by Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) providing courses that develop or improve skills in an occupation, other than courses designed for university credit;Universities, colleges, or other educational institutions in the United States that give courses at the post-secondary school level if the qualifying student is living in Canada throughout the year and commutes to that institution.Note: Each institution may have a different definition of full-time, please consult your school for confirmation.Eligible Activities:Primary Agriculture;Food, Beverage, and/or Seafood Processing;Fishing or Aquaculture;Nurseries for bedding plants.Eligible: Large-scale or wholesale production;Ineligible: garden centers, landscaping, and/or farm supply stores (feed included).Program Details:Summer season is defined as May 1 to September 1, 2024;Applicants may apply without confirmation of employment, but will only be conditionally approved;Funding is not secured until there is confirmation of employment;       The program offers funding up to 75% of expenses at a max of $750,000 to accelerate innovation and de-risk the development and adoption of agritech by combining the sciences of agriculture, engineering, and technology to address labour challenges and increase the sustainability of controlled environment agriculture businesses in B.C.Grant Value: Up to 75% of eligible project expenses;Minimum contribution of $150,000; andMaximum contribution of $750,000.Turnaround Time: Invitation to submit full proposal be announced by February 29, 2024.Eligible Applicants: Be a private corporation incorporated and headquartered in the province of British Columbia;Have 499 or less full-time employees;Have been in continuous operation for two years at the time of application;Have a clear plan to scale up their business;Support research and development activities that take place in B.C. or Canada;Have 50% or more full time employees in B.C as their ordinary place of work;Have SMEs, agri-businesses and farms, post-secondary institutions, Indigenous communities, or government as project collaborators; andContribute 25% of eligible project costs in cash.Eligible Projects: Integrating technologies, such as IoT sensors, AI-driven data analytics, and robotic automation;Precision indoor farming;Sustainable energy solutions;Biological pest control;Piloting new technologies;Breeding and developing new crop varieties and
cultivars;Precise nutrient management;Water recycling, sustainable water source
management;Vertical farming solutions;Post-harvest technologies;Waste reduction and recycling; andClimate resilience for CEA.Eligible Costs: Project-specific supplier such as

fees for applicable project required
applications;Learning management
systems/platforms;Supplies and materials:Soil, seeds, fertilizers, pesticides etc.Office supplies;Test samples, solutions etc.Training / workshop packages

equipment or space.Onsite training and certification fees

facilities by/for the lead applicant

pilots;Support developing and adopting enabling technologies for CEA;Enhance productivity and efficiency in CEA businesses via private, post-secondary institutes, and government partnerships;Establish BC’s agritech leadership while advancing climate adaptation and net-zero strategies; andEconomic development by talent attraction and retention with well-paying jobs.Project budgets should be between $200,000 and $1million;EOI is due February 16, 2024;Applicant invited to submit a full project proposal will be notified by February 29, 2024;Full project proposals are due April 12, 2024; andSuccessful applicants will be notified in late May.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Extreme Weather Preparedness for Agriculture Program is designed to increase BC's food security through environmental conservation and improved resiliency for select extreme weather events. The program provides funding of 40% up to $50,000 for select-on-farm projects. The program aims to increase preparedness of the sector to anticipate, respond to and recover from climate change and extreme weather events.Grant Value: 40% to a maximum of $50,000.Turnaround Time: Approximately 8 weeks.Eligible Applicants:Be a primary production agriculture business whose primary purpose is the production and sale of agricultural products and must be a BC registered business entity (including sole proprietor, partnership, corporations, cooperatives, Indigenous economic development corporations, and band-owned businesses). Applicants to the program must have farm status and, if involved in raising livestock, a premises ID;Be a taxable entity; andHave their main farmstead in B.C and file far, income tax Under the Income Tax Act in B.C.Ineligible Applicants:Landowners not registered as a BC entity;Hobby farms/farms without Farm status; andSilviculture farms/nurseries.Eligible Activities:Wildfire Preparedness:Farm & Ranch FireSmart Assessment;Farm building retrofits;Critical farm structure upgrades;Addressing vegetation &combustible materials; andFarm structure sprinkler protection project.Flood Preparedness:Planning & design of fill pad for farm buildings;Fill pads for farm buildings;Flood-resilient storage for farm inputs;Flood-resilient feed storage; andFlood-resilient Apiary Overwintering & Equipment storage.Extreme Heat Preparedness:Improved barn and indoor aquaculture cooling systems;Extreme heat protection for horticulture crops;Extreme heat protection outdoor livestock-shade trees;Extreme heat protection for outdoor livestock and seafood farms – infrastructure;Enhanced livestock watering to mitigate heat stress; andCooling systems for outdoor aquaculture operations.Innovation Projects:If an applicant can benefit from a different preparedness activity or technology not listed above and can demonstrate how it addresses a need to prepare for the impact of extreme weather events;Standard that must be met for the project to be considered for funding:Must address a demonstrated need related to impacts from extreme weather (wildfire preparedness, flood preparedness, or extreme heat);Must not be already commonplace activity or technology in the farm or agriculture business for which it is proposed;Must not be affected by any Regulations/authorization processes; andMust not be covered by other government programming.NOTE: Further breakdown of eligible activities can be found here.Ineligible Activities:GST;In-kind costs;Expenses incurred prior to project approval (no retroactive approval permitted) or after theproject completion date;Purchase of typical farm equipment and related accessories or attachments (includingtractors, skid steers and trailers);Costs of ongoing activities;Maintenance or repair costs unless specified as being eligible in the Appendices;Building of new infrastructure where there was none in place and operating prior to theextreme weather event in that area;Upgrades to farm buildings that were built during or after 2020 (with one notable exception:farm buildings that were destroyed by fire or flood where insurance will not cover theupgrade to an equivalent level of resiliency as the projects in this program);Financing charges, loan interest payments, bank fees and charges; andMaintenance or extended warranties on equipment, electronics, or technology purchases.Program Details:Project start date April 1, 2024;All projects must be completed by March 14, 2025;Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until funds are fully allocated; andIn order to apply for wildfire preparedness the farm & ranch firesmart assessment must be applied for and completed.

      Best Practices:Program allows for funding to be stacked with other funding sources but must not exceed 100% of eligible project expenses;All businesses from which claimed goods or services are purchases must be at arms length from the applicant; Funding cannot be used retroactively; andApplications will be reviewed on a first-come, first-serve basis.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click hereApplication Portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Agri-Tech Innovation Initiative provides funding up to $100,000 to support the growth and productivity through innovation, advanced manufacturing, improved food safety and enhanced cyber security, and energy efficiency with the agri-food sector.Grant Value:Stream 1: Up to 50% to a maximum of $49,999  (Total eligible costs per project must be less than $100,000);Stream 2: Up to 35% to a maximum of $100,000 ( Total eligible costs per project must be greater than $100,000); andStream 3: Up to 35% to a maximum of $100,000.Turnaround Time: 60 days after intake closes (intake closes March 28, 2024).Eligible Applicants: Be located in Ontario;Be one of the following:A producer (Stream 1 and 2); orA processor (Stream 1, 2 and 3);Provide its CRA Business Number;Have a valid and up to date Premises ID Number for the business locations where the Project is to take place;For producers applying for Stream 1 or 2, have a:Valid Farm Business Registration Number (FBRN) (unless a New Producer);An Order from the Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs Appeal Tribunal exempting
the Person from having to have a FBRN; or,A letter from the First Nations Agriculture & Finance Ontario (formerly known as
the Indian Agriculture Program of Ontario), orAn exemption from the income eligibility requirement of the Farm Property Class
Tax Rate Program, received from Agricorp.Eligible Activities: Stream 1 and 2: Implementing new equipment, or modification of equipment, technology, and
machinery for production and/or manufacturing that is Innovative; orImplementing new equipment, technology, and machinery or modification of
equipment, technology, and machinery for advanced manufacturing (i.e., through
automation, robotics, or digitization).Stream 3:Purchasing or installing new or refurbished equipment, parts, components and/or
technology that improves energy efficiency;Purchasing, installing or modifying water use equipment and technology that
improves energy efficiency (e.g., Clean in Place (CIP) systems that use cold water
instead of hot water, equipment to recover and reuse waste heat from processing
water); orFacility improvements related to building energy efficiency improvements (e.g.,
lighting, ventilation, heating, refrigeration).Eligible Supporting Activities:The following cannot be standalone projects and must support eligible activities:Stream 1 and 2:Purchasing equipment, technology, and machinery that advances food safety and
traceability including;Food safety equipment;Barcoding and product identification systems; Testing equipment for monitoring and analysis;Facility or cyber security changes, upgrades, or modifications;Purchasing software or upgrades; andHiring third-party expertise/services including engineering services, cyber security
assessments, software development, training, installation, and management.Stream 3: Third-party expertise/services required for the Project including engineering
services, staff training, and management of the Project.Eligible Costs:Stream 1 and 2:New or modified equipment, technology, and machinery that is commercially available
and Innovative or Advances Manufacturing;Supporting costs for a Project may include:Costs for food safety and traceability including;Food safety equipment;Barcoding and product identification systems; andTesting equipment for monitoring and analysis.One-time purchasing cost of software or upgrades as part of the Project;Costs for facility or cyber security changes, upgrades, or modifications or that are
required for the Project; andOne-time costs of third-party expertise/services required for the Project including
engineering services, cyber security assessments, software development, training installation and management.Stream 3:Equipment costs related to the purchase and installation of new or refurbished equipment,
parts, components and/or technology that improves energy efficiency;Water equipment costs related to the purchase, installation or modification of water use
equipment and technology that improve energy efficiency (e.g., Clean in Place (CIP)
systems that use cold water instead of hot water, equipment to recover and reuse waste
heat from processing water);Facility improvement costs related to building energy efficiency improvements (e.g.,
lighting, ventilation, heating, refrigeration); andOne-time costs for third-party expertise/services required for the Project including
engineering services, staff training, and management of the Project.Program Details:Applications deadline March 28, 2024;Projects must be complete by September 30, 2027;Purpose of Stream 1 and 2 is to support growth and productivity for Ontario Producers and Processors through the acquisition and implementation off new or modified commercially available equipment, technology, or machinery that is Innovative or Advances Manufacturing;Purpose of Stream 3 is to support Processors across Ontario through the implementation of energy cost saving equipment and technology that reduce greenhouse gas emissions; andApplicants may apply to stream 1 and 2 just once and to stream 3 once.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program does not allow funding to be used retroactively;The program can be stacked with other programs as long as the funding does not exceed 100% and is not from Sustainable CAP;Ensure applicant has registered on time in the portal.Links and Forms:Program webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereApplication Portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Agritech Development Program provides funding up to $250,000 which aims to accelerate growth and productivity through on-demand innovation support for agritech projects.Grant Value: From $25,000 to $250,000 in cost shared 1:1 funding (ie. 50% contribution)Turnaround Time: Varies based on how long it takes to scope project with the program. Eligible Applicants: Be private corporations, incorporated and headquartered in British Columbia (non BC companies are eligible but they must spend funds in BC);Have up to 499 employees;Be in operation for at least 2 years;Have a clear plan to scale-up their business; andBe able to contribute a cash investment between $25,000 to $250,000.Eligible Projects:Create products or services in the areas of agriculture, agri-technology and agri-foods with a focus on product development, testing and piloting solutions in simulated and real-world environments to be farm-ready;Have a product at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 5-9;Have a total project budget between $50,000 and $500,000, including the match funding from BCCAI;Projects can have a higher budget, but will not receive more that $250,000 contribution; andInvolve 1-5 collaborating organizations.Eligible Expenses:Eligible costs must be incremental, reasonable, and relate to the execution and achievement of project outcomes;Project costs can include contracted research services for personnel at BC post-secondary institutions and sub-contracted labour or services provided by Canadian corporations or contractors.Ineligible Expenses:Any project-related expenses incurred prior to selection by BCCAI and approval of a project proposal, and costs related to contracting for an approved project;In-kind contributions are not eligible for matching funds.Program Details: Projects must focus on one of the following targets: Strengthening food security and local food systems;Advancing and adopting Indigenous knowledge for economic development and food security;Supporting the reduction of greenhouse gases from the agriculture and food sectors to mitigate and adapt to climate change and net zero emission targets;Managing plant health and disease management;Utilizing innovative technology to alleviate labour shortage;Supporting diversifying domestic and international markets;Supporting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals in agricultural policies; and Supporting collaboration across post-secondary institutions to deepen the knowledge base and talent pool for agriculture innovation.Project term of 12 months, but lower or higher term can be considered by the program; andResult in scale-up or commercialization within 12-24 months from the start of the project.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Program does not allow funding to be used retroactively;The program requires a 1:1 cash match in funding;Projects can have a higher budget, but will not receive more that $250,000 contribution; andProgram cannot be stacked with other sources of funding.Links and Forms: Program Webpage: click hereApplication Form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The program provides non-repayable contributions up to $10 million to support investments in dairy, poultry and egg processing facilities that improve productivity and/or efficiency through the purchase of new automated equipment and technology.Grant Value:Up to $10 million for dairy processors; andUp to $5 million to all other eligible applicants.Turnaround Time: Approximately 100 days after full application submission.Eligible Applicants:Dairy processors;Poultry Primary processors (chicken and turkey);Poultry Further processors (chicken and turkey);Hatcheries (broiler, egg-type or turkey);Egg graders;Egg processors;In addition, eligible applicants must be:Operating in Canada;Processors buying domestic raw commodities;Predominantly processing supply-managed commodities at the project location;Holding an active federal or provincial processing licence;Able to provide financial statements demonstrating ongoing revenues from processing for a min of 2 years prior to application; Federally and provincially registered legal entities capable of entering into legally binding agreements.Priority will be given to:Small and Medium enterprises;First-time Applicants; andProjects that improve productivity.Eligible Expenses:Purchase and installation of new equipment;Costs related to the contracting of external expertise for services related to the equipment installation;Costs for the modification of the processing facility necessary for the installation of the equipment; andConstruction costs, for example expansion or modernization (dairy facilities only).Ineligible Expenses:Costs related to the purchase of land and buildings; Costs related to research and development;Costs related to regular ongoing operational and managerial activities of the organization;Project management costs;Administrative office supplies and expenses;Used or refurbished equipment;Rentals and or lease of facilities, equipment or machinery; andCosts related to acquisition of land or buildings.NOTE: Full list of eligible and ineligible expenses can be found hereEligible Activities:The program supports projects that increase automation and/or improve productivity in processing facilities, such as, but not limited to:Automation of an existing production process;Improvement to an existing automated or robotic process;Purchase of a new production line; andImplementation or improvement of integrated management software.Program Details:Projects must be complete prior to March 31, 2028;Projects should normally be completed over a maximum period of 3 years;Preferably, applications should be submitted 3 to 6 months before initiating project activities;Approved projects are expected to result in one or more of the following:Increase automation in processing facilities;Reduce production costs;Increase productivity; orIncrease annual revenues.Project activities are expected to provide additional benefits such as, but not limited to:Improving environmental sustainability such as:Equipment to reduce water and energy consumption;Equipment required to treat waste water resulting froma n increase in production.Responding to consumer demand concerning food safety and animal welfare, such as:Packaging equipment that increases shelf life; andProcessing equipment to reduce/control pathogen load.

      Grant Criteria 
      The AgriMarketing Program provides funding of up to 70% to a maximum of $2 million to non-profit or Indigenous organizations.
