The intent of the program is to help the Canadian agricultural sector capture domestic market opportunities and to increase and diversify exports to international markets.Grant Value:Regular applicants: 50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $2,000,000Underrepresented applicants: 70% of eligible costs to a maximum of $2,000,000Turnaround Time: within 100 business daysEligible Applicants:Be a non-profit organization, such as:Association of workers and/or employers;Local community, charitable, and voluntary organization;Sector council;Corporation;Indigenous communities;Indigenous associations;Indigenous non-profit organizations.Demonstrate ability to deliver national and/or sector-wide projects for agriculture and agri-food;Should be a member of the Canada Brand; andBe a legal entity capable of entering into legally binding agreements.Eligible Activities:Advertising or promotional campaigns via:Print, radio, television advertising and/or promotion;Online advertising and/or Promotion;Social media advertising and/or promotion.Incoming mission;Outgoing mission;Market research;Technical training;Trade advocacy; andTrade shows.Eligible Expenses:Administrative costs;Salaries and benefits;Contracted services;Travel; andCapital expenditures.Note: All expenses must be directly related and required for the project.Program Details:Documents required:Copy of Certificate of Incorporation or Articles of Incorporation;Financial statements for the last 2 years;AgriMarketing program questionnaire;List of all the members in your organization;Detailed project budget;Project endorsement letters (if applicable);Capital asset pre-approval for grants and contribution programs (if applicable);All capital asset purchases over $10,000 must be pre-approved by the program using the AAFC Capital Asset pre-approval template.Indigenous applicant documentation (if applicable);A copy of a Band Council Resolution (BCR), a Tribal Council Resolution (TCR), a Director's Resolution (DR), or legal document stating they are a legal entity.For each eligible activity, the program expects the applicant to state the expected results:Advertising or promotional campaigns: audience reach, click-through rate, unique website visits, engagement rate;Market research: estimated value of markets identified, number of members using research/data;Technical training: number of participants attended;Trade shows: value of estimated sales, number of buyers reached.

      Grant Criteria 
      The program aims to help Canadian technology companies develop solutions that improve the environmental sustainability of Canadian manufacturers by providing funding up to $5.25 million. Projects should support Canada's 2030 Emissions Reduction Plan and must be pushing the boundaries of advanced manufacturing technology and world-class cleantech.Grant Value: Up to 35% up to $5.25 millionTurnaround Time: Expected final results end of October 2024Eligible Applicants:Funding recipients must be one of the following:For-profit organizations;Not-for-profit organization that facilitate and fund research and development on behalf of the ecosystem and whose funding and/or revenue is received primarily from private-sector or industry organizations;Non-federal Crown corporations whose funding is from commercial activities; andIndigenous organizations.Any NGen member company may apply for project funding (it is free to become a member can register here);Business registered in Canada and have a value-added presence beyond a sales office;Projects should demonstrate meaningful collaboration by a minimum of two industry partners; At least one SME partner needs to be involved;International organizations may participate in projects however may not receive any NGen funding.Eligible Projects:All projects must demonstrate the development and application of ideally a combination of Clean Technologies, Advanced Technologies, and Greener Manufacturing Processes that enable sustainable manufacturing in Canada;Projects should focus on areas such as: Low carbon - fuel, feedstock, energy - applied to manufacturing;Innovative solutions for high heat generation - applied to manufacturing;Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage  - applied to manufacturing;Tracking and Managing GHG emissions across the supply chain;Transition to net-zero facilities;Smart Manufacturing for efficiency gains and GHG reduction;Greener/circular/sustainable materials.The project must focus on the development and/or scale-up of advanced sustainable manufacturing processes;Projects must demonstrate a strong commercialization strategy and path to commercial success;Project will ideally include advanced manufacturing and clean technology expertise; andProjects must have the potential to deliver significant commercial benefits and jobs both within the consortium and beyond.Ineligible Projects:Activities where benefits accrue to a single firm or organization;Projects that do not demonstrate collaborative partnerships with a manufacturer and a clean demonstration of improving sustainable manufacturing processes;Projects that would be undertaken at the same scale or scope and within the same period without NGen funding;Projects that focus primarily on product development or the design of products themselves;Project related to the experimental or theoretical work without any direct commercial application or use;Production activities themselves or activities that subsidize full-scale production;Capital investment for production or for purposes not related to the project. Equipment not related to sustainable manufacturing technology is out of scope;Activities that could be viewed as anti-competitive; andRepeat deployments of previously developed technologies.Program Details:The total amount of eligible project costs should be between $2 million and $15 million;Applications go through a mandatory screening process to ensure project is in scope deadline is June 26, 2024;Final application Deadline September 18, 2024;Projects should demonstrate how they will support Canada's 2030 Emissions Reductions targers and transition to a net-zero carbon economy e.g:GHG emissions reductions;Improved energy efficiencies and lower natural resource consumption;Operational efficiency gains;Waste reduction;Use of recycled/sustainable materials;Total life cycle product management and closed-loop manufacturing;Circular manufacturing of materials;Creation of new revenue streams/ business models Project participants must have robust project management processes in place, project work packages, milestones, timelines and estimated costs should be well-defined;For projects over $10 million will require dual state assessment and approval process;No single partner will receive more than 70% of NGen funding;The cost of new equipment to support sustainable manufacturing may be claimed but cannot exceed 25%Subcontracting cannot be more than 25% of the total eligible project costsProject partners cannot be subcontractor for labor services or consultants in the project;Project admin fees are applied to projects as a condition of funding %% of total costs of the project.NOTE: a full list of eligible and ineligible expenses can be found here

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Project participants must have robust project management processes in place, project work packages, milestones, timelines and estimated costs should be well-defined;Program does not allow retroactive funding;For projects over $10 million will require dual state assessment and approval process.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereFinancial Guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Biosecurity Enhancement Initiative provides funding of 35% of eligible costs to a maximum of $310,000 to agriculture and food sector businesses to address biosecurity risks and enhance emergency preparedness. The program has 7 streams that cover categories such as animal health risks, traceability equipment, plant health and pest management. The intent of the program is to enhance the protection of animal health, public health, and food safety.Grant Value:Schedule 1 (Reducing animal health risks) - 35% to a maximum of $50,000Schedule 2 (Livestock traceability equipment and processes) - 35% to a maximum of $50,000Schedule 3 (Plant health assessment, planning, training) - 50% to a maximum of $50,000Schedule 4 (Pest management sprayer upgrades) - 50% to a maximum of $5,000Schedule 5 (Pest prevention) - 35% to a maximum of $50,000Schedule 6 (Innovative pest monitoring and management) - 35% to a maximum of $50,000Schedule 7 (Technologies and process to reduce plant pest contamination) - 35% to a maximum of $100,000Note: There is no funding maximum per Recipient for the total Initiative. Funding maximums are set by Project Category.Turnaround Time: 15 business daysEligible Applicants:Have a Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) business number;Have a valid Social Insurance Number (SIN);Have valid and up-to-date Premises ID Number for the business locations where the projects will take place;Maintain a commercial general liability insurance of $2 million dollars per occurrence;Additional stream dependent eligibility:Schedule 1 (Reducing animal health risks)Must be primary producers, processors or service providers;Provide a copy of a completed operational, farm-wide or commodity-specific risk assessment against national biosecurity standards.Schedule 2 (Livestock traceability equipment and processes)Must be primary producers or service providers.Schedule 3 (Plant health assessment, planning, training)Must be primary producers, processors, or service providers.Schedule 4 (Pest management sprayer upgrades) - 50% to a maximum of $5,000Must be primary producers or service providers.Schedule 5 (Pest prevention) - 35% to a maximum of $50,000Must be primary producers or service providers.Schedule 6 (Innovative pest monitoring and management) - 35% to a maximum of $50,000Must be primary producers or service providers.Schedule 7 (Technologies and process to reduce plant pest contamination) - 35% to a maximum of $100,000Must be processors.If the applicant is a primary producer, they must have:A valid Farm Business Registration Number (FBRN);An Order from the Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs Appeal Tribunal exempting the Person from having to have a FBRN;A letter from the Indian Agriculture Program of Ontario; andIncome statements or other evidence that is acceptable to the Priority Administrator, Priority Operator, Designated Program Operator or AdministratorEligible Activities:Schedule 1 (Reducing animal health risks)Knowledge improvements to biosecurity and/or hazard prevention and preparedness (education, training, assessment and planning)Operational improvements and/or implementation of new technologies as preventative measures to reduce the likelihood of the introduction and spread of diseasesSchedule 2 (Livestock traceability equipment and processes)Acquiring, installing and upgrading equipment directly linked to the implementation or improvement of a traceability process.Writing, development, implementation or audit of a new traceability process.Structural modifications (building or production site upgrades) to support implementation of traceability equipment or system.Information sharing networks (for example, cloud-based subscription costs, one-time dedicated project staff), limited to the duration of the Project.Barcoding systems and automated product identification systems.Associated training for purchased equipment from vendor or supplier.Schedule 3 (Plant health assessment, planning, training)Third-party training/education regarding national biosecurity standards or commodity-specific risk management program.First-time assessment and recommendations by a Certified Crop Advisor (CCA) or Integrated Pest Management (IPM) consultant regarding biosecurity, IPM, best management practices, and/or risk management.Planning and decision support tools (for example, computer software, aerial photos, maps and land resource information) related to the Project.Baseline lab testing as part of IPM.Schedule 4 (Pest management sprayer upgrades)Purchasing and installing one or more of the items from the eligible equipment list;Modifying existing sprayers to install one or more items from the eligible equipment list.Schedule 5 (Pest prevention)Installation of specialized cleaning/disinfection equipment and treatment system for the purpose of disinfecting or removing pathogens, particulate, crop residue or contaminants from waterConstruction of a new structure, or modification of an existing structure, to be used only as a quarantine or isolation facility.Emergency elimination of plant or soil materials posing a biosecurity risk to plant health (for example, contaminated by spores or pests)Select technology for pest prevention in greenhouses, including screening and gravel perimeters.Schedule 6 (Innovative pest monitoring and management)Purchasing of select on-farm monitoring and diagnostic tools.Purchasing of select on-farm management tools and equipment to adopt innovative and integrated pest management practices.Schedule 7 (Technologies and process to reduce plant pest contamination)Purchasing select management, monitoring and diagnostic tools and equipment.Establishing new or modifying existing walkways, laneways or access routes to improve traffic flow efficiency and reduce contamination.Construction of hard surface pad or wash bay facility for cleaning and disinfecting vehicles and equipment.Purchasing plant hygiene or treatment equipment.Installation of a treatment system to remove pathogens, particulates, crop residue or contaminants from water.Construction or modification of a structure used only as a quarantine or isolation facility.Program Details:Applicants can have a maximum of 2 submitted applications/Projects in progress under the Initiative at any given time;All activities must be completed by February 1, 2025;In addition to a complete Application Form, Applicants must provide written quotes from any third party providing a good, service or both to the Applicant detailing the proposed Eligible Costs for the Project;All quotes must include:legal name of third party organization, consultant or manufacturer;Date;Clear description of good and/or service being provided;If equipment, all equipment specifications;Expected cost;Ancillary charges;Applicable taxes.To be eligible to receive an Initiative Payment, a Recipient must:Be registered with Transfer Payment Ontario;Be registered for Doing business with the Government of Ontario with Supply Ontario (to receive Initiative Payments).

      Best Practices:Applicants may leverage funding from other sources so long as it does not exceed 100% of the total eligible costs;There is a 75% stacking limit for capital items required to execute a Project in connection with a business carried out for profit;All funding for a Project, including from additional sources, must be listed on the Application Form.Forms:Program webpage: click hereProject category guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Sector Adoption program will support a consortium of partners working together to address a set challenge and to create an impactful change for the whole sector. The program provides up to $1 million in funding to eligible projects in one of the four focus sectors - advanced manufacturing, mining, agri-food, and construction. The current challenge is accelerating home construction through the adoption of critical technologies.Grant Value: Up to 33% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $1,000,000Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants:Lead Applicant:An SME with fewer than 500 global employees;Must have registered operations (R&D, manufacturing, product management, etc.) in Ontario and a valid CRA business number; andThe applicant is a co-signatory to the funding agreement.Primary Partner:An organization directly participating in the project and whose participation demonstrates "market pull" (e.g. as a customer) for the applicant's technology project solution.SMEs;National and multi-national Enterprises;Academic institutions;Municipalites;Crown Corporations;Indigenous Communities;  orNot-for-profit organizations representing industry.Applicant and Primary partner must have an arm's length business relationship;The Primary Partner may participate in multiple concurrent projects; andThe Primary Parter is a co-signatory to the funding agreement.Other Partners:Other Partners are additional organizations directly contributing and/or participating in the project;Partners providing matching leverage counted in the 2:1 industry contribution must be cosignatories to the Funding Agreement; andAn unlimited number of additional Other Partners can join the project consortium.Eligible Projects:The current challenge is to accelerate home construction through the adoption of critical technologies;CIT initiative is calling for transformational solutions that can significantly accelerate the building process through the adoption and integration of innovative critical technologies and automation in the construction industry Solutions could include:automated manufacturing of prefab housing;improvements through on-site tools;new products and automation technologies that significantly accelerate the building process.The program aims to achieve with this challenge to:Develop and implement innovative solutions that
significantly accelerate the building process, reducing
construction timelines and increasing efficiency;Create scalable solutions that can be easily replicated
and deployed across various construction projects and
sectors, fostering widespread adoption and impact;Successfully integrate critical technologies such as 5G,
AI, Robotics, Quantum, Cybersecurity, or Blockchain
into construction processes, leading to enhanced
productivity and performance;Implement cost-effective solutions that optimize
resource utilization, minimize waste, and reduce
overall construction costs, making housing more
affordable and accessible;Enhance the quality and durability of constructed
homes through the adoption of advanced construction
techniques and technologies, ensuring long-term
sustainability and customer satisfaction; andGenerate significant job creation and economic
growth for the applicant companies and construction
sector and related industries, supporting Ontario's
broader economic development objectives.Eligible expenses:Sub-contractor and consultant fees if approved by OCI management prior to
the start of the project;Research and Development costs directly related to the project;Project related computer hardware and software, including specialized
hardware and software;Cost of usage of equipment;Cost of direct materials, necessary for specifically identified activities and
measured as having been used for the completion of the project;Materials used for prototypes, configuring, testing production processes,
systems, and training employees;Cost of upgrade of project related equipment;Capital lease of equipment (interest costs are not eligible);Project-related leasehold improvement costs (prior OCI approval required);Sales and marketing cost attributed to the project;Training costs directly attributable to the project;Cost of regulatory compliance (up to maximum specified by OCI);Incremental salary and benefits for company employees working exclusively
on eligible project activities, to a maximum specified in the funding
agreement with OCI (specify position and employment status); andTravel expenses are explicitly project-related, represent themost economical
option (economy fare, and standard hotel room).Ineligible Expenses:Costs not directly associated with meeting the deliverables and milestones
as specified in the funding agreement with OCI;Expenses of a personal nature;Ongoing cost of production;Interest cost on capital leases;General working capital requirement;Costs related to staff awards and recognition;Bonuses, dividends, and cash incentives etc. NOTE: Full list of eligible an ineligible expenses can be found hereProgram Details:Projects must be carried out in Ontario;Must involve one Applicant and minimum of one Primary Partner;Minimum 2:1 contribution match by Applicants and/or industry Partners;Projects should be at Technology
Readiness Level (TRL) 3-9;Applicant and Partners should demonstrate close collaboration and scalable outcomes with high
potential for commercialization, strong commercial pull, competitive advantage, and alignment
with intended program benefits;Projects should demonstrate economic, environmental, or social benefit for Ontario; andTypical project activities include technology/product/service development, validation, testing, piloting, demonstration, commercialization and deployment of products and services.

      The Increasing Deadstock Capacity Initiative provides funding of up to 40% to a maximum of $100,000 to deadstock service providers, waste management companies, commodity associations, and commercial operations in Ontario. Eligible applicants may apply for a maximum of 3 projects for a grand total of $300,000. The intent of the program is to address immediate and short-term deadstock capacity needs and improve sustainability.Grant Value: Up to 40% to a maximum of $100,000Turnaround Time: within 20 business daysEligible Applicants:Located in Ontario;Involved in headstock collection in Ontario;Legal entities capable of entering into a legally binding agreement;Must have commercial general liability insurance on occurrence basis for a minimum of $2 million per occurrence; andBe one of the following:New or existing headstock service providers (must be licensed);Commodity association;Commercial operation requiring headstock services;Waste management company; ORMunicipalities.Eligible Activities:Purchasing, retrofitting, and/or modifying equipment to haul, store, or collect headstock;Retrofitting or modifying site for transfer stations, rendering, salvaging, and composting;Activities for construction or modifications related to increasing deadstock disposal capacity (e.g., new rendering or composting capacity, compliance with regulatory requirements); andPlanning and assessment activities to determine capacity options and contingency planning (i.e., rendering, collection, composting, traceability management, biosecurity measures, etc.).Note: Eligible activities cannot be located on-farm and must be carried out between April 1, 2024, and February 1, 2025.Program Details:Maximum 3 applications per applicant:Separate applicants must be submitted for each distinct project.Documents required for application:Application Form;Part 6 Eligible Project Costs and Activities and Sources of Funding in Excel;Quotes from the third party providing the good or service or both to the Applicant;Attestation that an Environmental Assessment is completed, if required to meet regulatory requirements (unless applying for planning and assessment activities).The reimbursement claim deadline is February 14, 2025, for costs incurred from April 1, 2024, to February 1, 2025.A minimum of one claim MUST be submitted per Project per Fiscal Year; andClaims submitted after the deadline will not be accepted for costs incurred in the previous Fiscal Year.

and similar organizations funded in whole or in part by the government;Retail businesses, restaurants, and food establishments; andAny other person deemed by the Minister to be ineligible.Eligible Activities:Applicants may apply for funding under one of the following:Processing capacity expansion;Food safety improvement;New product and process development; andMarket development and access.Ineligible Activities:Activities related to cleaning, bagging, sorting, handling and/or storing of
primary products;Construction of walls, floors, ceilings, or ancillary buildings;Labels and packaging design that is not in relation to New Products or for
New Markets;Advertising;Promotions;Activities associated with aquaculture, aquaponics, or seafood processing,
with the exception of activities related to the international marketing of fish
and seafood products which are eligible and may be included in an
application; andActivities that provide support for province-specific branding, promotion or
marketing activities that are detrimental to another province or territory.Eligible Expenses:25% of eligible capital expenses are covered by the program and the remainder by the applicant;50% of eligible non-capital expenses are covered by the program and the remainder by the applicant;Eligible expenses vary depending on which area the applicant is applying underProcessing Capacity Expansion:Eligible Capital Expenses:Processing Equipment;Food Safety Equipment;Software systems to assist in processing;Third party engineering related to purchase, and configuration of eligible equipment.NOTE: Leased equipment is ineligible.Eligible Non-Capital Expenses: Training costs associated with adopting new technologies, new equipment and/or new automation processes as related to processing.Food Safety Improvement:Eligible Non-Capital Expenses:Development and implementation of a food safety system;Training costs associated with adopting new technologies, new equipment and/or new food safety food processes related to food safety improvement.New Product and Process Development:Eligible Non-Capital Expenses:Sensory and shelf-life testing;Validation of nutritional or health claims;Attribute identification;Environmental product declaration;Non-food product regulation studies;Scale-up trials;Formulation development, including ingredient costs for trials;Process improvement;First run of labels and/or package printing used for new product launch to a max of 2500 units per new product; andFirst-time brand design and development. Market Development and Access:Eligible Non-Capital Expenses:Feasibility studies;Market readiness assessments;Marketing and export plans for local, domestic, or international market opportunities;Design of market support materials for new product and new market launch;Capital investment strategy development;First-time certification audit;Development of initial online presence for the purpose of e-commerce, including translation for new markets;Enhancement and expansion of an online marketing/sales platform;In-store or in-market product demonstrations, excluding the cost of product samples and shipping, and Trade shows and conference registration fees for events directly related to accessing new markets and/or launch of new products (max of two people per event) virtual events are included.Ineligible Expenses: Travel expenses not in compliance with the Sustainable CAP Travel Expense
Policy;Expenses not incurred by the Eligible Applicant in carrying out the Eligible Activity;Expenses associated with activities that are ineligible for the Program;Shipping costs for equipment;Costs of lease of office furniture, space, and equipment;Fixtures that are not an Eligible Capital Expense;Costs of equipment for storage purposes, not directly related to the Eligible
Activity;Costs associated with the building such as plumbing, framing, flooring, electrical
and insulation;On-going business operational activities and overhead expenses;Staff or consulting expenses for product sale activities, or in market representation
for existing products;Advertising expenses (including radio, social media, vehicle wraps, billboards,
signage);Sponsorship;Donation of product;Listing fees, distribution fees or shelf stocking fees;Website hosting, domain registration or ongoing website maintenance;Vehicles of any kind (e.g. trucks, fork lifts, refrigerated trucks);Expenses related to non-specific activities, such as those marked “miscellaneous”;Goods and Services Tax (GST).Program Details:Project activities can take place between January 1, 2025 and March 15, 2026;Applicants can apply once per program fiscal year;Funding is granted on a case-by-case basis and not on a first come, first served basis;The eligible applicant will also be required to submit a final report to the Minister;Stream A application must include: A completed application form, signed by an authorized representative, and all documents required to be submitted pursuant to that form;Quotations or invoices for capital expenses over $10,000; andAny additional supplementary documentation requested by the Minister.Stream B application must include:A completed application form, signed by an authorized representative, and all documents required to be submitted pursuant to that form;Documents to demonstrate the applicant has the necessary capacity to complete the activities included in the applications; andAny additional supplementary documentation requested by the Minister.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Program is retroactive to January 1, 2025;Funding received through any other Sustainable CAP programs may not be used toward the cost-share requirements of the Program.Funding can be combined with of federal and provincial programs as long as the funding doesn't exceed 100% of the eligible expenses.Process Best Practices:Funding is limited and applications are approved on a case to case basis and not on a first come first served basis.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereEligible Expenses: click hereApplication Form: click here

        Recently Changed 
        January 7, 2026As part of its 2026 renewal, the IFIT program will support projects that advance forest bioproducts, advanced biofuels, and low-carbon building materials.The funding cap for the capital investment stream has increased to up to $20 million, doubling the previous $10 million limit.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The Investment in Forest Industry Transformation (IFIT) program will provide 50% up to $10 million in non-repayable funding to help improve the environmental performance of the forest sector by supporting demonstration and adoption projects that  contribute to the decarbonization of industrial processes, as well as the efficient use of resources that generates more value from the same amount of wood.Grant Value: Stream 1 Capital Investment Projects: 50% of eligible project costs Up to $10 million;Stream 2 Studies: 50% of eligible project costs min $100,000 to a max of $1 million.Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants: Stream 1:For-profit companies;Located in Canada;Must produce either forest products in an existing forest product facility or are/will be new entrants in the forest sector for the purpose of the project;Clusters, joint ventures and consortiums are welcome to apply as long as the lead applicant is a for-profit.Stream 2: For-profit companies;Located in Canada;Must produce either forest products in an existing forest product facility or are/will be new entrants in the forest sector for the purpose of the project;Clusters, joint ventures and consortiums are welcome to apply; ORnot-for profits and industry associations.Eligible Projects:Stream 1: Be primarily based on wood fibre OR integrated within new or existing industrial
processes in the forest sector;Represent an innovative advancement of a technology or process improvement
to ensure the competitiveness of operations in Canada’s forest sector; andDemonstrate a first-in-kind innovation or an early adoption of technology that
requires further de-risking in a range of conditions before widespread
implementation.Stream 2:Advance a concept, technology, process, or product primarily based on wood fibre
OR integrated within new or existing industrial processes in the forest sector;Investigate the feasibility and/or advance a concept within the targeted innovation
categories described in the following section; andDisseminate project learnings beyond the applicant’s corporate structure.Eligible Expenses: Cost of salaries and benefits;Overhead expenditures provided they are directly related and essential to the
conduct of the project, up to 1.5% of eligible expenditures;Professional and technical services, such as, but not limited to research,
consulting, engineering, trades, and laboratory services;Travel expenses, including transportation, accommodation, and meals (based on
National Joint Council rates);Training;Publication, printing, and other media services;Data collection services, including processing, analysis, and management;Licence fees and permits;Capital expenses;Retrofitting and upgrading of existing capital;Material and supplies;Meeting hospitality and space rental;Costs associated with environmental assessments; andTechnical audits associated with project activities.Program Details:The Program will focus on the following innovation categories:Advanced BioMaterials and Biochemicals;Pulp and Paper Diversification;Next Generation Building Projects;Advanced Biofuels;Process Efficiency and Decarbonization; andImproved Fibre Utilization.Any costs associated with the production or exports of softwood lumber products are ineligible under this program; andInitially EOI must be submitted, if successful will be invited to submit full project proposal.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:The program funding cannot be used retroactively; andThe program allows funding to be stacked with other sources of federal and provincial funding as long as it does not exceed 100% of total eligible project costs.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click hereStream 1 Capital Investment projects guidelines: click hereStream 2 Studies guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Talent Development Internship Program provides funding up to $10,000 per internship to organizations to support recent undergraduate or Master's graduates to work on industry-driven projects related to the six CIT Critical Technology areas: 5G and advanced networks, AI, Blockchain, Cybersecurity, Quantum and Robotics in any one of the four key sector areas: Advanced Manufacturing, Agri-Food, Construction, Mining.Grant Value: 50% up to $10,000Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Employers:SME with fewer than 500 global full-time employees;Must have registered operations in Ontario and a valid CRA business number;Is using or developing technology-based innovation or innovation processes related to CIT's six critical technology areas and four key sectors for competitive advantage in provincial national and/or global markets;Has R&D operation in Ontario related to the project:Has the intent and potential to apply, exploit and/or commercialize the results of
the project for the economic benefit of Ontario;Has the necessary expertise and resources to put the project into effect within
an appropriate timeframe.Company subsidiaries (organizations with headquarters outside of Ontario) are
eligible, provided that the Ontario operations meet all of the above criteria;All applicants and partners must be in good financial and reporting standing with OCI; andApplicants who have received over $500,000 of funding from OCI administered programs in their
lifetime (excluding TalentEdge) are required to obtain OCI approval before a new application for
funding is initiated.Eligible Candidates:Recent Undergraduate or Masters graduates from an accredited College/University within three years of graduation;Must be eligible to work in Ontario(Ontario resident) and have employee status for the duration on the internship;Cannot be a conflict of interest with the company;Cannot be enrolled in a co-op program or other equivalent job placement/employment program; andCannot be previously employed by the employer.Program Details: Internships must be full time 4 months in length;Consecutive placements can be funded but only to a total of 2 placements;Internships must be working on an industry-driven project related to one of the six CIT critical technology ares:5G and advanced networks;Artificial Intelligence;Blockchain;Cybersecurity;Quantum; andRobotics.The internship must also be within one of the 4 key sectors:Advanced Manufacturing;Agri-Food; Construction; andMining.Projects must have an R&D component;Interns will receive on-the-job training in areas related to critical technologies;Commensurate with the intern's experience and expertise;Maximum funding per company is $20,000 (2 placements per employer); andProject activities must be carried out in Ontario.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Development and Commercialization Program supports the development and commercialization of Ontario made products and services that integrate/adopt Critical technologies by providing funding 50% up to $200,000. The program enables SMEs to access technology facilities an capabilities across the province to develop, test, validate and showcase their products and services.Grant Value: 50% of eligible costs to a minimum of $50,000 and a maximum of $200,000Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants:SME with fewer than 500 global full-time employees;Must have registered operations in Ontario and a valid CRA business number;Has the intent and potential to apply, exploit and/or commercialize the results of the project for the economic benefit of Ontario;Has the necessary expertise and resources to put the project into effect within an appropriate time frame;Adoption of critical technologies is part of their long-term product roadmap;All applicants and partners must be in good financial and reporting standing with OCI; andApplicants who have received over $500,000 of funding from OCI-administered programs in their lifetime (excluding TalentEdge) are required to obtain OCI approval before a new application for funding is initiated.Eligible Partners:SME applicant companies may choose to apply in collaboration with a strategic partner
company. (Not mandatory, but preference will be given to SME applicants with strategic
partners involved in their project outcomes);A strategic partner could be a private industry partner and/or public sector organizations such
as but not limited to a municipality, a healthcare facility, or a public utility;The strategic partner company should represent a significant potential commercial
partner/strategic client for the proposed innovative product/service;The SME and strategic partner must have an arm’s-length business relationship; andStrategic Partner must agree to complete the required OCI report.Eligible Project:Projects must support Critical Technology integration, adoption, demonstration, prototyping,
testing by the SME;The solution should involve the acceleration, development, or integration of at least one of the six
Critical Technologies (5G and Advanced networks, AI, blockchain, robotics, cybersecurity and
quantum);Projects should result in the development of a new solution, product, or service with strong
commercial opportunities in one or more of the four Key Sectors.Eligible Expenses:Sub-contractor and consultant fees if approved by OCI management prior to
the start of the project and if procured in accordance with the Broader Public
Sector (BPS) Procurement Directive;Research and Development costs directly related to the project;Project-related computer hardware and software, including specialized
hardware and software;Cost of usage of equipment;Cost of direct materials, necessary for specifically identified activities and
measured as having been used for, the completion of the project;Materials used for prototypes, configuring, testing production processes,
systems, and training employees;Cost of upgrade of project-related equipment;Capital lease of equipment (interest costs are not eligible);Project-related leasehold improvement costs (prior OCI approval required);Sales and marketing costs attributed to the project;Training costs directly attributable to the project; andCost of regulatory compliance (up to a maximum specified by OCI).Program Details:Project activities are to be carried out in Ontario;Minimum 1:1 contribution match from the Applicant;Project length maximum 6 months;Projects must involve the utilization of at least of the Technology development sites for a minimum of 2 hours per test bed; Projects must be the basis for a highly competitive business and must offer a good
return on investment and benefits to Ontario (e.g., new revenues, job creation/retention,
new customers, follow-on investment, and productivity improvement); andProjects must already have all necessary certifications, if required for a project to be executed.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:The program does not allow funding to be used retroactively;Funding cannot be stacked with other federal or provincial funding.Process Best Practices:Applicants must retain all proof of purchases, receipts and other relevant documentation relating to eligible expenses (These should be included in the final report).Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereEligible Expenses Guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The AI for Manufacturing challenge is targeting a co-investment up to 35% up to $2.1 million to build advanced manufacturing capability in Canada by integrating AI innovation in the manufacturing sectors. The aim is to enhance the efficiency, agility and competitiveness of Canadian manufacturers, thus enabling the development of new commercial opportunities for AI solution providers and manufacturers alike.Grant Value: Up to 35% of eligible expenses to a maximum of $2.1 million.Turnaround Time: Notified by July 19, 2024.Eligible Applicants: Must be incorporate in Canada;Be for-profit organization, not-for-profit, organizations that facilitate and fund research and development;Projects must include at least two industry partners, one manufacturing company and one AI company;At least one of these companies needs to be an SME.Eligible Projects:Project will support AI-enabled advanced manufacturing technology development and commercialization in areas such as: Systems optimization within manufacturing facilities or across supply chains. e.g.,Automating and optimizing machines and processes;Predictive Maintenance;Automating Quality Prediction and Control;Energy and emissions optimization;Demand-driven production
o Digitization of supply chains for traceability and evidence of Environmental, Social, and
Governance (ESG) compliance;Productivity optimization, including increasing Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE).The development of new advanced manufacturing capabilities, for example, new robotic or
automation equipment;Rapid prototyping and testing of materials, products, and processes. E.g., design for
manufacturing processes for new products, including adding new or sustainable materials into
the production or optimizing material use and reducing waste;Enhanced cybersecurity at the manufacturing process or facility level; andDevelopment of other disruptive AI-enabled manufacturing capabilities and services.Ineligible Projects:Projects related to experimental or theoretical work without any direct commercial application
or use. Projects must demonstrate a strong commercialization strategy;Production activities themselves or activities that subsidize full-scale production;Capital investment for purposes not related to the project. Capital investment must
demonstrate new AI-enabled manufacturing capabilities for the organization;Activities that could be viewed as anti-competitive;Projects where benefits accrue to a single firm or organization;Projects that would be undertaken at the same scale or scope and within the same timeframe
without NGen funding; andAny routine or periodic changes made to existing products, production lines, manufacturing
processes, services, and other operations in progress, even if those changes may represent
improvements.Eligible Costs:Salaries and wages for those working directly on the project;Sub-contract and consultancy fees;Capital, Non-Capital Equipment and Facilities;Materials and Supplies;Travel Costs;NOTE: for a full breakdown of eligible and ineligible costs click hereProgram Details: Projects are encouraged to support commercialization across a broad number of manufacturers or
manufacturing facilities rather than providing company or facility-specific solutions;All projects must demonstrate the development or application of AI solutions in support of Canadian manufacturers;Projects must be focused on commercializing AI solutions, business-led and collaborative;Projects must be in addition to the regular business undertakings of the applicants;Expression of Interest deadline June 14, 2024;Total project costs should be between $1.5 million and $6 million;Paid expenses to be submitted by all partners by the 31, January 2026;Projects must be transformative, applied, enduring and collaborative and meet the scope criteria; andProjects must have the potential to deliver significant commercial benefits and jobs among project
partners and beyond.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:Program does not allow funding to be used retroactively;No individual partner may receive more than 80% of NGen funding; Full application proposal requires 8 questions to be answered with a maximum of 7,000 characters to answer each question, any answers that exceed this will not be sent to be assessed; andAny single piece of capital expenditure exceeding $1 million will require pre-approval.Forms and Links: Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This competitive program provides grants of up to $3,000,000 in non-dilutive funding to support project proposals that develop commercial wildfire tech projects in B.C. Eligible projects include technologies and business processes that are at a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) between 4-9, ranging from early stage of prototype development to an early commercialization.  Projects should fall into one of the focus areas: 1) prevention solutions  ; 2) mitigation technologies; 3) adaption innovations. Grant Value: Up to $3,000,000.NOTE: Program is looking to fund several projects therefore highly unlikely to receive $3,000,000 The average funding awarded per project is below $700,000 covering up to 50% of expenses.Turnaround Time: Expressions of Interest are due August 7, 2024. The final stage of the application process will conclude on November 1, 2024.  Eligible Applicants:Private companies, organizations, and consortia of companies based in BC;Companies must demonstrate their ability to complete the project with sound management, operational capability, and financial management; andThe program may consider applicants from companies based outside fo the province with a project in B.C.Eligible Projects:Projects may be technologies or business processes in any of the following focus areas:Prevention solutions; Mitigation technologies; andAdaption innovations. The proposed technologies/processes should be at a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 4-9;Project activities can include, but are not limited to:Demonstration and pilot projects;Innovative implementation  solutions;Novel linkage of system components;Mitigation or monitoring technologies; andBusiness model innovations.Eligible Expenses:Wages and salaries;Consultant fees;Direct costs associated with project management;Securing of demonstration sites;Integration of system components;Pilot production; andScale-up of manufacturing.Ineligible Expenses:Enhancing normal business/operational capabilities;Purchasing capital equipment;Capital or leasehold improvements;Purchase of furniture or office equipment;Advertising or business promotion; andOverhead.Program Details: Applications proceed through a multi-stage elimination process;Stage 1 is an Expression of Interest, due August 7, 2024;Applicants complete a webform and upload a 5-minute video that introduces their basic details about the proposed project and short-form project description;Stage 1 applications will be evaluated by CICE.  By August 28,  2024, a limited number will be invited to sign a non-disclosure agreement, and proceed to Stage 2;Stage 2 is the Detailed Proposal Submission and Review, due September 18, 2024;Applicants will work with the CICE project review team to ensure adequate technical assessments are made;A template for the proposal will be provided;Stage 3 is the Funding Decision;Applicants will negotiate a contribution agreement with CICE by November 1, 2024, identifying obligations of all parties. The contribution agreement will include key milestones for the project;Grant funding will be paid in increments upon completion of project milestones; andThe program will prioritize solutions that have significant co-benefits such as integrating additional carbon reduction into projects, promoting ecosystem restoration and biodiversity conservation, and enhancing community resilience and socio-economic benefits through wildfire management efforts.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program does not allow for funding to be used retroactively;This program does allow for funding to be stacked and is encouraged to ensure projects are successful; andThe program will prioritize solutions that have significant co-benefits such as integrating additional carbon reduction into projects, promoting ecosystem restoration etc.Forms and Links: Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click here

The intent of the program is to help Canadian periodicals overcome market disadvantages by allowing publishers to direct funds to the area of greatest need, including content creation, production, distribution or business development.Grant Value: $1,500 - $150,000Turnaround Time: 30 weeksEligible Applicants:Canadian publishing firms producing either digital or print periodicals;Be one of the following organization types:For-profit organizations;Non-profit organizations;Partnerships; andHave published between two and 52 regular issues and no more than 56 issues during the financial year, including special issues.Digital magazines and community (non-daily) newspapers must:Be available through a valid URL, an app for download, email format, or a third-party publishing platform and provide access to the program;Maintain a regular publishing schedule in which the majority of editorial content changes at least twice during a 12-month period;Contain over 50% original editorial content, not reproduced from another website, publication or previous issues of the same publication;Maintain an editorial function where the editor is named and the date of publication of the article is identified;Regularly present written editorial content from more than one person;Generate revenues (e.g. subscription revenues, advertising sales, etc.); andPresent a clearly displayed masthead or contact page that includes, at minimum, the names of the publisher and editor in addition to the postal address for the publication.Note: Previous recipients of Canada Periodical Fund - Aid to Publishers for the same fiscal year are ineligible.Eligible Activities:Content creation (ie. writing, editing, photography, illustration, and design);Production (ie pre-press and printing);Marketing;Distribution;Website development and enhancement (ie. content development, and enhancements to the site's architecture and functionality); andProduction of digital periodical associated with an eligible print periodical.Program Details:At the end of an approved project, applicants may be required to submit a report and/or participate in the evaluation of results;If an applicant receives funding, they must publicly acknowledge – in English and/or in French – the financial support received from the Government of Canada in all communications materials and promotional activities.Additional requirements may be requested by the program.

andPriority will be given to those that are members of an equity deserving group (e.g. BIPOC, Women, LGBTQIA+, etc.) and are newcomers to Canada (having arrived less than 5 years ago).Program Details: Eligible roles are for digital marketing positions;Placement length 8 weeks;Full-time positions are preferred however part-time positions are also accepted;Maximum 5 funded placements per employer;Employers may reapply every 8 weeks until the full $25,000 is used up.Employers may apply with their own candidate as long as the participant:Is accepted into the training program on their own merit;Completes the entirety of one of the training programs; andWill be taking on new roles, a new title or promotion directly related to digital marketing and skills developed in the program.Participants must take 6-7 weeks training, the training organization they will complete the training in will be based on the number of years experience the participant has.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Market Entry Development Program provides access to an in-market business development consultant (valued at $24,000) for up to 20 days. Eligible applicants must be Atlantic Canadian Food and Beverage companies with an interest in expanding their export sales to Europe. The intent of the program is to establish a virtual presence for Atlantic Canadian companies in Europe or Asia and to grow export sales and establish new business relationships.Grant Value:  Consultant services valued at $26,000 (applicants to contribute $2500)Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants:Be headquartered in Atlantic Canada (Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, PEI, Newfoundland & Labrador);Possess a fully-developed, exportable product and/or service that can be sold into European and Asian markets;Interested in creating or expanding their international footprint, meaning a move to new markets or increasing their total sales volume in Europe or Asia;Possess a proven record or strong potential of revenue growth;Demonstrate the financial capacity to execute their strategy and support potential in-market activities;Have senior management commitment and the human resource capacity to execute the strategy, including internal and external sales and marketing support who will lead implementation including the potential of travel to market;Have the production and service capacity to meet projected increases in demand;Have considered their expected outcomes in international markets including anticipated sales growth;Have an understanding of factors that may need to be addressed (e.g., competition, cultural competencies, import controls, intellectual property status, certifications, and regulatory, legal, taxation issues); andDemonstrate how participation in this program is linked to the export planning and goals.Ineligible Applicants:Games of chance operations, bingo halls, small-scale gaming operations;Real estate developers;Retailers, franchises, distributors, agents, or associations;Creative industries companies;Publicly funded organizations.Program Details:Successful applicants will be required to work collaboratively with the consultant, participate regularly in virtual development and sales meetings, and be willing to travel and spend time in-market;Participating companies will be required to commit the financial resources necessary to execute on their market strategy, as agreed to between the company and the programParticipating companies will be required to report on progress/activities undertaken as per the agreed upon Statement of Work and may be asked to complete mandatory evaluations on the overall service delivery for up to a year following the MEDP end date.
